passages.heading: Exégesis de la sura:
passages.text:
(Di: “”Me refugio en el Señor del amanecer,)

Di- oh mensajero- me refugio en Al-láh el Señor del amanecer.

(de todo el mal que existe en lo que Él creó,)

De cualquier mal que puede venir de las criaturas, sean las vistas o las ocultas para nosotros.

(del mal de la oscuridad de la noche cuando se extiende,)

Y del mal de la noche cuando oscurece, y de todo lo que incluye de mal y de daños.

Al Ghasaq: la intensidad de la oscuridad de la noche.

Al-Falaq: el amanecer

passages.heading: El bendito mes de Ramadán:
passages.text:
Es el noveno mes del año lunar, es un mes bendito en lo cual Al-láh reveló el Corán a Su mensajero Muhammad -que la paz y las bendiciones de Al-láh sean con él-. Al-láh -Enaltecido sea- hizo del ayuno durante el día y la oración durante la noche una causa de expiación de los pecados. Se destaca una noche mejor que mil meses llamada (Laylatul Qadr= la noche del decreto). Quien dedica esta noche a recordar y orar Al-láh le perdona todos sus pecados anteriores.

**Los musulmanes realizan la oración de Tarawih en el mes de Ramadán, y es una sunna relacionada con Ramadán y que se realiza después de la oración del Isha.**

passages.heading: ¿Qué tengo que hacer al encontrar agua después de haber realizado la ablución seca (tayamum)?
passages.text: Cuando el musulmán encuentra agua o es capaz de usarla sin causarle daño, en este caso se anula su ablución seca y debe realizar la ablución menor o mayor con agua.

passages.heading: Preámbulo
passages.text: La ablución menor (wudu’) tiene una gran importancia en islam ya que está relacionada con un pilar fundamental que es la oración, desde entonces el musulmán debe aprender a realizarla correctamente, y en esta lección vamos a estudiar el significado de la ablución menor, lo que exige y lo que anula la ablución menor y cómo se realiza de la manera correcta.

passages.heading: Preámbulo
passages.text: El Islam es la religión con la cual Al-láh envió a Muhammad -que la paz y las bendiciones de Al-láh sean con él- y es una continuación de lo que han transmitido los enviados anteriores. Se basa en la adoración de un Dios Único que merece ser adorado solo sin socios, es decir Al-láh -Enaltecido y Exaltado sea- no tiene socio en Su reinado, no existe intermedio entre Él y Sus siervos. Pero ¿Por qué tengo que convertirme al Islam? ¿Acaso el Islam es una religión propia de los árabes o es para toda la humanidad? ¿Quién es el mensajero enviado para transmitir esta religión? ¿Habrá un mensajero después de él?

passages.heading: ¿Cómo rezamos?
passages.text: Si el musulmán quiere realizar la oración debe hacer los pasos siguientes:

passages.heading: Preámbulo
passages.text: La sura de Al Fatiha se considera una de las suras más grandiosas del Corán, en efecto el mensajero -que la paz y las bendiciones de Al-láh sean con él- insistió sobre su importancia y su gran valor en muchos de sus hadices, es la sura que todo musulmán debe memorizar, ya que es la única sura cuya recitación es obligatoria en cada oración, y en esta lección vamos a estudiar esta sura, memorizar sus aleyas y conocer sus significados, además de otras suras cortas que incluyen significados de suma relevancia.

passages.heading: Los frutos de la fe:
passages.text:
- La tranquilidad y la paz interna: con la fe el alma se encuentra tranquila, complacida por los decretos de Al-láh y teme solo a Él.
- Conocer a Al-láh -Enaltecido sea: el creyente conoce su Señor y Le quiere más conociendo Sus nombres bellos, Sus atributos sublimes y Sus actos.
- La veneración de Al-láh: el creyente cuando más sabe su Señor, su veneración se aumenta más. Su amor y esperanza hacia Él, su temor y reverencia se aumentan cada vez más.
- Sentir las gracias de Al-láh sobre sus criaturas: ya que se les envió mensajeros y libros para guiarles a la religión de la verdad.
- El amor hacia los ángeles debido a su adoración y su obediencia de Al-láh.
- El amor hacia los mensajeros que fueron elegidos por Al-láh -Enaltecido sea- para transmitir el mensaje divino a la gente.
- La diligencia en la adoración: cuanto más auténtica es la fe, más abundantes serán los actos de adoración del ser humano.
- La vida buena: ya que el creyente se complace con los decretos de Al-láh, y sabe que las desgracias que puede recibir en esta vida elevarán su grado y expiarán sus pecados, además espera lo que Al-láh preparó de buena recompensa para los creyentes en el Más-Allá.
- No ser engañado por la vida mundana, ya que esta vida es fugaz y es un camino para la vida eterna en el Más-Allá.
- Invalidar los mitos: la fe revela e invalida muchos de los mitos.
- Ingresar al Paraíso: es la morada del bienestar permanente, la morada que preparó Al-láh a sus siervos creyentes.

passages.heading: Exégesis de la sura:
passages.text:
(Di: “”Él es Al-láh, Uno.)

Di -Oh mensajero- a quien te pregunta sobre tu Señor: Es Al-láh Quien posee la Divinidad y El Señorío, no hay Dios excepto Él.

(Al-láh es el Absoluto).

Y es Al-láh el Perfecto en sus atributos, hacia Él todas las criaturas se dirigen para pedir y suplicar, mientras que Él es Absoluto y no necesita a nadie.

(No engendró ni fue engendrado.)

Es Al-láh Quien no engendró ni hijo ni hija, no fue engendrado por un padre ni por una madre.

(Y no hay nada ni nadie que se asemeje a Él).

Nadie se le asemeja entre sus criaturas, ni en Su esencia, ni en Sus nombres ni en Sus atributos ni en Sus actos.

passages.heading: Segunda lección
passages.text:
### Exégesis de las suras cortas

(del mal de las [hechiceras] sopladoras de nudos,)

Y del mal de las hechiceras, quienes soplan en los nudos para realizar actos de hechicería.;

(y del mal del envidioso cuando envidia)

Y del mal del envidioso quien busca la desaparición de la gracia y el daño para la persona agraciada.

passages.heading: La sura de An-Nas:
passages.text:
{{Q:114:1-6}}

**Exégesis de la sura:**

(Di: “”Me refugio en el Señor de los seres humanos,)

Di -Oh mensajero- me refugio en Al-láh Señor de la gente, el Todopoderoso.

(en el Rey Soberano de los seres humanos,)

El Rey Soberano de toda la gente, Quien maneja todos sus asuntos.

(en el [único] Dios de los seres humanos,)

El Dios de todos los seres humanos, entonces no hay nada ni nadie que merezca ser adorado fuera de Él.

(de la maldad del [demonio] susurrador que huye [cuando el nombre de Dios es mencionado],)

Contra el perjuicio del Satanás quien les susurra cuando dejan de recordar a Al-láh, y deja de susurrar cuando recuerdan a Al-láh.

(que susurra en los corazones de los seres humanos,)

El que esparce malos pensamientos en el pecho de las personas, y manipula sus sentimientos y pensamientos.

(ya sea que pertenezca a los yinn o a los hombres).

De los demonios de los genios y de los humanos.

passages.heading: Lo que anula el ayuno:
passages.text:
**El ayunante debe abstenerse de un conjunto de actos que anulan su ayuno como:**

1. Comer, beber, y las jeringas de alimentación intravenosas.
2. La eyaculación intencionalmente, sea con o sin coito, el coito durante el día de ayuno de Ramadán es un pecado muy grave.
3. El vómito intencional.

**En cuanto a la mujer, se anula su ayuno con:**

4. La salida de sangre de menstruación o de postparto.

passages.heading: ¿Quiénes pueden romper el ayuno durante el mes de Ramadán?
passages.text:
Al-láh -Enaltecido y Exaltado- permitió a algunas categorías de personas romper el ayuno durante el mes de Ramadán, éstas son:

1. El enfermo quien se hace daño al ayunar.
2. El mayor de edad que es incapaz de ayunar.
3. El viajero durante su viaje.
4. La mujer menstruante y en el postparto.
5. La embarazada y quien amamanta, si temen el daño para ellas o para sus niños.

passages.heading: Notas relacionadas con el ayuno:
passages.text:
- Quien rompe el ayuno en Ramadán por una excusa, debe recuperar los días no ayunados después de Ramadán.
- Cuando el enfermo rompe su ayuno por una enfermedad incurable, en este caso no debe recuperar los días rotos y solo debe dar a comer a un necesitado por cada día no ayunado.
- Cuando el enfermo es mayor de edad y no puede ayunar, en este caso no debe recuperar los días no ayunados y solo debe dar a comer a un necesitado por cada día no ayunado.

Los musulmanes comen al escuchar la llamada del Adhán del Maghreb, y muchos de los musulmanes insisten en romper el ayuno con sus hermanos.

passages.heading: Taiámmum (ablución seca):
passages.text: Cuando la persona que debe realizar la ablución menor o mayor es incapaz de realizarlas por la falta de agua, o por una enfermedad u otra causa, en este caso es permitido para él realizar la ablución seca (tayamum). La forma de realizarla es tener la intención en el corazón (sin pronunciarla), tocar con sus dos manos el suelo una sola vez, luego pasar sus manos sobre su cara, luego sus manos.

passages.heading: El significado del wudu (la ablución menor):
passages.text: La ablución menor (wudu’): lavarse la cara, las manos, los pies y pasar las manos mojadas sobre la cabeza con un modo específico.

passages.heading: Los actos que exigen la ablución menor:
passages.text:
Lo que exige la ablución menor son los actos que al realizarlos se debe estar puros y no se puede realizarlos sino al purificarse, y son:

Al Hadaz: es un estado moral del hombre que impide la realización de la oración antes de purificarse y no es algo tangible como las inmundicias, y es de dos tipos: uno exige la ablución menor (wudu) y el otro exige la ablución mayor (ghusl).

1. La oración.
2. La circunvalación alrededor de la Kaaba.
3. Al tocar el Libro del Corán.

passages.heading: ¿Cómo realizar la ablución menor (wudu)?
passages.text: Si el musulmán quiere realizar la ablución menor debe realizar los pasos siguientes:

passages.heading: ¿Por qué debo volverme musulmán?
passages.text:
Algunos pueden preguntarse: ¿Por qué tengo que convertirme al Islam?

Y la respuesta es: debo ser musulmán por las razones siguientes:

La primera: el Islam es la sola religión aceptada por Al-láh a sus siervos y no aceptará ninguna aparte de ella. Al-láh -Enaltecido sea- dice: {{Q:3:85}} Corán (3: 85).

La segunda: el Islam es la religión de todos los profetas, invita a creer en todos ellos, sin discriminar entre ellos. Al-láh -Enaltecido sea- dice: {{Q:2:136}} Corán (2:136).

La diferencia entre los profetas consiste en una diferencia de legislaciones relacionadas con las acciones de las personas, por ello Al-láh- Glorificado sea- dijo: {{Q:5:48}} Corán (5: 48).

Es decir: cada nación tiene una legisalción propia, una manera propia para acercarse a Al-láh con la adoración, entonces cada nación tiene normas legales propias, pero el credo de todos los profetas es igual y no cambia.

passages.heading: ¿Por qué debo volverme musulmán?
passages.text: Luego Al-láh envió al sello de los profetas y mensajeros: el profeta Muhammad -que la paz y las bendiciones de Al-láh sean con él- que es el último enviado, su legislación fue la última establecida, por ello no se aceptará ninguna otra religión fuera del Islam.

Tercero: Convertirse al Islam es el camino a la felicidad en esta vida y a la salvación en la otra vida, ya que no se salva en la otra vida sino quien al recibir el mensaje del profeta Muhammad -que la paz y las bendiciones de Al-láh sean con él- haya creído en él y le haya seguido, Al-láh-Enaltecido sea- dice: {{Q:3:85}} Corán (3: 85)

El profeta -que la paz y las bendiciones de Al-láh sean con él- dijo:» Juro por Aquel que posee mi alma en Su mano que, si una persona de este pueblo sea judío o cristiano, oye mi Mensaje y muere sin haber creído en él, será de la gente del infierno». Narrado por Muslim 153.

Cuarto: El Islam responde con respuestas evidentes a mis preguntas: ¿Por qué estoy en esta vida? ¿De dónde vine? y ¿A dónde iré después de la muerte?

passages.heading: Las cinco oraciones:
passages.text:
Al-láh -Enaltecido y Exaltado sea- prescribe a sus siervos rezar cinco oraciones al día que son:

| | El inicio de su tiempo | El fin de su tiempo | Sus unidades (Rak’as) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Salat al Fayer (el rezo del alba) | el alba. | el amanecer. | 2 |
| Salat ad-Duhur (el rezo del mediodía): | la puesta del sol (es decir cuando el sol empieza a dirigirse hacia el oeste a mediodía). | cuando se iguala la sombra de una cosa a su longitud. | 4 |
| Salat al- Asr (el rezo de la tarde): | cuando se iguala la sombra de una cosa a su longitud. | el atardecer. | 4 |
| Salat al Magrib (el rezo del ocaso): | el atardecer. | el crepúsculo. | 3 |
| Salat al ‘Isha (el rezo de la noche): | el crepúsculo. | la medianoche. | 4 |

passages.heading: ¿Cómo rezamos?
passages.text:
1. Tener la intención para la oración en su corazón (sin pronunciarla).
2. Ponerse de pie, dirigiéndose hacia la Quibla, levantando sus manos cerca de sus hombros o sus orejas diciendo: “”Al-láhu Akbar””.
3. Poner su mano derecha sobre la izquierda, luego decir la súplica de apertura de la oración (Istiftah) como:”””Glorificado seas Al-láh te alabamos. Bendito sea tu nombre y elevada sea tu majestad. No hay dios sino Tú””.Luego dice:(“”A’udhu bilahi mina shaytanir-rayim”” “”bismilahir-rahmanir-rahim””) es decir (“”Me refugio en Al-láh del maldito Satanás””, “”En el nombre de Al-láh el Clemente el Compasivo””).
Luego recita el capítulo de Al Fatiha y dice “”Amin”” (amén) después de acabarla, es decir: “”Oh Dios mío acepta mis súplicas””Luego recita algo que ha memorizado del Corán, aunque sea una sola aleya.
4. Levanta sus manos hasta sus hombros u orejas diciendo «»Al-láhu Akbar»» luego inclina su espalda poniendo sus manos sobre sus rodillas, estando su espalda y cabeza perpendiculares con sus piernas y dice durante su inclinación: «»Subhana rabial Adhim= Glorificado sea mi Señor Grandioso»» tres veces.

passages.heading: As-Salat (el rezo ritual)
passages.text:
5. Al levantar su cabeza y elevando sus manos cerca de sus hombros dice ‘”Samia’ Al-láhu liman hamidahu= Al-láh escucha quien lo alaba’” y al estar de pie dice: ‘”Rabana walakal Hamd= Señor mío a Ti pertenecen las alabanzas’”.

6. Luego prosterna poniendo su frente, su nariz, las palmas de sus manos, sus rodillas y las puntas de los dedos de sus pies en el suelo diciendo «»Subhana Rabial A›ala= Glorificado sea mi Señor el Altísimo»» tres veces.

passages.heading: Segunda lección
passages.text: ## Exégesis de las suras cortas

passages.heading: Exégesis de la sura:
passages.text:
(En el nombre de Dios, el Compasivo con toda la creación, el Misericordioso con los creyentes)

Empiezo la recitación del Corán con el nombre de Al-láh, pidiendo Su ayuda, Al-láh el Único que merece ser adorado, Quien posee la clemencia que abarca todas sus criaturas, el misericordioso con sus siervos creyentes ofreciéndoles una misericordia específica.

(Todas las alabanzas son para Dios, Señor de todo cuanto existe)

Alabar a Al-láh con los atributos perfectos, por Sus gracias sobre todas sus criaturas, es el Único que merece todo tipo de alabanza, es el Señor de todas las criaturas, Quien les creó de la nada,

(El Compasivo, el Misericordioso.)

El Compasivo: es Quien trata a todos sus siervos con clemencia, el Misericordioso: es Quien dedica Su misericordia para solo los creyentes de sus siervos.

El Clemente: para todas las criaturas.

El Misericordioso: solo para los creyentes

(Soberano absoluto del Día del Juicio Final,)

El Soberano del Día de Resurrección, el Día de Juicio y de la Recompensa según las obras realizadas.

(Solo a Ti te adoramos y solo de Ti imploramos ayuda.)

Solo te Adoramos a Ti, Señor nuestro, y de Ti imploramos ayuda en todos nuestros asuntos, Todo depende de Tu Voluntad.

(¡Guíanos por el camino recto!)

Guíanos al camino recto, y manténganos aferrados a la verdad (el Islam) hasta encontrarTe, al camino claro que lleva a la complacencia de Al-láh y a Su Paraíso.

(El camino de quienes has agraciado, no el de quienes han incurrido en Tu ira, ni el de quienes se han extraviado [a pesar de conocer la verdad].)

El mismo camino con el cual has agraciado a los profetas, a sus aliados y a todos sus seguidores, ellos son, sin duda, la gente de la buena guía y de la rectitud.

Y aléjanos del camino de quienes recibieron Tu ira, al saber la verdad y rechazarla, y del camino de los extraviados quienes no se guiaron al camino recto por su ignorancia.

passages.heading: Los frutos de la fe:
passages.text: La fe tiene muchos frutos, que son:

passages.heading: Mis notas
passages.text: Escribe algunos de los frutos de la fe que sientes al convertirte al Islam:

passages.heading: *Soorat Al-Kaafiroon* Explained
passages.text:
{{Q:109:1-6}}

“Say: Unbelievers!”

Say, Messenger, to those who disbelieve in Allah and His Messenger: You unbelievers.

“I do not worship what you worship”

I do not worship the false gods, such as idols, that you worship.

“nor do you worship what I worship”

nor do you worship the True God whom I worship, and who alone is worthy of worship.

“I will never worship what you worship”

I will never worship the false gods that you worship.

“nor will you ever worship what I worship”

nor will you ever worship the True God whom I worship, and who alone is worthy of worship.

Al-kaafir: The person who does not proclaim pure monotheism and does not follow the divine message Prophet Muhammad ﷺ has brought.

“You have your religion, and I have my religion”

You have your religion to which you adhere, and I have my religion to which I adhere.

passages.heading: What shall I do if I find water after having performed *tayammum*?
passages.text: If a Muslim finds water or can use it, his purity becomes invalid, in which case he must perform *wudoo’* or *ghusl*.

passages.heading: How Do We Pay *Zakaat* Due on Cash?
passages.text: A Muslim pays *zakaat* due on his cash once a year. 2.5% of its value must be given out as *zakaat*.

passages.heading: Discuss
passages.text: What do you think would happen if all the rich Muslims paid *zakaat* due on all their wealth?

passages.heading: Things That a Person Who Is in a State of *Jannabah* Must Not Do
passages.text:
The state into which a person gets following intercourse or ejaculation and because of which he must perform *ghusl* is called *janaabah*, and he is described as *junub*. In this case, he is not allowed to do the following:

1. perform the prayer
2. circumambulate the Ka’bah (*tawaaf*)
3. touch or carry the Qur’an
4. stay in the mosque
5. read the Qur’an

passages.heading: Who Are We?
passages.text:
He has provided him with an innate readiness to do good or evil but has at the same time furnished him with such cognitive tools as the innate human nature (*fitrah*) and the intellect to discern good from evil.

He has also given him free will to be responsible for his own choices and actions.

passages.heading: How Do We Pray?
passages.text: If a Muslim wants to pray, he must do the following:

passages.heading: Why Do We Perform *Hajj*?
passages.text: Muslims perform *Hajj* to the Sacred House in Makkah in response to Allah’s command to do so.

passages.heading: *Soorat An-Naas* Explained
passages.text:
“Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of mankind”

Say, Messenger, “I seek refuge and protection in Allah, the Lord of all mankind, who alone has power over all things.

“the King of mankind”

The King of all people, who manages all their affairs.

“the God of mankind”

The True God of all people, who alone deserves to be worshipped by them.

“from the evil of the slinking whisperer”

from the harm of Satan who whispers evil suggestions to people when they are heedless of Allah and refrains from doing so when they remember Him.

“who whispers into the hearts of mankind”

who whispers evil suggestions and thoughts into people’s chests and controls their feelings and thoughts.

“from among the jinn and mankind”

from the devils among the jinn and mankind.

passages.heading: Discuss
passages.text: What is the theme that is highlighted in *Soorat Al-Ikhlaas* and *Soorat Al-Kaafiroon*?

passages.heading: Lesson 2
passages.text: ## The Interpretation of Short *Surahs*

passages.heading: Soorat Al-Kawthar (Abundant Good)
passages.text:
*Soorat Al-Kawthar* **Explained**

{{Q:108:1-3}}

“We have bestowed on you abundant good”

We have given you, Messenger, immeasurable, abundant good in this life and the life to come, part of which is River Al-Kawthar in Paradise.

“So pray to your Lord and sacrifice to Him”

Therefore, sincerely pray to your Lord and worship Him alone, and sacrifice to Him, pronouncing Allah’s name alone when slaughtering animals, in gratitude to Him for the honour and good He has bestowed on you.

“He who hates you is the one who is truly cut off”

*Shaani’aka*: The one who hates you and hates the true religion you have brought.

The one who hates you and hates the true religion you have brought is the most disgraced and contemptible, whose mention is short-lived and who is cut off from all good.

passages.heading: *Tayammum* (Dry Ablution)
passages.text:
If a person who wants to perform *wudoo’* or *ghusl* is unable to do so due to illness, or when water is not readily available, or for any other legitimate reason, he may resort to dry ablution (*tayammum*) instead.

The Manner of Performing *Tayammum*: (1) Intend in his heart to perform *tayammum* and strike both hands slightly on pure earth once, (2) wipe the face with them, (3) wipe the back of the right hand with the palm of the left, and then the back of the left hand with the palm of the right hand.

passages.heading: What are the types of wealth upon which *zakaat* is due?
passages.text:
- **Gold and silver**
- **All types of currency (banknotes and coins)**
- **Farm produce (crops and fruit)**
- **Grazing livestock**

Grazing livestock: This refers to camels, cattle, sheep and goats.

- **Commercial commodities**

Commercial commodities: all properties owned with the aim of investing them in trade. They generally include assets, such as a house, a shop, a car and an animal.

passages.heading: Discuss
passages.text: What, in your opinion, does removing the major ritual impurity indicate?

passages.heading: The Five Obligatory Prayers
passages.text:
Allah Almighty has enjoined Muslims to perform five prayers throughout the day and night, namely:

| The Prayer | Beginning Time | Ending Time | Number of units (*rak‘ahs*) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| *Fajr* (Dawn) Prayer | at the break of dawn | sunrise | 2 |
| *Dhuhr* (Midday) Prayer | when the sun starts declining westward at midday after reaching its zenith | when the shadow of an object becomes equal in length to the object itself | 4 |
| *‘Asr* (Late Afternoon) Prayer | when the shadow of an object becomes equal in length to the object itself | sunset | 4 |
| *Maghrib* (Sunset) Prayer | sunset | when the red glow (evening twilight) on the western horizon disappears | 3 |
| *‘Ishaa’* (Late Evening) Prayer | when the red glow (evening twilight) on the western horizon disappears | midnight | 4 |

passages.heading: How Do We Pray?
passages.text:
1. He intends in his heart to pray.
2. He stands facing the *qiblah*, raises his hands up to the level of the shoulders or ears, and says, “*Allaahu akbar* Allah is the Greatest.”
3. He places his right hand on his left hand. Then he recites one of the opening supplications, such as, Subhaanak-Allaahumma wa bi hamdika, wa tabaarak-asmuka, wa ta’aalaa jadduka, wa laa ilaaha ghayruka “Glory be to You, O Allah; Yours is the praise, blessed is Your name, exalted is Your majesty, and there is no god besides You.” Then he says, A’oodhu billaahi min-ash-shaytaan-ir-rajeem. Bismillaah-ir-rahmaan-ir-raheem “I seek Allah’s protection from Satan, who has been expelled from His mercy. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.” Then he recites *Soorat Al-Faatihah* and says after it, “*Aameen*”, which means “Answer our supplications, O Allah”. After that, he recites whatever number of verses of the Qur’an as is easy for him, even if it is one verse.
4. He says, “Allaahu akbar Allah is the Greatest” while raising his hands up to the level of his shoulders or ears, and bows down, lowering his head and back and keeping them straight at a right angle, placing the palms of his hands on the knees. He says three times while in this position, “Subhaana rabbiy-al-’adheem Glory be to my Lord, the Almighty.”

passages.heading: The Position of Women in Islam
passages.text:
- Islam has granted women the right to inheritance, allocating them equitable shares with men, which sometimes differ under certain circumstances depending on their relationship with others and the financial obligations they have to discharge. While men support the family as a matter of religious obligation, women are not obliged to spend anything at all.
- It has established total equality between men and women in numerous matters including financial transactions.
- It has granted them the right to choose their own husbands.
- It has granted them the right to retain their maiden names. In Islam, a woman does not change her surname to that of her husband upon marriage; rather, she retains her maiden name, and thus her independent personality.
- It has made it the husband’s duty to spend on those women entitled to his support, such as his wife, mother and daughters, without attempting in the least to remind them of his favours.

passages.text:
Allah Almighty has prescribed several rulings relating to menstruating women and women experiencing their postnatal bleeding, including the following:

- They are exempt from performing the prayers during this period and do not have to make up for the prayers they have missed while in this state after the end of menstrual and postnatal bleeding.

- At the end of the menstrual and postnatal period, when bleeding stops completely, women must take a ritual bath (*ghusl*).

passages.heading: Important Notes Related to Fasting
passages.text:
- Whoever breaks his fast in Ramadaan for a legitimate reason must make up for every day he has missed after than Ramadaan.
- If a sick person breaks the fast because of an incurable disease, he is exempt from fasting the month of Ramadaan, but he must feed one poor person for each day he does not fast.
- If a Muslim cannot possibly fast due to old age, he is exempt from fasting the month of Ramadaan but he must feed one poor person for each day he does not fast.

**Muslims break their fast as soon as the call to *Maghrib* (sunset) prayer is announced, and many Muslims are very keen to share their Ramadaan breakfast, or *iftar*, with fellow Muslims.**

passages.heading: When do I have to perform wudoo’ again?
passages.text: If a Muslim performs wudoo’, the general rule is that his wudoo’ is still valid unless one of the previously-mentioned things that break wudoo’ happens, in which case he must perform it again.

passages.heading: The Types of People Who Are Exempt from Fasting
passages.text:
Allah Almighty has permitted several types of people to break their fast during the day in Ramadaan. They are:

1. Sick people whose medical condition is bound to be further worsened by fasting.
2. The elderly who are unable to fast.
3. Travellers, while moving from one place to another.
4. Menstruating women and women experiencing postnatal bleeding.
5. Pregnant and nursing mothers if they fear it would be dangerous for them or for their babies if they fast.

passages.heading: Things that render the Fast Invalid
passages.text:
The fasting person must abstain from several things which, if he does them, his fast will be invalid. They are:

1. Eating and drinking, including intravenous injections which have some nutritional value.
2. Deliberate seminal emission as a result of intercourse or any other means. Intercourse during the day in Ramadaan is a grave sin.
3. Deliberate vomiting.

A woman’s fast is broken as a result of:

4. Menstrual or postnatal bleeding.

passages.text:

passages.heading: The Blessed Month of Ramadaan
passages.text:
Ramadaan is the ninth month of the Islamic lunar calendar. It is a blessed month, in which Allah revealed the Qur’an to His Messenger, Muhammad ﷺ. Allah has promised to forgive all the past sins of those who fast during the daylight hours and stands in prayer at night throughout this month. The Almighty has also distinguished it with a night that is better than a thousand months. It is called *Laylat-ul-Qadr* (The Night of Decree; also called the Night of Power), and whoever spends it remembering Allah and standing in prayer will have all his past sins forgiven.

Muslims perform the *Taraaweeh* prayer in the month of Ramadaan. It is one of the Prophet’s practices (*Sunnah*) that is particularly associated with it, and it is performed after *'Ishaa’* (late evening) prayer.

2. He washes his hands up to the wrists with water.
3. He rinses out his mouth thoroughly by moving water around in the mouth and then spitting it out. This process is called *madmadah*) in Arabic.
4. He cleans his nose by sniffing water into the nostrils and ejecting it out by blowing his nose.
5. He washes his face thoroughly from the hairline at the top of the forehead to the bottom of the chin, along with the beard, if he is bearded, and from ear to ear.
6. He washes his hands from the fingertips up to the elbow, starting with his right hand.
7. With wet hands, and starting with his hands flat on the top of the head near the hairline, he wipes it to the back of the neck and back to the front.

He wipes the inner sides of the ears with his index fingers and behind them with his thumbs.
9. He washes his feet up to the ankles, which are the two prominent bones of the joint connecting the foot to the leg, starting with his right foot.

passages.text:
*Soorat Al-Kawthar* **Explained**

{{Q:108:1-3}}

“We have bestowed on you abundant good”

We have given you, Messenger, immeasurable, abundant good in this life and the life to come, part of which is River Al-Kawthar in Paradise.

“So pray to your Lord and sacrifice to Him”

Therefore, sincerely pray to your Lord and worship Him alone, and sacrifice to Him, pronouncing Allah’s name alone when slaughtering animals, in gratitude to Him for the honour and good He has bestowed on you.

“He who hates you is the one who is truly cut off”

passages.heading: What is *Hajj*?
passages.text:
*Hajj* is an act of worship for which physically and financially able Muslims travel to Makkah to perform certain acts of worship during the month of Dhul-Hijjah, which is the last month of the lunar calendar.

*Hajj* is the fifth pillar of Islam

The Islamic *Hijri* Calendar is a lunar calendar is associated with the Prophet’s migration, or *hijrah*, from Makkah to Madeenah. Third Rightly-Guided Caliph ‘Umar ibn Al-Khattaab, may Allah be pleased with him, decided that the most appropriate reference point for the Islamic calendar would be the Prophet’s *hijrah*. The Islamic Calendar has twelve months, beginning with the month of Muharram and ending with the month of Dhul-Hijjah. Muslims have adopted the Islamic *Hijri* calendar to date incidents and events.

passages.heading: The Blessed Month of Ramadaan
passages.text:
Ramadaan is the ninth month of the Islamic lunar calendar. It is a blessed month, in which Allah revealed the Qur’an to His Messenger, Muhammad ﷺ. Allah has promised to forgive all the past sins of those who fast during the daylight hours and stands in prayer at night throughout this month. The Almighty has also distinguished it with a night that is better than a thousand months. It is called *Laylat-ul-Qadr* (The Night of Decree; also called the Night of Power), and whoever spends it remembering Allah and standing in prayer will have all his past sins forgiven.

Muslims perform the *Taraaweeh* prayer in the month of Ramadaan. It is one of the Prophet’s practices (*Sunnah*) that is particularly associated with it, and it is performed after *'Ishaa’* (late evening) prayer.

passages.heading: What Is Fasting?
passages.text:
Fasting: an act of worship whereby a Muslim abstains from food, drink and sexual intercourse from dawn to sunset.

Fasting in the month of Ramadaan is the fourth pillar of Islam.

passages.heading: Important Notes Related to Fasting
passages.text:
- Whoever breaks his fast in Ramadaan for a legitimate reason must make up for every day he has missed after than Ramadaan.
- If a sick person breaks the fast because of an incurable disease, he is exempt from fasting the month of Ramadaan, but he must feed one poor person for each day he does not fast.
- If a Muslim cannot possibly fast due to old age, he is exempt from fasting the month of Ramadaan but he must feed one poor person for each day he does not fast.

**Muslims break their fast as soon as the call to *Maghrib* (sunset) prayer is announced, and many Muslims are very keen to share their Ramadaan breakfast, or *iftar*, with fellow Muslims.**

passages.heading: The Pillars of Islam
passages.text:
Islam is built on five pillars:

Every Muslim must strictly adhere to these pillars to ensure he is practising Islam in full; negligence in one of these pillars is bound to render the way you practise Islam deficient.

1. The two testimonies of faith: To bear witness that none is worthy of worship except Allah and that Muhammad is His His Messenger
2. Establish the prayer: A Muslim must pray five times a day. These prayers will be explained in due course.
3. Paying zakaat
4. Fasting in the month of Ramadaan
5. Making the pilgrimage to Allah’s House

passages.heading: Why Do We Fast?
passages.text: Muslims fast in obedience to Allah Almighty and in response to His command.

passages.heading: Introduction
passages.text: Islam is the religion with which Allah sent Muhammad ﷺ and is an extension of the same religion with which all the previous messengers came. It is essentially based on the belief that Allah Almighty is the only deity deserving of worship, who has no partners or assistants whatsoever in His kingdom, and who has no intermediaries between Him and His servants. But why should I embrace Islam? Is it a religion for all people or is it only for the Arabs? Who is its prophet, and is there another prophet who will come after him?

passages.heading: Why Should I Embrace Islam?
passages.text:
Some people may ask: Why should I embrace Islam?

The answer is: I must do so for a number of reasons, including the following:

1. Islam is the religion that Allah has approved and chosen for His servants and will not accept any other religion. The Almighty says, {{Q:3:85}} (Soorat Aal-’Imraan, 3:85).

2. Islam is the religion of all the prophets and commands its adherents to believe in all of them without exception. Allah says, {{Q:2:136}} (Soorat Al-Baqarah, 2:136).
The difference between prophets lies only in the laws relating to people’s actions, as the Almighty says, {{Q:5:48}} (Soorat Al-Maa’idah, 5:48) That is, for each nation before Islam, Allah appointed a law to which people referred for their disputes and a way of life whereby they drew near to Him. Thus, followers of every prophet had their respective laws and regulations, but the set of beliefs to which prophets called their people was the same. Then Allah sent the last prophet and messenger, Muhammad ﷺ, with the final divine laws, and thus the only religion acceptable to Allah is Islam.

passages.heading: Introduction
passages.text: *Hajj*, the annual Muslim pilgrimage to Makkah, is one of the pillars of Islam and one of the best deeds whereby Muslims seek to draw closer to Allah Almighty. Its virtues are mentioned in numerous traditions of the Prophet ﷺ. In this lesson, we are going to learn a little information about this great act of worship.

passages.heading: Why Do We Perform *Hajj*?
passages.text: Muslims perform *Hajj* to the Sacred House in Makkah in response to Allah’s command to do so.

passages.heading: Some of the Ultimate Objectives and Benefits of *Hajj*
passages.text:
- To follow the example of the honourable prophets who made the pilgrimage to the Sacred House.
- To occupy oneself with worship: Pilgrims devote themselves to the worship of Allah, moving from one act of worship to another.
- To meet Muslims who come from the four corners of the world and gather in the holy sites, get to know them and build bridges of communication with them.

2. Deliberate seminal emission as a result of intercourse or any other means. Intercourse during the day in Ramadaan is a grave sin.
3. Deliberate vomiting.

A woman’s fast is broken as a result of:

4. Menstrual or postnatal bleeding.

passages.heading: The Types of People Who Are Exempt from Fasting
passages.text:
Allah Almighty has permitted several types of people to break their fast during the day in Ramadaan. They are:

1. Sick people whose medical condition is bound to be further worsened by fasting.
2. The elderly who are unable to fast.
3. Travellers, while moving from one place to another.
4. Menstruating women and women experiencing postnatal bleeding.
5. Pregnant and nursing mothers if they fear it would be dangerous for them or for their babies if they fast.

passages.text:

While men support the family as a matter of religious obligation, women are not obliged to spend anything at all.
- It has established total equality between men and women in numerous matters including financial transactions.
- It has granted them the right to choose their own husbands.
- It has granted them the right to retain their maiden names. In Islam, a woman does not change her surname to that of her husband upon marriage; rather, she retains her maiden name, and thus her independent personality.
- It has made it the husband’s duty to spend on those women entitled to his support, such as his wife, mother and daughters, without attempting in the least to remind them of his favours.
- It stresses the importance of helping weak and vulnerable women who are in need of support, even if they are not one’s relatives, and urges its adherents to engage in such a noble act, which it considers one of the meritorious deeds in the sight of Allah.

passages.heading: The Conditions of the Prayer
passages.text:
- Purity: Once’s body and the place where the prayer is to be performed must be cleansed from physical impurities, and any ritual impurity must be removed with *wudoo’* or *ghusl*.
- Covering the intimate parts of the body (*‘awrah*): The word *‘awrah* refers to the parts of the body that must be covered in front of people. A man’s *‘awrah* that must be covered during the prayer extends from the navel to the knees; a woman’s *‘awrah* that must be covered during the prayer is her entire body except for the face and hands.
- Facing the *qiblah*: The *qiblah* is the direction of the Ka‘bah in Makkah. One must, therefore, pray in the direction of the Ka‘bah in Makkah.
- When its appointed time becomes due: The prayer will not be valid if it is performed before its time has started. It is not permissible to delay it beyond its due time, and it is best to perform it at the beginning of its time.

passages.heading: The Five Obligatory Prayers
passages.text:
Allah Almighty has enjoined Muslims to perform five prayers throughout the day and night, namely:

| The Prayer | Beginning Time | Ending Time | Number of units (*rak‘ahs*) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| *Fajr* (Dawn) Prayer | at the break of dawn | sunrise | 2 |
| *Dhuhr* (Midday) Prayer | when the sun starts declining westward at midday after reaching its zenith | when the shadow of an object becomes equal in length to the object itself | 4 |
| *‘Asr* (Late Afternoon) Prayer | when the shadow of an object becomes equal in length to the object itself | sunset | 4 |
| *Maghrib* (Sunset) Prayer | sunset | when the red glow (evening twilight) on the western horizon disappears | 3 |
| *‘Ishaa’* (Late Evening) Prayer | when the red glow (evening twilight) on the western horizon disappears | midnight | 4 |

passages.heading: How Do We Pray?
passages.text:
1. He intends in his heart to pray.
2. He stands facing the *qiblah*, raises his hands up to the level of the shoulders or ears, and says, “*Allaahu akbar* Allah is the Greatest.”
3. He places his right hand on his left hand. Then he recites one of the opening supplications, such as, Subhaanak-Allaahumma wa bi hamdika, wa tabaarak-asmuka, wa ta’aalaa jadduka, wa laa ilaaha ghayruka “Glory be to You, O Allah; Yours is the praise, blessed is Your name, exalted is Your majesty, and there is no god besides You.” Then he says, A’oodhu billaahi min-ash-shaytaan-ir-rajeem. Bismillaah-ir-rahmaan-ir-raheem “I seek Allah’s protection from Satan, who has been expelled from His mercy. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.” Then he recites *Soorat Al-Faatihah* and says after it, “*Aameen*”, which means “Answer our supplications, O Allah”. After that, he recites whatever number of verses of the Qur’an as is easy for him, even if it is one verse.
4. He says, “Allaahu akbar Allah is the Greatest” while raising his hands up to the level of his shoulders or ears, and bows down, lowering his head and back and keeping them straight at a right angle, placing the palms of his hands on the knees. He says three times while in this position, “Subhaana rabbiy-al-’adheem Glory be to my Lord, the Almighty.”

5. He resumes the standing position, raising his hands up to the level of the shoulders or the ears, saying: Sami’allaahu li man hamidah “Allah hears those who praise Him.” Then he says while standing: Rabbanaa wa lakal-hamd “Our Lord, to You is due all praise.”

6. He says, Allaahu akbar “Allah is the Greatest” and prostrates himself, with the toes of both feet, the knees, the palms of the hands and the forehead and the nose touching the floor. He says three times while in this position, “Glory be to my Lord, Most High.”

With your partners, discuss the reasons why some types of clothing are forbidden in Islam.

The Prophet ﷺ forbade men from imitating women and women from imitating men. This prohibition includes the type of clothing and the manner of speech. Islam strictly forbids imitation of the opposite sex, considering it a major sin that invites Allah’s punishment unless one repents and desists from committing it. Islam enjoins men to ensure that their true nature and appearance are distinct from that of women, and vice versa, which clearly testifies to common sense and sound logic.

passages.heading: Good Moral Character in Islam
passages.text:
- Good moral character occupies a lofty position in Islam, as it is one of the important objectives of *Sharee‘ah* and one of the goals behind the Prophet’s mission.
- Good moral character is closely linked to faith, and the believers with complete faith are those who demonstrate the best moral character.

passages.heading: Some Virtues of Good Moral Character
passages.text:
- The Prophet ﷺ informs us that the act that will cause people to enter Paradise the most will be piety and good character.
- He ﷺ states that the heaviest of a person’s good deeds that will be placed on the scales of deeds on the Day of Resurrection will be good moral character.
- He ﷺ further states that the closest believers to him on the Day of Resurrection will be those who possess good moral character.

> **The scales of deeds:** This will be on the Day of Resurrection when a person’s good and bad deeds will be weighed in a balance, whose shape or size none knows but Allah. Those whose good deeds outweigh their bad deeds will be admitted into Paradise, but those whose bad deeds outweigh their bad deeds will be sent to Hell.

passages.heading: Regras do período menstrual ou pós-parto
passages.text:
ALLAH Todo-Poderoso prescreveu várias regras para a menstruação e pós-parto, incluindo:

- A retirada das orações, portanto, elas não são obrigadas a orar durante a menstruação e o sangramento pós-parto, e não precisam compensar a oração após o término da menstruação e do sangramento pós-parto.
- Abandonar o jejum, não é permitido que jejuem durante a menstruação e no período pós-parto, mas devem compensar o jejum dos dias em que não jejuaram no Ramadan.
- Proibição de relações sexuais: O marido não pode ter relações sexuais com sua esposa menstruada ou no pós-parto até que ela tome um banho completo após o término da menstruação e sangramento pós-parto, e o marido acaricia-la sem que haja relação sexual pela vagina.
- Ghussl depois que cessar o sangramento. Se o sangramento da mulher menstruada ou pós-parto cessar, ela deve fazer ghussl como mencionado anteriormente.

É permitido que elas saiam na frente de seus mahrams com seus adornos que mostram os braços, pescoço, cabelos, e assim por diante, sem culpa ou excessos.

passages.heading: O véu da mulher muçulmana:
passages.text: ALLAH impôs o véu à mulher, não ao homem, por causa da beleza e dos fatores sedutores que estão depositados nela, o que faz dela uma tentação para o homem mais do que um homem seja uma tentação para ela. Os limites deste véu são cobrir todo o seu corpo de homens estranhos, e ela pode usar as formas e cores que quiser, respeitando quatro condições:

passages.heading: A segunda:
passages.text: Deve ser solta e larga, e não estreita, definindo as partes do corpo.

passages.heading: A relação de uma mulher com um homem:
passages.text: O relacionamento de uma mulher com um homem é dividido em três partes:

7. Ele levanta a cabeça dizendo: “ALLAH é O Maior” e se senta sobre o pé esquerdo, com o pé direito ainda ereto, e coloca as palmas das mãos sobre as coxas, e diz sentado: “Senhor, perdoa-me”.

8. Prostra-se novamente como na primeira prostração, e enquanto se inclina para a prostração, ele diz: “ALLAH é o Maior››. E faz na segunda prostração o que fez na primeira.

9. Ele levanta a cabeça e representa a segunda rak›ah, dizendo: «ALLAH é o Maior». E ele reza a segunda rak›ah exatamente como ele rezou a primeira rak›ah.

passages.heading: Sexta lição
passages.text:
11. Ele se vira para a direita e diz: “A paz e a misericórdia de ALLAH esteja convosco.” Então ele se vira para a esquerda e diz o mesmo. Assim termina sua oração.

Esta característica é se sua oração for de duas rak’ahs. como Fajr e sexta-feira, mas se for três rak’ahs; como Maghrib, ou quatro rak’ahs; Como Zuhr, Asr e Isha, depois de completar o primeiro tashahhud, ele completa as rak’ahs restantes como na primeira rak’ah, exceto que ele não recita nada depois de al-Fatihah, então se senta como sentou após a segunda rak’ah, e diz o primeiro tashahhud, então a oração abraâmica, e então dá as saudações.

passages.heading: Oração de Sexta-Feira (al-jumah)
passages.text:
- ALLAH Todo-Poderoso ordenou aos muçulmanos que fizessem uma oração especial na sexta-feira chamada (oração de sexta-feira), e tem um caráter especial e condições especiais, e é uma alternativa à oração do meio-dia para esse dia.
- Os muçulmanos se reúnem para isso na mesquita, então o pregador da mesquita faz dois sermões para eles, então reza com eles duas unidades de oração, nas quais ele recita o Alcorão em voz alta.
- Prescreve-se tomar banho para assistir à oração de sexta-feira e comparecer cedo. Não é permitido ausentar-se dela exceto por uma desculpa, e quem não o fizer deve fazer a oração do meio-dia quatro unidades de oração, durante as quais a recitação do Alcorão não é em voz alta.
- A oração de sexta-feira não é obrigatório para a mulher ou o viajante.

passages.heading: Discuta
passages.text:
Revise com seus colegas alguns dos desafios enfrentados pelo muçulmano que o impedem de realizar a oração na hora certa e como esses desafios são superados.

{{Q:62:9}} Al-Jumah:9

passages.heading: Terceiro:
passages.text: Não deve ser transparente para que as partes do corpo fiquem visíveis por fora.

passages.heading: O quarto:
passages.text: Não deve ser um adorno em si mesmo.

passages.heading: O lugar da mulher no Islam:
passages.text: Exemplos de disposições relacionadas ao respeito às mulheres no Islam:

passages.heading: Quinta lição
passages.text: ## REGRAS ESPECÍFICAS PARA A MULHER MUÇULMANA

passages.heading: Discuta
passages.text: Revisar algumas das decisões extraídas da retirada de alguns deveres legais sobre as mulheres?

Uma mulher muçulmana deve cobrir todo o seu corpo de:
a) outras mulheres.
b) Homens estranhos.
c) O sogro.

Quando a mulher menstruada ou no pós-parto se torna pura, ela deve repor:
a) A oração
b) O jejum
c) Tudo que precedeu

passages.heading: تمهيد
passages.text: يُعد الحج أحد أركان الإسلام، وهو من أفضل الأعمال التي يتقرَّب بها المسلم إلى الله عز وجل، وقد ورد في فضله أحاديث كثيرة عن الرسول ﷺ، وفي هذا الدرس سنتعرف على معلومات يسيرة عن هذه الشعيرة العظيمة.

passages.heading: مكانة المرأة في الإسلام:
passages.text:
من أمثلة الأحكام المتعلقة باحترام المرأة في الإسلام:
- أعطى الإسلام المرأة حقها من الميراث في قسمة عادلة كريمة، تساوي الرجل بالمرأة في مواضع، ويختلف نصيبها عنه في مواضع، بحسب قرابتها وتكاليف النفقة المناطة بها.
- ساوى بين الرجل والمرأة في شؤون كثيرة مختلفة ومن ذلك جميع التعاملات المالية..
- أعطى المرأة حرية اختيار الزوج.
- أبقى لها اسمها وشرف انتسابها لأبيها، فلا تتغير نسبتها بعد الزواج، بل تبقى منتسبة لأبيها وعائلتها.
- أوجب على الرجل رعايتها والإنفاق عليها بدون منّة إن كانت ممن تجب نفقته كالزوجة والأم والبنت.
- أكد على شرف وفضل خدمة المرأة الضعيفة التي ليس لها أحد، ولو لم تكن من الأقارب، ورغب في السعي لخدمتها وجعل ذلك من أفضل الأعمال عند الله.

passages.heading: مذكرتي
passages.text: دوّن بعض ثمرات الإيمان التي شعرت بها بعد دخولك في الإسلام:

passages.heading: الدرس الأول
passages.text: ## الإسلام والأسئلة الكبرى

passages.heading: تمهيد
passages.text:
الإسلام: هو الدين الذي بعث الله به محمدًا ﷺ، وهو امتدادٌ لما جاء به الرسل السابقون.
وأساسه قائمٌ على أن الإله المستحق للعبادة واحدٌ لا شريك له، وهو الله جلّ وعلا، ولا معين له في ملكه، ولا وسيط بينه وبين عباده، ولكن لماذا علي أن أعتنق الإسلام؟ وهل هو دين للناس كافة أم خاص بالعرب؟ ومن هو نبيه؟ وهل هناك نبي آخر سيأتي بعده؟

passages.heading: من خصائص الإسلام:
passages.text: يتميز الإسلام عن باقي الديانات بخصائص تجعل منه الدين الحق، وأبرز هذه الخصائص:

passages.heading: ٢ الإسلام يكفّر ما سبقه من الذنوب
passages.text:
إذا أسلم العبد، وفعل ما يجب عليه من الواجبات، واجتنب ما حرّم الله عليه، فإن الله تعالى يغفر له ما تقدّم من ذنوبه قبل إسلامه، وقد قال النبي ﷺ: « إذا أسلم العبد فحسن إسلامه، يكفر الله عنه كل سيئة كان زلفها، وكان بعد ذلك القصاص: الحسنة بعشر أمثالها إلى سبع مائة ضعف، والسيئة بمثلها إلا أن يتجاوز الله عنها ». أخرجه البخاري (٤١).

وقد سأل رجل النبي ﷺ: يا رسول الله، أنؤاخذ بما عملنا في الجاهلية؟ فأجابه النبي ﷺ: «من أحسن في الإسلام لم يؤاخذ بما عمل في الجاهلية، ومن أساء في الإسلام أُخذ بالأول والآخر». أخرجه البخاري (٦٩٢١).

passages.heading: الأخلاق في الإسلام:
passages.text:
- الأخلاق الحسنة لها مكانة عظيمة في الإسلام، فهي مقصد مهم من مقاصد الشرعية الإسلامية، وهدف من أهداف بعثة النبي ﷺ.
- الأخلاق لها ارتباط وثيق بالإيمان، فأكمل المؤمنين إيمانًا أحسنهم أخلاقًا.
- يؤجر العبد على حسن خلقه، كما يؤجر على الصلاة والصوم.

passages.heading: ما هو الحج؟
passages.text:
الحج: عبادة يذهب لأجلها المسلم المستطيع إلى مكة المكرمة للقيام بعبادات معينة في شهر ذي الحجة، وهو الشهر الأخير من السنة الهجرية.

والحج هو الركن الخامس من أركان الإسلام.

السنة الهجرية: هي إشارةٌ إلى الهجرة النبوية المباركة من مكة المكرمة إلى المدينة النبوية، وقد اختار الخليفة عمر بن الخطاب ؓ يوم هجرة الرسول ﷺ ليكون بداية لحساب التاريخ الإسلامي الهجري. وللسنة الهجرية إثنا عشر شهر تبدء بشهر (محرم) وتنتهي بشهر (ذي الحجة)، وقد اعتمد المسلمون التأريخ للحوادث والوقائع بالسنة الهجرية منذ السنة الأولى للهجرة والتي تقابلها سنة ٦٢٢ ميلادية.

passages.heading: لماذا نحج؟
passages.text:
يحجّ المسلم إلى مكة المكرمة:

- استجابة لنداء الله تعالى بالحج إلى البيت الحرام.
- اهتداء بالأنبياء الكرام الذين حجّوا إلى البيت الحرام، وعلى رأسهم إبراهيم عليه السلام.
- الانشغال بالعبادة، فالحاج يمكث أيامًا متفرغًا للعبادة، ينتقل من عبادة إلى أخرى.
- الالتقاء بالمسلمين المجتمعين في المشاعر المقدسة، والتعرف عليهم، وبناء جسور التواصل معهم.

passages.heading: ناقش
passages.text: يحتاج وضع موضوع مناسب للنقاش:

passages.heading: تمهيد
passages.text: خص الله عز وجل المرأة ببعض الصفات والخصائص التي تميزها عن الرجل، كما أوجب عليها بعض العبادات دون الرجل، وفي هذا الدرس سنتعرف على بعض الأحكام التي تخص المرأة المسلمة.

passages.heading: الدرس الخامس
passages.text: ## أحكام تخص المرأة المسلمة

passages.heading: علاقة المرأة بالرجل:
passages.text: تنقسم علاقة المرأة بالنسبة للرجل إلى ثلاثة أقسام:

passages.heading: ثمرات الإيمان:
passages.text:
للإيمان ثمرات كثيرة، منها:

- اطمئنان النفس: فالإيمان يجعل نفس المؤمن مطمئنة، راضية بالله وبقدره، لا تخاف إلا الله.
- معرفة الله تعالى: فيعرف المؤمن ربه معرفة تزيد من تعلّقه بربه، فيعرف أسماءه وصفاته وأفعاله.
- تعظيم الله: فالمؤمن كلّما عرفة ربه زاد له تعظيمًا وإجلالاً، وازداد له حبًا ورجاءً، وازداد منه خوفًا وخشية.
- العلم بحرص الله على هداية عباده: فقد أرسل إليهم الرسل وأنزل عليهم الكتب؛ ليهتدوا إلى الدين الحق.
- محبة الملائكة: لإعبادتهم لله، وطاعتهم له.
- محبة الرسل: فقد اصطفاهم الله تعالى لتبليغ رسالته للناس.
- الاجتهاد في العبادة: فكلما قوي الإيمان زادت عبادة الإنسان.
- الحياة الطيبة: فهو راضٍ بما قسمه الله له، ويعلم أن ما يصيبه في الدنيا من المصائب فهو رفعةٌ لدرجات، وتكفيرٌ لسيئاته، متأملًا لما أعدّه الله في الآخرة.
- عدم الاغترار بالدنيا: فالحياة الدنيا مؤقتة، وهي طريق إلى الحياة الأبدية في الآخرة.
- كشف الخرافات: فالإيمان يفضح كثيرًا من تلك الخرافات ويبطلها.
- دخول الجنة: فهي دار النعيم الدائم الذي لا ينقطع، وقد خصصها الله تعالى للمؤمنين من عباده.

passages.heading: تمهيد
passages.text:
تراود البشر أسئلة تتعلق بوجود الإنسان، فيتساءلون عن حقيقة أمرهم، وعن مصدر مجيئهم، وسببه، وعن منتهى أمرهم.

وقد أجاب الإسلام عن هذه التساؤلات بإجابات شافية:

passages.heading: من نحن؟
passages.text:
يعرّف الإسلام الإنسان بأنه مخلوق من مخلوقات الله تعالى الكثيرة، فضّله تعالى على كثيرٍ من المخلوقات، وسخّـر له كثيرًا من المخلوقات ليستعين بها على أداء مهامه المطلوبة منه مدة حياته. قال تعالى: {{Q:17:70}} (الإسراء: ٧٠).

وجعل الله تعالى في الإنسان شبهًا من:
- الملائكة في طهارتها وعبادتها.
- والشياطين في جحودها وعصيانها.
- والحيوانات في إشباعها لنزواتها وشهواتها.

> الملائكة: خلق من خلق الله تعالى، خلقهم الله عز وجل من نور، مربوبون مسخرون، عباد مكرمون، لا يعصون الله ما أمرهم ويفعلون ما يؤمرون، ولا يعلم عددهم إلا الله

وجعل فيه استعدادًا للخير، واستعدادًا للشر، وأعطاه ما يميّز به الخير من الشر؛ كالفطرة والعقل والحواس الخمسة.

وجعله حرًّا مختارًا مسؤولًا عن اختياراته وأعماله.

passages.heading: من أين جئنا؟
passages.text:
حكى الله لنا في القرآن قصة خلقه وكيف بدأ الشيطان في معاداته، أنظر تفسير سورة البقرة للآيات (٣٠-٣٩).

يبين الإسلام أن أصل خلق الإنسان من طين هذه الأرض، خلق الله منها آدم، وهو أبو البشر جميعًا، قال تعالى: {{Q:23:12}} (المؤمنون: ١٢).

والغاية من خلق هذا الإنسان عبادة الله تعالى، مع غناه سبحانه عن خلقه، قال تعالى: {{Q:51:56}} (الذاريات: ٥٦).

وهناك غاية أخرى فرعية، وهي عمارة هذه الأرض بإصلاحها، وإقامة العدل فيها، ونشر الخير، قال تعالى: {{Q:55:26}} (الرحمن: ٢٦).

passages.heading: لماذا أسلم؟
passages.text:
قد يتساءل بعض الناس: لماذا يجب عليّ أن أسلم؟

والجواب: يجب أن أسلم لأمور منها:

الأول: أن دين الإسلام هو الدين الذي ارتضاه الله لعباده، ولا يقبل من أحدٍ دين سواه، قال تعالى: {{Q:3:85}} (آل عمران:٨٥).

الثاني: أن دين الإسلام هو دين الأنبياء جميعًا، ويأمر بالإيمان بالأنبياء جميعًا، ولا يفرّق بينهم؛ لأنه دينهم جميعًا.

قال الله تعالى: {{Q:2:136}} (البقرة:١٣٦).

والاختلاف بين الأنبياء هو اختلاف في الأحكام التشريعية المتعلقة بأفعال العباد، كما قال سبحانه: {{Q:5:48}} (المائدة:٤٨). أي: جعل الله لكل أمةٍ من الأمم شريعةً يحتكمون إليها، وطريقًا يتقربون بها إليه، فلكل أهل ملة أحكامٌ تخصهم، وتشريعات تناسبهم.

ثم بعث الله خاتم أنبيائه ورسله محمدًا ﷺ فختم به الرسل، وختم بشريعته الشرائع، فلا يقبل من أحد دين غير الإسلام.

الثالث: أن الدخول في الإسلام سبيل النجاة في الآخرة فلا ينجو في الآخرة أحد بلغته إلا من آمن به واتبعه، قال تعالى: {{Q:3:85}} (آل عمران:٨٥)، وقال ﷺ: «وَالَّذِي نَفْسُ مُحَمَّدٍ بِيَدِهِ، لَا يَسْمَعُ بِي أَحَدٌ مِنْ هَذِهِ الْأُمَّةِ يَهُودِيٌّ وَلَا نَصْرَانِيٌّ، ثُمَّ يَمُوتُ، وَلَمْ يُؤْمِنْ بِالَّذِي أُرْسِلْتُ بِهِ إِلَّا كَانَ مِنْ أَصْحَابِ النَّارِ».

passages.heading: ناقش
passages.text: كيف يكون الإسلام دين جميع الأنبياء؟

passages.heading: فائدة
passages.text: يحترم الإسلام عادات الشعوب وتقاليدهم ولا يلزمهم بتغييرها إلا إذا خالفت شيئًا من شعائر الإسلام وتعاليمه.

passages.heading: ٣ الإسلام الدين الخاتم
passages.text: جعل الله تعالى الإسلام امتدادًا للشرائع السماويّة السابقة، وارتضاه دينًا للخَلق جميعًا إلى قيام الساعة، فلا يوجد على وجه الأرض دينٌ حقٌّ سوى دين الإسلام؛ قال تعالى: {{Q:3:85}} (آل عمران:٨٥).

passages.heading: ناقش
passages.text: كيف ترد على من يزعم أن الإسلام دين خاص بالعرب؟

passages.heading: من هو نبي الإسلام؟
passages.text: يعتقد المسلم أن محمد ﷺ هو خاتم النبيين الذين بعثهم الله إلى الناس لدعوتهم إلى عبادته وحده دون سواه، وأنه لا نبي بعده؛ قال الله - تعالى -: {{Q:33:40}} (الأحزاب : ٤٠)

passages.heading: مكانة المرأة في الإسلام:
passages.text:
من أمثلة الأحكام المتعلقة باحترام المرأة في الإسلام:
- أعطى الإسلام المرأة حقها من الميراث في قسمة عادلة كريمة، تساوي الرجل بالمرأة في مواضع، ويختلف نصيبها عنه في مواضع، بحسب قرابتها وتكاليف النفقة المناطة بها.
- ساوى بين الرجل والمرأة في شؤون كثيرة مختلفة ومن ذلك جميع التعاملات المالية..
- أعطى المرأة حرية اختيار الزوج.
- أبقى لها اسمها وشرف انتسابها لأبيها، فلا تتغير نسبتها بعد الزواج، بل تبقى منتسبة لأبيها وعائلتها.
- أوجب على الرجل رعايتها والإنفاق عليها بدون منّة إن كانت ممن تجب نفقته كالزوجة والأم والبنت.
- أكد على شرف وفضل خدمة المرأة الضعيفة التي ليس لها أحد، ولو لم تكن من الأقارب، ورغب في السعي لخدمتها وجعل ذلك من أفضل الأعمال عند الله.

passages.heading: معنى السورة:
تمهيد
passages.text:
الإسلام: هو الدين الذي بعث الله به محمدًا ﷺ، وهو امتدادٌ لما جاء به الرسل السابقون.
وأساسه قائمٌ على أن الإله المستحق للعبادة واحدٌ لا شريك له، وهو الله جلّ وعلا، ولا معين له في ملكه، ولا وسيط بينه وبين عباده، ولكن لماذا علي أن أعتنق الإسلام؟ وهل هو دين للناس كافة أم خاص بالعرب؟ ومن هو نبيه؟ وهل هناك نبي آخر سيأتي بعده؟

passages.heading: فضل قراءة القرآن:
passages.text:
- قال النبي ﷺ: «من قرأ حرفًا من كتاب الله فله به حسنة، والحسنة بعشر أمثالها، لا أقول: ﴿الم﴾ حرف، ولكن ألف حرف، ولام حرف، وميم حرف». أخرجه الترمذي في سننه (رقم 2910) بإسناد صحيح
- وقال النبي ﷺ: «اقرءوا القرآن، فإنه يأتي يوم القيامة شفيعًا لأصحابه». أخرجه مسلم في صحيحه (رقم 804)

ناقش

passages.heading: معنى السورة:
تعلم الدين:
passages.text:
- الواجب على المسلم أن يتعلّم من أمر دينه ما يحتاج إليه، حتى يعبد ربه على علم.
- رغّب النبي ﷺ في التفقّه في الدين فقال: «من يرد الله به خيرًا يفقهه في الدين». أخرجه البخاري (٧١).
- أخبر النبي ﷺ أن طلب العلم الشرعي طريقٌ لدخول الجنة، فقال ﷺ: «من سلك طريقًا يلتمس فيه علمًا، سهل الله له به طريقًا إلى الجنة». أخرجه مسلم (٢٦٩٩).

تتوفر العديد من الكتب التي يستطيع المسلم أن يتعلم منها أحكام دينه حتى يعبد ربه على بصيرة، وعليه بالاستعانة بالمختصين لإرشاده إلى أفضل هذه الكتب.

ناقش

passages.heading: لماذا أسلم؟
passages.text:
قد يتساءل بعض الناس: لماذا يجب عليّ أن أسلم؟

والجواب: يجب أن أسلم لأمور منها:

الأول: أن دين الإسلام هو الدين الذي ارتضاه الله لعباده، ولا يقبل من أحدٍ دين سواه، قال تعالى: {{Q:3:85}} (آل عمران:٨٥).

الثاني: أن دين الإسلام هو دين الأنبياء جميعًا، ويأمر بالإيمان بالأنبياء جميعًا، ولا يفرّق بينهم؛ لأنه دينهم جميعًا.

قال الله تعالى: {{Q:2:136}} (البقرة:١٣٦).

والاختلاف بين الأنبياء هو اختلاف في الأحكام التشريعية المتعلقة بأفعال العباد، كما قال سبحانه: {{Q:5:48}} (المائدة:٤٨). أي: جعل الله لكل أمةٍ من الأمم شريعةً يحتكمون إليها، وطريقًا يتقربون بها إليه، فلكل أهل ملة أحكامٌ تخصهم، وتشريعات تناسبهم.

ثم بعث الله خاتم أنبيائه ورسله محمدًا ﷺ فختم به الرسل، وختم بشريعته الشرائع، فلا يقبل من أحد دين غير الإسلام.

الثالث: أن الدخول في الإسلام سبيل النجاة في الآخرة فلا ينجو في الآخرة أحد بلغته إلا من آمن به واتبعه، قال تعالى: {{Q:3:85}} (آل عمران:٨٥)، وقال ﷺ: «وَالَّذِي نَفْسُ مُحَمَّدٍ بِيَدِهِ، لَا يَسْمَعُ بِي أَحَدٌ مِنْ هَذِهِ الْأُمَّةِ يَهُودِيٌّ وَلَا نَصْرَانِيٌّ، ثُمَّ يَمُوتُ، وَلَمْ يُؤْمِنْ بِالَّذِي أُرْسِلْتُ بِهِ إِلَّا كَانَ مِنْ أَصْحَابِ النَّارِ».

passages.heading: ناقش
passages.text: كيف يكون الإسلام دين جميع الأنبياء؟

passages.heading: ما القرآن؟
passages.text:
القرآن الكريم كلام الله تعالى الذي أنزله على رسوله محمد ﷺ وهو آخر كتب الله المنزلة، وليس بعده كتاب آخر.

الكتب المنزلة: هي الكتب التي أنزلها الله سبحانه وتعالى على أنبيائه، ويؤمن المسلم بهذه الكتب وأنها منزلة من عند الله تعالى، وأن الله تكلّم بما فيها بما يليق به سبحانه، ومن هذه الكتب: الزبور الذي أُنزل على داوود عليه السلام، والتوراة التي أُنزلت على موسى عليه السلام، والإنجيل المنزل على عيسى عليه السلام، وقد اعترى هذه الكتب تحريف وتبديل على مر العصور.

passages.heading: القرآن غذاء الروح والعقل:
passages.text:
خاطب القرآن الكريم عقول البشر وأرواحهم على حدّ سواء، فهو يخاطب العقل من خلال:

- الاستدلال العقلي على القضايا، قال تعالى: {{Q:21:22}} (الأنبياء: ٢٢).
- الدعوة إلى إعمال العقل والتفكر في الأدلة والبراهين، قال تعالى: {{Q:2:219}} (البقرة: ٢١٩).
- ذم الذين لا يُعملون عقولهم، ويتف ّكرون بها، قال تعالى: {{Q:25:44}} (الفرقان: ٤٤).

وخاطب أرواحهم وعواطفهم من خلال:

- التعبير عن المشاعر العاطفية، وإبرازها، وتصويرها في حالات كثيرة، قال تعالى: {{Q:2:165}} (البقرة: ١٦٥).
- التذكير بالعواطف الإنسانية، وبيان آثارها الحسنة والسيئة، قال تعالى: {{Q:5:82}} (المائدة: ٨٢).
- الأمر بالرفق والتلطف في الدعوة، قال تعالى: {{Q:16:125}} (النحل: ١٢٥).
- تضمين آيات الأحكام معاني إيمانية، قال تعالى: {{Q:4:94}} (النساء: ٩٤).
- استعمال الألفاظ المؤثرة في النفس، والمثيرة للعواطف الصادقة، قال تعالى: {{Q:24:22}} (النور: ٢٢).

وقد يجمع الخطابان: العقلي والروحي في آية واحدة، تناقش العقل وتقنعه، وتحرك العاطفة في الوقت نفسه، قال تعالى: {{Q:35:3}} (فاطر: ٣).

passages.heading: ناقش
passages.text: ما الوسائل المعينة على حفظ سورة الفاتحة؟

passages.heading: معنى السورة:
معيار التفاضل في الإسلام:
passages.text:
جعل الله عز وجل معيار التفاضل بين عباده بالإيمان والتقوى، فالتفاضل بين المسلمين بقوة إيمانهم، وليس بأشكالهم، ولا أنسابهم، ولا ألوانهم، ولا أموالهم، فقد قال تعالى: {{Q:49:13}} (الحجرات: ١٣).

وقال النبي ﷺ: «يا أيها الناس، ألا إن ربكم واحد، وإن أباكم واحد، ألا لا فضل لعربي على عجمي، ولا لعجمي على عربي، ولا أحمر على أسود، ولا أسود على أحمر، إلا بالتقوى». أخرجه البيهقي في شعب الإيمان (٤٧٧٤).

passages.heading: أركان الإسلام:
passages.text:
دين الإسلام مبني على خمسة أركان:

لابد لكلّ مُسلم أن يلتزم بهذه الأركان حتى يستقيم إسلامه؛ لأن عدم الالتزام بأحد هذه الأركان يُشكّل خطرًا على صحّة إسلامه.

passages.heading: أركان الإسلام
passages.text:

- **إقامة الصلاة**: يجب على المسلم أن يصلي خمس صلوات في كل يوم، وسيأتي شرحها.
- **إعطاء الزكاة**
- **صوم رمضان**
- **حج بيت الله**

passages.heading: What Are the Conditions for Islamic Slaughter?
passages.text:
Islamic slaughter is one that satisfies the following conditions:

1. The person undertaking the slaughtering process must be Muslim, Jew or Christian who has reached the age of discretion and carries out this act for the intended purpose.
2. The tool used for slaughter must be suitable for the intended purpose, causes blood to flow and sharp, such as a knife. It is forbidden to use anything that may kill the animal due to its heavy weight, hit its head to death or render it unconscious by resorting to electric stunning, for instance.
3. The name of Allah must be pronounced by saying *Bismillaah* (in the name of Allah) at the time of slaughtering the animal.
4. Cutting what must be cut in the Islamic slaughter, namely, the oesophagus, the throat, and the two jugular veins, or just three of these four.

passages.heading: The Types of Blood that Are Naturally Discharged by Women
passages.text:
The blood that is naturally discharged by women is of two types:

| Menstrual blood | Postnatal blood |
| --- | --- |
| This is a natural type of blood that flows from a woman’s uterus every month during her menstrual cycle and usually lasts for a few days. | This bleeding takes place after giving birth and lasts for several days, up to 40 days. |

passages.heading: Lesson 2
passages.text:
“The path of those whom You have blessed, not of those who have incurred Your wrath, nor of those who have gone astray”
It is the path of those whom You have blessed with guidance from among the prophets and their supporters, and those who follow in their footsteps—These are the ones who have been rightly guided.

Keep us away from the path of those with whom you are angry because they know the truth but choose not to follow it. Also, keep us away from the path of those who have not been guided to the straight path due to their ignorance.

passages.heading: Some of the Ultimate Objectives and Benefits of Fasting
passages.text:
- To attain true piety by increasing acts of worship and avoiding sins as much as possible.
- To experience the pangs of hunger from which the poor and needy often suffer.
- To train oneself to bring one’s whims and desires under control.

Allah has enjoined fasting on Muslims, just as He prescribed it on the other nations before them:
{{Q:2:183}} (Soorat Al-Baqarah, 2:183).

passages.heading: Introduction
passages.text: Since ancient times, people on this earth have led different lives with varying living standards. Some are very well-to-do; others are destitute and can barely find anything to eat. This is one of Allah’s ways in this universe. Islam enjoins the wealthy to pay a certain percentage of their wealth to the poor to relieve them of the burden of poverty and urges Muslims to spend more of what they are required to spend, promising them great rewards for doing so both in this life and after death. It also urges them to give charity to the needy at all times and on every occasion and encourages them to feed the hungry and clothe the naked in order for the Muslim community to become close-knit, just as Allah Almighty wants it to be. In this lesson, we are going to learn about the Islamic ruling on *zakaat*, the manner of paying it and the types of wealth upon which it is due.

passages.heading: Purification
passages.text:
* **Engaging in the worship of Almighty Allah**  
  This is expressed by the intention to act in obedience to Allah Almighty and to draw closer to Him

* **by removing ritual impurity**  
  Ritual impurity (*hadath*) refers to anything that takes place in the body, thus rendering purity invalid

* **and physical impurities**  
  Physical impurity (*najaasah*) refers to all physical substances which Islam considers impure, such as urine and faeces, and commands us to remove.

passages.heading: Islamic Rulings Pertaining to Menstrual and Postnatal Bleeding
passages.text:
Allah Almighty has prescribed several rulings relating to menstruating women and women experiencing their postnatal bleeding, including the following:

- They are exempt from performing the prayers during this period and do not have to make up for the prayers they have missed while in this state after the end of menstrual and postnatal bleeding.
- They are exempt from fasting and are not allowed to fast while in this state, but they must make up for the fasting days they have missed in Ramadaan.
- During this period, a husband must not have intercourse with his wife during her menstrual or postnatal period. He is allowed, however, to satisfy his sexual desire but without having intercourse.
- At the end of the menstrual and postnatal period, when bleeding stops completely, women must take a ritual bath (*ghusl*).

passages.heading: What is Faith?
passages.text: Faith (*Eemaan* in Arabic) is to confess with one’s mouth and believe in one’s heart everything that has come from Allah, totally submit to His will, out of love, hope and fear, and translate that into reality. Allah Almighty says, {{Q:4:136}} (Soorat An-Nisaa’, 4:136)

passages.heading: Allah Almighty has forbidden different types of food and drink, including the following:
passages.text:
- Alcohol, because it clouds the mind; indeed, preserving the mind is one of the objectives of Islamic law (*Sharee’ah*).
- Drugs, because they destroy the mind and body.
- Animals that die without having been slaughtered, or those that are slaughtered but the name of Allah (i.e., saying *Bismillaah* (in the name of Allah) was not mentioned at the time of slaughter.
- Pork—and indeed any of the pig’s body parts and by-products—because it is impure and thus forbidden for human consumption.
- Predatory animals, such as lions, tigers, hawks and eagles.
- Any animals that are sacrificed to false deities, such as idols.

The objectives of *Sharee’ah*: This is one of Islamic sciences by which Islamic laws are determined, such as the reason why Allah has laid down such-and-such a rule.

passages.heading: What is the Islamic Ruling on Seafood Consumption?
passages.text:
It is permissible to eat dead aquatic animals that can live only in water, such as fish and prawns, whether they live in the sea, rivers or lakes.

It is permissible to hunt wild, nonpredatory animals and consume their flesh provided that the name of Allah is mentioned before the hunting weapon is discharged, and the hunted game must be slaughtered if found still alive.

passages.heading: Islamic Rulings Pertaining to Meat Served in Restaurants and Shops
passages.text:
1. The meat of animals that are slaughtered by other than a Muslim or a member of the People of the Book (a Christian or a Jew), such as a Buddhist, or a Hindu is strictly forbidden. This includes meat served in restaurants and shops in countries where Muslims or People of the Book constitute a minority.
2. The meat of animals killed by a Muslim or a member of the People of the Book is lawful based on textual evidence to this effect in the Qur’an.
3. The meat of animals that are not killed according to Islamic law, such as by electrocution and drowning, is strictly forbidden.
4. The general rule is that it is permissible to consume the flesh of animals slaughtered by People of the Book as well as meat of animals generally found in their restaurants and shops, making sure, however, to invoke Allah’s name at the time of eating (that is, by saying *Bismillaah*), but it is better for Muslims to eat only meat that has been proven to be lawful (*halaal*).

passages.heading: Discuss
passages.text:
With your partners, browse some Internet websites that help you find lawful (*halaal*) foods in your country.

The Islamic rulings on the meat of animals that are sold in shops and restaurants vary according to the religion of the person who slaughtered such animals.

passages.heading: Muslim Women’s Modest Style of Dress (*Hijaab*)
passages.text:
Allah enjoins women to wear the *hijaab* because women enjoy natural beauty and attraction that could easily tempt men into sinful acts, more than the other way round. Women are to cover their entire bodies when in the presence of men who are not related to them, and they may choose any design or colour they like for their *hijaab* as long as the following four conditions are met:

| First Condition | Second Condition | Third condition | Fourth Condition |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| It must appropriately cover the parts of the body that must be covered in public. | It must hang loose and must not fit very closely to the body so that the shape of the body is not revealed. | It must not allow the wearer’s body to be seen through its fabric. | It must not be a type of clothing that is generally considered attractive. |

passages.heading: Discuss
passages.text: List some of the reasons why women are exempt from certain religious obligations.

passages.heading: Lesson 2
passages.text:
### The Interpretation of Short *Surahs*

“The All-Compassionate, the All-Merciful”
*Ar-Rahmaan*: The All-Gracious whose mercy encompasses all His creation; *Ar-Raheem*: The All-Merciful who bestows His special mercy to the believers.

The All-Gracious towards all His creation

The All-Merciful towards the believers in particular

“Master of the Day of Judgement” Owner of the Day of Judgement, the day He will judge everyone and repay them according to their deeds.

“You alone do we worship and You alone do we ask for help” We worship You alone, our Lord, and we seek help from You alone in all our affairs, for indeed all matters are in Your hands.

“Guide us to the straight path” Show us the straight path and make us firm on it until we meet You. The straight path here is Islam, the clear path that leads to Allah’s good pleasure and to His Gardens in Paradise.

passages.heading: Discuss
passages.text: What are the means of memorizing *Soorat Al-Faatihah*?

passages.heading: Soorat Al-Ikhlaas Explained
passages.text:
“Say: He is Allah, the One and Only”

Say, Messenger, to those who ask you about your Lord: He is Allah, the One and Only Lord and God, besides whom there is no deity deserving of worship.

“Allah, the Everlasting Sustainer of all”

He is Allah, the Eternal and Absolute God with perfect attributes, to whom all creation turns to fulfil their needs, while He stands in need of none.

“He has not begotten anyone, nor was He Himself begotten by anyone”

He is Allah, who has no offspring whatsoever, neither son nor daughter, and He has no parents, neither father nor mother.

“And none is equal to Him”

And there is no one and nothing among His creation that resembles Him in any way whatsoever with regard to His being, names attributes or actions.

passages.heading: Soorat Al-Falaq Explained
passages.text:
“Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of the daybreak” Say, Messenger: I seek refuge and protection in Allah, the Lord of the daybreak.

“from the evil of what He has created”

from the evil of everything He has created, visible and invisible.

“and from the evil of the night when it spreads its darkness”

and from the evil of the night when it comes and grows dark, and of whatever evil and harm that may happen in it.

Al-ghasaq: the intense darkness of the night

Al-falaq: the daybreak

passages.heading: Why Do We Fast?
passages.text: Muslims fast in obedience to Allah Almighty and in response to His command.

passages.heading: Things that render the Fast Invalid
passages.text:
The fasting person must abstain from several things which, if he does them, his fast will be invalid. They are:

1. Eating and drinking, including intravenous injections which have some nutritional value.
2. Deliberate seminal emission as a result of intercourse or any other means. Intercourse during the day in Ramadaan is a grave sin.
3. Deliberate vomiting.

A woman’s fast is broken as a result of:

4. Menstrual or postnatal bleeding.

passages.heading: The Blessed Month of Ramadaan
passages.text:
Ramadaan is the ninth month of the Islamic lunar calendar. It is a blessed month, in which Allah revealed the Qur’an to His Messenger, Muhammad ﷺ. Allah has promised to forgive all the past sins of those who fast during the daylight hours and stands in prayer at night throughout this month. The Almighty has also distinguished it with a night that is better than a thousand months. It is called *Laylat-ul-Qadr* (The Night of Decree; also called the Night of Power), and whoever spends it remembering Allah and standing in prayer will have all his past sins forgiven.

Muslims perform the *Taraaweeh* prayer in the month of Ramadaan. It is one of the Prophet’s practices (*Sunnah*) that is particularly associated with it, and it is performed after *'Ishaa’* (late evening) prayer.

passages.heading: Introduction
passages.text: Islam enjoins purity and cleanliness on its adherents and stresses that they must take good care of their personal hygiene and considers this matter one of the apparent rituals of religion and a requisite for the validity of many acts of worship. Indeed, observing purity and cleanliness is one of the characteristics of believers, which distinguishes them from others. In this lesson, we are going to learn the meaning of purity, its types, and some rulings on it.

passages.heading: Types of Purification
passages.text:
Purification falls into two types:

**Physical Purification**

This means the removal of impurities and the cleansing of the area affected by them

**Moral Purification**

This means the removal of those things that prevent one from performing the prayer, by washing certain parts of the body or the entire body.

Physical purification may be undertaken either by *wudoo’* or *ghusl*

*Wudoo’* (partial ablutions): the ritual washing of certain parts of the body with water

*Ghusl* (full ablutions/bath): the ritual washing of the entire body with water.

Purification must be undertaken with pure water, such as seawater, river water, well water, or any other water that has not been mixed with impurity.
