passages.heading: Introduction
passages.text: A Muslim often experiences peace and tranquillity when he reads or recites the Qur’an or worships Allah Almighty by engaging in prayer or any other act of worship. This good feeling which elevates some to higher levels of happiness and joy is one of the significant effects of faith that motivates Muslims to dedicate all their lives to Allah, comply with His commands cheerfully and out of love and avoid what He forbids in utter submission and obedience. In this lesson, we are going to learn about the concept of faith and its pillars and benefits.

passages.heading: Discuss
passages.text: What is the difference between hope and fear?

passages.heading: The Pillars of Faith
passages.text:
The Muslim faith rests on six pillars, namely:

1. **Belief in Allah:** A Muslim believes that Allah Almighty exists and believes in His names and attributes. He equally believes that He is the Lord and sole Creator of this vast universe, to whom belongs everything in it, who manages all its affairs and provides sustenance to all His creation, that there is no god is worthy of worship besides or instead of Him and that He has perfect attributes.
2. **Belief in the angels:** A Muslim believes that the honourable angels exist, that it is Allah Almighty who created them and that they worship Him, execute His commands and never disobey Him. He also believes in their attributes and duties which are mentioned in the Book and the *Sunnah*.

passages.heading: Shirk
passages.text:
This means the act of holding someone or something as equal to Allah and directing acts of worship to them. It is a grave and an unforgivable sin. The Qur’an says, {{Q:4:48}} (Soorat An-Nisaa’, 4:48).

By the phrase “the Book and Sunnah” is meant the Noble Qur’an and the sayings of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, as they are the two main sources of legislation in Islam.

passages.heading: معنى السورة:
المعاملات المالية المحرمة:
passages.text:
حرّم الله عز وجل بعض المعاملات المالية، منها:

- أخذ أموال الناس بغير وجه حق؛ كأخذها بحيلة أو بغصب.
- إكراه أحد المتعاملين على معاملة لا يريد القيام بها.
- الاتجار في المواد المضرّة بصحة الإنسان؛ كالخمر والمخدرات.
- الربا، وهو إقراض مالٍ بشرط زيادة نسبة على المال المقترض؛ كزيادة 5% مثلًا.
- بيع المجهول الذي لا يعرف ما هو؛ كبيع صندوق لا يعرف ما بداخله.
- القمار والمراهنات التي يأخذ فيها الفائز مال الخاسر بغير وجه حق.

passages.heading: تمهيد
passages.text:
الإسلام: هو الدين الذي بعث الله به محمدًا ﷺ، وهو امتدادٌ لما جاء به الرسل السابقون.
وأساسه قائمٌ على أن الإله المستحق للعبادة واحدٌ لا شريك له، وهو الله جلّ وعلا، ولا معين له في ملكه، ولا وسيط بينه وبين عباده، ولكن لماذا علي أن أعتنق الإسلام؟ وهل هو دين للناس كافة أم خاص بالعرب؟ ومن هو نبيه؟ وهل هناك نبي آخر سيأتي بعده؟

passages.heading: معنى السورة:
معنى السورة:
موجبات الوضوء:
passages.text:
> الحدث: وصف معنوي في الإنسان يمنعه من أداء الصلاة قبل أن يتطهر وليس شيئًا محسوسًا كالنجاسة، وهو نوعين أحدهما يلزم المسلم التوضأ لرفعه والآخر لا يُرفع إلا بالغُسل.

موجبات الوضوء هي الأمور التي يُشترط الوضوءُ لها، ويجب من أجلها، وإذا أحدث الشخصُ حَرُمَت عليه، وهي:

1. الصلاة
2. الطواف حول الكعبة
3. مس المصحف

5. يرفع رأسه ليعود قائمًا مع رفع يديه إلى جوار كتفيه، وهو يقول: «**سمع الله لمن حمده**». ثم يقول وهو واقف: «**ربنا ولك الحمد**».

6. ينحني ساجدًا على الأرض، فيضع جبهته وأنفه على الأرض، مع وضع كفيه وركبتيه وأطراف أصابع قدميه على الأرض، ويقول: «**سبحان ربي الأعلى**» ثلاث مرات.

passages.heading: الثاني
passages.text: الجماع، سواء حصل معه إنزال مني أو لا.

passages.heading: ناقش
passages.text: ما الوسائل المعينة على حفظ سورة الفاتحة؟

passages.heading: معنى السورة:
الأصل في المعاملات المالية:
passages.text:
**الأصل في المعاملات المالية الإباحة، فلا يحرم شيءٌ منها** إلا ما جاء في القرآن الكريم أو السنة النبوية تحريمه.

> الأصل في المعاملات ومنها المعاملات المالية الإباحة، فلا تحريم إلا بدليل، بعكس العبادات فالأصل فيها أنها توقيفية فلا تجب عبادة إلا بدليل.

passages.heading: أسباب تحريم المعاملة المالية:
passages.text:
الأسباب الرئيسة التي تقتضي تحريم المعاملة المالية هي:

1. الظلم
2. الربا
3. الغرر والقمار

passages.heading: ناقش
passages.text: في ظل كثرة المعاملات المالية التي يمارسها المسلم في حياته، كيف له أن يتنبه لما يحل منها وما يحرم؟

passages.heading: لماذا أسلم؟
passages.text:
قد يتساءل بعض الناس: لماذا يجب عليّ أن أسلم؟

والجواب: يجب أن أسلم لأمور منها:

الأول: أن دين الإسلام هو الدين الذي ارتضاه الله لعباده، ولا يقبل من أحدٍ دين سواه، قال تعالى: {{Q:3:85}} (آل عمران:٨٥).

الثاني: أن دين الإسلام هو دين الأنبياء جميعًا، ويأمر بالإيمان بالأنبياء جميعًا، ولا يفرّق بينهم؛ لأنه دينهم جميعًا.

قال الله تعالى: {{Q:2:136}} (البقرة:١٣٦).

والاختلاف بين الأنبياء هو اختلاف في الأحكام التشريعية المتعلقة بأفعال العباد، كما قال سبحانه: {{Q:5:48}} (المائدة:٤٨). أي: جعل الله لكل أمةٍ من الأمم شريعةً يحتكمون إليها، وطريقًا يتقربون بها إليه، فلكل أهل ملة أحكامٌ تخصهم، وتشريعات تناسبهم.

ثم بعث الله خاتم أنبيائه ورسله محمدًا ﷺ فختم به الرسل، وختم بشريعته الشرائع، فلا يقبل من أحد دين غير الإسلام.

الثالث: أن الدخول في الإسلام سبيل النجاة في الآخرة فلا ينجو في الآخرة أحد بلغته إلا من آمن به واتبعه، قال تعالى: {{Q:3:85}} (آل عمران:٨٥)، وقال ﷺ: «وَالَّذِي نَفْسُ مُحَمَّدٍ بِيَدِهِ، لَا يَسْمَعُ بِي أَحَدٌ مِنْ هَذِهِ الْأُمَّةِ يَهُودِيٌّ وَلَا نَصْرَانِيٌّ، ثُمَّ يَمُوتُ، وَلَمْ يُؤْمِنْ بِالَّذِي أُرْسِلْتُ بِهِ إِلَّا كَانَ مِنْ أَصْحَابِ النَّارِ».

passages.heading: ناقش
passages.text: كيف يكون الإسلام دين جميع الأنبياء؟

passages.heading: ناقش
passages.text: ما الموضوع الذي أكدت عليه سورتا الإخلاص والكافرون؟

passages.heading: سورة الكوثر:
سورة العصر:
معنى الوضوء:
passages.text: **الوضوء:** غسل الوجه واليدين والرجلين بصفة معينة.

passages.heading: كيف نتوضأ؟
passages.text:
إذا أراد المسلم أن يتوضأ فعليه القيام بالخطوات الآتية:

1. يقول: «بسم الله».
2. يغسل كفيّه بالماء مبتدئًا باليمنى.
3. ينظف فمه بإدخال الماء فيه، ثم يحركه، ثم يخرجه.
4. ينظف أنفه بإدخال الماء فيه مع الاستنشاق، ثم يخرجه مع نفخ الهواء من أنفه.
5. يغسل وجه كاملًا، وحدوده طولًا من منابت الشعر في أعلى الجبهة إلى أسفل الذقن، مع شعر اللحية إن وجدت، وحدوده عرضًا من الأذن إلى الأذن.
6. يغسل يديه من أطراف الأصابع إلى مفصل المرفق، مبتدئًا بيده اليمنى.
7. يبلل يديه بالماء، ثم يمسح بهما رأسه، مبتدئًا بمقدمة الرأس إلى القفا، ثم يعيد يديه إلى الأمام.
8. يمسح أذنيه بأصبعيه السبابتين داخل الأذنين، ويمسح خلف الأذنين بالإبهامين.
9. يغسل قدميه إلى الكعبين، وهما العظمان البارزان في مفصل القدم، مبتدئًا برجله اليمنى.

passages.heading: كيف نصلي؟
passages.text:
إذا أراد المسلم أن يصلي فعليه القيام بالخطوات الآتية:

1. يستحضر نية الصلاة بقلبه.
2. يقف مستقبلًا القبلة، ويرفع كفيه بجوار كتفيه، ويقول: «الله أكبر».
3. يضع يده اليمنى على يده اليسرى. ثم يقرأ دعاء من أدعية الاستفتاح، مثل: «سبحانك اللهم وبحمدك، وتبارك اسمك، وتعالى جدك، ولا إله غيرك». ثم يقول: «أعوذ بالله من الشيطان الرجيم، بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم». ثم يقرأ سورة الفاتحة، ثم يقول: «آمين» عند الانتهاء من قراءتها، ومعناها: اللهم استجب دعاءنا. ثم يقرأ بعد الفاتحة ما تيسّر له مما يحفظ من القرآن الكريم، ولو كان آية واحدة.
4. يرفع يديه بجوار كتفيه أو أذنيه، ويقول: «الله أكبر»، ويحني ظهره راكعًا، ويضع يديه على ركبتيه، ويجعل ظهره ورأسه في مستوى واحد.

ويقول أثناء ركوعه: «سبحان ربي العظيم» ثلاث مرات.

7. يرفع رأسه ويجلس على قدمه اليسرى، مع بقاء قدمه اليمنى منتصبة، ويضع كفيه على فخذيه، ويقول أثناء جلوسه: «**ربِّ اغفر لي**».

8. يسجد مرة أخرى كالسجدة الأولى، ويقول أثناء الانحناء للسجود: «**اللهُ أكبر**». ويفعل في سجوده الثاني ما فعل في سجوده الأول.

9. يرفع رأسه ويقوم للركعة الثانية، وهو يقول: «**اللهُ أكبر**». ويصلي الركعة الثانية كما صلى الركعة الأولى تمامًا.

passages.heading: الأول
passages.text: خروج المني بشهوة، سواء خرج أثناء اليقظة أو النوم.

passages.heading: الثالث
passages.text: نزول دم الحيض أو النفاس عند المرأة، فإذا انقطع الدم وجب عليها الغسل.

passages.heading: ناقش
passages.text: على ما يدل التوجيه بالاغتسال لرفع الحدث؟

passages.heading: ما يحرم فعله للجنب:
passages.text:
تسمى حال الشخص الذي وجب عليه الغسل بسبب الجماع أو خروج المني (جنابة)، ويسمى المتلبس بها (جنبًا) . ويحرم عليه في هذه الحال:

1. الصلاة
2. المكوث في المسجد
3. مس المصحف أو حمله
4. قراءة القرآن الكريم

passages.heading: Mengapa Saya Masuk Islam?
passages.text:
**Mungkin sebagian orang bertanya-tanya: mengapa saya harus masuk Islam?**

Jawabannya: Saya harus masuk Islam karena beberapa faktor, di antaranya:

Pertama: agama Islam adalah agama yang diridai oleh Allah bagi hamba-hamba-Nya, dan Allah tidak menerima agama lainnya dari siapa pun. Dia berfirman, {{Q:3:85}} (QS. Āli 'Imrān: 85)

Kedua: agama Islam adalah agama para nabi semuanya. Islam memerintahkan beriman kepada para nabi seluruhnya, dan tidak membeda-bedakan di antara mereka. Allah Ta'ālā berfirman, {{Q:2:136}} (QS. Al-Baqarah: 136)

passages.heading: Pendahuluan
passages.text: Islam adalah agama yang dengannya Allah mengutus Muhammad ﷺ dan merupakan kelanjutan dari agama yang dibawa oleh rasul-rasul terdahulu. Pilar Islam tegak di atas konsep bahwa sembahan yang berhak disembah ialah tunggal, tidak memiliki sekutu, yaitu Allah Jalla wa 'Alā; tidak ada yang membantu-Nya dalam kerajaan-Nya dan tidak pula ada perantara antara Dia dan hamba-hamba-Nya. Hanya saja, mengapa saya harus memeluk Islam? Apakah Islam agama bagi seluruh umat manusia ataukah khusus bagi bangsa Arab? Siapakah nabi Islam? Apakah akan ada nabi lain yang datang setelahnya?

passages.heading: Apa yang saya lakukan bila mendapatkan air setelah bertayamum?
passages.text: Bila seorang Muslim mendapatkan air atau telah mampu menggunakannya maka tayamumnya batal dan dia wajib berwudu ataupun mandi setelah itu.

passages.heading: Kapan saya diwajibkan mengulang wudu?
passages.text: Bila seorang Muslim telah berwudu, pada dasarnya wudunya tetap sah hingga terjadi padanya sesuatu yang mewajibkan wudu, sebagaimana yang telah disebutkan.

passages.heading: Mengapa Saya Masuk Islam?
passages.text: Perbedaan di antara para nabi terletak pada hukum-hukum syariat yang berkaitan dengan perbuatan hamba, sebagaimana Allah Subḥānahu wa Ta'ālā berfirman, {{Q:5:48}} (QS. Al-Mā'idah: 48) Maksudnya ialah Allah menetapkan bagi masing-masing umat satu syariat yang mereka jadikan sebagai acuan hukum serta jalan yang mereka lalui dalam mendekatkan diri kepada Allah. Sebab itu, masing-masing umat memiliki hukum yang khusus bagi mereka serta syariat-syariat yang sesuai dengan kondisi mereka. Adapun dalam persoalan akidah, maka akidah semua nabi sama. Kemudian Allah mengutus penutup para nabi dan rasul-Nya, Muhammad ﷺ. Dengannya, Allah menutup semua rasul, dengan syariatnya pula Allah menutup semua syariat. Sebab itulah, Allah tidak akan menerima agama selain Islam dari siapa pun.

passages.heading: Pelajaran 3
passages.text:
## Bagaimana Saya Masuk Islam?

Inti agama Islam yang merupakan agama seluruh para nabi ialah beribadah kepada Allah saja serta mengingkari semua yang disembah selain Allah. Allah *Ta'ālā* berfirman, "Kami tidak mengutus seorang rasul pun sebelum engkau (Muhammad), melainkan Kami wahyukan kepadanya, 'bahwa tidak ada tuhan (yang berhak disembah) selain Aku, maka sembahlah Aku!'" (QS. Al-Anbiyā`: 25)

Sebab itu, tidak diperbolehkan dalam keadaan apa pun untuk meyakini ketuhanan siapa pun selain Allah *Ta'ālā* serta tidak boleh beribadah mendekatkan diri kepada selain Allah *Ta'ālā* dengan jenis ibadah apa pun.

passages.heading: Hukum-hukum Terkait Hewan Sembelihan di Restoran dan Pusat Perbelanjaan
passages.text:
1. Hewan yang disembelih oleh selain Muslim dan Ahli Kitab (Yahudi atau Nasrani), seperti orang Budha, Hindu, dan tidak beragama, hukumnya haram. Termasuk yang ditemukan di restoran dan pusat perbelanjaan negara-negara mayoritas nonmuslim dan non-Ahli Kitab.
2. Hewan yang disembelih oleh seorang Muslim atau Ahli Kitab dengan cara yang sesuai syariat maka hukumnya halal berdasarkan nas Al-Qur`ān.
3. Hewan yang dibunuh oleh seorang Muslim atau Ahli Kitab dengan cara yang tidak sesuai syariat, seperti disetrum dan ditenggelamkan, ini hukumnya haram.
4. Pada dasarnya, boleh memakan hewan sembelihan Ahli Kitab serta yang ditemukan di restoran dan pusat perbelanjaan mereka, dengan disertai usaha untuk menyebut nama Allah ketika memakannya. Namun, yang paling utama bagi seorang Muslim ialah tidak memakan kecuali yang terbukti berasal dari daging halal.

passages.heading: Makanan dan Minuman yang Diharamkan
passages.text:
Allah *'Azza wa Jalla* mengharamkan beberapa jenis makanan dan minuman, di antaranya:

- Khamar; karena khamar menghilangkan akal, sedangkan melindungi akal adalah satu di antara *Maqāṣid syarī'ah* (tujuan besar syariat) Islam.
- Narkoba; karena merusak akal dan fisik.
- Hewan yang mati tanpa disembelih atau tidak dibacakan nama Allah ketika penyembelihannya.
- Daging babi; karena merupakan daging najis yang tidak boleh dimakan.
- Binatang buas; seperti singa, harimau, dan elang.
- Binatang yang disembelih dalam rangka mendekatkan diri kepada tuhan-tuhan yang batil, seperti berhala.

> *Maqāṣid syarī'ah* ialah salah satu ilmu Islam untuk mengetahui hikmah dan rahasia syariat. Misalnya: mengapa Allah mensyariatkan hukum-hukum ini? Untuk tujuan apa hukum ini ada?

passages.heading: Pelajaran 2
passages.text:
### Apakah Islam Itu?

Ketiga: masuk Islam adalah jalan kebahagiaan di dunia dan keselamatan di akhirat. Orang yang sampai kepadanya dakwah Nabi Muhammad ﷺ tidak akan selamat di akhirat kelak kecuali bila ia beriman kepadanya serta mengikutinya. Allah Ta’ālā berfirman, “Barang siapa mencari agama selain Islam, ia tidak akan diterima dan di akhirat dia termasuk orang yang rugi.” (QS. Āli ‘Imrān: 85)

Nabi ﷺ bersabda, “Demi (Tuhan) yang jiwa Muhammad berada di tangan-Nya! Tidak ada seorang pun dari umat ini, baik Yahudi maupun Nasrani, yang mendengar tentang diriku lalu ia meninggal dalam keadaan tidak beriman kepada apa yang aku bawa, melainkan ia adalah penghuni neraka.” (HR. Muslim: 153)

Keempat: Islam memberikan jawaban sempurna terhadap pertanyaan-pertanyaan besarku: untuk apa aku hadir ke dunia? Dari mana aku berasal? Dan kemana aku akan pergi setelah kematian?

Kelima: Islam adalah agama yang sejalan dengan fitrah, mulai dari nilai Islam yang paling besar, yaitu menauhidkan Allah, hingga pada adab-adabnya yang mengajak kepada akhlak baik nan lurus.

passages.heading: Diskusikan
passages.text: Bagaimana Islam menjadi agama semua nabi?

passages.heading: Tayamum
passages.text: Bila orang yang hendak berwudu atau mandi tidak bisa melakukannya karena ketidakadaan air atau tidak mampu menggunakan air dengan sebab sakit atau lainnya, maka dia diperintahkan untuk bertayamum sebagai gantinya. Tata cara tayamum ialah berniat tayamum dalam hati dan menepukkan kedua telapak tangan ke tanah satu kali tepukan, lalu mengusap muka dilanjutkan kedua telapak tangan menggunakan sisa tanah yang melekat di tangan.

passages.heading: Apa Hukum Memakan Hewan Laut?
passages.text:
Hewan air yang tidak hidup kecuali di air, bangkainya boleh dimakan, seperti ikan, udang, dan lainnya, baik hidupnya di laut, sungai, atau danau.

Dibolehkan berburu dan memakan hewan darat yang tidak buas, dengan syarat menyebut nama Allah ketika memburunya serta menyembelihnya bila ditemukan masih hidup.

passages.heading: Diskusikan!
passages.text:
Diskusikanlah bersama rekan-rekanmu tentang sebagian situs internet yang dapat membantumu untuk mendapatkan makanan halal di negaramu!

Hukum sembelihan yang dijual di pusat perbelanjaan serta restoran berbeda-beda tergantung agama orang yang melakukan langsung penyembelihannya.

passages.heading: The Five Obligatory Prayers
passages.text:
Allah Almighty has enjoined Muslims to perform five prayers throughout the day and night, namely:

| The Prayer | Beginning Time | Ending Time | Number of units (*rak‘ahs*) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| *Fajr* (Dawn) Prayer | at the break of dawn | sunrise | 2 |
| *Dhuhr* (Midday) Prayer | when the sun starts declining westward at midday after reaching its zenith | when the shadow of an object becomes equal in length to the object itself | 4 |
| *‘Asr* (Late Afternoon) Prayer | when the shadow of an object becomes equal in length to the object itself | sunset | 4 |
| *Maghrib* (Sunset) Prayer | sunset | when the red glow (evening twilight) on the western horizon disappears | 3 |
| *‘Ishaa’* (Late Evening) Prayer | when the red glow (evening twilight) on the western horizon disappears | midnight | 4 |

passages.heading: The Conditions of the Prayer
passages.text:
- Purity: Once’s body and the place where the prayer is to be performed must be cleansed from physical impurities, and any ritual impurity must be removed with *wudoo’* or *ghusl*.
- Covering the intimate parts of the body (*‘awrah*): The word *‘awrah* refers to the parts of the body that must be covered in front of people. A man’s *‘awrah* that must be covered during the prayer extends from the navel to the knees; a woman’s *‘awrah* that must be covered during the prayer is her entire body except for the face and hands.
- Facing the *qiblah*: The *qiblah* is the direction of the Ka‘bah in Makkah. One must, therefore, pray in the direction of the Ka‘bah in Makkah.
- When its appointed time becomes due: The prayer will not be valid if it is performed before its time has started. It is not permissible to delay it beyond its due time, and it is best to perform it at the beginning of its time.

passages.heading: The Meaning of the Prayer
passages.text:
The prayer: It is a daily act of worship that consists of a set of words and actions with which a Muslim seeks to draw closer to his Lord, and it is performed five times a day and night.

The prayer is the second pillar of Islam.

passages.heading: The Conditions of the Prayer
passages.text:
To perform the prayer, several conditions must be met:
There are several conditions required to perform the prayer, which are:

passages.heading: Introduction
passages.text: The prayer is the greatest religious duty that a Muslim must learn and perform. Allah’s Messenger ﷺ has taught us how to perform it in the manner most pleasing to Allah Almighty. In this lesson, we are going to learn about the obligatory prayers, the position of the prayer in Islam, its conditions, and the correct manner of performing it.

passages.heading: Important Notes Related to Fasting
passages.text:
- Whoever breaks his fast in Ramadaan for a legitimate reason must make up for every day he has missed after than Ramadaan.
- If a sick person breaks the fast because of an incurable disease, he is exempt from fasting the month of Ramadaan, but he must feed one poor person for each day he does not fast.
- If a Muslim cannot possibly fast due to old age, he is exempt from fasting the month of Ramadaan but he must feed one poor person for each day he does not fast.

**Muslims break their fast as soon as the call to *Maghrib* (sunset) prayer is announced, and many Muslims are very keen to share their Ramadaan breakfast, or *iftar*, with fellow Muslims.**

passages.heading: The Blessed Month of Ramadaan
passages.text:
Ramadaan is the ninth month of the Islamic lunar calendar. It is a blessed month, in which Allah revealed the Qur’an to His Messenger, Muhammad ﷺ. Allah has promised to forgive all the past sins of those who fast during the daylight hours and stands in prayer at night throughout this month. The Almighty has also distinguished it with a night that is better than a thousand months. It is called *Laylat-ul-Qadr* (The Night of Decree; also called the Night of Power), and whoever spends it remembering Allah and standing in prayer will have all his past sins forgiven.

Muslims perform the *Taraaweeh* prayer in the month of Ramadaan. It is one of the Prophet’s practices (*Sunnah*) that is particularly associated with it, and it is performed after *'Ishaa’* (late evening) prayer.

passages.heading: How Do We Pray?
passages.text:
1. He intends in his heart to pray.
2. He stands facing the *qiblah*, raises his hands up to the level of the shoulders or ears, and says, “*Allaahu akbar* Allah is the Greatest.”
3. He places his right hand on his left hand. Then he recites one of the opening supplications, such as, Subhaanak-Allaahumma wa bi hamdika, wa tabaarak-asmuka, wa ta’aalaa jadduka, wa laa ilaaha ghayruka “Glory be to You, O Allah; Yours is the praise, blessed is Your name, exalted is Your majesty, and there is no god besides You.” Then he says, A’oodhu billaahi min-ash-shaytaan-ir-rajeem. Bismillaah-ir-rahmaan-ir-raheem “I seek Allah’s protection from Satan, who has been expelled from His mercy. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.” Then he recites *Soorat Al-Faatihah* and says after it, “*Aameen*”, which means “Answer our supplications, O Allah”. After that, he recites whatever number of verses of the Qur’an as is easy for him, even if it is one verse.
4. He says, “Allaahu akbar Allah is the Greatest” while raising his hands up to the level of his shoulders or ears, and bows down, lowering his head and back and keeping them straight at a right angle, placing the palms of his hands on the knees. He says three times while in this position, “Subhaana rabbiy-al-’adheem Glory be to my Lord, the Almighty.”

passages.heading: How Do We Pray?
passages.text: If a Muslim wants to pray, he must do the following:

passages.heading: The Position of the Prayer in Islam
passages.text:
The prayer has a number of distinctive characteristics, including the following:

- It is the second pillar of Islam after the two testimonies of faith.
- It is the act of worship that must be performed under all circumstances, in times of war and peace, and whether one is sick or in good health.
- It is the act of worship that distinguishes a Muslim from a non-Muslim.

passages.heading: Why Do We Pray?
passages.text: We pray because the prayer is an act of worship that Allah has enjoined on Muslims.

passages.heading: Some of the Ultimate Objectives and Benefits of the Prayer:
passages.text:
- It is the direct, special and personal communion a Muslim establishes with his Lord.
- It relieves the mind of worry and all worldly anxieties.
- It strengthens a Muslim’s willpower and determination.
- It refines morals and keeps those who observe it away from evil.

passages.heading: How Many Times Do We Wash the Parts of the Body that Are Usually Washed in *Wudoo’*?
passages.text: According to the *Sunnah*, each part of the body is washed three times, except in the case of the head and ears, which are wiped only once. It would suffice, however, to wash these body parts once provided that they are washed thoroughly.

passages.heading: Wiping over the Socks
passages.text: If a person wants to perform *wudoo’* while he has his socks on, he is allowed to just wipe over the top of them with wet hands, and there is no need to take them off and wash the feet. Three conditions are required for this:

passages.heading: When do I have to perform wudoo’ again?
passages.text: If a Muslim performs wudoo’, the general rule is that his wudoo’ is still valid unless one of the previously-mentioned things that break wudoo’ happens, in which case he must perform it again.

passages.heading: The Manner of Performing *Wudoo’*
passages.text:
1. He intends in his heart to perform *wudoo’* and says, *bismillaah* “In the name of Allah”.
2. He washes his hands up to the wrists with water.
3. He rinses out his mouth thoroughly by moving water around in the mouth and then spitting it out. This process is called *madmadah*) in Arabic.
4. He cleans his nose by sniffing water into the nostrils and ejecting it out by blowing his nose.
5. He washes his face thoroughly from the hairline at the top of the forehead to the bottom of the chin, along with the beard, if he is bearded, and from ear to ear.
6. He washes his hands from the fingertips up to the elbow, starting with his right hand.
7. With wet hands, and starting with his hands flat on the top of the head near the hairline, he wipes it to the back of the neck and back to the front.
8. With wet fingers, he wipes  
He wipes the inner sides of the ears with his index fingers and behind them with his thumbs.
9. He washes his feet up to the ankles, which are the two prominent bones of the joint connecting the foot to the leg, starting with his right foot.

passages.heading: How to Perform *Ghusl*?
passages.text:
To perform *ghusl*, one must wash the entire body with water, rinse out one’s mouth and clean one’s nose by sniffing water into the nostrils and ejecting it out by blowing one’s nose. A Muslim removes the major ritual impurity by simply doing so.

> The major ritual impurity: what must be removed by ghusl, and ablution is not sufficient, and these are types:
> 
> 1- *Janaabah*: The state of ritual impurity following intercourse or ejaculation as a result of an orgasm even if no intercourse takes place.
> 2- Menstruation: the normal vaginal bleeding that occurs as part of a woman’s monthly cycle.
> 3- Postnatal bleeding: The vaginal bleeding that takes place following childbirth.

1. He intends in his heart to pray.
2. He stands facing the *qiblah*, raises his hands up to the level of the shoulders or ears, and says, “*Allaahu akbar* Allah is the Greatest.”
3. He places his right hand on his left hand. Then he recites one of the opening supplications, such as, Subhaanak-Allaahumma wa bi hamdika, wa tabaarak-asmuka, wa ta’aalaa jadduka, wa laa ilaaha ghayruka “Glory be to You, O Allah; Yours is the praise, blessed is Your name, exalted is Your majesty, and there is no god besides You.” Then he says, A’oodhu billaahi min-ash-shaytaan-ir-rajeem. Bismillaah-ir-rahmaan-ir-raheem “I seek Allah’s protection from Satan, who has been expelled from His mercy. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.” Then he recites *Soorat Al-Faatihah* and says after it, “*Aameen*”, which means “Answer our supplications, O Allah”. After that, he recites whatever number of verses of the Qur’an as is easy for him, even if it is one verse.
4. He says, “Allaahu akbar Allah is the Greatest” while raising his hands up to the level of his shoulders or ears, and bows down, lowering his head and back and keeping them straight at a right angle, placing the palms of his hands on the knees. He says three times while in this position, “Subhaana rabbiy-al-’adheem Glory be to my Lord, the Almighty.”

passages.heading: *Tayammum* (Dry Ablution)
passages.text:
If a person who wants to perform *wudoo’* or *ghusl* is unable to do so due to illness, or when water is not readily available, or for any other legitimate reason, he may resort to dry ablution (*tayammum*) instead.

The Manner of Performing *Tayammum*: (1) Intend in his heart to perform *tayammum* and strike both hands slightly on pure earth once, (2) wipe the face with them, (3) wipe the back of the right hand with the palm of the left, and then the back of the left hand with the palm of the right hand.

passages.heading: The Meaning of *Wudoo’*
passages.text: *Wudoo’*: The ritual of washing the face, hands, and feet, and wiping over the head in a specific manner.

passages.heading: Things That Render *Wudoo’* Invalid
passages.text:
*Wudoo’* becomes invalid as a result of four things:

- Natural discharges from the private parts (both the external genital and excretory organs), such as urine, excrement, wind, semen and the clear, colourless, viscous fluid that is emitted during sexual arousal
- Loss of consciousness due to sleep or intoxication
- Lustfully touching the private parts with bare hands
- Eating camel meat

passages.heading: Discuss
passages.text: List some of the means which help us learn *wudoo’* and perform it properly.

passages.heading: First
passages.text: He must be in a state of purity before putting them on.

passages.heading: Second
passages.text: The socks must cover the feet along with the ankles.

passages.heading: Third
passages.text:
The period of wiping over them must not exceed 24 hours for a resident and 72 hours for a traveller.

The period of wiping over the socks begins from the first time one wipes over them.

passages.heading: The Manner of Performing *Wudoo’*
passages.text: If a Muslim wants to perform his ablutions (*wudoo’*), he must do the following:

passages.heading: Introduction
passages.text: *Wudoo’* is very important in Islam because it is closely connected with the ritual prayer, which is itself the greatest ritual in Islam, hence the importance of learning it and performing it correctly. In this lesson, we are going to learn about the meaning of *wudoo’*, things that require us to perform it, things that make it invalid, and the proper manner of performing it.

passages.heading: Things Which Require Us to Perform *Wudoo’*:
passages.text:
These are those things for which *wudoo’* is necessary and must be performed before engaging in them and which we are forbidden to do once *wudoo’* is broken. They are:

> *Hadath*: This is the state of having our ablutions broken and thus prevents us from performing the prayer before purifying ourselves. It is of two types: one requires us to perform only partial ablutions (*wudoo’*) to remove it, and the other requires us to perform full ablutions (*ghusl*).

1. the prayer
2. circumambulation around the Ka’bah (*tawaaf*)
3. touching the Qur’an

passages.heading: Lesson 3
passages.text: ### *Wudoo’* (Partial Ablutions)

passages.heading: Discuss
passages.text:
Why does the testimony that there is no god but Allah require us to reject everything that is worshipped besides or instead of Allah?

With your partners, discuss the reasons why some people are keen to invent all sorts of gods and invite others to worship them.

One of the rational arguments Prophet Ibraaheem (Abraham), peace be upon him, used against his idolatrous people was: {{Q:37:95}} (Soorat As-Saafaat, 37:95)

passages.heading: The Requirements of the Two Testimonies of Faith
passages.text: It is not enough to verbally declare the two testimonies of faith. In addition to this, it is imperative to know what they mean and to meet their requirements. The testimony that there is no god but Allah requires us to reject everything that is worshipped besides or instead of Allah, to firmly believe that Allah alone is our Lord and Cherisher and the One True God worthy of worship and to worship Him sincerely. Allah Almighty says, {{Q:2:256}} (Soorat Al-Baqarah, 2:256) The testimony that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah requires us to believe what he says, do what he commands and avoid what he forbids and worship Allah only according to his instructions.

Islam is essentially the religion of all the prophets: to worship Allah alone and reject all false deities that are worshipped besides or instead of Him. Allah Almighty, says, {{Q:21:25}} (Surat al-Anbiyyaa’, 21:25).

Therefore, it is not permissible, under any circumstances, to believe in any deity other than Allah Almighty, nor is it permissible to perform any act of worship to draw nearer to anyone other than Allah Almighty.

passages.heading: 2. The Meaning of the Testimony that Muhammad is Allah’s Messenger
passages.text: The meaning of the testimony that Muhammad is Allah’s Messenger is: I firmly believe that Muhammad ﷺ is the Messenger of Allah, that he is the Final Prophet without there being any prophet whatsoever after him, and that his message is for all people without exception. Allah Almighty says: {{Q:25:1}} (Surat Al-Furqaan, 25:1).

passages.heading: 1. The Meaning of the Testimony that There Is no God but Allah
passages.text:
The meaning of “I bear witness that there is no god but Allah” is: I firmly believe that there is no god worthy of worship except Allah alone.

This testimony consists of two parts:

| The first part | The second part |
| --- | --- |
| negates the existence of any other deity besides Allah Almighty | confirms that Allah is the only True God worthy of worship |

passages.heading: The Two Testimonies of Faith
passages.text:
Allah Almighty has made the declaration of the two testimonies of faith the key to joining the fold of Islam. They are:

- I bear witness that there is no god worthy of worship but Allah,
- and I bear witness that Muhammad is Allah’s Messenger.

passages.heading: Introduction
passages.text: One of the most memorable moments of a new Muslim’s life must be the moment he joined the fold of Islam by pronouncing the two testimonies of faith. By so doing, he declared to himself before anyone else that he would begin a new chapter in his life and would, from the moment of making such a declaration, take the first steps towards finding the truth and adhering to it. In this lesson, we are going to learn about the two testimonies and their meaning and requirements.

passages.heading: الثاني
passages.text: الجماع، سواء حصل معه إنزال مني أو لا.

passages.heading: ماذا أفعل إذا وجدت الماء بعد أن تيممت؟
passages.text: إذا وجد المسلم الماء أو قدر على استعماله انتقضت طهارته ووجب عليه الوضوء أو الغسل بعد ذلك .

passages.heading: تنبيهات متعلقة بالصوم:
passages.text:
- من أفطر في رمضان لعذر، فإنه يصوم عن كل يوم أفطره يومًا آخر في غير رمضان.
- إذا أفطر المريض بسبب مرضٍ لا يرجى شفاؤه فإنه يسقط عنه صوم رمضان ويطعم عن كل يوم أفطره مسكينًا.
- أذا كان المسلم كبير السنّ لا يستطيع الصوم مطلقًا، فإنه يسقط عنه صوم رمضان ويطعم عن كل يوم أفطره مسكينًا.

يتناول المسلمون طعام الإفطار مع أذان المغرب، ويحرص الكثير من المسلمين على مشاركة إخوانهم الإفطار.

passages.heading: متى يجب على أن أعيد الوضوء؟
passages.text: إذا توضأ المسلم فالأصل بقاء وضوئه حتى يحصل معه ما يوجب الوضوء، مما سبق ذكره.

passages.heading: مفسدات الصوم:
passages.text:
يجب على الصائم الامتناع عن مجموعة أشياء، إذا فعلها يفسد صومه، وهي:
1. الأكل والشرب، ويدخل في حكمها أخذ الإبر المغذية عبر الوريد.
2. إنزال المني عن عمد، سواء كان بجماع أو من غير جماع، والجماع في نهار رمضان ذنب عظيم.
3. التقيؤ عمدًا.

أما المرأة فيفسد صومها كذلك عند:
4. خروج دم الحيض أو دم النفاس.

passages.heading: أحكام الذبائح في المطاعم والمحلات:
passages.text:
1. ما ذبحه غير المسلم والكتابي كالبوذيين والهندوس واللادينيين فهذا محرم، ويدخل فيه ما يوجد في مطاعم ومحلات البلاد التي غالب أهلها من غير المسلمين وأهل الكتاب.
2. ما ذبحه المسلم أو الكتابي بالطريقة الشرعية فهذا جائز بنص القرآن.
3. ما ذبحه المسلم أو الكتابي بطريقة غير شرعية كالصعق والإغراق فهذا محرم.
4. الأصل جواز ذبيحة الكتابي وما يوجد في مطاعمهم ومحلاتهم، وإن لم نتحقق من طريقة ذبحها، مع الحرص على التسمية عند الأكل. والأولى للمسلم ألا يأكل إلا ما تحقق من كونه من لحوم الحلال المباحة.

passages.heading: أن تكون المرأة أجنبية عنه
passages.text: المرأة الأجنبية هي كل امرأة ليست من محارمه، سواء كانت من أقاربه كبنت عمه وبنت عمته، وزوجة أخيه وقريبات العائلة، أو كانت من غير أقاربه ولا تربطه بها علاقة عائلية، وقد وضع الإسلام ضوابط للتعامل بين الجنسين كوجوب الحجاب وعدم الخلوة.

passages.heading: أركان الإسلام:
passages.text:
دين الإسلام مبني على خمسة أركان:

لابد لكلّ مُسلم أن يلتزم بهذه الأركان حتى يستقيم إسلامه؛ لأن عدم الالتزام بأحد هذه الأركان يُشكّل خطرًا على صحّة إسلامه.

passages.heading: الأول
passages.text: خروج المني بشهوة، سواء خرج أثناء اليقظة أو النوم.

passages.heading: الثالث
passages.text: نزول دم الحيض أو النفاس عند المرأة، فإذا انقطع الدم وجب عليها الغسل.

passages.heading: ناقش
passages.text: على ما يدل التوجيه بالاغتسال لرفع الحدث؟

passages.heading: ما يحرم فعله للجنب:
passages.text:
تسمى حال الشخص الذي وجب عليه الغسل بسبب الجماع أو خروج المني (جنابة)، ويسمى المتلبس بها (جنبًا) . ويحرم عليه في هذه الحال:

1. الصلاة
2. المكوث في المسجد
3. مس المصحف أو حمله
4. قراءة القرآن الكريم

passages.heading: التيمم:
passages.text:
إذا عجز من أراد الوضوء أو الغسل عن فعل ذلك لعدم وجود الماء، أو للعجز عن استعمال الماء بسبب مرضٍ أو غيره، فيشرع له التيمم بدلًا عنهما .

**وصفة التيمم:** أن يضرب بيديه على التراب ضربة واحدة، ثم يمسح بما تبقى من أثر التراب في يديه على وجهه، ثم يمسح كفيه .

لابد من تعميم جميع البدن بالماء حتى يكون الغسل صحيحا رافعًا للجنابة.
صح  خطأ

لا يجب الغسل عند خروج المني حال النوم، ويجب عند خروجه حال اليقظة.
صح  خطأ

لا يجوز للجنب أن يجلس في المسجد.
صح  خطأ

يشرع التيمم للمسلم عند:
أ) العجز عن استعمال الماء.
ب) فقد الماء.
ج) جميع ما سبق.

passages.heading: من يباح لهم الفطر في رمضان؟
passages.text:
أباح الله عز وجل الفطر في نهار رمضان لعدة أصنافٍ من الناس، وهم:

1. المريض الذي يتضرر من الصوم.
2. الكبير في السن الذي يعجز عن الصوم.
3. المسافر أثناء سفره.
4. الحائض والنفساء.
5. الحامل والمرضع إذا خافتا على نفسيهما أو على ولدهما.

passages.heading: لماذا نصوم؟
passages.text:
يصوم المسلم:
- طاعةً لله تعالى، واستجابةً لأمره.
- تحقيق التقوى بالإكثار من العبادة وتقليل المعاصي.
- ليحرر نفسه من شهواتها، ويتدرب على ضبطها والتحكم فيها.
- ليشعر بألم الجوع الذي يصيب الفقراء والمحتاجين.

فرض الله عبادة الصوم على المسلمين وعلى غيرهم من الأمم السابقة، كما قال تعالى: {{Q:2:183}} (البقرة: ١٨٣).

passages.heading: شهر رمضان المبارك:
passages.text:
هو الشهر التاسع من السنة الهجرية وهو شهرٌ مبارك، أنزل الله فيه القرآن على رسوله محمد ﷺ. وجعل الله تعالى صوم نهاره، والصلاة في ليله سببًا لمغفرة الذنوب. وميَّزه الله تعالى بليلة هي أفضل من ألف شهر، وتسمى (ليلة القدر)، من أحياها بالذكر والصلاة غفر له ما تقدم من ذنبه.

يؤدي المسلمون صلاة التراويح في شهر رمضان، وهي من السنن المرتبطة به وتؤدى بعد صلاة العشاء.

passages.heading: ما حكم أكل الحيوانات البحرية ؟
passages.text:
الحيوانات المائية التي لا تعيش إلا في الماء يجوز أكل ميتتها، كالأسماك والربيان وغير ذلك، سواء كانت تعيش في البحار أو الأنهار أو البحيرات.

يجوز صيد الحيوانات البرية غير المفترسة وأكلها، بشرط ذكر اسم الله أثناء صيدها، وذبحها إذا وجدها حيةً.

passages.heading: ناقش
passages.text:
استعرض مع زملائك بعض المواقع التي تعينك على الحصول على الأطعمة المباحة في بلدك.

تختلف أحكام الذبائح التي تباع في المحلات والمطاعم بحسب ديانة من باشر ذبحها.

passages.heading: أن تكون من محارمه
passages.text: المقصود بالمحارم كل من يحرم على الرجل الزواج بها تحريماً مؤبداً مثل: الأم والأخت وابنة الأخت، وأخت الأب وأخت الأم وأم الزوجة، وهؤلاء يجوز لهن أن يخرجن أمام محارمهن بزينتهن التي تظهر الذراعين والرقبة والشعر ونحو ذلك بدون إسفاف أو تجاوز.

passages.heading: حجاب المرأة المسلمة:
passages.text: فرض الله الحجاب على المرأة دون الرجل لما أودع فيها من مظاهر الجمال وعوامل الإغراء، مما يجعلها فتنة للرجل أكثر من أن يكون الرجل فتنة لها، وحدود هذا الحجاب أن تغطي جميع بدنها عن الرجال الأجانب عنها، ولها أن تلبس ما شاءت من الأشكال والألوان مع مراعاة ثلاثة شروط:

passages.heading: الأول
passages.text: أن يكون الحجاب ساتراً لما يجب تغطيته.

passages.heading: الثاني
passages.text: أن يكون فضفاضاً واسعاً وليس ضيقاً يحدد أعضاء الجسم.

passages.heading: The Meaning of *Ghusl*
passages.text: *Ghusl*: Washing the entire body with water to remove the major ritual impurity.

passages.heading: How to Perform *Ghusl*?
passages.text:
To perform *ghusl*, one must wash the entire body with water, rinse out one’s mouth and clean one’s nose by sniffing water into the nostrils and ejecting it out by blowing one’s nose. A Muslim removes the major ritual impurity by simply doing so.

> The major ritual impurity: what must be removed by ghusl, and ablution is not sufficient, and these are types:
> 
> 1- *Janaabah*: The state of ritual impurity following intercourse or ejaculation as a result of an orgasm even if no intercourse takes place.
> 2- Menstruation: the normal vaginal bleeding that occurs as part of a woman’s monthly cycle.
> 3- Postnatal bleeding: The vaginal bleeding that takes place following childbirth.

passages.heading: Discuss
passages.text: What, in your opinion, does removing the major ritual impurity indicate?

passages.heading: The Manner of Performing the Full Ritual Bath (*Ghusl*)
passages.text:
If a Muslim wants to perform *ghusl*, he must do the following:

1. He intends in his heart to perform *ghusl* and washes out his private parts with water.
2. He performs *wudoo’* like the one he performs before the prayer.
3. He washes his entire body with water.

passages.heading: Things That a Person Who Is in a State of *Jannabah* Must Not Do
passages.text:
The state into which a person gets following intercourse or ejaculation and because of which he must perform *ghusl* is called *janaabah*, and he is described as *junub*. In this case, he is not allowed to do the following:

1. perform the prayer
2. circumambulate the Ka’bah (*tawaaf*)
3. touch or carry the Qur’an
4. stay in the mosque
5. read the Qur’an

passages.heading: Introduction
passages.text: There are some cases where *wudoo’* is not sufficient to perform an act of worship, but *ghusl* is required. In this lesson, we are going to learn about the meaning of *ghusl*, the reasons for performing it, as well as how to perform it.

passages.heading: When Does It Become Necessary to Perform *Ghusl*?

passages.heading: *Tayammum* (Dry Ablution)
passages.text:
If a person who wants to perform *wudoo’* or *ghusl* is unable to do so due to illness, or when water is not readily available, or for any other legitimate reason, he may resort to dry ablution (*tayammum*) instead.

The Manner of Performing *Tayammum*: (1) Intend in his heart to perform *tayammum* and strike both hands slightly on pure earth once, (2) wipe the face with them, (3) wipe the back of the right hand with the palm of the left, and then the back of the left hand with the palm of the right hand.

passages.heading: What shall I do if I find water after having performed *tayammum*?
passages.text: If a Muslim finds water or can use it, his purity becomes invalid, in which case he must perform *wudoo’* or *ghusl*.

passages.heading: The Position of Women in Islam
passages.text:
- Islam has granted women the right to inheritance, allocating them equitable shares with men, which sometimes differ under certain circumstances depending on their relationship with others and the financial obligations they have to discharge. While men support the family as a matter of religious obligation, women are not obliged to spend anything at all.
- It has established total equality between men and women in numerous matters including financial transactions.
- It has granted them the right to choose their own husbands.
- It has granted them the right to retain their maiden names. In Islam, a woman does not change her surname to that of her husband upon marriage; rather, she retains her maiden name, and thus her independent personality.
- It has made it the husband’s duty to spend on those women entitled to his support, such as his wife, mother and daughters, without attempting in the least to remind them of his favours.
- It stresses the importance of helping weak and vulnerable women who are in need of support, even if they are not one’s relatives, and urges its adherents to engage in such a noble act, which it considers one of the meritorious deeds in the sight of Allah.

passages.heading: The Qur’an is a Way of Life
passages.text:
The Holy Qur’an is the Word of the Lord of all the worlds, who has created all mankind, knows them better than they know themselves and knows what benefits them and what harms them, hence the reason why Allah Almighty has made the Qur’an, which was the last of His revealed books, a didactic book which maps out a way of life for people, as evidenced by the following points:

- It deals with human life extensively, taking into account its three intrinsic spheres: personal life, family life and community life.
- Its deals with a wide array of matters, including, among other things, beliefs, acts of worship, customs, social and financial relations, man’s mental, emotional and physical states, international relations and peace and war.
- It promotes justice under all circumstances, even when dealing with enemies, and forbids injustice in all its forms.

> The Holy Qur’an maps out the way of life for people and defines and explains to them their rights and obligations with great flexibility, making its laws valid for all times and places.

passages.heading: Stories of the Prophets in the Qur’an
passages.text:
The Holy Qur’an is replete with stories of the previous prophets and their people, starting with Adam, and passing through Noah, Hud, Saalih, Shu’ayb, Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, Moses, Jesus, and other prophets and messengers, peace be upon them all. The Holy Qur’an mentions their stories for a number of reasons, including the following:

- to show that the religion of all the prophets is, in essence, the same and that its basis is to worship Allah Almighty alone.
- to give solace to Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and make him stand firm and steadfast, reminding him that prophets before him suffered the same hardships he himself was experiencing.
- to give comfort and solace to the believers, reminding them that even Allah’s honourable servants before them were afflicted with trials and tribulations.
- to afford people the opportunity to learn lessons from such true stories.

passages.heading: The Blessing of Right Guidance
passages.text: Whoever knows the purpose of his existence and the outcome that awaits people on the Day of Resurrection is bound to realise that the greatest blessing that Allah has ever bestowed upon people is that of guidance to the true religion and righteous deeds. Therefore, Allah Almighty has enjoined His servants to ask Him in their prayer to guide them to the straight path—the religion of Islam which leads to Allah’s good pleasure.

passages.heading: Why Should I Embrace Islam?
passages.text:
Some people may ask: Why should I embrace Islam?

The answer is: I must do so for a number of reasons, including the following:

1. Islam is the religion that Allah has approved and chosen for His servants and will not accept any other religion. The Almighty says, {{Q:3:85}} (Soorat Aal-’Imraan, 3:85).

2. Islam is the religion of all the prophets and commands its adherents to believe in all of them without exception. Allah says, {{Q:2:136}} (Soorat Al-Baqarah, 2:136).
The difference between prophets lies only in the laws relating to people’s actions, as the Almighty says, {{Q:5:48}} (Soorat Al-Maa’idah, 5:48) That is, for each nation before Islam, Allah appointed a law to which people referred for their disputes and a way of life whereby they drew near to Him. Thus, followers of every prophet had their respective laws and regulations, but the set of beliefs to which prophets called their people was the same. Then Allah sent the last prophet and messenger, Muhammad ﷺ, with the final divine laws, and thus the only religion acceptable to Allah is Islam.

3. Islam is the way to happiness in this life and salvation in the life to come; therefore, those who believe in Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and follow him after his message has reached them will be saved; as for those who deny him, they will be doomed to divine punishment. The Almighty says, {{Q:3:85}} (*Soorat Aal-’Imraan, 3:85*) The Prophet ﷺ also said, “By Him in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, any person of this Community, Jew or Christian, who hears of me and dies without believing in what I have been sent with will be among the dwellers of Hell” (*Saheeh Muslim;* No. 153).

4. Islam gives conclusive answers to the big questions of human existence: Where did we come from? Why are we here? Where do we go after death?

5. Islam is in perfect harmony with the innate human nature (*fitrah*), beginning with the greatest value it embraces, namely the declaration of Allah’s unity, and ending with the rules of etiquette it teaches its adherents to enable them to attain great perfection in moral excellence.

passages.text: Islam is distinguished from other religions by many characteristics, the most prominent of which are:

passages.heading: 1 Islam is a Universal Religion
passages.text: Islam is not only for the Arabs; rather, it is the religion that Allah Almighty has approved for all mankind. Addressing His Messenger Muhammad ﷺ, the Almighty says, {{Q:21:107}} (*Soorat Al-Anbiyaa’, 21:107*). passages.heading: Muslim Women’s Modest Style of Dress (*Hijaab*)
passages.text:
Allah enjoins women to wear the *hijaab* because women enjoy natural beauty and attraction that could easily tempt men into sinful acts, more than the other way round. Women are to cover their entire bodies when in the presence of men who are not related to them, and they may choose any design or colour they like for their *hijaab* as long as the following four conditions are met:

| First Condition | Second Condition | Third condition | Fourth Condition |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| It must appropriately cover the parts of the body that must be covered in public. | It must hang loose and must not fit very closely to the body so that the shape of the body is not revealed. | It must not allow the wearer’s body to be seen through its fabric. | It must not be a type of clothing that is generally considered attractive. |

passages.heading: The Types of Blood that Are Naturally Discharged by Women
passages.text:
The blood that is naturally discharged by women is of two types:

| Menstrual blood | Postnatal blood |
| --- | --- |
| This is a natural type of blood that flows from a woman’s uterus every month during her menstrual cycle and usually lasts for a few days. | This bleeding takes place after giving birth and lasts for several days, up to 40 days. |

passages.heading: Islamic Rulings Pertaining to Menstrual and Postnatal Bleeding
passages.text:
Allah Almighty has prescribed several rulings relating to menstruating women and women experiencing their postnatal bleeding, including the following:

- They are exempt from performing the prayers during this period and do not have to make up for the prayers they have missed while in this state after the end of menstrual and postnatal bleeding.
- They are exempt from fasting and are not allowed to fast while in this state, but they must make up for the fasting days they have missed in Ramadaan.
- During this period, a husband must not have intercourse with his wife during her menstrual or postnatal period. He is allowed, however, to satisfy his sexual desire but without having intercourse.
- At the end of the menstrual and postnatal period, when bleeding stops completely, women must take a ritual bath (*ghusl*).

passages.heading: Benefits of Faith
passages.text:
* **Getting to know Allah Almighty:** A believer gets to know his Lord and His names, attributes and actions, so much so that he becomes more attached to Him.
* **Glorying Allah:** the more a believer gets to know his Lord, the more he extols and loves Him, the more he hopes for His mercy and the more God-fearing he becomes.
* **Getting to know Allah’s graciousness to His servants:** for sending messengers to them and divine books to them to guide them to the true religion.
* **Loving the angels:** for worshipping Allah and showing obedience to Him.
* **Loving Allah’s Messengers:** Allah Almighty chose them to convey His message to people.
* **Diligent worship:** the stronger the faith, the more worship one performs.
* **A truly happy life:** A believer is content with what Allah has apportioned to him and knows that whatever calamities befall him in this world elevate his rank and efface his sins. He also hopes for the bliss He has prepared for the believers in the life to come.
* **Not to be deluded by this world:** The life of this world is temporary and only serves as a means to eternal life in the hereafter.
* **Exposing myths:** Faith exposes and nullifies many myths.
* **Entering Paradise:** This is the abode of eternal bliss which Allah Almighty has prepared for His believing servants.

passages.heading: Types of Acts of Worship
passages.text:
Acts of worship fall into different categories:

| Acts of worship involving the heart | A Muslim performs these with his heart. Examples include love, fear, hope and *khushoo’*. |
| --- | --- |
| Physical acts of worship | A Muslim performs these physically. Examples include the prayer, *zakaat* and pilgrimage. |
| Acts that are abandoned in obedience to Allah | A Muslim draws closer to his Lord by abandoning the acts He has forbidden him, such as drinking alcohol and committing adultery, or by refraining from certain permissible acts at specific times, such as abstaining from food and drink while fasting. |

> *Ar-Rajaa’*(Hope): This refers to rejoicing in Allah’s grace and hoping for His benevolence, while at the same time ensuring proper reliance on Allah by doing good deeds to the best of one’s ability.
> 
> *Al-khushoo’* is a state of utter humility and calmness and deep concentration into which one gets while performing an act of worship, such as the prayer, bringing about outward composure and tranquillity.

Who is Required to Perform _Hajj_?
passages.text: Hajj is a religious obligation that must be carried out once in a lifetime by every able Muslim man and woman. Thus, anyone who is physically and financially able must perform the pilgrimage.

passages.heading: What is *Hajj*?
passages.text:
*Hajj* is an act of worship for which physically and financially able Muslims travel to Makkah to perform certain acts of worship during the month of Dhul-Hijjah, which is the last month of the lunar calendar.

*Hajj* is the fifth pillar of Islam

The Islamic *Hijri* Calendar is a lunar calendar is associated with the Prophet’s migration, or *hijrah*, from Makkah to Madeenah. Third Rightly-Guided Caliph ‘Umar ibn Al-Khattaab, may Allah be pleased with him, decided that the most appropriate reference point for the Islamic calendar would be the Prophet’s *hijrah*. The Islamic Calendar has twelve months, beginning with the month of Muharram and ending with the month of Dhul-Hijjah. Muslims have adopted the Islamic *Hijri* calendar to date incidents and events.

passages.heading: Important Notes Related to _Hajj_
passages.text:
- A Muslim cannot perform hajj except in a specific place, namely Makkah, and only at a specific time of the year.
- Hajj includes several acts of worship that a Muslim must learn before going to perform the pilgrimage.

Every year, Muslims from different countries perform hajj in large groups. Donning uniform simple clothing, both rich and poor appear to be the same with all social barriers and distinctions broken down.

passages.heading: Why Do We Perform *Hajj*?
passages.text: Muslims perform *Hajj* to the Sacred House in Makkah in response to Allah’s command to do so.

passages.heading: Introduction
passages.text: *Hajj*, the annual Muslim pilgrimage to Makkah, is one of the pillars of Islam and one of the best deeds whereby Muslims seek to draw closer to Allah Almighty. Its virtues are mentioned in numerous traditions of the Prophet ﷺ. In this lesson, we are going to learn a little information about this great act of worship.

passages.heading: Some of the Ultimate Objectives and Benefits of *Hajj*
passages.text:
- To follow the example of the honourable prophets who made the pilgrimage to the Sacred House.
- To occupy oneself with worship: Pilgrims devote themselves to the worship of Allah, moving from one act of worship to another.
- To meet Muslims who come from the four corners of the world and gather in the holy sites, get to know them and build bridges of communication with them.

passages.heading: Discuss
passages.text: Discuss this act of worship with your partners who have already performed *hajj* and find out from them about their feelings when they performed it.

passages.heading: *Tayammum* (Dry Ablution)
passages.text:
If a person who wants to perform *wudoo’* or *ghusl* is unable to do so due to illness, or when water is not readily available, or for any other legitimate reason, he may resort to dry ablution (*tayammum*) instead.

The Manner of Performing *Tayammum*: (1) Intend in his heart to perform *tayammum* and strike both hands slightly on pure earth once, (2) wipe the face with them, (3) wipe the back of the right hand with the palm of the left, and then the back of the left hand with the palm of the right hand.

passages.heading: The Manner of Performing *Wudoo’*
passages.text:

2. He washes his hands up to the wrists with water.
3. He rinses out his mouth thoroughly by moving water around in the mouth and then spitting it out. This process is called *madmadah*) in Arabic.
4. He cleans his nose by sniffing water into the nostrils and ejecting it out by blowing his nose.
5. He washes his face thoroughly from the hairline at the top of the forehead to the bottom of the chin, along with the beard, if he is bearded, and from ear to ear.
6. He washes his hands from the fingertips up to the elbow, starting with his right hand.
7. With wet hands, and starting with his hands flat on the top of the head near the hairline, he wipes it to the back of the neck and back to the front.

He wipes the inner sides of the ears with his index fingers and behind them with his thumbs.
9. He washes his feet up to the ankles, which are the two prominent bones of the joint connecting the foot to the leg, starting with his right foot.

passages.heading: Islamic Rulings Pertaining to Menstrual and Postnatal Bleeding
passages.text:
Allah Almighty has prescribed several rulings relating to menstruating women and women experiencing their postnatal bleeding, including the following:

- They are exempt from performing the prayers during this period and do not have to make up for the prayers they have missed while in this state after the end of menstrual and postnatal bleeding.
- They are exempt from fasting and are not allowed to fast while in this state, but they must make up for the fasting days they have missed in Ramadaan.
- During this period, a husband must not have intercourse with his wife during her menstrual or postnatal period. He is allowed, however, to satisfy his sexual desire but without having intercourse.
- At the end of the menstrual and postnatal period, when bleeding stops completely, women must take a ritual bath (*ghusl*).

passages.heading: Things That a Person Who Is in a State of *Jannabah* Must Not Do
passages.text:

2. circumambulate the Ka’bah (*tawaaf*)
3. touch or carry the Qur’an

passages.text:
If a Muslim wants to perform *ghusl*, he must do the following:

2. He performs *wudoo’* like the one he performs before the prayer.
3. He washes his entire body with water.

passages.heading: The Position of Women in Islam
passages.text:
- Islam has granted women the right to inheritance, allocating them equitable shares with men, which sometimes differ under certain circumstances depending on their relationship with others and the financial obligations they have to discharge. While men support the family as a matter of religious obligation, women are not obliged to spend anything at all.
- It has established total equality between men and women in numerous matters including financial transactions.
- It has granted them the right to choose their own husbands.
- It has granted them the right to retain their maiden names. In Islam, a woman does not change her surname to that of her husband upon marriage; rather, she retains her maiden name, and thus her independent personality.
- It has made it the husband’s duty to spend on those women entitled to his support, such as his wife, mother and daughters, without attempting in the least to remind them of his favours.
- It stresses the importance of helping weak and vulnerable women who are in need of support, even if they are not one’s relatives, and urges its adherents to engage in such a noble act, which it considers one of the meritorious deeds in the sight of Allah.

passages.heading: What shall I do if I find water after having performed *tayammum*?
passages.text: If a Muslim finds water or can use it, his purity becomes invalid, in which case he must perform *wudoo’* or *ghusl*.

passages.text: If a Muslim wants to perform his ablutions (*wudoo’*), he must do the following:

passages.heading: How Many Times Do We Wash the Parts of the Body that Are Usually Washed in *Wudoo’*?
passages.text: According to the *Sunnah*, each part of the body is washed three times, except in the case of the head and ears, which are wiped only once. It would suffice, however, to wash these body parts once provided that they are washed thoroughly.

passages.heading: Things That Render *Wudoo’* Invalid
passages.text:
*Wudoo’* becomes invalid as a result of four things:

- Natural discharges from the private parts (both the external genital and excretory organs), such as urine, excrement, wind, semen and the clear, colourless, viscous fluid that is emitted during sexual arousal
- Loss of consciousness due to sleep or intoxication
- Lustfully touching the private parts with bare hands
- Eating camel meat

passages.heading: The Friday Prayer (Salaat-ul-Jumu’ah)
passages.text:
- Allah Almighty has enjoined Muslims to perform a special prayer on Friday, called *Salaat-ul-Jumu’ah* (the Friday prayer). It is performed in a special manner, has special conditions and takes the place of the daily *Dhuhr* (midday) prayer on this day.
- Muslims gather together to perform it in the mosque. The *imaam* delivers a two-section *khutbah* (sermon), then he leads them in a two-*rak’ahs* prayer in which he recites the Qur’an aloud.
- It is recommended to take a ritual bath (*ghusl*) to attend the Friday prayer and proceed early to the mosque. It is not permissible to miss it without a legitimate excuse, and if for any reason a person misses it he must perform the four-unit *Dhuhr* (midday) prayer instead but without reciting the Qur’an aloud.
- Women and people on a journey are exempt from performing the Friday prayer.

passages.heading: سورة العصر:
ما هي شروط الذكاة الشرعية ؟
passages.text:
الذكاة الشرعية هي الذبح أو النحر المستوفي للشروط التالية:

1. أن يكون الذابح مسلماً أو يهودياً أو نصرانياً يميز ويقصد الذكاة.
2. أن تكون الآلة صالحة للذبح وتُجري الدم وتقطع بحدها كالسكين، ويحرم استخدام ما يقتلها بثقله واصطدامه برأس الحيوان، أو بحرقه كالصعق الكهربائي.
3. أن يذكر اسم الله فيقول: (بسم الله) عند تحريك يده للذبح.
4. قطع ما يجب قطعه في الذكاة، وهو: المريء، والحلقوم، والودجان وهما العرقان الكبيران في الرقبة، أو قطع ثلاثة من هذه الأربعة.

2. ما ذبحه المسلم أو الكتابي بالطريقة الشرعية فهذا جائز بنص القرآن.

4. الأصل جواز ذبيحة الكتابي وما يوجد في مطاعمهم ومحلاتهم، وإن لم نتحقق من طريقة ذبحها، مع الحرص على التسمية عند الأكل. والأولى للمسلم ألا يأكل إلا ما تحقق من كونه من لحوم الحلال المباحة.

passages.heading: What Is Fasting?
passages.text:
Fasting: an act of worship whereby a Muslim abstains from food, drink and sexual intercourse from dawn to sunset.

Fasting in the month of Ramadaan is the fourth pillar of Islam.

passages.heading: Why Do We Fast?
passages.text: Muslims fast in obedience to Allah Almighty and in response to His command.

passages.heading: Some of the Ultimate Objectives and Benefits of Fasting
passages.text:
- To attain true piety by increasing acts of worship and avoiding sins as much as possible.
- To experience the pangs of hunger from which the poor and needy often suffer.
- To train oneself to bring one’s whims and desires under control.

Allah has enjoined fasting on Muslims, just as He prescribed it on the other nations before them:
{{Q:2:183}} (Soorat Al-Baqarah, 2:183).

passages.heading: The Qur’an is a Way of Life
passages.text:
The Holy Qur’an is the Word of the Lord of all the worlds, who has created all mankind, knows them better than they know themselves and knows what benefits them and what harms them, hence the reason why Allah Almighty has made the Qur’an, which was the last of His revealed books, a didactic book which maps out a way of life for people, as evidenced by the following points:

- It deals with human life extensively, taking into account its three intrinsic spheres: personal life, family life and community life.
- Its deals with a wide array of matters, including, among other things, beliefs, acts of worship, customs, social and financial relations, man’s mental, emotional and physical states, international relations and peace and war.
- It promotes justice under all circumstances, even when dealing with enemies, and forbids injustice in all its forms.

> The Holy Qur’an maps out the way of life for people and defines and explains to them their rights and obligations with great flexibility, making its laws valid for all times and places.

passages.heading: Stories of the Prophets in the Qur’an
passages.text:
The Holy Qur’an is replete with stories of the previous prophets and their people, starting with Adam, and passing through Noah, Hud, Saalih, Shu’ayb, Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, Moses, Jesus, and other prophets and messengers, peace be upon them all. The Holy Qur’an mentions their stories for a number of reasons, including the following:

- to show that the religion of all the prophets is, in essence, the same and that its basis is to worship Allah Almighty alone.
- to give solace to Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and make him stand firm and steadfast, reminding him that prophets before him suffered the same hardships he himself was experiencing.
- to give comfort and solace to the believers, reminding them that even Allah’s honourable servants before them were afflicted with trials and tribulations.
- to afford people the opportunity to learn lessons from such true stories.

passages.heading: Comment prions-nous ?
passages.text:
Lorsque le musulman souhaite prier, il doit accomplir les étapes suivantes :

1. Il doit avoir l’intention de la prière dans son cœur.

2. Il se tient debout en se dirigeant vers la Qiblah, il lève ses mains à hauteur de ses épaules ou de ses oreilles et il dit: “Allah est plus Grand [que tout] (Allah Akbar).“

7. Il relève sa tête en disant : «Allah est Plus Grand [que tout].» Il s’assied sur son pied gauche, le pied droit restant droit, il place ses paumes sur ses cuisses et pendant qu’il est assis il dit : «Seigneur ! Pardonne-moi.»

8. Il se prosterne encore une fois comme lors de la première prosternation et là pendant qu’il se penche en vue de la prosternation il dit : «Allah est Plus Grand [que tout].» Et il fait dans sa seconde prosternation ce qu’il a fait dans la première prosternation.

9. Il relève sa tête et il se lève en vue de la seconde unité de prière, et là il dit : «Allah est Plus Grand [que tout].» Puis, il prie la seconde unité de prière exactement comme il a prié la première (unité de prière).
