passages.text: Il a encouragé à nourrir les affamés et vêtir les besogneux, et tout cela afin que la société musulmane soit unies et liées et que les musulmans soient comme le veut Allah (Exalté et Magnifié soit-Il). Et dans cette leçon, nous allons apprendre le jugement de l’aumône légale (Az-Zakât), sa manière et les biens sur lesquels elle est obligatoire.

passages.heading: 1. Premièrement : la signification qu’Il n’y a aucune divinité digne d’adoration excepté Allah.
passages.text:
Sa signification est : J’atteste qu’il n’y a aucune divinité digne d’adoration excepté Allah :  
C’est-à-dire : Je crois d’une croyance catégorique et profonde qu’il n’y a aucune divinité méritant l’adoration excepté Allah l’Unique.

Cette attestation englobe deux éléments :

| Le premier : | Le second : |
| --- | --- |
| La négation de la divinité à autre qu’Allah (Élevé soit-Il) | L’affirmation de la divinité à Allah, Seul. |

passages.heading: Pourquoi embrasser l’Islam ?
passages.text: C’est-à-dire : Allah a établi pour chaque communauté parmi les communautés une législation vers laquelle ils reviennent pour juger et une voie à travers laquelle ils se rapprochent de Lui. En effet, tout peuple ayant une croyance a des jugements qui lui sont spécifiques et des législations qui lui conviennent. Mais en ce qui concerne la croyance, alors la croyance des prophètes est unique et identique.

passages.heading: Leçon 3
passages.text:
### Comment embrasser l'Islam ?

Le principe profond de la religion de l’Islam, qui est la religion de tous les prophètes, est l’adoration d’Allah, Seul, et la mécréance envers tout ce qui est adoré en dehors de Lui. Allah (Élevé soit-Il) a dit : {{Q:21:25}} (al Anbiyâ, 21 : 25).

Ainsi donc, il n’est pas permis en aucune circonstance de croire en la divinité de quoi que ce soit d’autre qu’Allah (Élevé soit-Il) et il n’est pas permis de se rapprocher d’autre qu’Allah (Élevé soit-Il) par quelconque type d’adoration.

**2. Deuxièmement : La signification de l’attestation que Muhammad est le Messager d’Allah.**

La signification de : “ J’atteste que Muhammad est le Messager d’Allah. “ : C’est-à-dire : je crois d’une croyance catégorique et profonde que Muhammad ﷺ est le Messager d’Allah et qu’il est le sceau des prophètes. Ainsi donc, il n’y a plus de prophète après lui et son message s’adresse à tous les hommes. Il (Glorifié et Élevé soit-Il) a dit : {{Q:25:1}} (Al Fourqâne, 25 : 1).

passages.heading: L’apprentissage de la religion :
passages.text:
- incombe au musulman d’apprendre ce dont il a besoin concernant sa religion, de sorte qu’il adore son Seigneur avec connaissance.
- Et le Prophète ﷺ a encouragé à s’instruire religieusement. En effet, il ﷺ a dit :”Celui à qui Allah veut du bien, Il lui fait comprendre la Religion. “Rapporté par Al Boukhârî (n°71).
- Le Prophète ﷺ a informé que la recherche de la science religieuse est une voie d’entrée au Paradis. En effet, il ﷺ a dit :” Quiconque emprunte une voie à la recherche d’un savoir, Allah lui facilite une voie vers le Paradis. “Rapporté par Mouslim (n°2699).

passages.heading: Sourate : al Kawthar :
Les cinq prières :
passages.text:
Allah (Exalté et Magnifié soit-Il) a imposé à Ses serviteurs de prier, de jour comme de nuit, cinq prières. Elles sont:

| La prière | Début de son temps | Fin de son temps | Nombre d’unités de prière |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :---: |
| La prière de l’aube (Al Fajr) | Le lever de l’aube. | Le lever du soleil. | 2 |
| La prière du midi (Az-Zuhr) | L’inclinaison du soleil (qui est son penchement en direction de l’Ouest à la mi-journée) | lorsque l’ombre d’une chose est équivalente à sa longueur. | 4 |
| La prière de l’après-midi (Al ‘Asr) | lorsque l’ombre d’une chose est équivalente à sa longueur. | Le coucher du soleil. | 4 |
| La prière du coucher (Al Maghrib) | Le coucher du soleil. | Disparition du crépuscule rouge. | 3 |
| La prière du soir (Al ‘Ichâ’) | Disparition du crépuscule rouge. | Milieu de la nuit. | 4 |

passages.heading: Comment prions-nous ?
passages.text:
3. Il pose sa main droite sur sa main gauche, ensuite il récite une des invocations de l’ouverture de la prière, comme:  
“Gloire à Toi, ô Allah, et à Toi la louange. Que Ton nom soit béni, que Ta majesté soit élevée et il n’y a aucune divinité [digne d’adoration] autre que Toi.“  
Ensuite, il dit:  
“Je me réfugie auprès d’Allah contre Satan le lapidé. Au nom d’Allah, le Tout Miséricordieux, le Très Miséricordieux.“  
Puis, il récite la sourate: L’Ouverture (Al Fâtiha) et à la fin de sa lecture il dit : “Âmîn.“ Et la signification de : “ Âmîn “ désigne: “ Ô Allah ! Exauce notre invocation.“  
Ensuite, après la lecture de la sourate: Al Fâtiha, il récite ce qu’il peut de ce qu’il a mémorisé du noble Coran, même si c’est un seul verset.

passages.heading: Comment prions-nous ?
passages.text:
4. Il lève ses mains à hauteur de ses épaules ou ses oreilles et il dit : «Allah est plus grand [que tout].»  
Il penche son dos en s’inclinant, en posant ses mains sur ses genoux et en alignant droit son dos et sa tête au même niveau. Et pendant son inclinaison, il dit : «Gloire à mon Seigneur, le Majestueux.» Trois fois.

5. Il relève sa tête pour revenir droit, tout en levant les mains à hauteur de ses épaules. Et là il dit: “Allah a entendu quiconque L’a loué.“ Puis, il dit en étant debout et droit: “Notre Seigneur ! La louange T’appartient.“

6. Il tombe prosterné sur le sol, en plaçant son front et son nez sur le sol, tout en plaçant ses paumes, ses genoux et les extrémités de ses orteils sur le sol, et là il dit : «Gloire à mon Seigneur, le Plus-Haut.» Trois fois.

passages.heading: Leçon 6
passages.text:
10. Après la seconde prosternation dans la seconde unité de prière, il s’assoit comme il s’est assit entre les deux prosternations et là il dit: Les salutations appartiennent à Allah ainsi que les prières et les bonnes œuvres. Que le salut soit sur toi, ô Prophète, ainsi que la miséricorde d’Allah et Ses bénédictions. Que le salut soit sur nous et sur les vertueux serviteurs d’Allah. J’atteste qu’il n’y a aucune divinité [digne d’adoration] excepté Allah et j’atteste que Muhammad est Son serviteur et Son Messager. (At-Tahiyâtou Lillahi Was-Salawâtou Wat-Tayyibât. As-Salâmou ‘Alayka Ayouhâ an-Nabiyou Wa Rahmatou Allâh Wa Barakâtouh. As-Salâmou ‘Alaynâ Wa ‘Alâ ‘Ibâdi Llâhi as-Sâlihîn. Achhadou Al-La Ilâha Ila Allâh Wa Achhadou Anna Muhammadan ‘Abdouhou Wa Rassoûlouhou) On appelle ceci: le premier Tachahoud. Ensuite, après cela, il dit: “ Ô Allah ! Prie sur Muḥammad et sur la famille de Muḥammad comme Tu as prié sur Abraham et sur la famille d’Abraham. Certes, Tu es digne de louange et de glorification. Ô Allah ! Bénis Muḥammad et la famille de Muḥammad comme Tu as béni Abraham et la famille d’Abraham [à travers l’univers]. Certes, Tu es digne de louange et de glorification. “
On l’appelle : La prière Abrahamique.

passages.heading: Leçon 6
passages.text:
11. Il se tourne sur sa droite et dit : “Paix sur vous ainsi que la miséricorde d’Allah. “Ensuite, il se tourne sur sa gauche et dit la même chose. Et ainsi sa prière se termine.

Cette description concerne la prière de deux unités, comme celle de l’aube (Al Fajr) et du vendredi (Al Jumu’ah). Toutefois, s’il y a trois unités de prière, comme celle du coucher (Al Maghrib) ou quatre unités de prière, comme celle du midi (Az-Zuhr), de l’après-midi (Al ‘Asr) et du soir (Al ‘Ichâ’), alors après avoir terminé le premier Tachahoud, il complète ce qui reste des unités de prières comme dans la première unité de prière sauf qu’il ne lit rien après Al Fâtiha. Ensuite, il s’assied comme il s’est assis après la seconde unité de prière et là il dit le premier Tachahoud, puis la prière Abrahamique et enfin il salue.

passages.heading: Avant-propos
passages.text: Depuis fort longtemps, les êtres humains qui vivent à la surface de cette Terre occupent différents niveaux : parmi eux, il y a le riche qui possède argent et biens de manière abondante; il y a aussi le pauvre qui ne trouve pas sa portion, etc. Et ceci est une des traditions immuables d’Allah dans cet univers. L’Islam a rendu obligatoire un impôt déduit de la richesse des riches qui doit être reversé aux pauvres pour les aider et les alléger du fardeau de la pauvreté. L’Islam a incité le musulman à dépenser du surplus de son argent. Et pour récompense, le musulman recevra durant sa vie et après sa mort une immense rétribution. De même, il a incité à la bienfaisance envers les pauvres en tout temps et en toute occasion.

passages.heading: Qu’est-ce que l’aumône légale?
passages.text: L’aumône légale consiste à reverser une part déterminée des biens des musulmans riches aux musulmans pauvres. C’est le troisième des piliers de l’Islam.

passages.heading: Pourquoi nous acquittons-nous de l’aumône légale?
passages.text: Nous nous acquittons de l’aumône légale afin de mettre en pratique l’ordre d’Allah, Celui qui nous a imposé l’aumône légale.

passages.heading: Les deux attestations :
passages.text:
Allah (Exalté et Magnifié soit-Il) a fait de la prononciation de ces deux attestations la clé d’entrée en l’Islam. Celle-ci est :

- J’atteste qu’il n’y a aucune divinité [digne d’adoration] excepté Allah.
- et j’atteste que Muhammad est le Messager d’Allah.

passages.heading: Ce qu’implique les deux attestions :
passages.text: Il ne suffit pas seulement de prononcer les deux attestations. Toutefois, il faut en connaître leur signification et agir selon ce qu’elles impliquent. Ainsi, l’attestation : “ Il n’y a aucune divinité [digne d’adoration] excepté Allah “ implique de mécroire en tout ce qui est adoré en dehors d’Allah (Élevé soit-Il) et la foi en Allah, le Seul Seigneur et Dieu qui mérite l’adoration, une adoration lui étant vouée exclusivement. Allah (Élevé soit-Il) a dit : {{Q:2:256}} (al Baqara, 2 : 256). L’attestation de : “ Muhammad est le Messager d’Allah “ implique de croire véridiquement à ce qu’il dit, lui obéir dans ce qu’il a ordonné ou interdit et de n’adorer Allah que selon ce qu’il a apporté.

passages.heading: Discute
passages.text:
Pourquoi l’attestation de : “ Il n’y a aucune divinité [digne d’adoration] excepté Allah “ implique de mécroire en l’ensemble de ce qui est adoré en dehors d’Allah ?

Partage avec tes camarades l’énumération des raisons pour lesquelles certaines personnes tiennent à inventer des types de dieux et appellent les gens à leur adoration...

Parmi les preuves rationnelles que le prophète d’Allah Abraham (paix sur lui) a argumenté avec son peuple, il y avait la question qu’il leur avait adressée: {{Q:37:95}} (As Saffât, 37 : 95).

passages.heading: Leçon 2
passages.text: ### Exégèse des sourates courtes

passages.heading: Sourate : al ‘Asr :
passages.text:
Signification de la sourate :

{{Q:103:1-3}}

{Par le temps !} Allah a juré par le temps durant lequel agissent les fils d’Adam, en bien ou en mal.

{Certes, l’homme est vraiment en perdition.} Les êtres humains sont vraiment dans la perdition et la ruine.

{Excepté ceux qui ont cru, ont accompli les œuvres vertueuses, se sont recommandés la vérité, et se sont recommandés la patience.} Excepté ceux qui ont cru en Allah, ont accompli les œuvres vertueuses, se sont mutuellement recommandés les uns les autres l’attachement à la vérité, son affermissement dessus et la patience sur cela.

passages.heading: ¿Cuándo tengo que repetir la ablución menor?
passages.text: Cuando el musulmán realiza la ablución menor, queda puro hasta realizar uno de los actos mencionados anteriormente que anulan la ablución menor.

passages.heading: ¿Qué tengo que hacer al encontrar agua después de haber realizado la ablución seca (tayamum)?
passages.text: Cuando el musulmán encuentra agua o es capaz de usarla sin causarle daño, en este caso se anula su ablución seca y debe realizar la ablución menor o mayor con agua.

passages.heading: ¿Por qué debo volverme musulmán?
passages.text:
Algunos pueden preguntarse: ¿Por qué tengo que convertirme al Islam?

Y la respuesta es: debo ser musulmán por las razones siguientes:

La primera: el Islam es la sola religión aceptada por Al-láh a sus siervos y no aceptará ninguna aparte de ella. Al-láh -Enaltecido sea- dice: {{Q:3:85}} Corán (3: 85).

La segunda: el Islam es la religión de todos los profetas, invita a creer en todos ellos, sin discriminar entre ellos. Al-láh -Enaltecido sea- dice: {{Q:2:136}} Corán (2:136).

La diferencia entre los profetas consiste en una diferencia de legislaciones relacionadas con las acciones de las personas, por ello Al-láh- Glorificado sea- dijo: {{Q:5:48}} Corán (5: 48).

Es decir: cada nación tiene una legisalción propia, una manera propia para acercarse a Al-láh con la adoración, entonces cada nación tiene normas legales propias, pero el credo de todos los profetas es igual y no cambia.

Tercero: Convertirse al Islam es el camino a la felicidad en esta vida y a la salvación en la otra vida, ya que no se salva en la otra vida sino quien al recibir el mensaje del profeta Muhammad -que la paz y las bendiciones de Al-láh sean con él- haya creído en él y le haya seguido, Al-láh-Enaltecido sea- dice: {{Q:3:85}} Corán (3: 85)

El profeta -que la paz y las bendiciones de Al-láh sean con él- dijo:» Juro por Aquel que posee mi alma en Su mano que, si una persona de este pueblo sea judío o cristiano, oye mi Mensaje y muere sin haber creído en él, será de la gente del infierno». Narrado por Muslim 153.

Cuarto: El Islam responde con respuestas evidentes a mis preguntas: ¿Por qué estoy en esta vida? ¿De dónde vine? y ¿A dónde iré después de la muerte?

passages.heading: A discutir
passages.text: ¿Qué pierde la persona que presume en sus actos de adoración al dejar la sinceridad?

passages.heading: Los tipos de adoración:
passages.text:
La adoración se divide en varios tipos:

* **Adoraciones del corazón.** Las realiza el musulmán con su corazón; como el amor, el temor, la esperanza y la devoción a Al-lah -Exaltado sea.

> La esperanza: es esperar los favores de Al-láh, Su Bondad y Sus gracias haciendo el esfuerzo necesario y con una confianza plena en Al-láh.
>
> La reverencia: es una postura del alma al sentir la tranquilidad y el desinterés por cualquier preocupación al realizar la adoración como la oración, y su influencia se muestra en la tranquilidad de los órganos del cuerpo.

* **Adoraciones corporales:** Las realiza el musumán con su cuerpo; como la oración, la Zakat y el peregrinaje

* **Actos que al no realizarlos se considera adoración.** El musulmán también adora a su Señor dejando lo que se le prohibió; como no beber sustancias embriagantes, no cometer adulterio, o al dejar algunos actos permitidos por unos tiempos específicos, tal como abstenerse de comer y beber durante el ayuno.

passages.heading: Preámbulo
passages.text: El Islam es la religión con la cual Al-láh envió a Muhammad -que la paz y las bendiciones de Al-láh sean con él- y es una continuación de lo que han transmitido los enviados anteriores. Se basa en la adoración de un Dios Único que merece ser adorado solo sin socios, es decir Al-láh -Enaltecido y Exaltado sea- no tiene socio en Su reinado, no existe intermedio entre Él y Sus siervos. Pero ¿Por qué tengo que convertirme al Islam? ¿Acaso el Islam es una religión propia de los árabes o es para toda la humanidad? ¿Quién es el mensajero enviado para transmitir esta religión? ¿Habrá un mensajero después de él?

passages.heading: ¿Por qué debo volverme musulmán?
passages.text: Luego Al-láh envió al sello de los profetas y mensajeros: el profeta Muhammad -que la paz y las bendiciones de Al-láh sean con él- que es el último enviado, su legislación fue la última establecida, por ello no se aceptará ninguna otra religión fuera del Islam.

passages.heading: A discutir
passages.text: ¿Menciona algunos de los medios que facilitan el aprendizaje de la ablución menor y de su práctica de manera correcta?

passages.heading: El Maseh sobre los juffain (pasar la mano húmeda sobre los calcetines):
passages.text:
Si la persona que va a realizar la ablución menor está llevando unos calcetines, entonces le está permitido pasar las manos mojadas sobre la parte externa de los pies, sin necesitadad de quitarse los calcetines ni lavarse los pies. Para realizar el Maseh se debe cumplir tres condiciones:

**Primero:**  
que los calcetines estén en estado de pureza.

**Segundo:**  
que los calcetines cubran los pies y los tobillos.

**Tercero:**  
que el período del Maseh no supere las 24 horas para el residente y los 72 horas para el viajero.

El período del Maseh inicia desde la realización del Maseh por primera vez.

passages.heading: Taiámmum (ablución seca):
passages.text: Cuando la persona que debe realizar la ablución menor o mayor es incapaz de realizarlas por la falta de agua, o por una enfermedad u otra causa, en este caso es permitido para él realizar la ablución seca (tayamum). La forma de realizarla es tener la intención en el corazón (sin pronunciarla), tocar con sus dos manos el suelo una sola vez, luego pasar sus manos sobre su cara, luego sus manos.

Quinto: El Islam es una religión que coincide con la inclinación natural del ser humano, desde el valor más importante que presenta -que es el Monoteísmo- hasta llegar a los buenos modales hacia los cuales invita.

passages.heading: A discutir
passages.text: ¿Cómo puede ser que el Islam sea la religión de todos los profetas?

passages.heading: تنبيهات متعلقة بالحج:
passages.text:
- لا يمكن للمسلم أداء الحج إلا في مكان مخصوص هو (مكة)، وفي وقت مخصوص من السنة.
- يشتمل الحج على عدد من العبادات التي ينبغي على المسلم تعلمها قبل ذهابه لأداء الحج.

يؤدي الحج في كل عام مجموعة من المسلمين من دول مختلفة، ويتوحدون في لباسهم فلا يكون هناك تمييز بين الغني والفقير منهم.

passages.heading: على من يجب الحج؟
passages.text: يجب الحج مرة واحدة في العمر على من يقدر عليه من المسلمين والمسلمات، فكل من قدر على الحج جسديًا وماليًا فإن الحج واجب عليه.

passages.heading: موجبات الوضوء:
passages.text:
> الحدث: وصف معنوي في الإنسان يمنعه من أداء الصلاة قبل أن يتطهر وليس شيئًا محسوسًا كالنجاسة، وهو نوعين أحدهما يلزم المسلم التوضأ لرفعه والآخر لا يُرفع إلا بالغُسل.

موجبات الوضوء هي الأمور التي يُشترط الوضوءُ لها، ويجب من أجلها، وإذا أحدث الشخصُ حَرُمَت عليه، وهي:

1. الصلاة
2. الطواف حول الكعبة
3. مس المصحف

passages.heading: تمهيد
passages.text: من أكثر اللحظات التي لا ينساها المسلم الجديد، هي لحظة إعلان دخوله الإسلام من خلال نطقه للشهادتين، فبهذا الإعلان يُعلن لنفسه قبل أي أحد أنه غدا شيئًا آخر غير ما كان، وأنه منذ هذه اللحظات خطى خطواته الأولى نحو معرفة الحق والتمسك به. وفي هذا الدرس سنتعرف على الشهادتين ومعناهما ولوازمهما على المسلم.

يجوز للمسلم أن يصلي الفريضة حتى قبل أن يدخل وقتها.
صح
خطأ

ينتهي وقت صلاة الفجر عند شروق الشمس.
صح
خطأ

passages.heading: تمهيد
passages.text: يُعد الحج أحد أركان الإسلام، وهو من أفضل الأعمال التي يتقرَّب بها المسلم إلى الله عز وجل، وقد ورد في فضله أحاديث كثيرة عن الرسول ﷺ، وفي هذا الدرس سنتعرف على معلومات يسيرة عن هذه الشعيرة العظيمة.

passages.heading: فائدة
passages.text: يحترم الإسلام عادات الشعوب وتقاليدهم ولا يلزمهم بتغييرها إلا إذا خالفت شيئًا من شعائر الإسلام وتعاليمه.

passages.heading: ما هو الحج؟
passages.text:
الحج: عبادة يذهب لأجلها المسلم المستطيع إلى مكة المكرمة للقيام بعبادات معينة في شهر ذي الحجة، وهو الشهر الأخير من السنة الهجرية.

والحج هو الركن الخامس من أركان الإسلام.

السنة الهجرية: هي إشارةٌ إلى الهجرة النبوية المباركة من مكة المكرمة إلى المدينة النبوية، وقد اختار الخليفة عمر بن الخطاب ؓ يوم هجرة الرسول ﷺ ليكون بداية لحساب التاريخ الإسلامي الهجري. وللسنة الهجرية إثنا عشر شهر تبدء بشهر (محرم) وتنتهي بشهر (ذي الحجة)، وقد اعتمد المسلمون التأريخ للحوادث والوقائع بالسنة الهجرية منذ السنة الأولى للهجرة والتي تقابلها سنة ٦٢٢ ميلادية.

passages.heading: ناقش
passages.text: يحتاج وضع موضوع مناسب للنقاش:

passages.heading: معنى الوضوء:
passages.text: **الوضوء:** غسل الوجه واليدين والرجلين بصفة معينة.

passages.heading: كيف نتوضأ؟
passages.text:
إذا أراد المسلم أن يتوضأ فعليه القيام بالخطوات الآتية:

1. يقول: «بسم الله».
2. يغسل كفيّه بالماء مبتدئًا باليمنى.
3. ينظف فمه بإدخال الماء فيه، ثم يحركه، ثم يخرجه.
4. ينظف أنفه بإدخال الماء فيه مع الاستنشاق، ثم يخرجه مع نفخ الهواء من أنفه.
5. يغسل وجه كاملًا، وحدوده طولًا من منابت الشعر في أعلى الجبهة إلى أسفل الذقن، مع شعر اللحية إن وجدت، وحدوده عرضًا من الأذن إلى الأذن.
6. يغسل يديه من أطراف الأصابع إلى مفصل المرفق، مبتدئًا بيده اليمنى.
7. يبلل يديه بالماء، ثم يمسح بهما رأسه، مبتدئًا بمقدمة الرأس إلى القفا، ثم يعيد يديه إلى الأمام.
8. يمسح أذنيه بأصبعيه السبابتين داخل الأذنين، ويمسح خلف الأذنين بالإبهامين.
9. يغسل قدميه إلى الكعبين، وهما العظمان البارزان في مفصل القدم، مبتدئًا برجله اليمنى.

passages.heading: Important Notes Related to Fasting
passages.text:
- Whoever breaks his fast in Ramadaan for a legitimate reason must make up for every day he has missed after than Ramadaan.
- If a sick person breaks the fast because of an incurable disease, he is exempt from fasting the month of Ramadaan, but he must feed one poor person for each day he does not fast.
- If a Muslim cannot possibly fast due to old age, he is exempt from fasting the month of Ramadaan but he must feed one poor person for each day he does not fast.

**Muslims break their fast as soon as the call to *Maghrib* (sunset) prayer is announced, and many Muslims are very keen to share their Ramadaan breakfast, or *iftar*, with fellow Muslims.**

passages.heading: The Types of People Who Are Exempt from Fasting
passages.text:
Allah Almighty has permitted several types of people to break their fast during the day in Ramadaan. They are:

1. Sick people whose medical condition is bound to be further worsened by fasting.
2. The elderly who are unable to fast.
3. Travellers, while moving from one place to another.
4. Menstruating women and women experiencing postnatal bleeding.
5. Pregnant and nursing mothers if they fear it would be dangerous for them or for their babies if they fast.

passages.heading: Things that render the Fast Invalid
passages.text:
The fasting person must abstain from several things which, if he does them, his fast will be invalid. They are:

1. Eating and drinking, including intravenous injections which have some nutritional value.
2. Deliberate seminal emission as a result of intercourse or any other means. Intercourse during the day in Ramadaan is a grave sin.
3. Deliberate vomiting.

A woman’s fast is broken as a result of:

4. Menstrual or postnatal bleeding.

passages.heading: When do I have to perform wudoo’ again?
passages.text: If a Muslim performs wudoo’, the general rule is that his wudoo’ is still valid unless one of the previously-mentioned things that break wudoo’ happens, in which case he must perform it again.

passages.heading: The Blessed Month of Ramadaan
passages.text:
Ramadaan is the ninth month of the Islamic lunar calendar. It is a blessed month, in which Allah revealed the Qur’an to His Messenger, Muhammad ﷺ. Allah has promised to forgive all the past sins of those who fast during the daylight hours and stands in prayer at night throughout this month. The Almighty has also distinguished it with a night that is better than a thousand months. It is called *Laylat-ul-Qadr* (The Night of Decree; also called the Night of Power), and whoever spends it remembering Allah and standing in prayer will have all his past sins forgiven.

Muslims perform the *Taraaweeh* prayer in the month of Ramadaan. It is one of the Prophet’s practices (*Sunnah*) that is particularly associated with it, and it is performed after *'Ishaa’* (late evening) prayer.

passages.heading: Some of the Ultimate Objectives and Benefits of Fasting

- To experience the pangs of hunger from which the poor and needy often suffer.
- To train oneself to bring one’s whims and desires under control.

passages.heading: The Position of Women in Islam
passages.text:
- Islam has granted women the right to inheritance, allocating them equitable shares with men, which sometimes differ under certain circumstances depending on their relationship with others and the financial obligations they have to discharge. While men support the family as a matter of religious obligation, women are not obliged to spend anything at all.
- It has established total equality between men and women in numerous matters including financial transactions.
- It has granted them the right to choose their own husbands.
- It has granted them the right to retain their maiden names. In Islam, a woman does not change her surname to that of her husband upon marriage; rather, she retains her maiden name, and thus her independent personality.
- It has made it the husband’s duty to spend on those women entitled to his support, such as his wife, mother and daughters, without attempting in the least to remind them of his favours.
- It stresses the importance of helping weak and vulnerable women who are in need of support, even if they are not one’s relatives, and urges its adherents to engage in such a noble act, which it considers one of the meritorious deeds in the sight of Allah.

passages.heading: Islamic Rulings Pertaining to Menstrual and Postnatal Bleeding
passages.text:
Allah Almighty has prescribed several rulings relating to menstruating women and women experiencing their postnatal bleeding, including the following:

- They are exempt from performing the prayers during this period and do not have to make up for the prayers they have missed while in this state after the end of menstrual and postnatal bleeding.
- They are exempt from fasting and are not allowed to fast while in this state, but they must make up for the fasting days they have missed in Ramadaan.
- During this period, a husband must not have intercourse with his wife during her menstrual or postnatal period. He is allowed, however, to satisfy his sexual desire but without having intercourse.
- At the end of the menstrual and postnatal period, when bleeding stops completely, women must take a ritual bath (*ghusl*).

passages.heading: The Types of Blood that Are Naturally Discharged by Women
passages.text:

passages.heading: Muslim Women’s Modest Style of Dress (*Hijaab*)

Women are to cover their entire bodies when in the presence of men who are not related to them, and they may choose any design or colour they like for their *hijaab* as long as the following four conditions are met:

passages.heading: What Is the Qur’an?
passages.text:
The Holy Qur’an is the Word of Allah Almighty that He revealed to His Messenger, Muhammad ﷺ. It is the last of Allah’s revealed books, and there is no other book after it.

The revealed books are the books that Allah Almighty revealed to His prophets.
A Muslim believes that these books were revealed by Allah Almighty, and that Allah spoke in them in a manner that befits Him. These books include Az-Zaboor (the Psalms), which He revealed to Daawood (David) عليه السلام; At-Tawraat (the Torah), which He revealed to Moosaa (Moses) عليه السلام and Al-Injeel (the Gospel), which He revealed to Jesus, عليه السلام. All these books have undergone alteration and corruption through the ages.

passages.heading: Conditions for Acts of Worship to Be Accepted
passages.text:

The first condition: It has to be done sincerely for the sake of Allah to draw closer to alone, without showing off.

The second condition: It has to be done in the manner Allah has enjoined it and exactly as it was performed by the Prophet ﷺ.

passages.heading: Introduction
passages.text: Islam enjoins purity and cleanliness on its adherents and stresses that they must take good care of their personal hygiene and considers this matter one of the apparent rituals of religion and a requisite for the validity of many acts of worship. Indeed, observing purity and cleanliness is one of the characteristics of believers, which distinguishes them from others. In this lesson, we are going to learn the meaning of purity, its types, and some rulings on it.

passages.heading: Introduction
passages.text: People have always pondered the big questions of human existence: Where did we come from? Why are we here? Where do we go after death? Islam provides definitive and conclusive answers to these questions which arise in the heart of every reflective human being.

passages.heading: Introduction
passages.text: *Wudoo’* is very important in Islam because it is closely connected with the ritual prayer, which is itself the greatest ritual in Islam, hence the importance of learning it and performing it correctly. In this lesson, we are going to learn about the meaning of *wudoo’*, things that require us to perform it, things that make it invalid, and the proper manner of performing it.

passages.heading: Purification
passages.text:
* **Engaging in the worship of Almighty Allah**  
  This is expressed by the intention to act in obedience to Allah Almighty and to draw closer to Him

* **by removing ritual impurity**  
  Ritual impurity (*hadath*) refers to anything that takes place in the body, thus rendering purity invalid

* **and physical impurities**  
  Physical impurity (*najaasah*) refers to all physical substances which Islam considers impure, such as urine and faeces, and commands us to remove.

passages.heading: The Meaning of Worship
passages.text: By worship is meant everything that Allah has enjoined on us for us to draw closer to Him. It comprises all words and deeds that Allah loves, whether they are outward like the physical acts of worship, such as the prayer and pilgrimage, or inward, like the acts of worship involving the heart, such as love of Allah, fearing His punishment and hoping for His mercy. A person can transform everyday habits into acts of worship simply by having a good intention. If, for instance, he eats, drinks and sleeps with the intention of gaining enough strength to worship Allah better, he will certainly be rewarded for doing so

passages.heading: Introduction
passages.text: *Soorat Al-Faatihah* is the greatest *soorah* in the Qur’an. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ emphasized its virtues and greatness in many of his sayings. It is the *soorah* that every Muslim must learn by heart because it is the only *soorah* that he must recite in every single prayer. In this lesson, we are going to study this *soorah*, memorize its verses and understand its meanings, in addition to studying several other short *suwar* (sing, *soorah*) that have great significance.

passages.heading: Introduction
passages.text: Islam urges its followers to observe high moral character. The Prophet ﷺ stressed the importance of morals in many of his traditions, combining many acts of worship Muslims perform with good moral character. Islam promises a Muslim who displays such good character great rewards both in this world and the hereafter. In this lesson, we are going to learn about the importance of good moral character in Islam, as well as some of its virtues.

passages.heading: Forbidden Types of Clothing
passages.text:
A man's *'awrah* that must be covered extends from the navel to the knees. A woman must cover herself entirely in the presence of men not related to her; as for men to whom she is related and is forbidden to marry, such as her father, son and brother, she may appear before them as she would normally do in front of other women, showing such parts of her body as the face, hair, the neck and feet.

- Clothing that reveals the *'awrah* and does not conceal it
- Clothing that involves dressing like or imitating the opposite sex, such as when men dress like women and vice versa.
- Clothing that is worn with an air of pride and conceit
- Extravagant clothing
- Men are particularly forbidden to wear silk clothing or adorn themselves with gold or silver jewellery.
- Clothing that involves imitation of the dress traditionally worn by non-Muslims and specific to a certain religion, such as the type of clothing worn by monks and priests

passages.heading: Types of Purification
passages.text:
Purification falls into two types:

**Physical Purification**

This means the removal of impurities and the cleansing of the area affected by them

**Moral Purification**

This means the removal of those things that prevent one from performing the prayer, by washing certain parts of the body or the entire body.

Physical purification may be undertaken either by *wudoo’* or *ghusl*

*Wudoo’* (partial ablutions): the ritual washing of certain parts of the body with water

*Ghusl* (full ablutions/bath): the ritual washing of the entire body with water.

Purification must be undertaken with pure water, such as seawater, river water, well water, or any other water that has not been mixed with impurity.

passages.heading: Who Are We?
passages.text:
Islam defines ‘man’ as one of Allah’s many creatures. The Almighty has honoured man and favoured him greatly above many other creatures, and subjected many of them to him so that he may benefit from them to perform the duties required of him during his life. The Almighty says, {{Q:17:70}} (Surat Al-Israa’, 17:70).

Allah Almighty has made in man some kind of likeness to:

> The angels are among Allah’s creatures. The Almighty created them from light and with a natural predisposition to worship and obey Him. They are His honoured servants who never disobey His orders but always do as they are commanded. There are a great many of them, but only Allah knows their number.

- the angels in their purity and worship.
- the devils in their ingratitude and disobedience, and
- the animals in their satisfying their whims and desires.

passages.heading: Who Are We?
passages.text:
He has provided him with an innate readiness to do good or evil but has at the same time furnished him with such cognitive tools as the innate human nature (*fitrah*) and the intellect to discern good from evil.

He has also given him free will to be responsible for his own choices and actions.

passages.heading: How Do We Pray?
passages.text:
1. He intends in his heart to pray.
2. He stands facing the *qiblah*, raises his hands up to the level of the shoulders or ears, and says, “*Allaahu akbar* Allah is the Greatest.”
3. He places his right hand on his left hand. Then he recites one of the opening supplications, such as, Subhaanak-Allaahumma wa bi hamdika, wa tabaarak-asmuka, wa ta’aalaa jadduka, wa laa ilaaha ghayruka “Glory be to You, O Allah; Yours is the praise, blessed is Your name, exalted is Your majesty, and there is no god besides You.” Then he says, A’oodhu billaahi min-ash-shaytaan-ir-rajeem. Bismillaah-ir-rahmaan-ir-raheem “I seek Allah’s protection from Satan, who has been expelled from His mercy. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.” Then he recites *Soorat Al-Faatihah* and says after it, “*Aameen*”, which means “Answer our supplications, O Allah”. After that, he recites whatever number of verses of the Qur’an as is easy for him, even if it is one verse.
4. He says, “Allaahu akbar Allah is the Greatest” while raising his hands up to the level of his shoulders or ears, and bows down, lowering his head and back and keeping them straight at a right angle, placing the palms of his hands on the knees. He says three times while in this position, “Subhaana rabbiy-al-’adheem Glory be to my Lord, the Almighty.”

passages.heading: The Manner of Performing the Full Ritual Bath (*Ghusl*)
passages.text:
If a Muslim wants to perform *ghusl*, he must do the following:

1. He intends in his heart to perform *ghusl* and washes out his private parts with water.
2. He performs *wudoo’* like the one he performs before the prayer.
3. He washes his entire body with water.

passages.heading: The Five Obligatory Prayers
passages.text:
Allah Almighty has enjoined Muslims to perform five prayers throughout the day and night, namely:

| The Prayer | Beginning Time | Ending Time | Number of units (*rak‘ahs*) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| *Fajr* (Dawn) Prayer | at the break of dawn | sunrise | 2 |
| *Dhuhr* (Midday) Prayer | when the sun starts declining westward at midday after reaching its zenith | when the shadow of an object becomes equal in length to the object itself | 4 |
| *‘Asr* (Late Afternoon) Prayer | when the shadow of an object becomes equal in length to the object itself | sunset | 4 |

passages.heading: Islamic Rulings Pertaining to Menstrual and Postnatal Bleeding
passages.text:
Allah Almighty has prescribed several rulings relating to menstruating women and women experiencing their postnatal bleeding, including the following:

- They are exempt from performing the prayers during this period and do not have to make up for the prayers they have missed while in this state after the end of menstrual and postnatal bleeding.
- They are exempt from fasting and are not allowed to fast while in this state, but they must make up for the fasting days they have missed in Ramadaan.
- During this period, a husband must not have intercourse with his wife during her menstrual or postnatal period. He is allowed, however, to satisfy his sexual desire but without having intercourse.
- At the end of the menstrual and postnatal period, when bleeding stops completely, women must take a ritual bath (*ghusl*).

passages.heading: The Conditions of the Prayer
passages.text:
- Purity: Once’s body and the place where the prayer is to be performed must be cleansed from physical impurities, and any ritual impurity must be removed with *wudoo’* or *ghusl*.
- Covering the intimate parts of the body (*‘awrah*): The word *‘awrah* refers to the parts of the body that must be covered in front of people. A man’s *‘awrah* that must be covered during the prayer extends from the navel to the knees; a woman’s *‘awrah* that must be covered during the prayer is her entire body except for the face and hands.
- Facing the *qiblah*: The *qiblah* is the direction of the Ka‘bah in Makkah. One must, therefore, pray in the direction of the Ka‘bah in Makkah.
- When its appointed time becomes due: The prayer will not be valid if it is performed before its time has started. It is not permissible to delay it beyond its due time, and it is best to perform it at the beginning of its time.

passages.heading: Things Which Require Us to Perform *Wudoo’*:
passages.text:

### TAFSIR SURAH-SURAH PENDEK

*Arraḥmānirraḥīm* [Yang Maha Pengasih, Maha Penyayang]. *Ar-Raḥmān* bermakna yang memilik sifat rahmat yang umum untuk semua makhluk-Nya. *Ar-Raḥīm* bermakna yang memiliki sifat rahmat yang khusus bagi orang-orang beriman di antara mereka.

*Ar-Raḥmān*: bagi semua makhluk-Nya.

*Ar-Raḥīm*: khusus bagi orang-orang beriman.

*Māliki yaumid-dīn* [Yang menguasai hari pembalasan]. Penguasa hari Kiamat, yaitu hari perhitungan dan pembalasan amal.

*Iyyāka na’budu wa iyyāka nasta’īn* [Hanya kepada Engkau kami menyembah dan hanya kepada Engkau kami memohon pertolongan]. Kami hanya beribadah kepada-Mu semata, wahai Tuhan kami, dan kami hanya memohon pertolongan kepada-Mu dalam semua urusan kami. Seluruh urusan hanya ada di tangan-Mu.

*Ihdinaṣ-ṣirāṭal-mustaqīm* [Tunjukilah kami ke jalan yang lurus]. Tunjuki kami jalan yang lurus dan teguhkan kami di atasnya hingga kami bertemu Engkau. Jalan lurus ini ialah Islam, jalan yang terang, yang mengantarkan kepada rida dan surga Allah.

passages.heading: Ke mana tujuan kita?
passages.text:
Al-Qur`ān al-Karīm telah menjelaskan bahwa setiap orang di dunia ini akan mati. Dengan kematiannya maka berakhirlah fase beramalnya dan dimulailah fase perhitungan dan pembalasan amalnya. Allah Ta’ālā berfirman, “Sesungguhnya engkau (Muhammad) akan mati dan mereka akan mati pula. Kemudian sesungguhnya kamu pada hari Kiamat akan berbantah-bantahan di hadapan Tuhanmu.” (QS. Az-Zumar: 30-31)

Bila manusia telah mati, dia berpindah ke fase tempat ia ditanya tentang agamanya dan diberikan balasan atas amal perbuatannya. Allah Ta’ālā berfirman, “Setiap yang bernyawa akan merasakan mati. Dan hanya pada hari Kiamat sajalah diberikan dengan sempurna balasanmu. Barang siapa dijauhkan dari neraka dan dimasukkan ke dalam surga, sungguh dia memperoleh kemenangan. Kehidupan dunia hanyalah kesenangan yang memperdaya.” (QS. Āli ‘Imrān: 185)

passages.heading: Kesyirikan kepada Allah:
passages.text:
Yaitu meyakini ketuhanan seseorang selain Allah *Ta'ālā* atau mendekatkan diri kepadanya dengan sebagian ibadah. Kesyirikan adalah dosa dan kejahatan besar yang tidak diampuni oleh Allah *Ta'ālā*, sebagaimana dalam firman-Nya: *"Sesungguhnya Allah tidak akan mengampuni (dosa) karena mempersekutukan-Nya (syirik), dan Dia mengampuni apa (dosa) yang selain (syirik) itu bagi siapa yang Dia kehendaki. Barang siapa mempersekutukan Allah, maka sungguh dia telah berbuat dosa yang besar."* (QS. An-Nisā`: 48)

> Yang dimaksud dengan Al-Kitāb dan As-Sunnah ialah Al-Qur`ān Al-Karīm dan hadis-hadis Rasul Muhammad ﷺ karena keduanya merupakan sumber utama bagi pensyariatan dalam Islam.

passages.heading: Pelajaran 3
passages.text:
## Bagaimana Saya Masuk Islam?

Inti agama Islam yang merupakan agama seluruh para nabi ialah beribadah kepada Allah saja serta mengingkari semua yang disembah selain Allah. Allah *Ta'ālā* berfirman, "Kami tidak mengutus seorang rasul pun sebelum engkau (Muhammad), melainkan Kami wahyukan kepadanya, 'bahwa tidak ada tuhan (yang berhak disembah) selain Aku, maka sembahlah Aku!'" (QS. Al-Anbiyā`: 25)

Sebab itu, tidak diperbolehkan dalam keadaan apa pun untuk meyakini ketuhanan siapa pun selain Allah *Ta'ālā* serta tidak boleh beribadah mendekatkan diri kepada selain Allah *Ta'ālā* dengan jenis ibadah apa pun.

Nikmat Hidayah Orang yang memahami hikmah penciptaannya serta kesudahan yang menanti manusia kelak hari Kiamat, pasti meyakini bahwa nikmat terbesar yang Allah berikan kepada hamba-hamba-Nya ialah nikmat hidayah (petunjuk) kepada agama yang benar serta amal saleh. Oleh sebab itu, Allah’ *Azza wa Jalla* mewajibkan kepada hamba-hamba-Nya di dalam salat agar meminta petunjuk kepada jalan yang lurus, yaitu agama Islam yang akan mengantarkan kepada rida-Nya.

passages.heading: Allah Almighty has forbidden different types of food and drink, including the following:
passages.text:
- Alcohol, because it clouds the mind; indeed, preserving the mind is one of the objectives of Islamic law (*Sharee’ah*).
- Drugs, because they destroy the mind and body.
- Animals that die without having been slaughtered, or those that are slaughtered but the name of Allah (i.e., saying *Bismillaah* (in the name of Allah) was not mentioned at the time of slaughter.
- Pork—and indeed any of the pig’s body parts and by-products—because it is impure and thus forbidden for human consumption.
- Predatory animals, such as lions, tigers, hawks and eagles.
- Any animals that are sacrificed to false deities, such as idols.

The objectives of *Sharee’ah*: This is one of Islamic sciences by which Islamic laws are determined, such as the reason why Allah has laid down such-and-such a rule.

passages.heading: The Position of Women in Islam
passages.text:
- Islam has granted women the right to inheritance, allocating them equitable shares with men, which sometimes differ under certain circumstances depending on their relationship with others and the financial obligations they have to discharge. While men support the family as a matter of religious obligation, women are not obliged to spend anything at all.
- It has established total equality between men and women in numerous matters including financial transactions.
- It has granted them the right to choose their own husbands.
- It has granted them the right to retain their maiden names. In Islam, a woman does not change her surname to that of her husband upon marriage; rather, she retains her maiden name, and thus her independent personality.
- It has made it the husband’s duty to spend on those women entitled to his support, such as his wife, mother and daughters, without attempting in the least to remind them of his favours.
- It stresses the importance of helping weak and vulnerable women who are in need of support, even if they are not one’s relatives, and urges its adherents to engage in such a noble act, which it considers one of the meritorious deeds in the sight of Allah.

passages.heading: Prohibited Forms of Financial Transactions
passages.text:
**Allah Almighty has forbidden some financial transactions, including the following:**

- The unlawful taking of other people’s property, such as by using deceptive tricks or by force.
- Conducting a transaction under coercion, such as by forcing someone to enter into a transaction against his will.
- Trafficking in substances that are injurious to human health, such as alcohol, drugs and tobacco.
- Charging interest on loans, an example of which is to lend money to someone on condition that the borrower must pay, say, 5% on the borrowed amount to the lender.
- Selling things that are not known, such as selling a box the contents of which are unknown.
- Gambling and betting whereby the winner unlawfully takes the money of the loser.

passages.heading: Note
passages.text: Islam respects the customs and traditions of all peoples and does not require them to change them unless they contravene any of the teachings of Islam.

passages.heading: Things That a Person Who Is in a State of *Jannabah* Must Not Do
passages.text:
The state into which a person gets following intercourse or ejaculation and because of which he must perform *ghusl* is called *janaabah*, and he is described as *junub*. In this case, he is not allowed to do the following:

1. perform the prayer
2. circumambulate the Ka’bah (*tawaaf*)
3. touch or carry the Qur’an
4. stay in the mosque
5. read the Qur’an

passages.heading: Islamic Rulings Pertaining to Meat Served in Restaurants and Shops
passages.text:
1. The meat of animals that are slaughtered by other than a Muslim or a member of the People of the Book (a Christian or a Jew), such as a Buddhist, or a Hindu is strictly forbidden. This includes meat served in restaurants and shops in countries where Muslims or People of the Book constitute a minority.
2. The meat of animals killed by a Muslim or a member of the People of the Book is lawful based on textual evidence to this effect in the Qur’an.
3. The meat of animals that are not killed according to Islamic law, such as by electrocution and drowning, is strictly forbidden.
4. The general rule is that it is permissible to consume the flesh of animals slaughtered by People of the Book as well as meat of animals generally found in their restaurants and shops, making sure, however, to invoke Allah’s name at the time of eating (that is, by saying *Bismillaah*), but it is better for Muslims to eat only meat that has been proven to be lawful (*halaal*).

passages.heading: Wiping over the Socks
passages.text: If a person wants to perform *wudoo’* while he has his socks on, he is allowed to just wipe over the top of them with wet hands, and there is no need to take them off and wash the feet. Three conditions are required for this:

passages.heading: Forbidden Types of Clothing
passages.text:
A man's *'awrah* that must be covered extends from the navel to the knees. A woman must cover herself entirely in the presence of men not related to her; as for men to whom she is related and is forbidden to marry, such as her father, son and brother, she may appear before them as she would normally do in front of other women, showing such parts of her body as the face, hair, the neck and feet.

- Clothing that reveals the *'awrah* and does not conceal it
- Clothing that involves dressing like or imitating the opposite sex, such as when men dress like women and vice versa.
- Clothing that is worn with an air of pride and conceit
- Extravagant clothing
- Men are particularly forbidden to wear silk clothing or adorn themselves with gold or silver jewellery.
- Clothing that involves imitation of the dress traditionally worn by non-Muslims and specific to a certain religion, such as the type of clothing worn by monks and priests

passages.heading: The General Islamic Rule Regarding Food and drink
passages.text: The general Islamic rule is that everything is presumed permissible unless proven otherwise in the Qur’an or the Prophet’s *Sunnah*. The Almighty says, {{Q:2:168}} *(Soorat Al-Baqarah, 2:168)*.

passages.heading: What Are the Conditions for Islamic Slaughter?
passages.text:
Islamic slaughter is one that satisfies the following conditions:

1. The person undertaking the slaughtering process must be Muslim, Jew or Christian who has reached the age of discretion and carries out this act for the intended purpose.
2. The tool used for slaughter must be suitable for the intended purpose, causes blood to flow and sharp, such as a knife. It is forbidden to use anything that may kill the animal due to its heavy weight, hit its head to death or render it unconscious by resorting to electric stunning, for instance.
3. The name of Allah must be pronounced by saying *Bismillaah* (in the name of Allah) at the time of slaughtering the animal.
4. Cutting what must be cut in the Islamic slaughter, namely, the oesophagus, the throat, and the two jugular veins, or just three of these four.

passages.heading: What is the Islamic Ruling on Seafood Consumption?
passages.text:
It is permissible to eat dead aquatic animals that can live only in water, such as fish and prawns, whether they live in the sea, rivers or lakes.

It is permissible to hunt wild, nonpredatory animals and consume their flesh provided that the name of Allah is mentioned before the hunting weapon is discharged, and the hunted game must be slaughtered if found still alive.

passages.heading: The General Islamic Rule Regarding Financial Transactions in Islam
passages.text:
The general Islamic rule is that all types of transactions are permissible, and that none of them is forbidden unless declared as such in the Qur’an or the Prophet’s *Sunnah*.

> The general Islamic rule regarding transactions in general, including financial transactions, is that they are permissible, and thus nothing is considered impermissible without evidence, as opposed to acts of worship, where the general rule regarding them is that they are not permissible unless there is evidence which states otherwise.

passages.heading: The Reasons for the Prohibition of Financial Transactions
passages.text:
The main reasons for the prohibition of financial transactions are:

1. Injustice
2. Usury (interest)
3. Ignorance and uncertainty (*gharar*) and gambling

passages.heading: Discuss
passages.text: In the light of the large number of financial transactions that Muslims carry out in their daily lives, how can they be aware of what transactions are permissible or prohibited?

passages.heading: Discuss

passages.heading: *Tayammum* (Dry Ablution)
passages.text:
If a person who wants to perform *wudoo’* or *ghusl* is unable to do so due to illness, or when water is not readily available, or for any other legitimate reason, he may resort to dry ablution (*tayammum*) instead.

The Manner of Performing *Tayammum*: (1) Intend in his heart to perform *tayammum* and strike both hands slightly on pure earth once, (2) wipe the face with them, (3) wipe the back of the right hand with the palm of the left, and then the back of the left hand with the palm of the right hand.

passages.heading: What shall I do if I find water after having performed *tayammum*?
passages.text: If a Muslim finds water or can use it, his purity becomes invalid, in which case he must perform *wudoo’* or *ghusl*.

passages.heading: Introduction
passages.text: One of the most memorable moments of a new Muslim’s life must be the moment he joined the fold of Islam by pronouncing the two testimonies of faith. By so doing, he declared to himself before anyone else that he would begin a new chapter in his life and would, from the moment of making such a declaration, take the first steps towards finding the truth and adhering to it. In this lesson, we are going to learn about the two testimonies and their meaning and requirements.

passages.heading: Prohibited Forms of Financial Transactions
passages.text:
**Allah Almighty has forbidden some financial transactions, including the following:**

- The unlawful taking of other people’s property, such as by using deceptive tricks or by force.
- Conducting a transaction under coercion, such as by forcing someone to enter into a transaction against his will.
- Trafficking in substances that are injurious to human health, such as alcohol, drugs and tobacco.
- Charging interest on loans, an example of which is to lend money to someone on condition that the borrower must pay, say, 5% on the borrowed amount to the lender.
- Selling things that are not known, such as selling a box the contents of which are unknown.
- Gambling and betting whereby the winner unlawfully takes the money of the loser.

passages.heading: The Meaning of Worship
passages.text: By worship is meant everything that Allah has enjoined on us for us to draw closer to Him. It comprises all words and deeds that Allah loves, whether they are outward like the physical acts of worship, such as the prayer and pilgrimage, or inward, like the acts of worship involving the heart, such as love of Allah, fearing His punishment and hoping for His mercy. A person can transform everyday habits into acts of worship simply by having a good intention. If, for instance, he eats, drinks and sleeps with the intention of gaining enough strength to worship Allah better, he will certainly be rewarded for doing so

passages.heading: The Two Testimonies of Faith
passages.text:
Allah Almighty has made the declaration of the two testimonies of faith the key to joining the fold of Islam. They are:

- I bear witness that there is no god worthy of worship but Allah,
- and I bear witness that Muhammad is Allah’s Messenger.

passages.heading: 1. The Meaning of the Testimony that There Is no God but Allah
passages.text:
The meaning of “I bear witness that there is no god but Allah” is: I firmly believe that there is no god worthy of worship except Allah alone.

This testimony consists of two parts:

| The first part | The second part |
| --- | --- |
| negates the existence of any other deity besides Allah Almighty | confirms that Allah is the only True God worthy of worship |

Islam is essentially the religion of all the prophets: to worship Allah alone and reject all false deities that are worshipped besides or instead of Him. Allah Almighty, says, {{Q:21:25}} (Surat al-Anbiyyaa’, 21:25).

Therefore, it is not permissible, under any circumstances, to believe in any deity other than Allah Almighty, nor is it permissible to perform any act of worship to draw nearer to anyone other than Allah Almighty.

passages.heading: The General Islamic Rule Regarding Financial Transactions in Islam
passages.text:
The general Islamic rule is that all types of transactions are permissible, and that none of them is forbidden unless declared as such in the Qur’an or the Prophet’s *Sunnah*.

> The general Islamic rule regarding transactions in general, including financial transactions, is that they are permissible, and thus nothing is considered impermissible without evidence, as opposed to acts of worship, where the general rule regarding them is that they are not permissible unless there is evidence which states otherwise.

passages.heading: The Reasons for the Prohibition of Financial Transactions
passages.text:
The main reasons for the prohibition of financial transactions are:

1. Injustice
2. Usury (interest)
3. Ignorance and uncertainty (*gharar*) and gambling

It is permissible to eat dead aquatic animals that can live only in water, such as fish and prawns, whether they live in the sea, rivers or lakes.

It is permissible to hunt wild, nonpredatory animals and consume their flesh provided that the name of Allah is mentioned before the hunting weapon is discharged, and the hunted game must be slaughtered if found still alive.

passages.text:
*Wudoo’* becomes invalid as a result of four things:

- Natural discharges from the private parts (both the external genital and excretory organs), such as urine, excrement, wind, semen and the clear, colourless, viscous fluid that is emitted during sexual arousal
- Loss of consciousness due to sleep or intoxication
- Lustfully touching the private parts with bare hands
- Eating camel meat

passages.heading: What Are the Conditions for Islamic Slaughter?
passages.text:
Islamic slaughter is one that satisfies the following conditions:

1. The person undertaking the slaughtering process must be Muslim, Jew or Christian who has reached the age of discretion and carries out this act for the intended purpose.
2. The tool used for slaughter must be suitable for the intended purpose, causes blood to flow and sharp, such as a knife. It is forbidden to use anything that may kill the animal due to its heavy weight, hit its head to death or render it unconscious by resorting to electric stunning, for instance.
3. The name of Allah must be pronounced by saying *Bismillaah* (in the name of Allah) at the time of slaughtering the animal.
4. Cutting what must be cut in the Islamic slaughter, namely, the oesophagus, the throat, and the two jugular veins, or just three of these four.

1. He intends in his heart to pray.

3. He places his right hand on his left hand. Then he recites one of the opening supplications, such as, Subhaanak-Allaahumma wa bi hamdika, wa tabaarak-asmuka, wa ta’aalaa jadduka, wa laa ilaaha ghayruka “Glory be to You, O Allah; Yours is the praise, blessed is Your name, exalted is Your majesty, and there is no god besides You.” Then he says, A’oodhu billaahi min-ash-shaytaan-ir-rajeem. Bismillaah-ir-rahmaan-ir-raheem “I seek Allah’s protection from Satan, who has been expelled from His mercy. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.” Then he recites *Soorat Al-Faatihah* and says after it, “*Aameen*”, which means “Answer our supplications, O Allah”. After that, he recites whatever number of verses of the Qur’an as is easy for him, even if it is one verse.
4. He says, “Allaahu akbar Allah is the Greatest” while raising his hands up to the level of his shoulders or ears, and bows down, lowering his head and back and keeping them straight at a right angle, placing the palms of his hands on the knees. He says three times while in this position, “Subhaana rabbiy-al-’adheem Glory be to my Lord, the Almighty.”

passages.heading: Why Should I Embrace Islam?
passages.text:
Some people may ask: Why should I embrace Islam?

The answer is: I must do so for a number of reasons, including the following:

1. Islam is the religion that Allah has approved and chosen for His servants and will not accept any other religion. The Almighty says, {{Q:3:85}} (Soorat Aal-’Imraan, 3:85).

2. Islam is the religion of all the prophets and commands its adherents to believe in all of them without exception. Allah says, {{Q:2:136}} (Soorat Al-Baqarah, 2:136).
The difference between prophets lies only in the laws relating to people’s actions, as the Almighty says, {{Q:5:48}} (Soorat Al-Maa’idah, 5:48) That is, for each nation before Islam, Allah appointed a law to which people referred for their disputes and a way of life whereby they drew near to Him. Thus, followers of every prophet had their respective laws and regulations, but the set of beliefs to which prophets called their people was the same. Then Allah sent the last prophet and messenger, Muhammad ﷺ, with the final divine laws, and thus the only religion acceptable to Allah is Islam.

3. Islam is the way to happiness in this life and salvation in the life to come; therefore, those who believe in Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and follow him after his message has reached them will be saved; as for those who deny him, they will be doomed to divine punishment. The Almighty says, {{Q:3:85}} (*Soorat Aal-’Imraan, 3:85*) The Prophet ﷺ also said, “By Him in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, any person of this Community, Jew or Christian, who hears of me and dies without believing in what I have been sent with will be among the dwellers of Hell” (*Saheeh Muslim;* No. 153).

4. Islam gives conclusive answers to the big questions of human existence: Where did we come from? Why are we here? Where do we go after death?

5. Islam is in perfect harmony with the innate human nature (*fitrah*), beginning with the greatest value it embraces, namely the declaration of Allah’s unity, and ending with the rules of etiquette it teaches its adherents to enable them to attain great perfection in moral excellence.

passages.heading: The Position of the Prayer in Islam
passages.text:
The prayer has a number of distinctive characteristics, including the following:

- It is the second pillar of Islam after the two testimonies of faith.
- It is the act of worship that must be performed under all circumstances, in times of war and peace, and whether one is sick or in good health.
- It is the act of worship that distinguishes a Muslim from a non-Muslim.

passages.heading: Some of the Ultimate Objectives and Benefits of the Prayer:
passages.text:
- It is the direct, special and personal communion a Muslim establishes with his Lord.
- It relieves the mind of worry and all worldly anxieties.
- It strengthens a Muslim’s willpower and determination.
- It refines morals and keeps those who observe it away from evil.

passages.heading: The Conditions of the Prayer
passages.text:
To perform the prayer, several conditions must be met:
There are several conditions required to perform the prayer, which are:

passages.heading: The Conditions of the Prayer
passages.text:
- Purity: Once’s body and the place where the prayer is to be performed must be cleansed from physical impurities, and any ritual impurity must be removed with *wudoo’* or *ghusl*.
- Covering the intimate parts of the body (*‘awrah*): The word *‘awrah* refers to the parts of the body that must be covered in front of people. A man’s *‘awrah* that must be covered during the prayer extends from the navel to the knees; a woman’s *‘awrah* that must be covered during the prayer is her entire body except for the face and hands.
- Facing the *qiblah*: The *qiblah* is the direction of the Ka‘bah in Makkah. One must, therefore, pray in the direction of the Ka‘bah in Makkah.
- When its appointed time becomes due: The prayer will not be valid if it is performed before its time has started. It is not permissible to delay it beyond its due time, and it is best to perform it at the beginning of its time.

“You have your religion, and I have my religion”

You have your religion to which you adhere, and I have my religion to which I adhere.

passages.heading: Soorat Al-Falaq Explained
passages.text:
“Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of the daybreak” Say, Messenger: I seek refuge and protection in Allah, the Lord of the daybreak.

“from the evil of what He has created”

from the evil of everything He has created, visible and invisible.

“and from the evil of the night when it spreads its darkness”

and from the evil of the night when it comes and grows dark, and of whatever evil and harm that may happen in it.

Al-ghasaq: the intense darkness of the night

Al-falaq: the daybreak

“and from the evil of those who blow on knots”

and from the evil of those witches who blow on knots when they practise magic.

“and from the evil of the envier when he envies”

and from the evil of an envier who wishes for blessings to be removed from those they envy and for harm to come to them.

passages.heading: Soorat Al-’A<u>s</u>r (The Time)
passages.text:
*Soorat Al-’A<u>s</u>r* **Explained**

{{Q:103:1-3}}

“By the time”

Allah swears by the time in which people’s good and evil deeds take place.

“Truly man is in loss”

Mankind is indeed in sheer loss and ruin,

“except for those who believe and do good works; who exhort each other to justice and to fortitude”

except for those who believe in Allah, do righteous deeds, and urge one another to adhere to the truth and to be patient and steadfast in doing so.

passages.heading: Soorat Al-Ikhlaas Explained
passages.text:
“Say: He is Allah, the One and Only”

Say, Messenger, to those who ask you about your Lord: He is Allah, the One and Only Lord and God, besides whom there is no deity deserving of worship.

“Allah, the Everlasting Sustainer of all”

He is Allah, the Eternal and Absolute God with perfect attributes, to whom all creation turns to fulfil their needs, while He stands in need of none.

“He has not begotten anyone, nor was He Himself begotten by anyone”

He is Allah, who has no offspring whatsoever, neither son nor daughter, and He has no parents, neither father nor mother.

“And none is equal to Him”

And there is no one and nothing among His creation that resembles Him in any way whatsoever with regard to His being, names attributes or actions.

passages.heading: Soorat Al-Kawthar (Abundant Good)
passages.text:
*Soorat Al-Kawthar* **Explained**

{{Q:108:1-3}}

“We have bestowed on you abundant good”

We have given you, Messenger, immeasurable, abundant good in this life and the life to come, part of which is River Al-Kawthar in Paradise.

“So pray to your Lord and sacrifice to Him”

Therefore, sincerely pray to your Lord and worship Him alone, and sacrifice to Him, pronouncing Allah’s name alone when slaughtering animals, in gratitude to Him for the honour and good He has bestowed on you.

“He who hates you is the one who is truly cut off”

*Shaani’aka*: The one who hates you and hates the true religion you have brought.

The one who hates you and hates the true religion you have brought is the most disgraced and contemptible, whose mention is short-lived and who is cut off from all good.

passages.heading: Islamic Rulings Pertaining to Menstrual and Postnatal Bleeding
passages.text:
Allah Almighty has prescribed several rulings relating to menstruating women and women experiencing their postnatal bleeding, including the following:

- They are exempt from performing the prayers during this period and do not have to make up for the prayers they have missed while in this state after the end of menstrual and postnatal bleeding.
- They are exempt from fasting and are not allowed to fast while in this state, but they must make up for the fasting days they have missed in Ramadaan.
- During this period, a husband must not have intercourse with his wife during her menstrual or postnatal period. He is allowed, however, to satisfy his sexual desire but without having intercourse.
- At the end of the menstrual and postnatal period, when bleeding stops completely, women must take a ritual bath (*ghusl*).

passages.heading: Wiping over the Socks
passages.text: If a person wants to perform *wudoo’* while he has his socks on, he is allowed to just wipe over the top of them with wet hands, and there is no need to take them off and wash the feet. Three conditions are required for this:

passages.heading: Things That a Person Who Is in a State of *Jannabah* Must Not Do
passages.text:
The state into which a person gets following intercourse or ejaculation and because of which he must perform *ghusl* is called *janaabah*, and he is described as *junub*. In this case, he is not allowed to do the following:

1. perform the prayer
2. circumambulate the Ka’bah (*tawaaf*)
3. touch or carry the Qur’an
4. stay in the mosque
5. read the Qur’an

passages.heading: The General Islamic Rule Regarding Clothing
passages.text:
The general Islamic rule is that all types of clothing are allowed, unless stated otherwise in the Qur’an or the Prophet’s Sunnah.

the general Islamic rule regarding dealings in general, including clothing, is that everything is permissible unless there is evidence to the contrary. All types of clothing mentioned here are forbidden due to textual evidence either in the Qur’an or the Prophet’s Sunnah.

passages.heading: What Are the Conditions for Islamic Slaughter?
passages.text:
Islamic slaughter is one that satisfies the following conditions:

1. The person undertaking the slaughtering process must be Muslim, Jew or Christian who has reached the age of discretion and carries out this act for the intended purpose.
2. The tool used for slaughter must be suitable for the intended purpose, causes blood to flow and sharp, such as a knife. It is forbidden to use anything that may kill the animal due to its heavy weight, hit its head to death or render it unconscious by resorting to electric stunning, for instance.
3. The name of Allah must be pronounced by saying *Bismillaah* (in the name of Allah) at the time of slaughtering the animal.
4. Cutting what must be cut in the Islamic slaughter, namely, the oesophagus, the throat, and the two jugular veins, or just three of these four.

passages.heading: Islamic Rulings Pertaining to Meat Served in Restaurants and Shops
passages.text:
1. The meat of animals that are slaughtered by other than a Muslim or a member of the People of the Book (a Christian or a Jew), such as a Buddhist, or a Hindu is strictly forbidden. This includes meat served in restaurants and shops in countries where Muslims or People of the Book constitute a minority.
2. The meat of animals killed by a Muslim or a member of the People of the Book is lawful based on textual evidence to this effect in the Qur’an.
3. The meat of animals that are not killed according to Islamic law, such as by electrocution and drowning, is strictly forbidden.
4. The general rule is that it is permissible to consume the flesh of animals slaughtered by People of the Book as well as meat of animals generally found in their restaurants and shops, making sure, however, to invoke Allah’s name at the time of eating (that is, by saying *Bismillaah*), but it is better for Muslims to eat only meat that has been proven to be lawful (*halaal*).

passages.heading: Good Moral Character in Islam
passages.text:
- Good moral character occupies a lofty position in Islam, as it is one of the important objectives of *Sharee‘ah* and one of the goals behind the Prophet’s mission.
- Good moral character is closely linked to faith, and the believers with complete faith are those who demonstrate the best moral character.
- A Muslim will be rewarded for his good manners, just as he will be rewarded for the prayer and fasting.

passages.heading: Women in Relation to a Man
passages.text: Women in relation to a man fall into three categories:

passages.heading: Muslim Women’s Modest Style of Dress (*Hijaab*)
passages.text:
Allah enjoins women to wear the *hijaab* because women enjoy natural beauty and attraction that could easily tempt men into sinful acts, more than the other way round. Women are to cover their entire bodies when in the presence of men who are not related to them, and they may choose any design or colour they like for their *hijaab* as long as the following four conditions are met:

| First Condition | Second Condition | Third condition | Fourth Condition |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| It must appropriately cover the parts of the body that must be covered in public. | It must hang loose and must not fit very closely to the body so that the shape of the body is not revealed. | It must not allow the wearer’s body to be seen through its fabric. | It must not be a type of clothing that is generally considered attractive. |

passages.heading: The Types of Blood that Are Naturally Discharged by Women
passages.text:
The blood that is naturally discharged by women is of two types:

| Menstrual blood | Postnatal blood |
| --- | --- |
| This is a natural type of blood that flows from a woman’s uterus every month during her menstrual cycle and usually lasts for a few days. | This bleeding takes place after giving birth and lasts for several days, up to 40 days. |

passages.heading: *Tayammum* (Dry Ablution)
passages.text:
If a person who wants to perform *wudoo’* or *ghusl* is unable to do so due to illness, or when water is not readily available, or for any other legitimate reason, he may resort to dry ablution (*tayammum*) instead.

The Manner of Performing *Tayammum*: (1) Intend in his heart to perform *tayammum* and strike both hands slightly on pure earth once, (2) wipe the face with them, (3) wipe the back of the right hand with the palm of the left, and then the back of the left hand with the palm of the right hand.

passages.heading: What shall I do if I find water after having performed *tayammum*?
passages.text: If a Muslim finds water or can use it, his purity becomes invalid, in which case he must perform *wudoo’* or *ghusl*.

passages.heading: Introduction
passages.text: The clothes we wear are some of the countless blessings Allah has bestowed on us. The Qur’an states, {{Q:7:26}} (Soorat Al-A’raaf, 7:26).

passages.heading: Discuss
passages.text: What purposes does clothing serve?

passages.heading: Forbidden Types of Clothing
passages.text:
A man's *'awrah* that must be covered extends from the navel to the knees. A woman must cover herself entirely in the presence of men not related to her; as for men to whom she is related and is forbidden to marry, such as her father, son and brother, she may appear before them as she would normally do in front of other women, showing such parts of her body as the face, hair, the neck and feet.

- Clothing that reveals the *'awrah* and does not conceal it
- Clothing that involves dressing like or imitating the opposite sex, such as when men dress like women and vice versa.
- Clothing that is worn with an air of pride and conceit
- Extravagant clothing
- Men are particularly forbidden to wear silk clothing or adorn themselves with gold or silver jewellery.
- Clothing that involves imitation of the dress traditionally worn by non-Muslims and specific to a certain religion, such as the type of clothing worn by monks and priests

passages.heading: Forbidden Types of Clothing
passages.text:
With your partners, discuss the reasons why some types of clothing are forbidden in Islam.

The Prophet ﷺ forbade men from imitating women and women from imitating men. This prohibition includes the type of clothing and the manner of speech. Islam strictly forbids imitation of the opposite sex, considering it a major sin that invites Allah’s punishment unless one repents and desists from committing it. Islam enjoins men to ensure that their true nature and appearance are distinct from that of women, and vice versa, which clearly testifies to common sense and sound logic.

passages.heading: Allah Almighty has forbidden different types of food and drink, including the following:
passages.text:
- Alcohol, because it clouds the mind; indeed, preserving the mind is one of the objectives of Islamic law (*Sharee’ah*).
- Drugs, because they destroy the mind and body.
- Animals that die without having been slaughtered, or those that are slaughtered but the name of Allah (i.e., saying *Bismillaah* (in the name of Allah) was not mentioned at the time of slaughter.
- Pork—and indeed any of the pig’s body parts and by-products—because it is impure and thus forbidden for human consumption.
- Predatory animals, such as lions, tigers, hawks and eagles.
- Any animals that are sacrificed to false deities, such as idols.

The objectives of *Sharee’ah*: This is one of Islamic sciences by which Islamic laws are determined, such as the reason why Allah has laid down such-and-such a rule.

passages.heading: What is the Islamic Ruling on Seafood Consumption?
passages.text:
It is permissible to eat dead aquatic animals that can live only in water, such as fish and prawns, whether they live in the sea, rivers or lakes.

It is permissible to hunt wild, nonpredatory animals and consume their flesh provided that the name of Allah is mentioned before the hunting weapon is discharged, and the hunted game must be slaughtered if found still alive.

The Islamic rulings on the meat of animals that are sold in shops and restaurants vary according to the religion of the person who slaughtered such animals.
