passages.heading: Who is the prophet of Islam?
passages.text: Muslims believe that Muhammad ﷺ is the Last Prophet whom Allah has sent to all mankind to call them to worship Allah alone and to declare that Muhammad is His Last Prophet. Allah Almighty says, {{Q:33:40}} (Soorat Al-Ahzaab, 33:40)

passages.heading: *Tayammum* (Dry Ablution)
passages.text:
If a person who wants to perform *wudoo’* or *ghusl* is unable to do so due to illness, or when water is not readily available, or for any other legitimate reason, he may resort to dry ablution (*tayammum*) instead.

The Manner of Performing *Tayammum*: (1) Intend in his heart to perform *tayammum* and strike both hands slightly on pure earth once, (2) wipe the face with them, (3) wipe the back of the right hand with the palm of the left, and then the back of the left hand with the palm of the right hand.

passages.heading: Introduction
passages.text: In his life, a Muslim performs a number of acts of worship whereby he draws closer to his Creator, Glory is to Him. We do such acts to glorify Allah Almighty and submit to Him alone. The more a Muslim’s heart glorifies Allah, Exalted be He, the greater the effect of doing so is on his worship. A true Muslim dedicates all life, including the time he spends at work, sleeping and having fun, to Allah Almighty, bearing in mind the verse: {{Q:6:162-163}} (Soorat Al-An’aam, 6:162-163) In this lesson, we are going to learn about the meaning of worship, its types, the conditions that must be met for it to be accepted, and its levels.

passages.heading: Types of Acts of Worship
passages.text:
Acts of worship fall into different categories:

| Acts of worship involving the heart | A Muslim performs these with his heart. Examples include love, fear, hope and *khushoo’*. |
| --- | --- |
| Physical acts of worship | A Muslim performs these physically. Examples include the prayer, *zakaat* and pilgrimage. |
| Acts that are abandoned in obedience to Allah | A Muslim draws closer to his Lord by abandoning the acts He has forbidden him, such as drinking alcohol and committing adultery, or by refraining from certain permissible acts at specific times, such as abstaining from food and drink while fasting. |

> *Ar-Rajaa’*(Hope): This refers to rejoicing in Allah’s grace and hoping for His benevolence, while at the same time ensuring proper reliance on Allah by doing good deeds to the best of one’s ability.
> 
> *Al-khushoo’* is a state of utter humility and calmness and deep concentration into which one gets while performing an act of worship, such as the prayer, bringing about outward composure and tranquillity.

passages.heading: Conditions for Acts of Worship to Be Accepted
passages.text:
For an act of worship to be accepted, two conditions must be fulfilled:

The first condition: It has to be done sincerely for the sake of Allah to draw closer to alone, without showing off.

The second condition: It has to be done in the manner Allah has enjoined it and exactly as it was performed by the Prophet ﷺ.

> *Aririyyaa’* (showing off) is the act of doing an act of worship only to be seen and praised by people for doing it.

passages.heading: The Two Testimonies of Faith
passages.text:
Allah Almighty has made the declaration of the two testimonies of faith the key to joining the fold of Islam. They are:

- I bear witness that there is no god worthy of worship but Allah,
- and I bear witness that Muhammad is Allah’s Messenger.

passages.heading: 1. The Meaning of the Testimony that There Is no God but Allah
passages.text:
The meaning of “I bear witness that there is no god but Allah” is: I firmly believe that there is no god worthy of worship except Allah alone.

This testimony consists of two parts:

| The first part | The second part |
| --- | --- |
| negates the existence of any other deity besides Allah Almighty | confirms that Allah is the only True God worthy of worship |

Islam is essentially the religion of all the prophets: to worship Allah alone and reject all false deities that are worshipped besides or instead of Him. Allah Almighty, says, {{Q:21:25}} (Surat al-Anbiyyaa’, 21:25).

Therefore, it is not permissible, under any circumstances, to believe in any deity other than Allah Almighty, nor is it permissible to perform any act of worship to draw nearer to anyone other than Allah Almighty.

passages.heading: The Conditions of the Prayer
passages.text:
- Purity: Once’s body and the place where the prayer is to be performed must be cleansed from physical impurities, and any ritual impurity must be removed with *wudoo’* or *ghusl*.
- Covering the intimate parts of the body (*‘awrah*): The word *‘awrah* refers to the parts of the body that must be covered in front of people. A man’s *‘awrah* that must be covered during the prayer extends from the navel to the knees; a woman’s *‘awrah* that must be covered during the prayer is her entire body except for the face and hands.
- Facing the *qiblah*: The *qiblah* is the direction of the Ka‘bah in Makkah. One must, therefore, pray in the direction of the Ka‘bah in Makkah.
- When its appointed time becomes due: The prayer will not be valid if it is performed before its time has started. It is not permissible to delay it beyond its due time, and it is best to perform it at the beginning of its time.

- It is the direct, special and personal communion a Muslim establishes with his Lord.
- It relieves the mind of worry and all worldly anxieties.
- It strengthens a Muslim’s willpower and determination.

passages.heading: The Position of the Prayer in Islam
passages.text:
The prayer has a number of distinctive characteristics, including the following:

- It is the second pillar of Islam after the two testimonies of faith.
- It is the act of worship that must be performed under all circumstances, in times of war and peace, and whether one is sick or in good health.
- It is the act of worship that distinguishes a Muslim from a non-Muslim.

passages.heading: Islamic Rulings Pertaining to Meat Served in Restaurants and Shops
passages.text:
1. The meat of animals that are slaughtered by other than a Muslim or a member of the People of the Book (a Christian or a Jew), such as a Buddhist, or a Hindu is strictly forbidden. This includes meat served in restaurants and shops in countries where Muslims or People of the Book constitute a minority.
2. The meat of animals killed by a Muslim or a member of the People of the Book is lawful based on textual evidence to this effect in the Qur’an.
3. The meat of animals that are not killed according to Islamic law, such as by electrocution and drowning, is strictly forbidden.
4. The general rule is that it is permissible to consume the flesh of animals slaughtered by People of the Book as well as meat of animals generally found in their restaurants and shops, making sure, however, to invoke Allah’s name at the time of eating (that is, by saying *Bismillaah*), but it is better for Muslims to eat only meat that has been proven to be lawful (*halaal*).

passages.heading: Levels of Worship
Introduction
passages.text: Since ancient times, people on this earth have led different lives with varying living standards. Some are very well-to-do; others are destitute and can barely find anything to eat. This is one of Allah’s ways in this universe. Islam enjoins the wealthy to pay a certain percentage of their wealth to the poor to relieve them of the burden of poverty and urges Muslims to spend more of what they are required to spend, promising them great rewards for doing so both in this life and after death. It also urges them to give charity to the needy at all times and on every occasion and encourages them to feed the hungry and clothe the naked in order for the Muslim community to become close-knit, just as Allah Almighty wants it to be. In this lesson, we are going to learn about the Islamic ruling on *zakaat*, the manner of paying it and the types of wealth upon which it is due.

passages.heading: Introduction
passages.text: When Allah sent prophets to their people to call them to the truth, he supported them with some miracles to prove to them that they were true prophets. These miracles, however, ended with the passing of these prophets. As for the Messenger of Islam ﷺ, Allah also furnished him with certain miracles to show his people, and all mankind, for that matter, but the greatest of all of them was His Glorious Book, which He took upon Himself to preserve even after the demise of His prophet ﷺ. In this lesson, we are going to learn about some virtues and etiquette associated with the Qur’an.

passages.heading: Shirk
passages.text:
3. **Belief in the divinely revealed books:** A Muslim believes that Allah sent down divine books to His Messengers to guide people to the truth and teach them their religion. These include the Torah (*At-Tawraah*) which He revealed to Moses (Moosaa) son of ‘Imraan, the Zaboor which He revealed to David (Daawood), the Gospel (*Al-Injeel*) which He revealed to Jesus (‘Eesaa) son of Mary and the Qur’an which He revealed to Muhammad, peace be upon them all. He also believes that the Qur’an is the last of them and that it has final authority over them all.
4. **Belief in the prophets:** A Muslim believes that Allah Almighty sent messengers to their people and supported them with miracles to prove their truthfulness. He sent them to give the believers good news of reward, warn the unbelievers of punishment and teach their people their religion. Those to whom they were sent must obey and follow them. Muhammad ﷺ was the final prophet whom He sent to all mankind.
5. **Belief in the Last Day:** A Muslim believes in Resurrection Day. He believes that Allah will raise the dead from their graves on that day and judge and repay them according to their deeds. Some will enter Paradise while others will enter Hell.
6. **Belief in the divine decree:** A Muslim believes that everything in this universe, whether good or evil, happens according to Allah’s decree, that He foreknows all events which He has already written in the Preserved Tablet, and that everything in this universe happens according to His will.

passages.heading: *Tayammum* (Dry Ablution)
passages.text:
If a person who wants to perform *wudoo’* or *ghusl* is unable to do so due to illness, or when water is not readily available, or for any other legitimate reason, he may resort to dry ablution (*tayammum*) instead.

The Manner of Performing *Tayammum*: (1) Intend in his heart to perform *tayammum* and strike both hands slightly on pure earth once, (2) wipe the face with them, (3) wipe the back of the right hand with the palm of the left, and then the back of the left hand with the palm of the right hand.

passages.heading: The Criterion of Superiority in Islam
passages.text:
Piety is the criterion whereby Allah grants superiority to some over others. Superiority among Muslims can only be attained through strong faith, not one’s appearance, lineage, colour, or wealth. Allah Almighty says, {{Q:49:13}} (Soorat Al-Hjuraat, 49:13).

The Prophet ﷺ said: “O people! Your Lord is one and your father [Adam] is one. An Arab has no superiority over a non-Arab, nor does a non-Arab have any superiority over an Arab; a white person has no superiority over a black person, nor does a black person have any superiority over a white person except in piety.” (Reported by Al-Bayhaqee in Shu’ab al-Eemaan; No. 4774).

passages.heading: What is the Islamic Ruling on Seafood Consumption?
passages.text:
It is permissible to eat dead aquatic animals that can live only in water, such as fish and prawns, whether they live in the sea, rivers or lakes.

It is permissible to hunt wild, nonpredatory animals and consume their flesh provided that the name of Allah is mentioned before the hunting weapon is discharged, and the hunted game must be slaughtered if found still alive.

passages.heading: Discuss
passages.text:
With your partners, browse some Internet websites that help you find lawful (*halaal*) foods in your country.

The Islamic rulings on the meat of animals that are sold in shops and restaurants vary according to the religion of the person who slaughtered such animals.

passages.heading: Women in Relation to a Man
passages.text: Women in relation to a man fall into three categories:

passages.heading: Muslim Women’s Modest Style of Dress (*Hijaab*)
passages.text:
Allah enjoins women to wear the *hijaab* because women enjoy natural beauty and attraction that could easily tempt men into sinful acts, more than the other way round. Women are to cover their entire bodies when in the presence of men who are not related to them, and they may choose any design or colour they like for their *hijaab* as long as the following four conditions are met:

| First Condition | Second Condition | Third condition | Fourth Condition |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| It must appropriately cover the parts of the body that must be covered in public. | It must hang loose and must not fit very closely to the body so that the shape of the body is not revealed. | It must not allow the wearer’s body to be seen through its fabric. | It must not be a type of clothing that is generally considered attractive. |

passages.heading: The Types of Blood that Are Naturally Discharged by Women
passages.text:
The blood that is naturally discharged by women is of two types:

| Menstrual blood | Postnatal blood |
| --- | --- |
| This is a natural type of blood that flows from a woman’s uterus every month during her menstrual cycle and usually lasts for a few days. | This bleeding takes place after giving birth and lasts for several days, up to 40 days. |

passages.heading: Islamic Rulings Pertaining to Menstrual and Postnatal Bleeding
passages.text:
Allah Almighty has prescribed several rulings relating to menstruating women and women experiencing their postnatal bleeding, including the following:

- They are exempt from performing the prayers during this period and do not have to make up for the prayers they have missed while in this state after the end of menstrual and postnatal bleeding.
- They are exempt from fasting and are not allowed to fast while in this state, but they must make up for the fasting days they have missed in Ramadaan.
- During this period, a husband must not have intercourse with his wife during her menstrual or postnatal period. He is allowed, however, to satisfy his sexual desire but without having intercourse.
- At the end of the menstrual and postnatal period, when bleeding stops completely, women must take a ritual bath (*ghusl*).

passages.heading: Discuss
passages.text: What will a person who shows off his acts of worship lose by not intending to do them for the sake of Allah?

passages.heading: The Pillars of Islam
passages.text:
Islam is built on five pillars:

Every Muslim must strictly adhere to these pillars to ensure he is practising Islam in full; negligence in one of these pillars is bound to render the way you practise Islam deficient.

1. The two testimonies of faith: To bear witness that none is worthy of worship except Allah and that Muhammad is His His Messenger
2. Establish the prayer: A Muslim must pray five times a day. These prayers will be explained in due course.
3. Paying zakaat
4. Fasting in the month of Ramadaan
5. Making the pilgrimage to Allah’s House

passages.heading: Islamic Rulings Pertaining to Meat Served in Restaurants and Shops
passages.text:
1. The meat of animals that are slaughtered by other than a Muslim or a member of the People of the Book (a Christian or a Jew), such as a Buddhist, or a Hindu is strictly forbidden. This includes meat served in restaurants and shops in countries where Muslims or People of the Book constitute a minority.
2. The meat of animals killed by a Muslim or a member of the People of the Book is lawful based on textual evidence to this effect in the Qur’an.
3. The meat of animals that are not killed according to Islamic law, such as by electrocution and drowning, is strictly forbidden.
4. The general rule is that it is permissible to consume the flesh of animals slaughtered by People of the Book as well as meat of animals generally found in their restaurants and shops, making sure, however, to invoke Allah’s name at the time of eating (that is, by saying *Bismillaah*), but it is better for Muslims to eat only meat that has been proven to be lawful (*halaal*).

passages.heading: What is the Islamic Ruling on Seafood Consumption?

It is permissible to eat dead aquatic animals that can live only in water, such as fish and prawns, whether they live in the sea, rivers or lakes.

It is permissible to hunt wild, nonpredatory animals and consume their flesh provided that the name of Allah is mentioned before the hunting weapon is discharged, and the hunted game must be slaughtered if found still alive.

passages.heading: The Qur’an is a Way of Life
passages.text: A Muslim should be keen on reading/reciting the Holy Qur’an and studying the rules it prescribes.

passages.heading: What Are the Conditions for Islamic Slaughter?
passages.text:
Islamic slaughter is one that satisfies the following conditions:

1. The person undertaking the slaughtering process must be Muslim, Jew or Christian who has reached the age of discretion and carries out this act for the intended purpose.
2. The tool used for slaughter must be suitable for the intended purpose, causes blood to flow and sharp, such as a knife. It is forbidden to use anything that may kill the animal due to its heavy weight, hit its head to death or render it unconscious by resorting to electric stunning, for instance.
3. The name of Allah must be pronounced by saying *Bismillaah* (in the name of Allah) at the time of slaughtering the animal.
4. Cutting what must be cut in the Islamic slaughter, namely, the oesophagus, the throat, and the two jugular veins, or just three of these four.

5. He resumes the standing position, raising his hands up to the level of the shoulders or the ears, saying: Sami’allaahu li man hamidah “Allah hears those who praise Him.” Then he says while standing: Rabbanaa wa lakal-hamd “Our Lord, to You is due all praise.”

6. He says, Allaahu akbar “Allah is the Greatest” and prostrates himself, with the toes of both feet, the knees, the palms of the hands and the forehead and the nose touching the floor. He says three times while in this position, “Glory be to my Lord, Most High.”

passages.heading: Introduction
passages.text: Islam is the religion with which Allah sent Muhammad ﷺ and is an extension of the same religion with which all the previous messengers came. It is essentially based on the belief that Allah Almighty is the only deity deserving of worship, who has no partners or assistants whatsoever in His kingdom, and who has no intermediaries between Him and His servants. But why should I embrace Islam? Is it a religion for all people or is it only for the Arabs? Who is its prophet, and is there another prophet who will come after him?

passages.heading: How Do We Pray?
passages.text:
1. He intends in his heart to pray.
2. He stands facing the *qiblah*, raises his hands up to the level of the shoulders or ears, and says, “*Allaahu akbar* Allah is the Greatest.”
3. He places his right hand on his left hand. Then he recites one of the opening supplications, such as, Subhaanak-Allaahumma wa bi hamdika, wa tabaarak-asmuka, wa ta’aalaa jadduka, wa laa ilaaha ghayruka “Glory be to You, O Allah; Yours is the praise, blessed is Your name, exalted is Your majesty, and there is no god besides You.” Then he says, A’oodhu billaahi min-ash-shaytaan-ir-rajeem. Bismillaah-ir-rahmaan-ir-raheem “I seek Allah’s protection from Satan, who has been expelled from His mercy. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.” Then he recites *Soorat Al-Faatihah* and says after it, “*Aameen*”, which means “Answer our supplications, O Allah”. After that, he recites whatever number of verses of the Qur’an as is easy for him, even if it is one verse.
4. He says, “Allaahu akbar Allah is the Greatest” while raising his hands up to the level of his shoulders or ears, and bows down, lowering his head and back and keeping them straight at a right angle, placing the palms of his hands on the knees. He says three times while in this position, “Subhaana rabbiy-al-’adheem Glory be to my Lord, the Almighty.”

The Islamic rulings on the meat of animals that are sold in shops and restaurants vary according to the religion of the person who slaughtered such animals.

passages.heading: The Qur’an is a Way of Life
passages.text:
The Holy Qur’an is the Word of the Lord of all the worlds, who has created all mankind, knows them better than they know themselves and knows what benefits them and what harms them, hence the reason why Allah Almighty has made the Qur’an, which was the last of His revealed books, a didactic book which maps out a way of life for people, as evidenced by the following points:

- It deals with human life extensively, taking into account its three intrinsic spheres: personal life, family life and community life.
- Its deals with a wide array of matters, including, among other things, beliefs, acts of worship, customs, social and financial relations, man’s mental, emotional and physical states, international relations and peace and war.
- It promotes justice under all circumstances, even when dealing with enemies, and forbids injustice in all its forms.

> The Holy Qur’an maps out the way of life for people and defines and explains to them their rights and obligations with great flexibility, making its laws valid for all times and places.

passages.heading: Stories of the Prophets in the Qur’an
passages.text:
The Holy Qur’an is replete with stories of the previous prophets and their people, starting with Adam, and passing through Noah, Hud, Saalih, Shu’ayb, Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, Moses, Jesus, and other prophets and messengers, peace be upon them all. The Holy Qur’an mentions their stories for a number of reasons, including the following:

- to show that the religion of all the prophets is, in essence, the same and that its basis is to worship Allah Almighty alone.
- to give solace to Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and make him stand firm and steadfast, reminding him that prophets before him suffered the same hardships he himself was experiencing.
- to give comfort and solace to the believers, reminding them that even Allah’s honourable servants before them were afflicted with trials and tribulations.
- to afford people the opportunity to learn lessons from such true stories.

passages.heading: Allah Almighty has forbidden different types of food and drink, including the following:
passages.text:
- Alcohol, because it clouds the mind; indeed, preserving the mind is one of the objectives of Islamic law (*Sharee’ah*).
- Drugs, because they destroy the mind and body.
- Animals that die without having been slaughtered, or those that are slaughtered but the name of Allah (i.e., saying *Bismillaah* (in the name of Allah) was not mentioned at the time of slaughter.
- Pork—and indeed any of the pig’s body parts and by-products—because it is impure and thus forbidden for human consumption.
- Predatory animals, such as lions, tigers, hawks and eagles.
- Any animals that are sacrificed to false deities, such as idols.

The objectives of *Sharee’ah*: This is one of Islamic sciences by which Islamic laws are determined, such as the reason why Allah has laid down such-and-such a rule.

passages.heading: Quel est le jugement relatif à la consommation des animaux marins?
passages.text:
Concernant les animaux aquatiques qui ne vivent que dans l’eau, il est permis de consommer ceux qui sont morts, comme : les poissons, les crevettes, etc., qu’ils vivent dans les mers, les rivières ou les lacs.

Il est permis de chasser et de consommer les animaux terrestres à l’exception des prédateurs, à condition que le nom d’Allah soit mentionné lors de la chasse et qu’ils soient sacrifiés si on les trouve vivants.

passages.heading: Les nourritures et les boissons interdites:
passages.text:
Allah (Exalté et Magnifié soit-Il) a interdit certaines catégories de nourritures et de boissons, notamment :

- L’alcool: il dissipe la raison ; et la préservation de la raison est un but parmi les buts de la loi islamique.
- Les drogues: elles détruisent la raison et le corps.
- Les animaux morts sans avoir été sacrifiés ou ceux dont le nom d’Allah n’a pas été mentionné au moment de leur sacrifice.
- La viande de porc, car c’est une viande impure qui n’est pas permis de consommer.
- Les animaux prédateurs qui chassent, comme les lions, les tigres, les faucons et les aigles.
- Ce qui a été sacrifié pour des fausses divinités, comme les statues.

Les buts de la loi islamique:  
C’est une science parmi les sciences islamiques grâce à laquelle on découvre les jugements de la Charia ainsi que ses secrets tels que :  
Pourquoi Allah a-t-il légiféré ces lois et jugements ?  
Quelle est la raison de cette loi et de ce jugement ?

passages.heading: Jugements relatifs à la viande vendue dans les restaurants et les magasins:
passages.text:
1. Ce qui a été sacrifié par un non-musulman et quelqu’un ne faisant pas partie des Gens du Livre (juif ou chrétien), comme : les bouddhistes, les hindous et les athées, alors ceci est interdit. Est inclus dans cela ce que l’on trouve dans les restaurants et les magasins des pays dont les résidents sont majoritairement des non-musulmans et des Gens du Livre.
2. Ce que le musulman ou quelqu’un faisant partie des Gens du Livre a sacrifié de manière légale, alors ceci est permis, conformément au Coran.
3. Ce que le musulman ou quelqu’un faisant partie des Gens du Livre a tué d’une manière non conforme à la Charia, comme par décharge électrique ou par noyade, alors ceci est interdit.
4. La règle de base est le caractère licite de la bête de sacrifiée par personne faisant partie des Gens du Livre et donc ce que l’on trouve comme bêtes sacrifiées dans leurs restaurants et leurs magasins, tout en étant assidu à prononcer le nom d’Allah au moment de manger. Toutefois, il est préférable pour le musulman de ne manger que ce dont il est sûr comme étant des viandes halals et permises.

passages.heading: Les transactions financières interdites:
passages.text:
Allah (Exalté et Magnifié soit-Il) a interdit certaines transactions financières, notamment:

- Prendre illégalement et injustement l’argent ou les biens des gens, comme le prendre par ruse ou par spoliation.
- Contraindre ou Forcer une des deux parties à une transaction qu’elle ne veut pas accomplir.
- Faire du trafic de substances nocives pour la santé de l’homme, comme l’alcool, les drogues, le tabac, etc.
- L’intérêt usuraire qui est le prêt d’argent à condition qu’il soit rendu avec une augmentation d’un pourcentage sur l’argent emprunté, comme une augmentation de 5 % par exemple.
- Effectuer une vente de quelque chose d’inconnue, comme vendre une boîte dans laquelle on ne sait pas ce qu’il y a à l’intérieur.
- Tout ce qui concerne les jeux de hasard et les paris dans lesquels le gagnant prend illégalement et injustement l’argent du perdant.

passages.heading: Jugements liés à la purification :
passages.text:
- La règle de base concernant tout corps est la pureté et on ne juge de l’impureté d’une chose seulement si la Loi l’a jugée comme étant impure.
- Il suffit pour purifier le corps ou l’habit d’une impureté, d’enlever celle-ci avec de l’eau ou n’importe quel autre purifiant.
- Lorsqu’une personne entre dans la salle de bain pour faire ses besoins, il est préférable de nettoyer l’endroit de l’urine et des selles avec de l’eau. Il est [aussi] permis de se nettoyer avec des mouchoirs ou autre qui élimine les impuretés.

passages.heading: Le rang de la prière :
passages.text:
La prière se distingue par un ensemble de spécificités, notamment :

- Elle est considérée comme le second pilier parmi les piliers de l’Islam après les deux attestations.
- C’est l’adoration dont on doit s’acquitter en toute circonstance, que l’on soit en bonne santé ou malade, en situation de sécurité ou de peur, etc.
- C’est l’adoration qui distingue le musulman du mécréant.

passages.heading: Son miracle
passages.text: Les mécréants parmi les Arabes ont nié le Coran, alors Allah les a mis au défi d’en apporter un semblable, ou une sourate de celui-ci, ou dix versets, mais ils en ont été incapables.

passages.heading: La règle de base concernant la nourriture et la boisson.
passages.text: La règle de base concernant les nourritures et les boissons est la permission. Ainsi, rien concernant ces deux choses n’est interdit excepté si son interdiction a été rapportée dans le noble Coran ou la Tradition prophétique. Allah (Élevé soit-Il) a dit: {{Q:2:168}} (al Baqara, 2 : 168).

passages.heading: Quelles sont les conditions du sacrifice religieux?
passages.text:
Le sacrifice religieux est le sacrifice qui remplit les conditions suivantes:

1. Le sacrificateur doit être musulman ou juif ou chrétien, pubère et sachant sacrifier.
2. L’outil doit être adapté au sacrifice, faire couler le sang et couper avec son tranchant comme un couteau. Il est interdit d’utiliser tout ce qui tue la bête en la frappant à l’aide d’un objet lourd, ou de la brûler à l’aide de décharge électrique.
3. Le nom d’Allah doit être mentionné : “ Au nom d’Allah (BismiLlah) “ lors du geste de la main en vue du sacrifice.
4. Le fait de couper ce qui doit être coupé lors du sacrifice, qui correspond à : l’œsophage, la gorge et les deux jugulaires, qui sont les deux principales veines du cou, ou coupez trois de ces quatre.

passages.heading: Discute
passages.text:
Parcours avec tes camarades certains des sites Internet qui t’aident à obtenir des nourritures permises dans ton pays.

Le jugement concernant la viande qui est vendue dans les magasins et les restaurants diffère en fonction de la confession de la personne qui les a sacrifiés.

passages.heading: Leçon 2
passages.text: ## La nourriture et la boisson

passages.heading: Avant-propos
passages.text: Le musulman regarde la nourriture et la boisson comme étant parmi des bienfaits d’Allah qui impliquent le remerciement. Et parmi leur remerciement, il y a le fait de se renforcer à travers eux afin de s’acquitter des adorations. Et dans cette leçon, nous allons faire connaissance avec un ensemble de décrets et de bonnes manières liées à la nourriture et à la boisson tout comme nous allons découvrir des nourritures interdites que le musulman doit (obligatoirement) éviter.

passages.heading: Things That a Person Who Is in a State of *Jannabah* Must Not Do
passages.text:
The state into which a person gets following intercourse or ejaculation and because of which he must perform *ghusl* is called *janaabah*, and he is described as *junub*. In this case, he is not allowed to do the following:

1. perform the prayer
2. circumambulate the Ka’bah (*tawaaf*)
3. touch or carry the Qur’an
4. stay in the mosque
5. read the Qur’an

passages.heading: Soorat Al-Falaq Explained
passages.text:
“Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of the daybreak” Say, Messenger: I seek refuge and protection in Allah, the Lord of the daybreak.

“from the evil of what He has created”

from the evil of everything He has created, visible and invisible.

“and from the evil of the night when it spreads its darkness”

and from the evil of the night when it comes and grows dark, and of whatever evil and harm that may happen in it.

Al-ghasaq: the intense darkness of the night

Al-falaq: the daybreak

passages.heading: *Soorat Al-Kaafiroon* Explained
passages.text:
{{Q:109:1-6}}

“Say: Unbelievers!”

Say, Messenger, to those who disbelieve in Allah and His Messenger: You unbelievers.

“I do not worship what you worship”

I do not worship the false gods, such as idols, that you worship.

“nor do you worship what I worship”

nor do you worship the True God whom I worship, and who alone is worthy of worship.

“I will never worship what you worship”

I will never worship the false gods that you worship.

“nor will you ever worship what I worship”

nor will you ever worship the True God whom I worship, and who alone is worthy of worship.

Al-kaafir: The person who does not proclaim pure monotheism and does not follow the divine message Prophet Muhammad ﷺ has brought.

“You have your religion, and I have my religion”

You have your religion to which you adhere, and I have my religion to which I adhere.

passages.heading: The Virtue of Reading/Reciting the Qur’an
passages.text:
- The Prophet ﷺ said, “If anyone reads/recites one single letter in Allah’s Book, he will be credited with a good deed, and a good deed gets a tenfold reward. I do not say that *alif*, *laam*, *meem* are one letter; rather, *alif* is a letter, *laam* is a letter and *meem* is a letter” (Reported by At-Tirmidhee; No. 2910 with an authentic chain of narrators).

- The Prophet ﷺ also said, “Read the Qur’an, for it will come on the Day of Resurrection as an intercessor for those who read it.” (Reported by Muslim; No. 804).

passages.heading: When do I have to perform wudoo’ again?
passages.text: If a Muslim performs wudoo’, the general rule is that his wudoo’ is still valid unless one of the previously-mentioned things that break wudoo’ happens, in which case he must perform it again.

passages.heading: Soorat Al-Kawthar (Abundant Good)
passages.text:
*Soorat Al-Kawthar* **Explained**

{{Q:108:1-3}}

“We have bestowed on you abundant good”

We have given you, Messenger, immeasurable, abundant good in this life and the life to come, part of which is River Al-Kawthar in Paradise.

“So pray to your Lord and sacrifice to Him”

Therefore, sincerely pray to your Lord and worship Him alone, and sacrifice to Him, pronouncing Allah’s name alone when slaughtering animals, in gratitude to Him for the honour and good He has bestowed on you.

“He who hates you is the one who is truly cut off”

*Shaani’aka*: The one who hates you and hates the true religion you have brought.

The one who hates you and hates the true religion you have brought is the most disgraced and contemptible, whose mention is short-lived and who is cut off from all good.

passages.heading: Discuss
passages.text: What, in your opinion, does removing the major ritual impurity indicate?

passages.heading: *Tayammum* (Dry Ablution)
passages.text:
If a person who wants to perform *wudoo’* or *ghusl* is unable to do so due to illness, or when water is not readily available, or for any other legitimate reason, he may resort to dry ablution (*tayammum*) instead.

The Manner of Performing *Tayammum*: (1) Intend in his heart to perform *tayammum* and strike both hands slightly on pure earth once, (2) wipe the face with them, (3) wipe the back of the right hand with the palm of the left, and then the back of the left hand with the palm of the right hand.

passages.heading: What shall I do if I find water after having performed *tayammum*?

passages.heading: What Is the Qur’an?
passages.text:
The Holy Qur’an is the Word of Allah Almighty that He revealed to His Messenger, Muhammad ﷺ. It is the last of Allah’s revealed books, and there is no other book after it.

The revealed books are the books that Allah Almighty revealed to His prophets.
A Muslim believes that these books were revealed by Allah Almighty, and that Allah spoke in them in a manner that befits Him. These books include Az-Zaboor (the Psalms), which He revealed to Daawood (David) عليه السلام; At-Tawraat (the Torah), which He revealed to Moosaa (Moses) عليه السلام and Al-Injeel (the Gospel), which He revealed to Jesus, عليه السلام. All these books have undergone alteration and corruption through the ages.

passages.heading: The Qur’an is a Way of Life
passages.text:
The Holy Qur’an is the Word of the Lord of all the worlds, who has created all mankind, knows them better than they know themselves and knows what benefits them and what harms them, hence the reason why Allah Almighty has made the Qur’an, which was the last of His revealed books, a didactic book which maps out a way of life for people, as evidenced by the following points:

- It deals with human life extensively, taking into account its three intrinsic spheres: personal life, family life and community life.
- Its deals with a wide array of matters, including, among other things, beliefs, acts of worship, customs, social and financial relations, man’s mental, emotional and physical states, international relations and peace and war.
- It promotes justice under all circumstances, even when dealing with enemies, and forbids injustice in all its forms.

> The Holy Qur’an maps out the way of life for people and defines and explains to them their rights and obligations with great flexibility, making its laws valid for all times and places.

passages.heading: Introduction
passages.text: When Allah sent prophets to their people to call them to the truth, he supported them with some miracles to prove to them that they were true prophets. These miracles, however, ended with the passing of these prophets. As for the Messenger of Islam ﷺ, Allah also furnished him with certain miracles to show his people, and all mankind, for that matter, but the greatest of all of them was His Glorious Book, which He took upon Himself to preserve even after the demise of His prophet ﷺ. In this lesson, we are going to learn about some virtues and etiquette associated with the Qur’an.

passages.heading: Discuss
passages.text: What Qur’anic verses did you read before your conversion to Islam? How did they affect you?

passages.heading: Stories of the Prophets in the Qur’an
passages.text:
The Holy Qur’an is replete with stories of the previous prophets and their people, starting with Adam, and passing through Noah, Hud, Saalih, Shu’ayb, Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, Moses, Jesus, and other prophets and messengers, peace be upon them all. The Holy Qur’an mentions their stories for a number of reasons, including the following:

- to show that the religion of all the prophets is, in essence, the same and that its basis is to worship Allah Almighty alone.
- to give solace to Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and make him stand firm and steadfast, reminding him that prophets before him suffered the same hardships he himself was experiencing.
- to give comfort and solace to the believers, reminding them that even Allah’s honourable servants before them were afflicted with trials and tribulations.
- to afford people the opportunity to learn lessons from such true stories.

passages.heading: The Virtue of Reading/Reciting the Qur’an
passages.text:
- The Prophet ﷺ said, “If anyone reads/recites one single letter in Allah’s Book, he will be credited with a good deed, and a good deed gets a tenfold reward. I do not say that *alif*, *laam*, *meem* are one letter; rather, *alif* is a letter, *laam* is a letter and *meem* is a letter” (Reported by At-Tirmidhee; No. 2910 with an authentic chain of narrators).

- The Prophet ﷺ also said, “Read the Qur’an, for it will come on the Day of Resurrection as an intercessor for those who read it.” (Reported by Muslim; No. 804).

passages.heading: The Qur’an is Food for the Soul and Mind
passages.text:
The Holy Qur’an addresses both people’s minds and souls. It addresses the mind by:

- encouraging them to use logical reasoning on the various issues. The Almighty says, {{Q:21:22}} (Soorat Al-Anbiyyaa’, 21:22).
- calling them to exercise their intellects and contemplate His signs and the proofs of His power. The Almighty says, {{Q:2:219}} (Soorat Al-Baqarah, 2:219).
- reproving those who do not use their intellects to reflect on His signs. The Almighty says, {{Q:25:44}} (Soorat Al-Furqaan, 25: 44).

It also addresses the soul and emotions by:

- spotlighting and depicting human feelings in many cases. The Almighty says, {{Q:2:165}} (Soorat Al-Baqarah, 2:165).
- calling attention to human emotions and pointing out their good and bad effects. The Almighty says, {{Q:5:82}} (Soorat Al-Maa’idah, 5:82).
- commanding Muslims to exercise kindness and gentleness when inviting others to Islam. The Almighty says, {{Q:16:125}} (Soorat An-Nahl, 16: 125).
- incorporating aspects of faith into verses on legal rules. The Almighty says, {{Q:4:94}} (Soorat An-Nisaa’, 4:94).
- using moving words that evoke genuine emotions. The Almighty says, {{Q:24:22}} (Soorat An-Noor, 24:22).

passages.text: A Muslim should be keen on reading/reciting the Holy Qur’an and studying the rules it prescribes.

passages.heading: The Qur’an is Food for the Soul and Mind
passages.text: It may at times address the mind and the soul at the same time in one single verse which not only convinces the mind through logical reasoning but also arouses human passions. The Almighty says, {{Q:35:3}} (Soorat Faaṭir, 35:3).

passages.heading: Oração de Sexta-Feira (al-jumah)
passages.text:
- ALLAH Todo-Poderoso ordenou aos muçulmanos que fizessem uma oração especial na sexta-feira chamada (oração de sexta-feira), e tem um caráter especial e condições especiais, e é uma alternativa à oração do meio-dia para esse dia.
- Os muçulmanos se reúnem para isso na mesquita, então o pregador da mesquita faz dois sermões para eles, então reza com eles duas unidades de oração, nas quais ele recita o Alcorão em voz alta.
- Prescreve-se tomar banho para assistir à oração de sexta-feira e comparecer cedo. Não é permitido ausentar-se dela exceto por uma desculpa, e quem não o fizer deve fazer a oração do meio-dia quatro unidades de oração, durante as quais a recitação do Alcorão não é em voz alta.
- A oração de sexta-feira não é obrigatório para a mulher ou o viajante.

passages.heading: O bom comportamento no Islam:
passages.text:
- A boa moral tem um grande lugar no Islam, pois é um objetivo importante da Sharia islâmica e um dos objetivos da missão do Profeta ﷺ.
- A ética está intimamente relacionada à fé, de modo que os crentes com a fé mais completa são aqueles com a melhor moral.
- Um muçulmano é recompensado por suas boas maneiras, bem como pela oração e jejum.

passages.heading: A EXCELÊNCIA DO CARÁTER
passages.text:
* O Profeta, que a paz e as bênçãos de ALLAH estejam com ele, disse que as coisas que mais admitem as pessoas no Paraíso: temor a ALLAH e bom caráter.
* E ele disse, que a paz e as bênçãos estejam com ele, que a mais pesada das boas ações que serão colocadas na balança de uma pessoa no Dia da Ressurreição serão boas maneiras.
* E ele disse, que a paz e as bênçãos estejam com ele, que os crentes mais próximos dele no Dia da Ressurreição serão aqueles com a melhor moral.

> A balança do homem: Isso será no Dia da Ressurreição, quando os bons e maus do homem serão pesados em uma balança particular, e ninguém conhece sua forma ou tamanho, então quem supera suas boas ações entrará no Paraíso, e quem supera suas más ações entrará no inferno.

## A oração

10. É chamada de oração abraâmica.

passages.heading: Regras relacionadas com a pureza:
passages.text:
- O princípio em relação às coisas é sua pureza, e nada é julgado impuro exceto o que a religião decretou que é impuro.
- É suficiente para purificar o corpo ou a roupa da impureza removendo-o com água ou qualquer desinfetante.
- Quando a pessoa entra no banheiro para se aliviar, é melhor limpar o local da urina e fezes com água, e é permitido limpar com lenços ou outra coisa que remova a impureza.

passages.heading: Condições para a validade da oração
passages.text:
Existem várias condições necessárias para realizar a oração, que são:

- Pureza: Inclui a purificação do corpo e do local de impurezas e a pureza é feita através do wudhu ou do banho obrigatório.
- Cobrir a ‘awrah: A ‘awrah: o que deve ser coberto do corpo diante das pessoas. A awrah de um homem que deve ser coberta durante a oração é do umbigo ao joelho, e a awrah de uma mulher que deve ser coberta durante a oração é todo o seu corpo, exceto o rosto e as mãos.
- Direcionar para a Qibla: É a direção da Kaaba em Makkah Al-Mukarramah, então o adorador deve virar em sua direção durante a oração.
- Entrada do tempo da oração: Não é válido rezar antes de seu tempo começar, e não é permitido atrasá-la, e é melhor realizá-la no início do seu tempo.

A descrição do tayammum: Ele pretende fazer tayammum com o coração e bate as mãos na terra de uma só vez, depois passa com os restos de pó das mãos no rosto, depois enxuga as mãos.

passages.heading: O que devo fazer se encontrar água depois de realizar tayammum?
passages.text: Se um muçulmano encontra água ou é capaz de usá-la, sua pureza é invalidada e ele deve realizar ablução ou ghussl depois disso.

passages.heading: Islamic Rulings Pertaining to Menstrual and Postnatal Bleeding
passages.text:
Allah Almighty has prescribed several rulings relating to menstruating women and women experiencing their postnatal bleeding, including the following:

- They are exempt from performing the prayers during this period and do not have to make up for the prayers they have missed while in this state after the end of menstrual and postnatal bleeding.
- They are exempt from fasting and are not allowed to fast while in this state, but they must make up for the fasting days they have missed in Ramadaan.
- During this period, a husband must not have intercourse with his wife during her menstrual or postnatal period. He is allowed, however, to satisfy his sexual desire but without having intercourse.
- At the end of the menstrual and postnatal period, when bleeding stops completely, women must take a ritual bath (*ghusl*).

passages.heading: When do I have to perform wudoo’ again?
passages.text: If a Muslim performs wudoo’, the general rule is that his wudoo’ is still valid unless one of the previously-mentioned things that break wudoo’ happens, in which case he must perform it again.

passages.heading: Introduction
passages.text: There are some cases where *wudoo’* is not sufficient to perform an act of worship, but *ghusl* is required. In this lesson, we are going to learn about the meaning of *ghusl*, the reasons for performing it, as well as how to perform it.

passages.heading: Wiping over the Socks
passages.text: If a person wants to perform *wudoo’* while he has his socks on, he is allowed to just wipe over the top of them with wet hands, and there is no need to take them off and wash the feet. Three conditions are required for this:

passages.heading: The Manner of Performing the Full Ritual Bath (*Ghusl*)
passages.text:
If a Muslim wants to perform *ghusl*, he must do the following:

1. He intends in his heart to perform *ghusl* and washes out his private parts with water.
2. He performs *wudoo’* like the one he performs before the prayer.
3. He washes his entire body with water.

passages.heading: How to Perform *Ghusl*?
passages.text:
To perform *ghusl*, one must wash the entire body with water, rinse out one’s mouth and clean one’s nose by sniffing water into the nostrils and ejecting it out by blowing one’s nose. A Muslim removes the major ritual impurity by simply doing so.

> The major ritual impurity: what must be removed by ghusl, and ablution is not sufficient, and these are types:
> 
> 1- *Janaabah*: The state of ritual impurity following intercourse or ejaculation as a result of an orgasm even if no intercourse takes place.
> 2- Menstruation: the normal vaginal bleeding that occurs as part of a woman’s monthly cycle.
> 3- Postnatal bleeding: The vaginal bleeding that takes place following childbirth.

passages.text:

passages.heading: مجالات الأخلاق في الإسلام:
passages.text:
الأخلاق في الإسلام ليس لها مجالٌ واحد فقط، بل لها مجالات متعددة، وهي:

- الأخلاق مع الله عز وجل؛ كتقوى الله والإخلاص له.
- الأخلاق مع النبي ﷺ؛ كمحبته واحترامه ونصرته بالنفس والمال.
- الأخلاق مع الشريعة، كالتسليم لأحكام الشرع وتوقيرها.
- الأخلاق مع النفس؛ كالصبر والحلم.
- الأخلاق مع الآخرين؛ كالصدق والأمانة.
- الأخلاق مع الحيوانات؛ كالرعاية وعدم ضربها وتعذيبها.
- الأخلاق مع البيئة؛ كالمحافظة عليها من الفساد، وغرس الأشجار، وعدم الإسراف في خيراتها.

passages.heading: ناقش
passages.text: هل يمكن أن تكون الموضة أو العادات والتقاليد أو الأنظمة هي المرجعية التي من خلالها يتحدد اللباس المناسب للرجل أو المرأة؟

passages.heading: الأخلاق في الإسلام:
passages.text:
- الأخلاق الحسنة لها مكانة عظيمة في الإسلام، فهي مقصد مهم من مقاصد الشرعية الإسلامية، وهدف من أهداف بعثة النبي ﷺ.
- الأخلاق لها ارتباط وثيق بالإيمان، فأكمل المؤمنين إيمانًا أحسنهم أخلاقًا.
- يؤجر العبد على حسن خلقه، كما يؤجر على الصلاة والصوم.

passages.heading: مكانة المرأة في الإسلام:
passages.text:
من أمثلة الأحكام المتعلقة باحترام المرأة في الإسلام:
- أعطى الإسلام المرأة حقها من الميراث في قسمة عادلة كريمة، تساوي الرجل بالمرأة في مواضع، ويختلف نصيبها عنه في مواضع، بحسب قرابتها وتكاليف النفقة المناطة بها.
- ساوى بين الرجل والمرأة في شؤون كثيرة مختلفة ومن ذلك جميع التعاملات المالية..
- أعطى المرأة حرية اختيار الزوج.
- أبقى لها اسمها وشرف انتسابها لأبيها، فلا تتغير نسبتها بعد الزواج، بل تبقى منتسبة لأبيها وعائلتها.
- أوجب على الرجل رعايتها والإنفاق عليها بدون منّة إن كانت ممن تجب نفقته كالزوجة والأم والبنت.
- أكد على شرف وفضل خدمة المرأة الضعيفة التي ليس لها أحد، ولو لم تكن من الأقارب، ورغب في السعي لخدمتها وجعل ذلك من أفضل الأعمال عند الله.

passages.heading: لماذا نزكي؟
passages.text: يزكي المسلم من ماله؛ لأن في الزكاة ثلاثة أمور:

passages.heading: من أين جئنا؟
passages.text:
حكى الله لنا في القرآن قصة خلقه وكيف بدأ الشيطان في معاداته، أنظر تفسير سورة البقرة للآيات (٣٠-٣٩).

يبين الإسلام أن أصل خلق الإنسان من طين هذه الأرض، خلق الله منها آدم، وهو أبو البشر جميعًا، قال تعالى: {{Q:23:12}} (المؤمنون: ١٢).

والغاية من خلق هذا الإنسان عبادة الله تعالى، مع غناه سبحانه عن خلقه، قال تعالى: {{Q:51:56}} (الذاريات: ٥٦).

وهناك غاية أخرى فرعية، وهي عمارة هذه الأرض بإصلاحها، وإقامة العدل فيها، ونشر الخير، قال تعالى: {{Q:55:26}} (الرحمن: ٢٦).

passages.heading: فائدة
passages.text: يحترم الإسلام عادات الشعوب وتقاليدهم ولا يلزمهم بتغييرها إلا إذا خالفت شيئًا من شعائر الإسلام وتعاليمه.

passages.heading: تمهيد
passages.text: دعى الإسلام إلى الطهارة والنظافة، وأكد على المسلم أن يعتني بنظافته الشخصية، وجعل هذا الأمر من شعائر الدين، وربط صحة كثير من العبادات بتحقيق المسلم للطهارة، وهي من خصال المؤمن، ومن السمات التي يتميز بها المسلم عن غيره، وفي هذا الدرس سنتعرف على معنى الطهارة، وأنواعها، وبعض الأحكام المتعلقة بها.

passages.heading: تمهيد
passages.text: حث الإسلام أتباعه على التحلي بالأخلاق الحسنة، وقد أرشد الرسول ﷺ إلى أهمية الأخلاق في كثير من الأحاديث النبوية، وقرن بين كثير من العبادات التي يؤديها المسلم وبين حسن الخلق، والمسلم ذو الأخلاق الحميدة موعود بأجور عظيمة في الدنيا والآخرة، وفي هذا الدرس سنتعرف على أهمية الأخلاق في الإسلام، مع بيان بعض فضائلها.

passages.heading: ناقش
passages.text: كيف يمكن أن تكون أخلاق المسلم مع الآخرين؟ وهل لهذه الأخلاق أثر في حكمهم على الإسلام؟

passages.heading: فضل حسن الخلق:
passages.text:
- أخبر النبي ﷺ أن أكثر ما يدخل الناس الجنة: تقوى الله وحسن الخلق.
- وأخبر ﷺ أن أثقل ما يوضع في ميزان الإنسان يوم القيامة من الحسنات: حسن الخلق.
- وأخبر ﷺ أن أقرب المؤمنين منه منزلة يوم القيامة: أحسنهم أخلاقًا.

> يكون ذلك يوم القيامة حين يتم وزن حسنات الإنسان وسيئاته في ميزان مخصص لا يعلم أحدٌ هيئته ولا حجمه، فمن رجحت كفة حسناته دخل الجنة ومن رجحت كفة سيئاته دخل النار.

passages.heading: تمهيد
passages.text: خص الله عز وجل المرأة ببعض الصفات والخصائص التي تميزها عن الرجل، كما أوجب عليها بعض العبادات دون الرجل، وفي هذا الدرس سنتعرف على بعض الأحكام التي تخص المرأة المسلمة.

passages.heading: الدرس الخامس
passages.text: ## أحكام تخص المرأة المسلمة

passages.heading: علاقة المرأة بالرجل:
passages.text: تنقسم علاقة المرأة بالنسبة للرجل إلى ثلاثة أقسام:

passages.heading: الأول
passages.text: تطهير للنفس من التعلق بالمال والبخل به.

passages.heading: الثاني
passages.text: تكثيرٌ للمال، فإنها لا تنقصه بل تزيده وتبارك فيه.

passages.heading: الثالث
passages.text: إعانة للمحتاجين من الفقراء والمساكين وغيرهم.

passages.heading: من نحن؟
passages.text:
يعرّف الإسلام الإنسان بأنه مخلوق من مخلوقات الله تعالى الكثيرة، فضّله تعالى على كثيرٍ من المخلوقات، وسخّـر له كثيرًا من المخلوقات ليستعين بها على أداء مهامه المطلوبة منه مدة حياته. قال تعالى: {{Q:17:70}} (الإسراء: ٧٠).

وجعل الله تعالى في الإنسان شبهًا من:
- الملائكة في طهارتها وعبادتها.
- والشياطين في جحودها وعصيانها.
- والحيوانات في إشباعها لنزواتها وشهواتها.

> الملائكة: خلق من خلق الله تعالى، خلقهم الله عز وجل من نور، مربوبون مسخرون، عباد مكرمون، لا يعصون الله ما أمرهم ويفعلون ما يؤمرون، ولا يعلم عددهم إلا الله

وجعل فيه استعدادًا للخير، واستعدادًا للشر، وأعطاه ما يميّز به الخير من الشر؛ كالفطرة والعقل والحواس الخمسة.

وجعله حرًّا مختارًا مسؤولًا عن اختياراته وأعماله.

passages.heading: ناقش
passages.text: قارن بين نظرتك لمعنى وجودك قبل دخولك الإسلام وبعده:

passages.heading: إلى أين نذهب؟
passages.text:
بين القرآن الكريم أن كل إنسان سوف يموت في هذه الدنيا، وبموته تنتهي مرحلة العمل، وتبدأ مرحلة الحساب والجزاء، قال تعالى: {{Q:39:30-31}} (الزمر: ٣٠-٣١).

فإذا مات الإنسان انتقل إلى مرحلةٍ يسأل فيها عن دينه، ويجازى فيها على أعماله، قَالَ تَعَالَى: {{Q:3:185}} (آل عمران: ١٨٥).

فإذا جاء يوم القيامة، بعث الله تعالى الموتى من قبورهم للحساب والجزاء، ويجازى أهل الإيمان بالجنات، ويجازى أهل الكفر بالنيران، قال تعالى: {{Q:42:7}} (الشورى: ٧).

passages.heading: نعمة الهداية:
passages.text:
من عرف الحكمة من خلقه، والعاقبة التي تنتظر الناس يوم القيامة، أيقن أن أعظم نعمة ينعم الله بها على عباده هي نعمة الهداية إلى الدين الحق والعمل الصالح.

ولذلك أوجب الله عز وجل على عباده في صلاة أن يسألوه الهداية إلى الطريق المستقيم، الذي هو دين الإسلام، الموصل إلى رضوان الله تعالى.

passages.heading: ١ الإسلام دين عالمي
passages.text:
دين الإسلام ليس خاصًا بالعرب، بل هو الدين الذي ارتضاه الله تعالى للبشر جميعًا، ولذلك قال الله تعالى لرسوله محمد ﷺ: {{Q:21:107}} (الأنبياء:١٠٧).

فقد جعل الله عز وجل النبي ﷺ رحمةً عامّةً للناس جميعًا، يهديهم لطريق الإيمان، وجعل شريعته أوسع الشرائع رحمةً بالناس.

passages.heading: ٢ الإسلام يكفّر ما سبقه من الذنوب
passages.text:
إذا أسلم العبد، وفعل ما يجب عليه من الواجبات، واجتنب ما حرّم الله عليه، فإن الله تعالى يغفر له ما تقدّم من ذنوبه قبل إسلامه، وقد قال النبي ﷺ: « إذا أسلم العبد فحسن إسلامه، يكفر الله عنه كل سيئة كان زلفها، وكان بعد ذلك القصاص: الحسنة بعشر أمثالها إلى سبع مائة ضعف، والسيئة بمثلها إلا أن يتجاوز الله عنها ». أخرجه البخاري (٤١).

وقد سأل رجل النبي ﷺ: يا رسول الله، أنؤاخذ بما عملنا في الجاهلية؟ فأجابه النبي ﷺ: «من أحسن في الإسلام لم يؤاخذ بما عمل في الجاهلية، ومن أساء في الإسلام أُخذ بالأول والآخر». أخرجه البخاري (٦٩٢١).

passages.heading: ٣ الإسلام الدين الخاتم
passages.text: جعل الله تعالى الإسلام امتدادًا للشرائع السماويّة السابقة، وارتضاه دينًا للخَلق جميعًا إلى قيام الساعة، فلا يوجد على وجه الأرض دينٌ حقٌّ سوى دين الإسلام؛ قال تعالى: {{Q:3:85}} (آل عمران:٨٥).

passages.heading: ناقش
passages.text: كيف ترد على من يزعم أن الإسلام دين خاص بالعرب؟

passages.heading: The Friday Prayer (Salaat-ul-Jumu’ah)
passages.text:
- Allah Almighty has enjoined Muslims to perform a special prayer on Friday, called *Salaat-ul-Jumu’ah* (the Friday prayer). It is performed in a special manner, has special conditions and takes the place of the daily *Dhuhr* (midday) prayer on this day.
- Muslims gather together to perform it in the mosque. The *imaam* delivers a two-section *khutbah* (sermon), then he leads them in a two-*rak’ahs* prayer in which he recites the Qur’an aloud.
- It is recommended to take a ritual bath (*ghusl*) to attend the Friday prayer and proceed early to the mosque. It is not permissible to miss it without a legitimate excuse, and if for any reason a person misses it he must perform the four-unit *Dhuhr* (midday) prayer instead but without reciting the Qur’an aloud.
- Women and people on a journey are exempt from performing the Friday prayer.

passages.heading: Islamic Rulings Pertaining to Menstrual and Postnatal Bleeding
passages.text:
Allah Almighty has prescribed several rulings relating to menstruating women and women experiencing their postnatal bleeding, including the following:

- They are exempt from performing the prayers during this period and do not have to make up for the prayers they have missed while in this state after the end of menstrual and postnatal bleeding.
- They are exempt from fasting and are not allowed to fast while in this state, but they must make up for the fasting days they have missed in Ramadaan.
- During this period, a husband must not have intercourse with his wife during her menstrual or postnatal period. He is allowed, however, to satisfy his sexual desire but without having intercourse.
- At the end of the menstrual and postnatal period, when bleeding stops completely, women must take a ritual bath (*ghusl*).

Islam has made it the husband’s duty to spend on those women entitled to his support without attempting in the least to remind them of his favours.

A woman’s style of dress (*hijaab*) does not have to be loose.

Menstrual blood is a natural type of blood that flows from a woman’s uterus after childbirth.

passages.heading: Things That a Person Who Is in a State of *Jannabah* Must Not Do
passages.text:
The state into which a person gets following intercourse or ejaculation and because of which he must perform *ghusl* is called *janaabah*, and he is described as *junub*. In this case, he is not allowed to do the following:

1. perform the prayer
2. circumambulate the Ka’bah (*tawaaf*)
3. touch or carry the Qur’an
4. stay in the mosque
5. read the Qur’an

passages.heading: The Meaning of Worship
passages.text: By worship is meant everything that Allah has enjoined on us for us to draw closer to Him. It comprises all words and deeds that Allah loves, whether they are outward like the physical acts of worship, such as the prayer and pilgrimage, or inward, like the acts of worship involving the heart, such as love of Allah, fearing His punishment and hoping for His mercy. A person can transform everyday habits into acts of worship simply by having a good intention. If, for instance, he eats, drinks and sleeps with the intention of gaining enough strength to worship Allah better, he will certainly be rewarded for doing so

passages.heading: Introduction
passages.text: Allah Almighty has bestowed some characteristics on women that distinguish them from men and enjoined on them certain acts of worship to the exclusion of men. In this lesson, we are going to learn about some rulings that pertain to Muslim women.

passages.heading: Introduction
passages.text: Muslims consider food and drink to be among the countless blessings of Allah for which they must show gratitude. Part of showing gratitude for them lies in gaining strength from them to perform the acts of worship properly. In this lesson, we are going to learn about a set of rulings and etiquette related to food and drink, as well as forbidden foods that Muslims must avoid.

11. He turns his face to his right and says: Assalaamu ‘alaykum wa rahmatullaah “May Allah’s peace and mercy be upon you.” Then he turns his face to his left and says the same this. With this, he concludes his prayer.

This manner only applies to a prayer that consists of two units (*rak’ahs*), such as *Fajr* and *Jumu’ah* prayers. If, however, the prayer consists of three units (*rak’ahs*), namely *Maghrib*, or four units (*rak’ahs*), namely *Dhuhr*, *‘Asr* and *‘Ishaa’*, he completes the remaining units after concluding the first *tashahhud*, in the same way he has performed the first *rak’ah* but without reciting anything else after *Soorat Al-Faatihah*, then sits as he has done after the second *rak’ah*, recites the first *tashahhud* and *As-Salaatu Al-Ibraaheemiyyah*, and then concludes the prayer by saying, Assalaamu ‘alaykum wa rahmatullaah May Allah’s peace and mercy be upon you.” first to the right and then to the left.

passages.heading: *Tayammum* (Dry Ablution)
passages.text:
If a person who wants to perform *wudoo’* or *ghusl* is unable to do so due to illness, or when water is not readily available, or for any other legitimate reason, he may resort to dry ablution (*tayammum*) instead.

The Manner of Performing *Tayammum*: (1) Intend in his heart to perform *tayammum* and strike both hands slightly on pure earth once, (2) wipe the face with them, (3) wipe the back of the right hand with the palm of the left, and then the back of the left hand with the palm of the right hand.

passages.heading: What shall I do if I find water after having performed *tayammum*?
passages.text: If a Muslim finds water or can use it, his purity becomes invalid, in which case he must perform *wudoo’* or *ghusl*.

passages.heading: The Position of Women in Islam
passages.text: Examples of rulings that honour and show respect to women in Islam:

passages.heading: The Position of Women in Islam
passages.text:
- Islam has granted women the right to inheritance, allocating them equitable shares with men, which sometimes differ under certain circumstances depending on their relationship with others and the financial obligations they have to discharge. While men support the family as a matter of religious obligation, women are not obliged to spend anything at all.
- It has established total equality between men and women in numerous matters including financial transactions.
- It has granted them the right to choose their own husbands.
- It has granted them the right to retain their maiden names. In Islam, a woman does not change her surname to that of her husband upon marriage; rather, she retains her maiden name, and thus her independent personality.
- It has made it the husband’s duty to spend on those women entitled to his support, such as his wife, mother and daughters, without attempting in the least to remind them of his favours.
- It stresses the importance of helping weak and vulnerable women who are in need of support, even if they are not one’s relatives, and urges its adherents to engage in such a noble act, which it considers one of the meritorious deeds in the sight of Allah.

passages.heading: Soorat Al-Kawthar (Abundant Good)
passages.text:
*Soorat Al-Kawthar* **Explained**

{{Q:108:1-3}}

“We have bestowed on you abundant good”

We have given you, Messenger, immeasurable, abundant good in this life and the life to come, part of which is River Al-Kawthar in Paradise.

“So pray to your Lord and sacrifice to Him”

Therefore, sincerely pray to your Lord and worship Him alone, and sacrifice to Him, pronouncing Allah’s name alone when slaughtering animals, in gratitude to Him for the honour and good He has bestowed on you.

“He who hates you is the one who is truly cut off”

*Shaani’aka*: The one who hates you and hates the true religion you have brought.

The one who hates you and hates the true religion you have brought is the most disgraced and contemptible, whose mention is short-lived and who is cut off from all good.

passages.heading: What Are the Conditions for Islamic Slaughter?
passages.text:
Islamic slaughter is one that satisfies the following conditions:

1. The person undertaking the slaughtering process must be Muslim, Jew or Christian who has reached the age of discretion and carries out this act for the intended purpose.
2. The tool used for slaughter must be suitable for the intended purpose, causes blood to flow and sharp, such as a knife. It is forbidden to use anything that may kill the animal due to its heavy weight, hit its head to death or render it unconscious by resorting to electric stunning, for instance.
3. The name of Allah must be pronounced by saying *Bismillaah* (in the name of Allah) at the time of slaughtering the animal.
4. Cutting what must be cut in the Islamic slaughter, namely, the oesophagus, the throat, and the two jugular veins, or just three of these four.

passages.text: A Muslim must perform *ghusl* in three cases:

passages.text:
- **Gold and silver**
- **All types of currency (banknotes and coins)**
- **Farm produce (crops and fruit)**
- **Grazing livestock**

Grazing livestock: This refers to camels, cattle, sheep and goats.

- **Commercial commodities**

Commercial commodities: all properties owned with the aim of investing them in trade. They generally include assets, such as a house, a shop, a car and an animal.

passages.heading: The Second Question
passages.text:
#### Where Did We Come from, and Why Are We Here?

Islam explains that the origin of man’s creation is clay from which Allah Almighty created Adam, the father of all mankind: {{Q:23:12}} (Soorat Al-Mu’minoon, 23:12) Allah created mankind for the sole purpose of worshipping Him even though He is Self-Sufficient and does not stand in need of their worship. The Almighty says, {{Q:51:56}} (Soorat Adh-Dhaariyyaat, 51:56) A secondary reason for human existence is for man to settle on the earth and thus build civilisation, establish justice and spread good. The Almighty says, {{Q:11:61}} (Soorat Hood, 11:61).

**Adam**
Allah tells us in the Qur’an the story of Adam’s creation and how Satan’s enmity towards him started. See the interpretation of Verses 30-39 in Soorat Al-Baqarah.

passages.heading: *Soorat Al-Kaafiroon* Explained
passages.text:
{{Q:109:1-6}}

“Say: Unbelievers!”

Say, Messenger, to those who disbelieve in Allah and His Messenger: You unbelievers.

“I do not worship what you worship”

I do not worship the false gods, such as idols, that you worship.

“nor do you worship what I worship”

nor do you worship the True God whom I worship, and who alone is worthy of worship.

“I will never worship what you worship”

I will never worship the false gods that you worship.

“nor will you ever worship what I worship”

nor will you ever worship the True God whom I worship, and who alone is worthy of worship.

Al-kaafir: The person who does not proclaim pure monotheism and does not follow the divine message Prophet Muhammad ﷺ has brought.

“You have your religion, and I have my religion”

You have your religion to which you adhere, and I have my religion to which I adhere.

passages.heading: Introduction
passages.text: In his life, a Muslim performs a number of acts of worship whereby he draws closer to his Creator, Glory is to Him. We do such acts to glorify Allah Almighty and submit to Him alone. The more a Muslim’s heart glorifies Allah, Exalted be He, the greater the effect of doing so is on his worship. A true Muslim dedicates all life, including the time he spends at work, sleeping and having fun, to Allah Almighty, bearing in mind the verse: {{Q:6:162-163}} (Soorat Al-An’aam, 6:162-163) In this lesson, we are going to learn about the meaning of worship, its types, the conditions that must be met for it to be accepted, and its levels.

passages.heading: What is *Hajj*?
passages.text:
*Hajj* is an act of worship for which physically and financially able Muslims travel to Makkah to perform certain acts of worship during the month of Dhul-Hijjah, which is the last month of the lunar calendar.

*Hajj* is the fifth pillar of Islam

The Islamic *Hijri* Calendar is a lunar calendar is associated with the Prophet’s migration, or *hijrah*, from Makkah to Madeenah. Third Rightly-Guided Caliph ‘Umar ibn Al-Khattaab, may Allah be pleased with him, decided that the most appropriate reference point for the Islamic calendar would be the Prophet’s *hijrah*. The Islamic Calendar has twelve months, beginning with the month of Muharram and ending with the month of Dhul-Hijjah. Muslims have adopted the Islamic *Hijri* calendar to date incidents and events.

passages.heading: Lesson 2
passages.text: ## The Interpretation of Short *Surahs*

passages.heading: Soorat Al-’A<u>s</u>r (The Time)
passages.text:
*Soorat Al-’A<u>s</u>r* **Explained**

{{Q:103:1-3}}

“By the time”

Allah swears by the time in which people’s good and evil deeds take place.

“Truly man is in loss”

Mankind is indeed in sheer loss and ruin,

“except for those who believe and do good works; who exhort each other to justice and to fortitude”

except for those who believe in Allah, do righteous deeds, and urge one another to adhere to the truth and to be patient and steadfast in doing so.

passages.heading: Allah Almighty has forbidden different types of food and drink, including the following:
passages.text:
- Alcohol, because it clouds the mind; indeed, preserving the mind is one of the objectives of Islamic law (*Sharee’ah*).
- Drugs, because they destroy the mind and body.
- Animals that die without having been slaughtered, or those that are slaughtered but the name of Allah (i.e., saying *Bismillaah* (in the name of Allah) was not mentioned at the time of slaughter.
- Pork—and indeed any of the pig’s body parts and by-products—because it is impure and thus forbidden for human consumption.
- Predatory animals, such as lions, tigers, hawks and eagles.
- Any animals that are sacrificed to false deities, such as idols.

The objectives of *Sharee’ah*: This is one of Islamic sciences by which Islamic laws are determined, such as the reason why Allah has laid down such-and-such a rule.

passages.heading: What is the Islamic Ruling on Seafood Consumption?
passages.text:
It is permissible to eat dead aquatic animals that can live only in water, such as fish and prawns, whether they live in the sea, rivers or lakes.

It is permissible to hunt wild, nonpredatory animals and consume their flesh provided that the name of Allah is mentioned before the hunting weapon is discharged, and the hunted game must be slaughtered if found still alive.

passages.heading: Islamic Rulings Pertaining to Meat Served in Restaurants and Shops
passages.text:
1. The meat of animals that are slaughtered by other than a Muslim or a member of the People of the Book (a Christian or a Jew), such as a Buddhist, or a Hindu is strictly forbidden. This includes meat served in restaurants and shops in countries where Muslims or People of the Book constitute a minority.
2. The meat of animals killed by a Muslim or a member of the People of the Book is lawful based on textual evidence to this effect in the Qur’an.
3. The meat of animals that are not killed according to Islamic law, such as by electrocution and drowning, is strictly forbidden.
4. The general rule is that it is permissible to consume the flesh of animals slaughtered by People of the Book as well as meat of animals generally found in their restaurants and shops, making sure, however, to invoke Allah’s name at the time of eating (that is, by saying *Bismillaah*), but it is better for Muslims to eat only meat that has been proven to be lawful (*halaal*).

passages.heading: Discuss
passages.text:
With your partners, browse some Internet websites that help you find lawful (*halaal*) foods in your country.

The Islamic rulings on the meat of animals that are sold in shops and restaurants vary according to the religion of the person who slaughtered such animals.

passages.heading: The Manner of Performing the Full Ritual Bath (*Ghusl*)
passages.text:
If a Muslim wants to perform *ghusl*, he must do the following:

1. He intends in his heart to perform *ghusl* and washes out his private parts with water.
2. He performs *wudoo’* like the one he performs before the prayer.
3. He washes his entire body with water.

passages.heading: Introduction
passages.text: *Hajj*, the annual Muslim pilgrimage to Makkah, is one of the pillars of Islam and one of the best deeds whereby Muslims seek to draw closer to Allah Almighty. Its virtues are mentioned in numerous traditions of the Prophet ﷺ. In this lesson, we are going to learn a little information about this great act of worship.

passages.heading: Why Do We Perform *Hajj*?
passages.text: Muslims perform *Hajj* to the Sacred House in Makkah in response to Allah’s command to do so.

passages.heading: Some of the Ultimate Objectives and Benefits of *Hajj*
passages.text:
- To follow the example of the honourable prophets who made the pilgrimage to the Sacred House.
- To occupy oneself with worship: Pilgrims devote themselves to the worship of Allah, moving from one act of worship to another.
- To meet Muslims who come from the four corners of the world and gather in the holy sites, get to know them and build bridges of communication with them.

passages.heading: Discuss
passages.text: Discuss this act of worship with your partners who have already performed *hajj* and find out from them about their feelings when they performed it.

passages.heading: Pourquoi embrasser l’Islam ?
passages.text:
Certaines personnes peuvent s’interroger :

“ Pourquoi m’est-il obligatoire d’embrasser l’Islam ?

La réponse : Il est obligatoire que j’embrasse l’Islam pour diverses raisons, notamment :

1. La religion de l’Islam est la religion qu’Allah a agréé pour Ses serviteurs et Il n’accepte aucune autre religion en dehors de celle-ci. Il (Élevé soit-Il) a dit : {{Q:3:85}} (Âl ‘Imrâne, 3 : 85).

2. La religion de l’Islam est la religion de l’ensemble des prophètes. L’Islam ordonne de croire en tous les prophètes et ne fait pas de différence entre eux. Il (Élevé soit-Il) a dit : {{Q:2:136}} (al Baqara, 2 : 136).

Et la différence entre les prophètes est une différence dans les jugements législatifs qui sont liés aux actes des serviteurs, comme Il (Glorifié soit-Il) a dit : {{Q:5:48}} (al Mâida, 5 : 48).

passages.heading: Pourquoi embrasser l’Islam ?
passages.text: C’est-à-dire : Allah a établi pour chaque communauté parmi les communautés une législation vers laquelle ils reviennent pour juger et une voie à travers laquelle ils se rapprochent de Lui. En effet, tout peuple ayant une croyance a des jugements qui lui sont spécifiques et des législations qui lui conviennent. Mais en ce qui concerne la croyance, alors la croyance des prophètes est unique et identique.

Ensuite, Allah a envoyé le sceau de Ses prophètes et messagers Muhammad ﷺ, et par son biais Il a scellé la prophétie et Il a [aussi] scellé les lois par sa législation. Ainsi, aucune religion n’est acceptée de qui que ce soit si ce n’est l’Islam.

3. L’entrée en l’Islam est la voie du bonheur dans ce bas monde et celle du salut dans l’au-delà. Ainsi donc, dans l’au-delà, personne ayant reçu l’appel du Prophète Muhammad ﷺ ne sera sauvé, excepté quiconque aura cru en lui et l’aura suivi. Il (Élevé soit-Il) a dit : {{Q:3:85}} (Âl ‘Imrâne 3 : 85) Il ﷺ a dit : “ Par Celui qui détient l’âme de Muhammad dans Sa Main ! Pas un juif ou un chrétien de cette communauté entend parler de moi, et ensuite meurt sans croire en ce avec quoi j’ai été envoyé sans qu’il soit parmi les gens de l’Enfer. “ (Rapporté par Mouslim n°153).

passages.heading: Parmi les spécificités de l’Islam :
passages.text: L’Islam se distingue du reste des religions par de nombreuses spécificités dont les plus manifestes sont :

passages.heading: 1 L’Islam est une religion universelle
passages.text: La religion de l’Islam n’est pas spécifique aux Arabes ; plutôt, elle est la religion qu’Allah (Élevé soit-Il) a agréé pour tous les êtres humains et c’est pourquoi Allah (Élevé soit-Il) a dit à Son Messager Muhammad ﷺ {{Q:21:107}} (al Anbiyâ, 21 : 107). Ainsi donc, Allah (Exalté et Magnifié soit-Il) a fait du Prophète ﷺ une miséricorde générale pour tous les hommes, les guidant sur le chemin de la foi, et Il a fait de sa loi la plus large des lois comme une miséricorde pour les hommes.

passages.heading: Les bienfaits de la foi :
passages.text:
- **La sérénité de l’âme :** En effet, la foi tranquillise l’âme du croyant, elle est satisfaite d’Allah et de Son destin et elle ne craint qu’Allah.
- **La connaissance d’Allah (Élevé soit-Il) :** Le croyant connaît ainsi son Seigneur par la connaissance de Ses Noms, Ses Attributs et Ses Actes. Et celle-ci accroît son attachement à Lui.
- **La grandeur d’Allah :** Plus le croyant connait son Seigneur, plus cela augmente la grandeur et la splendeur qu’il a de son Seigneur et ainsi cela augmente son amour et l’espoir qu’Il a en Lui, et par conséquent cela accroît sa peur et sa crainte de Lui.
- **Le sentiment de la grâce d’Allah sur Ses serviteurs :** En effet, Il leur a envoyé des messagers et Il a fait descendre sur eux des livres pour qu’ils soient guidés vers religion de la vérité.
- **L’amour des Anges :** En raison de leur adoration d’Allah et de leur obéissance à leur Seigneur.
- **L’amour des Messagers :** En effet, Allah (Élevé soit-Il) les a élus en vue de la transmission de Son message aux gens.
- **L’effort dans l’adoration :** Plus la foi se renforce, plus l’adoration de la personne augmente.
- **La vie agréable :** le croyant se satisfait de ce qu’Allah lui a attribué et il sait que ce qui l’atteint comme calamités en ce bas monde sont une élévation de ses degrés et une expiation de ses mauvaises actions. Il en est de même de ce qu’il espère concernant ce qu’Allah lui a préparé comme délices pour les croyants dans l’au-delà.
- **Le fait de ne pas être leurré par ce bas monde :** En effet, la vie d’ici-bas est temporaire et elle n’est qu’un chemin vers la vie éternelle dans l’au-delà.
- **La mise en évidence de la fausseté des superstitions :** En effet, la foi rend caduc beaucoup de ces mythes et fausses croyances.
- **L’entrée au Paradis :** Elle est la demeure des Délices perpétuels qui ne cesseront pas. Et Allah (Élevé soit-Il) l’a spécifiquement accordée aux croyants parmi Ses serviteurs.

passages.heading: Qui est le prophète de l’Islam ?
passages.text: Le musulman croit que Muhammad ﷺ est le sceau des prophètes qu’Allah a envoyé aux hommes pour les appeler à Son adoration uniquement. Nul prophète ne lui succédera, Allah (Élevé soit-Il) a dit : {{Q:33:40}} (al Ahzâb, 33 : 40).

passages.heading: Le critère de supériorité en l’Islam :
passages.text:
Allah (Exalté et Magnifié soit-Il) a établi le critère de supériorité entre Ses serviteurs par la foi et la piété. Ainsi donc, la supériorité entre les musulmans est basée sur la force de leur foi et non sur leurs apparences, leurs lignées, leurs couleurs, ou leurs richesses. En effet, Il (Élevé soit-Il) a dit : {{Q:49:13}} (Al Houjourât, 49 : 13).

Le Prophète ﷺ a dit : ” Ô gens ! Votre Seigneur n’est-il pas Unique et votre père n’est-il pas unique ? Certes, l’Arabe n’est pas supérieur au non Arabe et le non-Arabe n’est pas supérieur à l’Arabe, le rouge n’est pas supérieur au noir et le noir n’est pas supérieur au rouge, excepté par la piété. “ Rapporté par Al Bayhaqî dans “ Chou’ab al Îmâne “ (n°4774).
