passages.heading: Its names
passages.text: Allah calls it Al-Qur’aan (the Qur’an), *Al-Kitaab* (the Book), *Al-Furqaan* (the Criterion) and *Adh-Dhhikr* (the Remembrance). It has several other names.

passages.heading: The Pillars of Faith
passages.text:
The Muslim faith rests on six pillars, namely:

1. **Belief in Allah:** A Muslim believes that Allah Almighty exists and believes in His names and attributes. He equally believes that He is the Lord and sole Creator of this vast universe, to whom belongs everything in it, who manages all its affairs and provides sustenance to all His creation, that there is no god is worthy of worship besides or instead of Him and that He has perfect attributes.
2. **Belief in the angels:** A Muslim believes that the honourable angels exist, that it is Allah Almighty who created them and that they worship Him, execute His commands and never disobey Him. He also believes in their attributes and duties which are mentioned in the Book and the *Sunnah*.

passages.heading: Islamic Rulings Pertaining to Menstrual and Postnatal Bleeding
passages.text:
Allah Almighty has prescribed several rulings relating to menstruating women and women experiencing their postnatal bleeding, including the following:

- They are exempt from performing the prayers during this period and do not have to make up for the prayers they have missed while in this state after the end of menstrual and postnatal bleeding.
- They are exempt from fasting and are not allowed to fast while in this state, but they must make up for the fasting days they have missed in Ramadaan.
- During this period, a husband must not have intercourse with his wife during her menstrual or postnatal period. He is allowed, however, to satisfy his sexual desire but without having intercourse.
- At the end of the menstrual and postnatal period, when bleeding stops completely, women must take a ritual bath (*ghusl*).

passages.heading: Some of the Ultimate Objectives and Benefits of the Prayer:
passages.text:
- It is the direct, special and personal communion a Muslim establishes with his Lord.
- It relieves the mind of worry and all worldly anxieties.
- It strengthens a Muslim’s willpower and determination.
- It refines morals and keeps those who observe it away from evil.

passages.heading: The Conditions of the Prayer
passages.text:
- Purity: Once’s body and the place where the prayer is to be performed must be cleansed from physical impurities, and any ritual impurity must be removed with *wudoo’* or *ghusl*.
- Covering the intimate parts of the body (*‘awrah*): The word *‘awrah* refers to the parts of the body that must be covered in front of people. A man’s *‘awrah* that must be covered during the prayer extends from the navel to the knees; a woman’s *‘awrah* that must be covered during the prayer is her entire body except for the face and hands.
- Facing the *qiblah*: The *qiblah* is the direction of the Ka‘bah in Makkah. One must, therefore, pray in the direction of the Ka‘bah in Makkah.
- When its appointed time becomes due: The prayer will not be valid if it is performed before its time has started. It is not permissible to delay it beyond its due time, and it is best to perform it at the beginning of its time.

passages.heading: The Five Obligatory Prayers
passages.text:
Allah Almighty has enjoined Muslims to perform five prayers throughout the day and night, namely:

| The Prayer | Beginning Time | Ending Time | Number of units (*rak‘ahs*) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| *Fajr* (Dawn) Prayer | at the break of dawn | sunrise | 2 |
| *Dhuhr* (Midday) Prayer | when the sun starts declining westward at midday after reaching its zenith | when the shadow of an object becomes equal in length to the object itself | 4 |
| *‘Asr* (Late Afternoon) Prayer | when the shadow of an object becomes equal in length to the object itself | sunset | 4 |
| *Maghrib* (Sunset) Prayer | sunset | when the red glow (evening twilight) on the western horizon disappears | 3 |
| *‘Ishaa’* (Late Evening) Prayer | when the red glow (evening twilight) on the western horizon disappears | midnight | 4 |

passages.heading: The General Islamic Rule Regarding Food and drink
passages.text: The general Islamic rule is that everything is presumed permissible unless proven otherwise in the Qur’an or the Prophet’s *Sunnah*. The Almighty says, {{Q:2:168}} *(Soorat Al-Baqarah, 2:168)*.

passages.heading: Allah Almighty has forbidden different types of food and drink, including the following:
passages.text:
- Alcohol, because it clouds the mind; indeed, preserving the mind is one of the objectives of Islamic law (*Sharee’ah*).
- Drugs, because they destroy the mind and body.
- Animals that die without having been slaughtered, or those that are slaughtered but the name of Allah (i.e., saying *Bismillaah* (in the name of Allah) was not mentioned at the time of slaughter.
- Pork—and indeed any of the pig’s body parts and by-products—because it is impure and thus forbidden for human consumption.
- Predatory animals, such as lions, tigers, hawks and eagles.
- Any animals that are sacrificed to false deities, such as idols.

The objectives of *Sharee’ah*: This is one of Islamic sciences by which Islamic laws are determined, such as the reason why Allah has laid down such-and-such a rule.

passages.heading: What Are the Conditions for Islamic Slaughter?
passages.text:
Islamic slaughter is one that satisfies the following conditions:

1. The person undertaking the slaughtering process must be Muslim, Jew or Christian who has reached the age of discretion and carries out this act for the intended purpose.
2. The tool used for slaughter must be suitable for the intended purpose, causes blood to flow and sharp, such as a knife. It is forbidden to use anything that may kill the animal due to its heavy weight, hit its head to death or render it unconscious by resorting to electric stunning, for instance.
3. The name of Allah must be pronounced by saying *Bismillaah* (in the name of Allah) at the time of slaughtering the animal.
4. Cutting what must be cut in the Islamic slaughter, namely, the oesophagus, the throat, and the two jugular veins, or just three of these four.

passages.heading: Названия Корана
passages.text: Аллах назвал его Кораном, Писанием (аль-Китаб), Различением (аль-Фуркан), Напоминанием (аз-Зикр). У него есть и другие названия.

passages.heading: Чудо Корана
passages.text: Неверующие из числа арабов не признали Коран, и тогда Аллах бросил им вызов, предложив им сочинить что-то подобное ему, или хотя бы одной его суре, или хотя бы десяти его аятам, но они не смогли этого сделать.

passages.heading: Сура «аль-Кяусар»
passages.text:
**Смысл суры:**

«Поистине, Мы даровали тебе Кяусар» Поистине, Мы даровали тебе, о Пророк, множество благ в этом мире и мире вечном, в том числе и реку Кяусар в Раю.

«Потому молись своему Господу и закалывай [жертву]» Посвяти свою молитву целиком своему Господу, и совершай заклание жертвенного животного только ради Него и с Его Именем.

«Поистине, твой ненавистник сам лишен всякого блага» Поистине, тот, кто ненавидит тебя и принесенное тобой верное руководство и свет, сам является ничтожным и презренным, и он будет лишен всякого блага.

Твой ненавистник — тот, кто ненавидит тебя и истинную религию, которую ты принес.

passages.heading: Смысл суры:
passages.text:
«Скажи: “Я ищу защиты у Господа рассвета”» Скажи, о Посланник: «Я прошу защиты у Аллаха — Господа рассвета, то есть начала утра».

«От зла того, что Он сотворил» От зла всех творений и вреда, причиняемого ими, видимого нам и невидимого.

«И от зла мрака, когда он наступает» От зла наступающей ночи с ее мраком и от дурных и вредных вещей, таящихся под ее покровом.

Аль-фаляк — начало утра.

Аль-гасак — непроглядный мрак ночи.

passages.heading: Изучение религии
passages.text:
- На мусульманина возложена обязанность получать религиозные знания, необходимые, чтобы осознанно поклоняться своему Господу.
- Пророк ﷺ побуждал мусульман стремиться к пониманию религии. Он ﷺ сказал: «Аллах приводит к пониманию религии того, кому Он желает блага» (аль-Бухари № 71).
- Пророк ﷺ сообщил, что поиск шариатских знаний — это путь, ведущий в Рай. Он сказал: «Тому, кто отправился в путь, желая обрести знания, Аллах облегчит путь в Рай» (Муслим № 2699).

Сегодня есть множество доступных книг, которые помогут мусульманину больше узнать о своей религии, чтобы поклоняться своему Господу осознанно и с пониманием. Ему следует обратиться за помощью к специалистам, которые посоветуют ему лучшие из этих книг.

passages.heading: Плоды имана
passages.text:
У имана много плодов, и мы приведем здесь лишь некоторые из них:

* Умиротворение души. Иман умиротворяет душу человека, вселяет в нее довольство Аллахом и Его предопределением и избавляет ее от страха перед кем-либо или чем-либо, помимо Аллаха.

> Аль-Кадар (судьба) — это изначальное предопределение Всевышним Аллахом всех вещей и Его знание, что они произойдут в известное Ему время определенным образом.

passages.heading: Сура «аль-‘Аср» (Время)
passages.text:
**Смысл суры:**

«Клянусь временем» Аллах клянется временем, в ходе которого сыны Адама совершают свои деяния, как хорошие, так и дурные.

«Поистине, каждый человек в убытке» Поистине, люди неизменно подвержены гибели и ущербу.

«…кроме тех, которые уверовали, и совершали праведные деяния, и заповедали друг другу держаться истины, и заповедали друг другу терпеть». Исключение составляют лишь те, кто уверовал в Аллаха и совершал благие деяния, завещал друг другу придерживаться истины, трудиться в покорности Аллаху и проявлять терпение в этом.

passages.heading: Смысл суры:
passages.text:
«Скажи: “Он — Аллах — Един”» Скажи, о Посланник, тем, кто попросил тебя описать своего Господа: «Он — Аллах, Единственный обладающий Божественностью и Господством, нет божества, кроме Него».

«Аллах самодостаточен» Он — Аллах, который совершенен в качествах славы и величия, к Которому творения обращаются за удовлетворением своих нужд и желаний.

«Он не родил и не был рожден» У него нет ни детей, ни родителей, ни супруги.

«…и нет никого, равного Ему» Среди Его творений нет никого, такого же, как Он, или хотя бы подобного Ему, — ни в Его именах, ни в Его качествах, ни в Его действиях.

passages.heading: Ниспослание Корана
passages.text: Всевышний Аллах ниспосылал его частями на протяжении двадцати трех лет в Мекке и Медине.

passages.heading: Важнейшие вопросы, затронутые в Коране
Язык Корана
passages.text: Всевышний Аллах ниспослал его на арабском языке.

passages.heading: Источник Корана
passages.text: Всевышний Аллах ниспослал его Своему Посланнику ﷺ через ангела Джибриля, мир ему.

passages.heading: The Friday Prayer (Salaat-ul-Jumu’ah)
passages.text:
- Allah Almighty has enjoined Muslims to perform a special prayer on Friday, called *Salaat-ul-Jumu’ah* (the Friday prayer). It is performed in a special manner, has special conditions and takes the place of the daily *Dhuhr* (midday) prayer on this day.
- Muslims gather together to perform it in the mosque. The *imaam* delivers a two-section *khutbah* (sermon), then he leads them in a two-*rak’ahs* prayer in which he recites the Qur’an aloud.
- It is recommended to take a ritual bath (*ghusl*) to attend the Friday prayer and proceed early to the mosque. It is not permissible to miss it without a legitimate excuse, and if for any reason a person misses it he must perform the four-unit *Dhuhr* (midday) prayer instead but without reciting the Qur’an aloud.
- Women and people on a journey are exempt from performing the Friday prayer.

passages.heading: Why Do We Pray?
passages.text: We pray because the prayer is an act of worship that Allah has enjoined on Muslims.

passages.heading: The Five Obligatory Prayers
passages.text:
Allah Almighty has enjoined Muslims to perform five prayers throughout the day and night, namely:

| The Prayer | Beginning Time | Ending Time | Number of units (*rak‘ahs*) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| *Fajr* (Dawn) Prayer | at the break of dawn | sunrise | 2 |
| *Dhuhr* (Midday) Prayer | when the sun starts declining westward at midday after reaching its zenith | when the shadow of an object becomes equal in length to the object itself | 4 |
| *‘Asr* (Late Afternoon) Prayer | when the shadow of an object becomes equal in length to the object itself | sunset | 4 |
| *Maghrib* (Sunset) Prayer | sunset | when the red glow (evening twilight) on the western horizon disappears | 3 |
| *‘Ishaa’* (Late Evening) Prayer | when the red glow (evening twilight) on the western horizon disappears | midnight | 4 |

passages.heading: How to Perform *Ghusl*?
passages.text:
To perform *ghusl*, one must wash the entire body with water, rinse out one’s mouth and clean one’s nose by sniffing water into the nostrils and ejecting it out by blowing one’s nose. A Muslim removes the major ritual impurity by simply doing so.

> The major ritual impurity: what must be removed by ghusl, and ablution is not sufficient, and these are types:
> 
> 1- *Janaabah*: The state of ritual impurity following intercourse or ejaculation as a result of an orgasm even if no intercourse takes place.
> 2- Menstruation: the normal vaginal bleeding that occurs as part of a woman’s monthly cycle.
> 3- Postnatal bleeding: The vaginal bleeding that takes place following childbirth.

passages.heading: How Do We Pray?
passages.text: If a Muslim wants to pray, he must do the following:

passages.heading: How Do We Pray?
passages.text:
1. He intends in his heart to pray.
2. He stands facing the *qiblah*, raises his hands up to the level of the shoulders or ears, and says, “*Allaahu akbar* Allah is the Greatest.”
3. He places his right hand on his left hand. Then he recites one of the opening supplications, such as, Subhaanak-Allaahumma wa bi hamdika, wa tabaarak-asmuka, wa ta’aalaa jadduka, wa laa ilaaha ghayruka “Glory be to You, O Allah; Yours is the praise, blessed is Your name, exalted is Your majesty, and there is no god besides You.” Then he says, A’oodhu billaahi min-ash-shaytaan-ir-rajeem. Bismillaah-ir-rahmaan-ir-raheem “I seek Allah’s protection from Satan, who has been expelled from His mercy. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.” Then he recites *Soorat Al-Faatihah* and says after it, “*Aameen*”, which means “Answer our supplications, O Allah”. After that, he recites whatever number of verses of the Qur’an as is easy for him, even if it is one verse.
4. He says, “Allaahu akbar Allah is the Greatest” while raising his hands up to the level of his shoulders or ears, and bows down, lowering his head and back and keeping them straight at a right angle, placing the palms of his hands on the knees. He says three times while in this position, “Subhaana rabbiy-al-’adheem Glory be to my Lord, the Almighty.”

passages.heading: The Prayer
passages.text:
11. He turns his face to his right and says: Assalaamu ‘alaykum wa rahmatullaah “May Allah’s peace and mercy be upon you.” Then he turns his face to his left and says the same this. With this, he concludes his prayer.

This manner only applies to a prayer that consists of two units (*rak’ahs*), such as *Fajr* and *Jumu’ah* prayers. If, however, the prayer consists of three units (*rak’ahs*), namely *Maghrib*, or four units (*rak’ahs*), namely *Dhuhr*, *‘Asr* and *‘Ishaa’*, he completes the remaining units after concluding the first *tashahhud*, in the same way he has performed the first *rak’ah* but without reciting anything else after *Soorat Al-Faatihah*, then sits as he has done after the second *rak’ah*, recites the first *tashahhud* and *As-Salaatu Al-Ibraaheemiyyah*, and then concludes the prayer by saying, Assalaamu ‘alaykum wa rahmatullaah May Allah’s peace and mercy be upon you.” first to the right and then to the left.

7. He says, Allaahu akbar “Allah is the Greatest” and sits down on the left leg while keeping the right foot upright with the toes pointing towards the *qiblah*, resting his hands on his thighs close to the knees. He says while in this position, “My Lord, forgive me.”

8. He says, Allaahu akbar “Allah is the Greatest” and prostrates himself again just as he has done the first time, saying the same thing.

9. Then he rises to the standing position again, saying, Allaahu akbar “Allah is the Greatest” as he does so, and performs the second unit (*rak’ah*) in exactly the same way as the first one.

passages.heading: Discuss
passages.text:
Discuss with your classmates some of the challenges facing Muslims that prevent them from performing the prayers on time, and how to overcome these challenges.

{{Q:62:9}} (Soorat Al-Jumu’ah, 62:9)

passages.heading: The Position of the Prayer in Islam
passages.text:
The prayer has a number of distinctive characteristics, including the following:

- It is the second pillar of Islam after the two testimonies of faith.
- It is the act of worship that must be performed under all circumstances, in times of war and peace, and whether one is sick or in good health.
- It is the act of worship that distinguishes a Muslim from a non-Muslim.

passages.heading: Some of the Ultimate Objectives and Benefits of the Prayer:
passages.text:
- It is the direct, special and personal communion a Muslim establishes with his Lord.
- It relieves the mind of worry and all worldly anxieties.
- It strengthens a Muslim’s willpower and determination.
- It refines morals and keeps those who observe it away from evil.

passages.heading: The Conditions of the Prayer
passages.text:
To perform the prayer, several conditions must be met:
There are several conditions required to perform the prayer, which are:

passages.heading: The Conditions of the Prayer
passages.text:
- Purity: Once’s body and the place where the prayer is to be performed must be cleansed from physical impurities, and any ritual impurity must be removed with *wudoo’* or *ghusl*.
- Covering the intimate parts of the body (*‘awrah*): The word *‘awrah* refers to the parts of the body that must be covered in front of people. A man’s *‘awrah* that must be covered during the prayer extends from the navel to the knees; a woman’s *‘awrah* that must be covered during the prayer is her entire body except for the face and hands.
- Facing the *qiblah*: The *qiblah* is the direction of the Ka‘bah in Makkah. One must, therefore, pray in the direction of the Ka‘bah in Makkah.
- When its appointed time becomes due: The prayer will not be valid if it is performed before its time has started. It is not permissible to delay it beyond its due time, and it is best to perform it at the beginning of its time.

4. Il lève ses mains à hauteur de ses épaules ou ses oreilles et il dit : «Allah est plus grand [que tout].»  
Il penche son dos en s’inclinant, en posant ses mains sur ses genoux et en alignant droit son dos et sa tête au même niveau. Et pendant son inclinaison, il dit : «Gloire à mon Seigneur, le Majestueux.» Trois fois.

passages.heading: Comment prions-nous ?
passages.text:
Lorsque le musulman souhaite prier, il doit accomplir les étapes suivantes :

1. Il doit avoir l’intention de la prière dans son cœur.

2. Il se tient debout en se dirigeant vers la Qiblah, il lève ses mains à hauteur de ses épaules ou de ses oreilles et il dit: “Allah est plus Grand [que tout] (Allah Akbar).“

passages.heading: Les conditions de la prière:
passages.text:
Plusieurs conditions doivent être remplies pour s’acquitter de la prière. Ces conditions sont :

■ La purification: Cela inclut la purification du corps et du lieu de prière des souillures. Et la purification de l’impureté s’effectue par l’ablution ou le lavage.

■ Le fait de couvrir la partie intime (Al ‘Awrah): Cela désigne l’obligation de couvrir ce qui doit l’être du corps devant les gens. La “Awrah“ de l’homme qui doit être couverte dans la prière va du nombril au genou et la ‘Awrah“ de la femme qui doit être couverte dans la prière est l’ensemble de son corps excepté le visage et les mains.

■ Se tourner vers la Qiblah: C’est la direction de l’honorable Ka’bah présente à La Mecque. Ainsi, le fidèle doit se diriger dans sa direction durant la prière.

■ L’entrée du temps de la prière: En effet, la prière n’est pas valide avant l’entrée de son temps tout comme il n’est pas permis de la retarder au-delà de son temps. Le meilleur est de s’en acquitter au début de son temps.

La partie intime que l’homme doit cacher dans la prière :
A- L’ensemble du corps à l’exception du visage, des mains et des pieds.
B- Du nombril au genoux.
C- Des épaules aux genoux.

La direction vers laquelle le fidèle doit se tourner [durant la prière]:
A- En direction du Nord.
B- En direction de l’Ouest.
C- En direction de la Ka’bah.

Dans sa prosternation, le fidèle dit :
A- Gloire à mon Seigneur, le Majestueux.
B- Gloire à mon Seigneur, le Plus-Haut.
C- Seigneur ! Pardonne-moi.

7. Il relève sa tête en disant : «Allah est Plus Grand [que tout].» Il s’assied sur son pied gauche, le pied droit restant droit, il place ses paumes sur ses cuisses et pendant qu’il est assis il dit : «Seigneur ! Pardonne-moi.»

8. Il se prosterne encore une fois comme lors de la première prosternation et là pendant qu’il se penche en vue de la prosternation il dit : «Allah est Plus Grand [que tout].» Et il fait dans sa seconde prosternation ce qu’il a fait dans la première prosternation.

9. Il relève sa tête et il se lève en vue de la seconde unité de prière, et là il dit : «Allah est Plus Grand [que tout].» Puis, il prie la seconde unité de prière exactement comme il a prié la première (unité de prière).

passages.heading: Les cinq prières :
passages.text:
Allah (Exalté et Magnifié soit-Il) a imposé à Ses serviteurs de prier, de jour comme de nuit, cinq prières. Elles sont:

| La prière | Début de son temps | Fin de son temps | Nombre d’unités de prière |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :---: |
| La prière de l’aube (Al Fajr) | Le lever de l’aube. | Le lever du soleil. | 2 |
| La prière du midi (Az-Zuhr) | L’inclinaison du soleil (qui est son penchement en direction de l’Ouest à la mi-journée) | lorsque l’ombre d’une chose est équivalente à sa longueur. | 4 |
| La prière de l’après-midi (Al ‘Asr) | lorsque l’ombre d’une chose est équivalente à sa longueur. | Le coucher du soleil. | 4 |
| La prière du coucher (Al Maghrib) | Le coucher du soleil. | Disparition du crépuscule rouge. | 3 |
| La prière du soir (Al ‘Ichâ’) | Disparition du crépuscule rouge. | Milieu de la nuit. | 4 |

passages.heading: Comment effectuer l’ablution ?
passages.text:
1. Il doit avoir l’intention d’effectuer l’ablution dans son cœur et dire : “Au nom d’Allah.“
2. Il se lave les mains avec de l’eau, en commençant par la [main] droite.
3. Il se lave la bouche en ingurgitant de l’eau, en la gargarisant et ensuite en la recrachant. [En arabe] On appelle cela : “Al Madmadah“
4. Il se lave le nez en aspirant de l’eau et ensuite en l’expirant en faisant ressortir l’air de son nez.
5. Il doit se laver complètement le visage : dans ses limites en longueur, de la racine des cheveux en haut du front jusqu’au bas du menton, ainsi que les poils de la barbe, s’il y en a ; et dans ses limites en largeur, d’une oreille à l’autre.
6. Il se lave les mains, des extrémités des doigts jusqu’à l’articulation du coude, en commençant par la droite.
7. Il mouille ses mains avec de l’eau, puis il s’essuie la tête, en commençant de l’avant de la tête jusqu’à la nuque, puis il revient avec ses mains vers l’avant.
8. Il s’essuie les oreilles avec ses index à l’intérieur des oreilles et il essuie [en même temps] derrière les oreilles avec ses pouces.
9. Il se lave les pieds jusqu’aux chevilles, qui sont les deux os saillants de l’articulation du pied, en commençant par son pied droit.

5. Il relève sa tête pour revenir droit, tout en levant les mains à hauteur de ses épaules. Et là il dit: “Allah a entendu quiconque L’a loué.“ Puis, il dit en étant debout et droit: “Notre Seigneur ! La louange T’appartient.“

6. Il tombe prosterné sur le sol, en plaçant son front et son nez sur le sol, tout en plaçant ses paumes, ses genoux et les extrémités de ses orteils sur le sol, et là il dit : «Gloire à mon Seigneur, le Plus-Haut.» Trois fois.

passages.heading: Comment prions-nous ?
passages.text:
3. Il pose sa main droite sur sa main gauche, ensuite il récite une des invocations de l’ouverture de la prière, comme:  
“Gloire à Toi, ô Allah, et à Toi la louange. Que Ton nom soit béni, que Ta majesté soit élevée et il n’y a aucune divinité [digne d’adoration] autre que Toi.“  
Ensuite, il dit:  
“Je me réfugie auprès d’Allah contre Satan le lapidé. Au nom d’Allah, le Tout Miséricordieux, le Très Miséricordieux.“  
Puis, il récite la sourate: L’Ouverture (Al Fâtiha) et à la fin de sa lecture il dit : “Âmîn.“ Et la signification de : “ Âmîn “ désigne: “ Ô Allah ! Exauce notre invocation.“  
Ensuite, après la lecture de la sourate: Al Fâtiha, il récite ce qu’il peut de ce qu’il a mémorisé du noble Coran, même si c’est un seul verset.

passages.heading: Parmi les sagesses et les bénéfices de la prière:
passages.text:
- Elle est le lien entre le musulman et son Seigneur.
- Elle repose l’âme des soucis de ce bas monde.
- Elle renforce chez le musulman la force de la volonté et de la résolution.
- Elle raffine les comportements et éloigne la personne des choses blâmables.

passages.heading: Forbidden Types of Clothing
passages.text:
A man's *'awrah* that must be covered extends from the navel to the knees. A woman must cover herself entirely in the presence of men not related to her; as for men to whom she is related and is forbidden to marry, such as her father, son and brother, she may appear before them as she would normally do in front of other women, showing such parts of her body as the face, hair, the neck and feet.

- Clothing that reveals the *'awrah* and does not conceal it
- Clothing that involves dressing like or imitating the opposite sex, such as when men dress like women and vice versa.
- Clothing that is worn with an air of pride and conceit
- Extravagant clothing
- Men are particularly forbidden to wear silk clothing or adorn themselves with gold or silver jewellery.
- Clothing that involves imitation of the dress traditionally worn by non-Muslims and specific to a certain religion, such as the type of clothing worn by monks and priests

passages.heading: Women in Relation to a Man
passages.text:
| She could be his wife | She could be a relative he is never permitted to marry (a *mahram*) | She could be one he is not related to and thus is allowed to marry (*ajnabiyah*) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| In this case, they are allowed to enjoy each other’s company in any way they like. Allah describes each one of them to be a ‘garment’ for the other, revealing an excellent image of a perfect physical, emotional and mental union. | A man’s *mahram* (pl. *mahaarim*) refers to any of his female relatives whom he is not allowed to marry at any time in his life whatsoever, such as his mother, his sisters, his brother’s or sister’s daughters, his paternal or maternal aunts and his mother-in-law. These may, therefore, appear before him without covering those body parts that are not, according to the prevailing custom, generally covered in front of relatives but without excess and without exceeding the limits of decency. These body parts include the forearms, the neck and the hair. | Such a woman does not belong to the category of women known as *mahaarim* (sing. *mahram*) whether she is one of his relatives, such as his maternal or paternal uncle’s daughter, or she is not one of his relatives at all. Islam has laid down some criteria that govern a Muslim man’s relationship with such women. For instance, she must wear the modest Muslim style of dress (*hijaab*), and they must not be alone with each other in a place where no one can see them (*khalwah*). |

passages.heading: What shall I do if I find water after having performed *tayammum*?
passages.text: If a Muslim finds water or can use it, his purity becomes invalid, in which case he must perform *wudoo’* or *ghusl*.

passages.heading: Introduction
passages.text: The clothes we wear are some of the countless blessings Allah has bestowed on us. The Qur’an states, {{Q:7:26}} (Soorat Al-A’raaf, 7:26).

passages.heading: Discuss
passages.text: Can we turn to fashion trends, customs, traditions or official regulations to determine for us what the appropriate clothing for men and women is?

passages.heading: What is the Islamic Ruling on Seafood Consumption?
passages.text:
It is permissible to eat dead aquatic animals that can live only in water, such as fish and prawns, whether they live in the sea, rivers or lakes.

It is permissible to hunt wild, nonpredatory animals and consume their flesh provided that the name of Allah is mentioned before the hunting weapon is discharged, and the hunted game must be slaughtered if found still alive.

passages.heading: Muslim Women’s Modest Style of Dress (*Hijaab*)
passages.text:
Allah enjoins women to wear the *hijaab* because women enjoy natural beauty and attraction that could easily tempt men into sinful acts, more than the other way round. Women are to cover their entire bodies when in the presence of men who are not related to them, and they may choose any design or colour they like for their *hijaab* as long as the following four conditions are met:

| First Condition | Second Condition | Third condition | Fourth Condition |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| It must appropriately cover the parts of the body that must be covered in public. | It must hang loose and must not fit very closely to the body so that the shape of the body is not revealed. | It must not allow the wearer’s body to be seen through its fabric. | It must not be a type of clothing that is generally considered attractive. |

Islam has made it the husband’s duty to spend on those women entitled to his support without attempting in the least to remind them of his favours.

- False

A woman’s style of dress (*hijaab*) does not have to be loose.

- True

If a woman’s monthly period stops, she must take a ritual bath (*ghusl*) before she can pray.

- True
- False

Menstrual blood is a natural type of blood that flows from a woman’s uterus after childbirth.

passages.heading: Discuss
passages.text: What purposes does clothing serve?

passages.heading: Forbidden Types of Clothing
passages.text:
With your partners, discuss the reasons why some types of clothing are forbidden in Islam.

The Prophet ﷺ forbade men from imitating women and women from imitating men. This prohibition includes the type of clothing and the manner of speech. Islam strictly forbids imitation of the opposite sex, considering it a major sin that invites Allah’s punishment unless one repents and desists from committing it. Islam enjoins men to ensure that their true nature and appearance are distinct from that of women, and vice versa, which clearly testifies to common sense and sound logic.

passages.heading: Women in Relation to a Man
passages.text: Women in relation to a man fall into three categories:

passages.heading: The Types of Blood that Are Naturally Discharged by Women
passages.text:
The blood that is naturally discharged by women is of two types:

| Menstrual blood | Postnatal blood |
| --- | --- |
| This is a natural type of blood that flows from a woman’s uterus every month during her menstrual cycle and usually lasts for a few days. | This bleeding takes place after giving birth and lasts for several days, up to 40 days. |

passages.heading: Islamic Rulings Pertaining to Menstrual and Postnatal Bleeding
passages.text:
Allah Almighty has prescribed several rulings relating to menstruating women and women experiencing their postnatal bleeding, including the following:

- They are exempt from performing the prayers during this period and do not have to make up for the prayers they have missed while in this state after the end of menstrual and postnatal bleeding.
- They are exempt from fasting and are not allowed to fast while in this state, but they must make up for the fasting days they have missed in Ramadaan.
- During this period, a husband must not have intercourse with his wife during her menstrual or postnatal period. He is allowed, however, to satisfy his sexual desire but without having intercourse.
- At the end of the menstrual and postnatal period, when bleeding stops completely, women must take a ritual bath (*ghusl*).

passages.heading: *Tayammum* (Dry Ablution)
passages.text:
If a person who wants to perform *wudoo’* or *ghusl* is unable to do so due to illness, or when water is not readily available, or for any other legitimate reason, he may resort to dry ablution (*tayammum*) instead.

The Manner of Performing *Tayammum*: (1) Intend in his heart to perform *tayammum* and strike both hands slightly on pure earth once, (2) wipe the face with them, (3) wipe the back of the right hand with the palm of the left, and then the back of the left hand with the palm of the right hand.

passages.heading: The General Islamic Rule Regarding Clothing
passages.text:
The general Islamic rule is that all types of clothing are allowed, unless stated otherwise in the Qur’an or the Prophet’s Sunnah.

the general Islamic rule regarding dealings in general, including clothing, is that everything is permissible unless there is evidence to the contrary. All types of clothing mentioned here are forbidden due to textual evidence either in the Qur’an or the Prophet’s Sunnah.

passages.heading: What Are the Conditions for Islamic Slaughter?
passages.text:
Islamic slaughter is one that satisfies the following conditions:

1. The person undertaking the slaughtering process must be Muslim, Jew or Christian who has reached the age of discretion and carries out this act for the intended purpose.
2. The tool used for slaughter must be suitable for the intended purpose, causes blood to flow and sharp, such as a knife. It is forbidden to use anything that may kill the animal due to its heavy weight, hit its head to death or render it unconscious by resorting to electric stunning, for instance.
3. The name of Allah must be pronounced by saying *Bismillaah* (in the name of Allah) at the time of slaughtering the animal.
4. Cutting what must be cut in the Islamic slaughter, namely, the oesophagus, the throat, and the two jugular veins, or just three of these four.

passages.heading: Islamic Rulings Pertaining to Meat Served in Restaurants and Shops
passages.text:
1. The meat of animals that are slaughtered by other than a Muslim or a member of the People of the Book (a Christian or a Jew), such as a Buddhist, or a Hindu is strictly forbidden. This includes meat served in restaurants and shops in countries where Muslims or People of the Book constitute a minority.
2. The meat of animals killed by a Muslim or a member of the People of the Book is lawful based on textual evidence to this effect in the Qur’an.
3. The meat of animals that are not killed according to Islamic law, such as by electrocution and drowning, is strictly forbidden.
4. The general rule is that it is permissible to consume the flesh of animals slaughtered by People of the Book as well as meat of animals generally found in their restaurants and shops, making sure, however, to invoke Allah’s name at the time of eating (that is, by saying *Bismillaah*), but it is better for Muslims to eat only meat that has been proven to be lawful (*halaal*).

passages.heading: Discuss
passages.text:
With your partners, browse some Internet websites that help you find lawful (*halaal*) foods in your country.

The Islamic rulings on the meat of animals that are sold in shops and restaurants vary according to the religion of the person who slaughtered such animals.

passages.heading: سورة الكوثر:
تعلم الدين:
passages.text:
- الواجب على المسلم أن يتعلّم من أمر دينه ما يحتاج إليه، حتى يعبد ربه على علم.
- رغّب النبي ﷺ في التفقّه في الدين فقال: «من يرد الله به خيرًا يفقهه في الدين». أخرجه البخاري (٧١).
- أخبر النبي ﷺ أن طلب العلم الشرعي طريقٌ لدخول الجنة، فقال ﷺ: «من سلك طريقًا يلتمس فيه علمًا، سهل الله له به طريقًا إلى الجنة». أخرجه مسلم (٢٦٩٩).

تتوفر العديد من الكتب التي يستطيع المسلم أن يتعلم منها أحكام دينه حتى يعبد ربه على بصيرة، وعليه بالاستعانة بالمختصين لإرشاده إلى أفضل هذه الكتب.

passages.heading: ٢ الإسلام يكفّر ما سبقه من الذنوب
passages.text:
إذا أسلم العبد، وفعل ما يجب عليه من الواجبات، واجتنب ما حرّم الله عليه، فإن الله تعالى يغفر له ما تقدّم من ذنوبه قبل إسلامه، وقد قال النبي ﷺ: « إذا أسلم العبد فحسن إسلامه، يكفر الله عنه كل سيئة كان زلفها، وكان بعد ذلك القصاص: الحسنة بعشر أمثالها إلى سبع مائة ضعف، والسيئة بمثلها إلا أن يتجاوز الله عنها ». أخرجه البخاري (٤١).

وقد سأل رجل النبي ﷺ: يا رسول الله، أنؤاخذ بما عملنا في الجاهلية؟ فأجابه النبي ﷺ: «من أحسن في الإسلام لم يؤاخذ بما عمل في الجاهلية، ومن أساء في الإسلام أُخذ بالأول والآخر». أخرجه البخاري (٦٩٢١).

passages.heading: فضل قراءة القرآن:
passages.text:
- قال النبي ﷺ: «من قرأ حرفًا من كتاب الله فله به حسنة، والحسنة بعشر أمثالها، لا أقول: ﴿الم﴾ حرف، ولكن ألف حرف، ولام حرف، وميم حرف». أخرجه الترمذي في سننه (رقم 2910) بإسناد صحيح
- وقال النبي ﷺ: «اقرءوا القرآن، فإنه يأتي يوم القيامة شفيعًا لأصحابه». أخرجه مسلم في صحيحه (رقم 804)

passages.heading: الشهادتان:
passages.text:
جعل الله عز وجل مفتاح الدخول في الإسلام النطق بالشهادتين، وهما:

- أشهد أن لا إله إلا الله.
- وأشهد أن محمدًا رسول الله.

passages.heading: لغته
passages.text: أنزل الله تعالى باللغة العربية.

passages.heading: أولاً: معنى شهادة ألا إله إلا الله
passages.text:
معنى (أشهد ألا إله إلا الله): أي أعتقد اعتقادًا جازمًا ألا معبود يستحق العبادة إلا الله وحده.

وقد تضمنت هذه الشهادة أمرين

| الأول | الثاني |
| :-: | :-: |
| نفي الإلهية عن غير الله تعالى | إثبات الإلهية لله وحده |

passages.heading: فضل حسن الخلق:
passages.text:
- أخبر النبي ﷺ أن أكثر ما يدخل الناس الجنة: تقوى الله وحسن الخلق.
- وأخبر ﷺ أن أثقل ما يوضع في ميزان الإنسان يوم القيامة من الحسنات: حسن الخلق.
- وأخبر ﷺ أن أقرب المؤمنين منه منزلة يوم القيامة: أحسنهم أخلاقًا.

> يكون ذلك يوم القيامة حين يتم وزن حسنات الإنسان وسيئاته في ميزان مخصص لا يعلم أحدٌ هيئته ولا حجمه، فمن رجحت كفة حسناته دخل الجنة ومن رجحت كفة سيئاته دخل النار.

---

passages.heading: ناقش
passages.text: ما الموضوع الذي أكدت عليه سورتا الإخلاص والكافرون؟

passages.heading: سورة العصر:
معيار التفاضل في الإسلام:
passages.text:
جعل الله عز وجل معيار التفاضل بين عباده بالإيمان والتقوى، فالتفاضل بين المسلمين بقوة إيمانهم، وليس بأشكالهم، ولا أنسابهم، ولا ألوانهم، ولا أموالهم، فقد قال تعالى: {{Q:49:13}} (الحجرات: ١٣).

وقال النبي ﷺ: «يا أيها الناس، ألا إن ربكم واحد، وإن أباكم واحد، ألا لا فضل لعربي على عجمي، ولا لعجمي على عربي، ولا أحمر على أسود، ولا أسود على أحمر، إلا بالتقوى». أخرجه البيهقي في شعب الإيمان (٤٧٧٤).

passages.heading: أركان الإسلام:
passages.text:
دين الإسلام مبني على خمسة أركان:

لابد لكلّ مُسلم أن يلتزم بهذه الأركان حتى يستقيم إسلامه؛ لأن عدم الالتزام بأحد هذه الأركان يُشكّل خطرًا على صحّة إسلامه.

passages.heading: أركان الإسلام
passages.text:
- **الشهادتين**: شهادة أنْ لا إله إلا الله وأنَّ محمدًا رسول الله
- **إقامة الصلاة**: يجب على المسلم أن يصلي خمس صلوات في كل يوم، وسيأتي شرحها.
- **إعطاء الزكاة**
- **صوم رمضان**
- **حج بيت الله**

passages.heading: فائدة
passages.text: يحترم الإسلام عادات الشعوب وتقاليدهم ولا يلزمهم بتغييرها إلا إذا خالفت شيئًا من شعائر الإسلام وتعاليمه.

passages.heading: ٣ الإسلام الدين الخاتم
passages.text: جعل الله تعالى الإسلام امتدادًا للشرائع السماويّة السابقة، وارتضاه دينًا للخَلق جميعًا إلى قيام الساعة، فلا يوجد على وجه الأرض دينٌ حقٌّ سوى دين الإسلام؛ قال تعالى: {{Q:3:85}} (آل عمران:٨٥).

passages.heading: ناقش
passages.text: كيف ترد على من يزعم أن الإسلام دين خاص بالعرب؟

passages.heading: من هو نبي الإسلام؟
passages.text: يعتقد المسلم أن محمد ﷺ هو خاتم النبيين الذين بعثهم الله إلى الناس لدعوتهم إلى عبادته وحده دون سواه، وأنه لا نبي بعده؛ قال الله - تعالى -: {{Q:33:40}} (الأحزاب : ٤٠)

passages.heading: ما القرآن؟
passages.text:
القرآن الكريم كلام الله تعالى الذي أنزله على رسوله محمد ﷺ وهو آخر كتب الله المنزلة، وليس بعده كتاب آخر.

الكتب المنزلة: هي الكتب التي أنزلها الله سبحانه وتعالى على أنبيائه، ويؤمن المسلم بهذه الكتب وأنها منزلة من عند الله تعالى، وأن الله تكلّم بما فيها بما يليق به سبحانه، ومن هذه الكتب: الزبور الذي أُنزل على داوود عليه السلام، والتوراة التي أُنزلت على موسى عليه السلام، والإنجيل المنزل على عيسى عليه السلام، وقد اعترى هذه الكتب تحريف وتبديل على مر العصور.

passages.heading: القرآن غذاء الروح والعقل:
passages.text:
خاطب القرآن الكريم عقول البشر وأرواحهم على حدّ سواء، فهو يخاطب العقل من خلال:

- الاستدلال العقلي على القضايا، قال تعالى: {{Q:21:22}} (الأنبياء: ٢٢).
- الدعوة إلى إعمال العقل والتفكر في الأدلة والبراهين، قال تعالى: {{Q:2:219}} (البقرة: ٢١٩).
- ذم الذين لا يُعملون عقولهم، ويتف ّكرون بها، قال تعالى: {{Q:25:44}} (الفرقان: ٤٤).

وخاطب أرواحهم وعواطفهم من خلال:

- التعبير عن المشاعر العاطفية، وإبرازها، وتصويرها في حالات كثيرة، قال تعالى: {{Q:2:165}} (البقرة: ١٦٥).
- التذكير بالعواطف الإنسانية، وبيان آثارها الحسنة والسيئة، قال تعالى: {{Q:5:82}} (المائدة: ٨٢).
- الأمر بالرفق والتلطف في الدعوة، قال تعالى: {{Q:16:125}} (النحل: ١٢٥).
- تضمين آيات الأحكام معاني إيمانية، قال تعالى: {{Q:4:94}} (النساء: ٩٤).
- استعمال الألفاظ المؤثرة في النفس، والمثيرة للعواطف الصادقة، قال تعالى: {{Q:24:22}} (النور: ٢٢).

وقد يجمع الخطابان: العقلي والروحي في آية واحدة، تناقش العقل وتقنعه، وتحرك العاطفة في الوقت نفسه، قال تعالى: {{Q:35:3}} (فاطر: ٣).

passages.heading: ناقش
passages.text: ما الآيات التي طالعتها قبل إسلامك؟ وكيف كان أثرها عليك؟

passages.heading: تمهيد
passages.text: من أكثر اللحظات التي لا ينساها المسلم الجديد، هي لحظة إعلان دخوله الإسلام من خلال نطقه للشهادتين، فبهذا الإعلان يُعلن لنفسه قبل أي أحد أنه غدا شيئًا آخر غير ما كان، وأنه منذ هذه اللحظات خطى خطواته الأولى نحو معرفة الحق والتمسك به. وفي هذا الدرس سنتعرف على الشهادتين ومعناهما ولوازمهما على المسلم.

وجوهر دين الإسلام الذي هو دين الأنبياء جميعًا: عبادة الله وحده، والكفر بكل ما يعبد من دونه.

قال الله تعالى: {{Q:21:25}} (الأنبياء: ٢٥).

فلا يجوز بأي حال من الأحوال اعتقاد ألوهية أي شيء سوى الله تعالى، ولا يجوز التقرب إلى غير الله تعالى بأي نوعٍ من العبادات.

passages.heading: ثانيًا: معنى شهادة أن محمدًا رسول الله
passages.text: معنى (أشهد أن محمدًا رسول الله): أي أعتقد اعتقادًا جازمًا أن محمدًا ﷺ هو رسول الله، وأنه خاتم النبيين، فلا نبي بعده، وأن رسالته للناس جميعًا، قال سبحانه وتعالى: {{Q:25:1}} (الفرقان: ١).

passages.heading: إعجازه
passages.text: أنكر كفّار العرب القرآن، فتحداهم الله بالإتيان بمثله أو بسورة منه أو بعشر آيات أو بآية واحدة منه، فعجزوا عن ذلك.

passages.heading: مصدره
passages.text: أنزل الله عز وجل على رسوله ﷺ عن طريق جبريل ؑ.

passages.heading: نزوله
passages.text: أنزل الله تعالى مفرّقًا في ٢٣ سنة، في مكة المكرمة والمدينة المنورة.

passages.heading: أسماؤه
passages.text: سماه الله بالقرآن والكتاب والفرقان والذكر، وله عدة أسماء أخرى.

passages.heading: ناقش
passages.text: كيف يمكن أن تكون أخلاق المسلم مع الآخرين؟ وهل لهذه الأخلاق أثر في حكمهم على الإسلام؟

passages.heading: مجالات الأخلاق في الإسلام:
passages.text:
الأخلاق في الإسلام ليس لها مجالٌ واحد فقط، بل لها مجالات متعددة، وهي:

- الأخلاق مع الله عز وجل؛ كتقوى الله والإخلاص له.
- الأخلاق مع النبي ﷺ؛ كمحبته واحترامه ونصرته بالنفس والمال.
- الأخلاق مع الشريعة، كالتسليم لأحكام الشرع وتوقيرها.
- الأخلاق مع النفس؛ كالصبر والحلم.
- الأخلاق مع الآخرين؛ كالصدق والأمانة.
- الأخلاق مع الحيوانات؛ كالرعاية وعدم ضربها وتعذيبها.
- الأخلاق مع البيئة؛ كالمحافظة عليها من الفساد، وغرس الأشجار، وعدم الإسراف في خيراتها.

7. يرفع رأسه ويجلس على قدمه اليسرى، مع بقاء قدمه اليمنى منتصبة، ويضع كفيه على فخذيه، ويقول أثناء جلوسه: «**ربِّ اغفر لي**».

8. يسجد مرة أخرى كالسجدة الأولى، ويقول أثناء الانحناء للسجود: «**اللهُ أكبر**». ويفعل في سجوده الثاني ما فعل في سجوده الأول.

9. يرفع رأسه ويقوم للركعة الثانية، وهو يقول: «**اللهُ أكبر**». ويصلي الركعة الثانية كما صلى الركعة الأولى تمامًا.

10. بعد السجود الثاني في الركعة الثانية يجلس كجلوسه بين السجدتين، ويقول: «التحيات للَّه والصلوات الطيبات، السلام عليك أيها النبي ورحمة الله وبركاته، السلام علينا وعلى عباد الله الصالحين، أشهد أن لا إله إلا الله، وأشهد أن محمداً عبده ورسوله»، ويسمى التشهد الأول.

ثم يقول بعده: «اللهم صلِّ على محمد وعلى آل محمد، كما صليت على إبراهيم وعلى آل إبراهيم، إنك حميدٌ مجيد، وبارك على محمد وعلى آل محمد، كما باركت على إبراهيم وعلى آل إبراهيم، إنك حميدٌ مجيد» وتسمى الصلاة الإبراهيمية.

11. يلتفت عن يمينه ويقول: «السلام عليكم ورحمة الله» ثم يلتفت عن شماله ويقول مثل ذلك.

وبذلك تنتهي صلاته.

هذه الصفة إذا كانت صلاته ركعتان؛ كالفجر والجمعة، أما إذا كانت ثلاث ركعات؛ كالمغرب، أو أربع ركعات؛ كالظهر والعصر والعشاء، فإنه بعد الانتهاء من التشهد الأول يكمل ما تبقى من الركعات، ثم يجلس كما جلس بعد الركعة الثانية، ويقول التشهد الأول، ثم يقرأ الصلاة الإبراهيمية على النبي ﷺ، ثم يسلم.

passages.heading: كيف نتوضأ؟
passages.text:
إذا أراد المسلم أن يتوضأ فعليه القيام بالخطوات الآتية:

1. يقول: «بسم الله».
2. يغسل كفيّه بالماء مبتدئًا باليمنى.
3. ينظف فمه بإدخال الماء فيه، ثم يحركه، ثم يخرجه.
4. ينظف أنفه بإدخال الماء فيه مع الاستنشاق، ثم يخرجه مع نفخ الهواء من أنفه.
5. يغسل وجه كاملًا، وحدوده طولًا من منابت الشعر في أعلى الجبهة إلى أسفل الذقن، مع شعر اللحية إن وجدت، وحدوده عرضًا من الأذن إلى الأذن.
6. يغسل يديه من أطراف الأصابع إلى مفصل المرفق، مبتدئًا بيده اليمنى.
7. يبلل يديه بالماء، ثم يمسح بهما رأسه، مبتدئًا بمقدمة الرأس إلى القفا، ثم يعيد يديه إلى الأمام.
8. يمسح أذنيه بأصبعيه السبابتين داخل الأذنين، ويمسح خلف الأذنين بالإبهامين.
9. يغسل قدميه إلى الكعبين، وهما العظمان البارزان في مفصل القدم، مبتدئًا برجله اليمنى.

passages.heading: شروط الصلاة:
passages.text:
يشترط لأداء الصلاة عدة شروط، وهي:

- **الطهارة:** وتشمل طهارة البدن والمكان من النجاسات، والطهارة من الحدث بالوضوء أو الغسل.
- **تغطية العورة:** والعورة: ما يجب ستره من البدن أمام الناس. وعورة الرجل التي يجب سترها في الصلاة هي من السرة إلى الركبة، وعورة المرأة التي يجب سترها في الصلاة هي جميع بدنها إلا الوجه والكفّين.
- **استقبال القبلة:** وهي جهة الكعبة المشرفة الموجودة في مكة المكرمة، فيجب على المصلي التوجه إلى جهتها في صلاته.
- **دخول وقت الصلاة:** فلا تصح الصلاة قبل دخول وقتها، ولا يجوز تأخيرها عن وقتها، والأفضل أداؤها في أول وقتها.

passages.heading: نزوله
passages.text: أنزل الله تعالى مفرّقًا في ٢٣ سنة، في مكة المكرمة والمدينة المنورة.

passages.heading: ما هو الحج؟
passages.text:
الحج: عبادة يذهب لأجلها المسلم المستطيع إلى مكة المكرمة للقيام بعبادات معينة في شهر ذي الحجة، وهو الشهر الأخير من السنة الهجرية.

والحج هو الركن الخامس من أركان الإسلام.

السنة الهجرية: هي إشارةٌ إلى الهجرة النبوية المباركة من مكة المكرمة إلى المدينة النبوية، وقد اختار الخليفة عمر بن الخطاب ؓ يوم هجرة الرسول ﷺ ليكون بداية لحساب التاريخ الإسلامي الهجري. وللسنة الهجرية إثنا عشر شهر تبدء بشهر (محرم) وتنتهي بشهر (ذي الحجة)، وقد اعتمد المسلمون التأريخ للحوادث والوقائع بالسنة الهجرية منذ السنة الأولى للهجرة والتي تقابلها سنة ٦٢٢ ميلادية.

passages.heading: ما هي الصلاة؟
passages.text:
الصلاة: عبادة يومية، تشتمل على مجموعة من الأقوال والأعمال يتقرب بها العبد إلى ربه، وتؤدى خمس مرات في اليوم.

والصلاة هي الركن الثاني من أركان الإسلام.

5. يرفع رأسه ليعود قائمًا مع رفع يديه إلى جوار كتفيه، وهو يقول: «**سمع الله لمن حمده**». ثم يقول وهو واقف: «**ربنا ولك الحمد**».

6. ينحني ساجدًا على الأرض، فيضع جبهته وأنفه على الأرض، مع وضع كفيه وركبتيه وأطراف أصابع قدميه على الأرض، ويقول: «**سبحان ربي الأعلى**» ثلاث مرات.

passages.heading: صلاة الجمعة:
passages.text:
- فرض الله عز وجل على المسلمين أداء صلاة خاصة يوم الجمعة تسمى (صلاة الجمعة)، ولها صفة خاصة وشروط خاصة، وهي بدل عن صلاة الظهر لذلك اليوم.
- يجتمع المسلمون من أجلها في المسجد، يخطب فيهم إمام المسجد خطبتين، ثم يصلي بهم ركعتين، يجهر فيها بقراءة القرآن.
- يشرع الاغتسال لحضور صلاة الجمعة، والتبكير لحضورها. ولا يجوز التخلف عنها إلا لعذر، ومن تخلّف عنها فإنه يصلي صلاة الظهر أربع ركعات، لا يجهر فيها بقراءة القرآن.
- لا تجب صلاة الجمعة على المرأة أو المسافر.

passages.heading: ناقش
passages.text:
استعرض مع زملائك بعض التحديات التي تواجه المسلم لتمنعه من أداء الصلاة في وقتها، وكيف يتم تجاوز هذه التحديات؟

{{Q:62:9}} (الجمعة: 9).

اذكر عبادتين من العبادات الخاصة بيوم الجمعة.

ما أثر الصلوات الخمس على حياة المسلم اليومية؟

من خلال زيارتك لهذا الموقع: islamicfiqh.net/en تحدث عن حكم تارك الصلاة في الإسلام

العورة التي يجب على الرجل سترها في الصلاة:
أ) جميع البدن باستثناء الوجه واليدين والقدمين.
ب) من السرة إلى الركبة.
ج) من الكتف إلى الركبة.

الجهة التي يجب على المصلي التوجه لها هي:
أ) جهة الشمال.
ب) جهة الغرب.
ج) جهة الكعبة.

يقول المصلي في سجوده:
أ) سبحان ربي العظيم.
ب) سبحان ربي الأعلى.
ج) رب اغفر لي.

passages.heading: تمهيد
passages.text: تعتبر الصلاة أعظم شعائر الدين التي يجب على المسلم تعلمها وأدؤها، وقد علمنا رسول الله ﷺ كيفية أدائها بالطريقة التي يرضاها الله عز وجل عنا، وفي هذا الدرس سنتعرف على الصلوات الواجبة، ومنزلتها، وشروطها، وكيفية أدائها بالطريقة الصحيحة.

passages.heading: منزلة الصلاة:
passages.text:
تتميز الصلاة بمجموعة من الخصائص، منها:
- تعد الركن الثاني من أركان الإسلام بعد الشهادتين.
- العبادة التي يجب أداؤها على كل حال، في حال الصحة والمرض، والأمن والخوف.
- العبادة التي يتميّز بها المسلم من الكافر.

passages.heading: لماذا نصلي؟
passages.text:
نصلي لأن الصلاة:

- صلة بين العبد وربه.
- تريح النفس من هموم الدنيا.
- تقوي لدى العبد قوة الإرادة والعزيمة.
- تهذب الأخلاق، وتبعد صاحبها عن المنكرات.

passages.heading: Segunda pregunta
passages.text:
#### ¿De dónde vinimos? y ¿Por qué?

El Islam explica que el ser humano fue creado de un barro con lo cual Al-láh creó a Adán, el padre de toda la humanidad. Al-láh -Enaltecido sea- dice: {{Q:23:12}} Corán (23: 12).

El objetivo por lo cual fue creado el ser humano es la adoración a Al-láh -Enaltecido sea- Quien no necesita esta adoración, Glorificado y Exaltado sea.

**Adán**
Al-láh nos ha contado en el Corán la historia de la creación y el inicio de la enemistad del Satanás hacia al ser humano, véase la exégesis del capítulo de Al Baqara (la vaca), las aleyas (30-39).

Al-láh -Enaltecido sea- dice: {{Q:51:56}} Corán (51: 56).

passages.heading: ¿Qué es el Corán?
passages.text:
El Noble Corán es la palabra de Al-láh -Enaltecido sea- revelada a su mensajero Muhammad -que la paz y las bendiciones de Al-láh sean con él- y es el último libro revelado, es decir que no hay ningún libro revelado después de él.

> Los libros revelados son los libros que reveló Al-láh- Glorificado y Enaltecido sea- a los profetas.  
> Sin embargo, el musulmán cree en estos libros y que son revelados por Al-láh -Enaltecido sea- y que son palabra de Al-láh -Exaltado sea-, entre estos libros: los Salmos revelados a David -la paz sea con él-, la Torá a Moisés -la paz sea con él-, el Evangelio a Jesús -la paz sea con él- pero desafortunadamente estos libros han sido falsificados a lo largo de la historia.

passages.heading: Sus temas trascendentales.
passages.text:
Entre los temas tratados por el Noble Corán mencionamos:

- Hablar del monoteísmo y de la unicidad de Al-láh y rechazar la asociación (Shirk) a alguien con Al-láh.
- Hablar de la perfección del universo que presenta una prueba clara sobre la existencia del Creador -Enaltecido y Exaltado sea-.
- Las historias coránicas llenas de lecciones y morales.
- Hablar del inicio de la creación, de la resurrección de la gente después de la muerte y cómo serán recompensados según sus obras.
- Educación y legislación para los creyentes.

passages.heading: La sura de Al Asr:
passages.text:
{{Q:103:1-3}}

**Exégesis de la sura:**

(Juro por el tiempo)

Al-láh ha jurado por el tiempo en lo cual se realizan todos los actos de los hijos de Adán, sean buenos o malos.

(que los seres humanos están en la perdición,)

Ciertamente la gente está en total perdición y destrucción.

(excepto aquellos que crean, obren rectamente, y se aconsejen mutuamente con la verdad y con la paciencia [ante las adversidades].)

Salvo aquellos quienes creyeron, realizaron buenas obras, y se aconsejaron entre sí para quedarse firmes y aferrados a la verdad estando pacientes en eso.

passages.heading: Las historias de los profetas en el Corán:
passages.text:
El Noble Corán está lleno de historias de los profetas anteriores con sus pueblos, empezando por Adan -la paz sea con él- pasando por Noé, Hud, Saleh, Shuaib, Ibrahim, Ismael, Isaac, Jacob, Moisés y Jesús -la paz sea con ellos-, entre otros profetas y mensajeros.

Por ello sus historias fueron relatadas en el Corán para varias instrucciones, de las cuales citamos:

- Mostrar que la religión de todos los profetas es una,y está basada sobre el monoteísmo y la unicidad de Al-láh -Enaltecido sea-.
- Calmar al profeta Muhammad -que la paz y las bendiciones de Al-láh sean con él- y apoyarle para que estuviera firme ante los daños, algo que también le sucedió a los demás profetas anteriores.
- Calmar a los creyentes al saber que les pueden suceder penas y desgracias igual que los piadosos anteriores.
- Tomar lecciones de ellas ya que son historias reales.

passages.heading: Tercera pregunta
passages.text:
#### ¿Adónde vamos?

El Noble Corán explica que cada ser humano acabará al morir, y con su muerte se termina la fase de las obras y empieza la del Juicio y de la Recompensa. Al-láh -Enaltecido sea- dice: {{Q:39:30-31}} Corán (39: 30-31).

El ser humano, al morir, se le preguntará sobre su fe, y será recompensado por sus obras. Al-láh -Enaltecido sea- dice: {{Q:3:185}} Corán (3: 185).

El día de la Resurrección, Al-láh -Enaltecido sea- resucita a los difuntos de sus tumbas para recibir el juicio y la recompensa; la gente de fe ingresará en el Paraíso, y la gente de la incredulidad ingresará en el fuego del Infierno. Al-láh -Enaltecido sea- dice: {{Q:42:7}} Corán (42: 7).

passages.heading: Preámbulo
passages.text: A las personas les viene a la mente preguntas acerca de la existencia del ser humano y se preguntan por su origen, la causa y el objetivo de su existencia. Por ello, el Islam ha respondido estas cuestiones con respuestas útiles:

passages.heading: Exégesis de la sura:
passages.text:
(En el nombre de Dios, el Compasivo con toda la creación, el Misericordioso con los creyentes)

Empiezo la recitación del Corán con el nombre de Al-láh, pidiendo Su ayuda, Al-láh el Único que merece ser adorado, Quien posee la clemencia que abarca todas sus criaturas, el misericordioso con sus siervos creyentes ofreciéndoles una misericordia específica.

(Todas las alabanzas son para Dios, Señor de todo cuanto existe)

Alabar a Al-láh con los atributos perfectos, por Sus gracias sobre todas sus criaturas, es el Único que merece todo tipo de alabanza, es el Señor de todas las criaturas, Quien les creó de la nada,

passages.heading: Primera lección
passages.text: ## El Islam y las grandes cuestiones

passages.heading: A discutir
passages.text: Compara tu visión sobre el sentido de la existencia humana, antes y después de convertirte al Islam:

passages.heading: La gracia de la buena guía:
passages.text: quien conoce la sabiduría de su creación, y lo que recibirá la gente el día de Resurrección, sabrá claramente que la gracia más grande que puede un siervo recibir de Al-láh es guiarle a la religión de la verdad y a realizar buenas obras. Por ello Al-láh -Enaltecido y Exaltado sea- guía a sus siervos en la oración para pedir la buena guía hacia el camino recto, el camino del Islam que lleva a la complacencia de Al-láh, el Enaltecido.

passages.heading: Preámbulo
passages.text:
Cuando Al-láh enviaba a los profetas a sus pueblos para invitarlos a la religión, les daba algunos milagros para que sus pueblos creyeran en sus profecías, pero dichos milagros se acabaron con el fallecimiento de dichos profetas. En cuanto al mensajero del Islam -que la paz y las bendiciones de Al-láh sean con él-, su milagro no fue solo para su pueblo sino que fue universal, para toda la humanidad, este milagro es (el Libro Grandioso) o sea el Corán que fue protegido por Al-láh hasta después la muerte del profeta -que la paz y las bendiciones de Al-láh sean con él.

En este curso vamos a saber los méritos del Corán y sus modales.

passages.heading: Los méritos de la recitación del Corán:
passages.text:
* El profeta -que la paz y las bendiciones de Al-láh sean con él- dijo:«. Quien recita una letra del Libro de Al-láh recibirá una buena recompensa, y la recompensa será multiplicada por diez, no digo: que (Alif, lam, mim) sea una letra sino que (Alif) es una letra, (Lam) es una letra y (Mim) es una letra » Reportado por At-Tirmidhi en su “Sunan” (nº 2910) con una cadena de transmisión auténtica.

* El profeta -que la paz y las bendiciones de Al-láh sean con él- dijo:«. Recitad el Qurán pues ciertamente llega el Día del Juicio como un intercesor para quienes lo recitan ». Reportado por Muslim en su Sahih (Auténtico) (nº 804).

passages.heading: El Corán nutre el alma y la mente:
passages.text:
El Corán se dirige tanto a la mente como al alma del ser humano, a la mente a través del:

- Razonamiento mental al tratar los temas, Al-láh -Enaltecido sea- dice: {{Q:21:22}} Corán (21: 22)
- La invitación a usar el razonamiento y la reflexión en las pruebas y evidencias, Al-láh -Enaltecido sea- dice: {{Q:2:219}} Corán (2: 219).
- Critica a quienes no razonan y no reflexionan con sus mentes, Al-láh -Enaltecido sea- dice: {{Q:25:44}} Corán (25: 44).

Y se dirige hacia sus almas y sentimientos a través de:

passages.heading: El Corán nutre el alma y la mente:
passages.text:
- Expresar sentimientos y emociones en varias ocasiones. Al-láh -Enaltecido sea- dice: {{Q:2:165}} Corán (2: 165).
- Un recordatorio de los sentimientos humanos, y de sus efectos buenos y malos. El Todopoderoso dijo: {{Q:5:82}} Corán (5: 82).
- El consejo con bondad y la dulzura para invitar a las personas al Islam, Al-láh -Enaltecido sea- dice: {{Q:16:125}} Corán (16: 125).
- Las aleyas de las normas legales incluyen valores relacionados con la fe, Al-láh -Enaltecido sea- dice: {{Q:4:94}} Corán (4: 94).
- El uso de palabras que influyen sobre el alma, y que producen sentimientos sinceros. Al-láh -Enaltecido sea- dice: {{Q:24:22}} Corán (24: 22).

Y puede también incluir ambos discursos: el mental y el espiritual en una sola aleya; se dirige a la mente y la convence, e influye sobre el alma al mismo tiempo, Al-láh -Enaltecido sea- dice: {{Q:35:3}} Corán (35: 3).

passages.heading: Sus nombres.
passages.text: Al-láh ha nombrado el Corán, el Libro, el Criterio, el Recuerdo, y tiene también muchos otros nombres.

passages.heading: El Corán es un estilo de vida:
passages.text:
> El Noble Corán delinea la trayectoria que debe seguir las gentes en sus vidas, mostrándoles sus derechos y sus deberes con tanta flexibilidad que hace que sus normas sean útiles para cada época y cada lugar.

El musulmán debe interesarse por la recitación del Noble Corán y saber sus normas.

passages.heading: Sus milagros.
passages.text: Los incrédulos desmintieron el Corán y lo rechazaron, entonces Al-láh les desafió con traer algo igual, escribir un capítulo o hasta diez aleyas iguales al Corán, pero no pudieron.

passages.heading: Su lengua.
passages.text: Fue revelado por Al-láh -Enaltecido sea- en lengua árabe.

passages.heading: Primera lección
passages.text: ## El Islam y las grandes cuestiones

passages.heading: ¿Quiénes somos?
passages.text:
El Islam define al hombre como un ser creado por Al-láh y favorecido más que de las demás criaturas. Al-láh también ha creado a muchas criaturas para que ayuden al hombre y le ayuden en cumplir su misión durante toda su vida. Al-láh -Enaltecido sea- dice:

{{Q:17:70}} Corán (17: 70).

Al-láh -Enaltecido sea- hizo al hombre parecerse:

Los ángeles: son creados por Al-láh -Enaltecido sea-. Creados de la luz, son siervos nobles de Al-láh, no Le desobedecen jamás y hacen siempre lo que Les ordena, nadie sabe cuántos son, salvo Al-láh.

• A los ángeles en su pureza y adoración.
• A los demonios en su ingratitud y desobediencia.
• Y a los animales en la satisfacción de sus caprichos y deseos.

Le dio una inclinación hacia el bien y otra hacia el mal, y le dio una razón para diferenciar entre ambos.

Le hizo libre en sus preferencias y responsable de sus actos y obras.

passages.heading: The Qur’an is a Way of Life
passages.text: A Muslim should be keen on reading/reciting the Holy Qur’an and studying the rules it prescribes.

passages.heading: The Qur’an is a Way of Life
passages.text:
The Holy Qur’an is the Word of the Lord of all the worlds, who has created all mankind, knows them better than they know themselves and knows what benefits them and what harms them, hence the reason why Allah Almighty has made the Qur’an, which was the last of His revealed books, a didactic book which maps out a way of life for people, as evidenced by the following points:

- It deals with human life extensively, taking into account its three intrinsic spheres: personal life, family life and community life.
- Its deals with a wide array of matters, including, among other things, beliefs, acts of worship, customs, social and financial relations, man’s mental, emotional and physical states, international relations and peace and war.
- It promotes justice under all circumstances, even when dealing with enemies, and forbids injustice in all its forms.

> The Holy Qur’an maps out the way of life for people and defines and explains to them their rights and obligations with great flexibility, making its laws valid for all times and places.

passages.heading: Benefits of Faith
passages.text:
* **Getting to know Allah Almighty:** A believer gets to know his Lord and His names, attributes and actions, so much so that he becomes more attached to Him.
* **Glorying Allah:** the more a believer gets to know his Lord, the more he extols and loves Him, the more he hopes for His mercy and the more God-fearing he becomes.
* **Getting to know Allah’s graciousness to His servants:** for sending messengers to them and divine books to them to guide them to the true religion.
* **Loving the angels:** for worshipping Allah and showing obedience to Him.
* **Loving Allah’s Messengers:** Allah Almighty chose them to convey His message to people.
* **Diligent worship:** the stronger the faith, the more worship one performs.
* **A truly happy life:** A believer is content with what Allah has apportioned to him and knows that whatever calamities befall him in this world elevate his rank and efface his sins. He also hopes for the bliss He has prepared for the believers in the life to come.
* **Not to be deluded by this world:** The life of this world is temporary and only serves as a means to eternal life in the hereafter.
* **Exposing myths:** Faith exposes and nullifies many myths.
* **Entering Paradise:** This is the abode of eternal bliss which Allah Almighty has prepared for His believing servants.

passages.heading: Soorat Al-Kawthar (Abundant Good)
passages.text:
*Soorat Al-Kawthar* **Explained**

{{Q:108:1-3}}

“We have bestowed on you abundant good”

We have given you, Messenger, immeasurable, abundant good in this life and the life to come, part of which is River Al-Kawthar in Paradise.

“So pray to your Lord and sacrifice to Him”

Therefore, sincerely pray to your Lord and worship Him alone, and sacrifice to Him, pronouncing Allah’s name alone when slaughtering animals, in gratitude to Him for the honour and good He has bestowed on you.

“He who hates you is the one who is truly cut off”

*Shaani’aka*: The one who hates you and hates the true religion you have brought.

The one who hates you and hates the true religion you have brought is the most disgraced and contemptible, whose mention is short-lived and who is cut off from all good.

passages.heading: Introduction
passages.text: In his life, a Muslim performs a number of acts of worship whereby he draws closer to his Creator, Glory is to Him. We do such acts to glorify Allah Almighty and submit to Him alone. The more a Muslim’s heart glorifies Allah, Exalted be He, the greater the effect of doing so is on his worship. A true Muslim dedicates all life, including the time he spends at work, sleeping and having fun, to Allah Almighty, bearing in mind the verse: {{Q:6:162-163}} (Soorat Al-An’aam, 6:162-163) In this lesson, we are going to learn about the meaning of worship, its types, the conditions that must be met for it to be accepted, and its levels.

passages.heading: Introduction
passages.text: One of the most memorable moments of a new Muslim’s life must be the moment he joined the fold of Islam by pronouncing the two testimonies of faith. By so doing, he declared to himself before anyone else that he would begin a new chapter in his life and would, from the moment of making such a declaration, take the first steps towards finding the truth and adhering to it. In this lesson, we are going to learn about the two testimonies and their meaning and requirements.

3. Islam is the way to happiness in this life and salvation in the life to come; therefore, those who believe in Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and follow him after his message has reached them will be saved; as for those who deny him, they will be doomed to divine punishment. The Almighty says, {{Q:3:85}} (*Soorat Aal-’Imraan, 3:85*) The Prophet ﷺ also said, “By Him in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, any person of this Community, Jew or Christian, who hears of me and dies without believing in what I have been sent with will be among the dwellers of Hell” (*Saheeh Muslim;* No. 153).

4. Islam gives conclusive answers to the big questions of human existence: Where did we come from? Why are we here? Where do we go after death?

5. Islam is in perfect harmony with the innate human nature (*fitrah*), beginning with the greatest value it embraces, namely the declaration of Allah’s unity, and ending with the rules of etiquette it teaches its adherents to enable them to attain great perfection in moral excellence.

passages.heading: Why Should I Embrace Islam?
passages.text:
Some people may ask: Why should I embrace Islam?

The answer is: I must do so for a number of reasons, including the following:

1. Islam is the religion that Allah has approved and chosen for His servants and will not accept any other religion. The Almighty says, {{Q:3:85}} (Soorat Aal-’Imraan, 3:85).

2. Islam is the religion of all the prophets and commands its adherents to believe in all of them without exception. Allah says, {{Q:2:136}} (Soorat Al-Baqarah, 2:136).
The difference between prophets lies only in the laws relating to people’s actions, as the Almighty says, {{Q:5:48}} (Soorat Al-Maa’idah, 5:48) That is, for each nation before Islam, Allah appointed a law to which people referred for their disputes and a way of life whereby they drew near to Him. Thus, followers of every prophet had their respective laws and regulations, but the set of beliefs to which prophets called their people was the same. Then Allah sent the last prophet and messenger, Muhammad ﷺ, with the final divine laws, and thus the only religion acceptable to Allah is Islam.

passages.heading: Stories of the Prophets in the Qur’an
passages.text:
The Holy Qur’an is replete with stories of the previous prophets and their people, starting with Adam, and passing through Noah, Hud, Saalih, Shu’ayb, Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, Moses, Jesus, and other prophets and messengers, peace be upon them all. The Holy Qur’an mentions their stories for a number of reasons, including the following:

- to show that the religion of all the prophets is, in essence, the same and that its basis is to worship Allah Almighty alone.
- to give solace to Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and make him stand firm and steadfast, reminding him that prophets before him suffered the same hardships he himself was experiencing.
- to give comfort and solace to the believers, reminding them that even Allah’s honourable servants before them were afflicted with trials and tribulations.
- to afford people the opportunity to learn lessons from such true stories.

passages.heading: Benefits of Faith
passages.text:
Faith has many benefits, including the following:

* **Peace and tranquillity:** Faith gives the believer tranquillity and reassurance. He submits to Allah’s decree, or *qadar*, and fears none but Allah.

> Al-Qadar, or divine decree, refers to the things Allah Almighty has already preordained and His foreknowledge that they will occur at times known only to Him and in a particular manner.

“By the time”

Allah swears by the time in which people’s good and evil deeds take place.

Mankind is indeed in sheer loss and ruin,

“except for those who believe and do good works; who exhort each other to justice and to fortitude”

except for those who believe in Allah, do righteous deeds, and urge one another to adhere to the truth and to be patient and steadfast in doing so.

passages.heading: The Meaning of Worship
passages.text: By worship is meant everything that Allah has enjoined on us for us to draw closer to Him. It comprises all words and deeds that Allah loves, whether they are outward like the physical acts of worship, such as the prayer and pilgrimage, or inward, like the acts of worship involving the heart, such as love of Allah, fearing His punishment and hoping for His mercy. A person can transform everyday habits into acts of worship simply by having a good intention. If, for instance, he eats, drinks and sleeps with the intention of gaining enough strength to worship Allah better, he will certainly be rewarded for doing so

passages.heading: Types of Acts of Worship
passages.text:
Acts of worship fall into different categories:

| Acts of worship involving the heart | A Muslim performs these with his heart. Examples include love, fear, hope and *khushoo’*. |
| --- | --- |
| Physical acts of worship | A Muslim performs these physically. Examples include the prayer, *zakaat* and pilgrimage. |
| Acts that are abandoned in obedience to Allah | A Muslim draws closer to his Lord by abandoning the acts He has forbidden him, such as drinking alcohol and committing adultery, or by refraining from certain permissible acts at specific times, such as abstaining from food and drink while fasting. |

> *Ar-Rajaa’*(Hope): This refers to rejoicing in Allah’s grace and hoping for His benevolence, while at the same time ensuring proper reliance on Allah by doing good deeds to the best of one’s ability.
> 
> *Al-khushoo’* is a state of utter humility and calmness and deep concentration into which one gets while performing an act of worship, such as the prayer, bringing about outward composure and tranquillity.

passages.heading: Conditions for Acts of Worship to Be Accepted
passages.text:
For an act of worship to be accepted, two conditions must be fulfilled:

The first condition: It has to be done sincerely for the sake of Allah to draw closer to alone, without showing off.

The second condition: It has to be done in the manner Allah has enjoined it and exactly as it was performed by the Prophet ﷺ.

> *Aririyyaa’* (showing off) is the act of doing an act of worship only to be seen and praised by people for doing it.

passages.heading: Introduction
passages.text: Islam is the religion with which Allah sent Muhammad ﷺ and is an extension of the same religion with which all the previous messengers came. It is essentially based on the belief that Allah Almighty is the only deity deserving of worship, who has no partners or assistants whatsoever in His kingdom, and who has no intermediaries between Him and His servants. But why should I embrace Islam? Is it a religion for all people or is it only for the Arabs? Who is its prophet, and is there another prophet who will come after him?

passages.heading: Some Distinguishing Characteristics of Islam
passages.text: Islam is distinguished from other religions by many characteristics, the most prominent of which are:

passages.heading: Things That a Person Who Is in a State of *Jannabah* Must Not Do
passages.text:
The state into which a person gets following intercourse or ejaculation and because of which he must perform *ghusl* is called *janaabah*, and he is described as *junub*. In this case, he is not allowed to do the following:

1. perform the prayer
2. circumambulate the Ka’bah (*tawaaf*)
3. touch or carry the Qur’an
4. stay in the mosque
5. read the Qur’an

passages.heading: Islamic Rulings Pertaining to Menstrual and Postnatal Bleeding
passages.text:
Allah Almighty has prescribed several rulings relating to menstruating women and women experiencing their postnatal bleeding, including the following:

- They are exempt from performing the prayers during this period and do not have to make up for the prayers they have missed while in this state after the end of menstrual and postnatal bleeding.
- They are exempt from fasting and are not allowed to fast while in this state, but they must make up for the fasting days they have missed in Ramadaan.
- During this period, a husband must not have intercourse with his wife during her menstrual or postnatal period. He is allowed, however, to satisfy his sexual desire but without having intercourse.
- At the end of the menstrual and postnatal period, when bleeding stops completely, women must take a ritual bath (*ghusl*).

passages.text: A Muslim must perform *ghusl* in three cases:

passages.heading: Second Case
passages.text: Intercourse, whether or not ejaculation takes place.

passages.heading: How to Perform *Ghusl*?
passages.text:
To perform *ghusl*, one must wash the entire body with water, rinse out one’s mouth and clean one’s nose by sniffing water into the nostrils and ejecting it out by blowing one’s nose. A Muslim removes the major ritual impurity by simply doing so.

> The major ritual impurity: what must be removed by ghusl, and ablution is not sufficient, and these are types:
> 
> 1- *Janaabah*: The state of ritual impurity following intercourse or ejaculation as a result of an orgasm even if no intercourse takes place.
> 2- Menstruation: the normal vaginal bleeding that occurs as part of a woman’s monthly cycle.
> 3- Postnatal bleeding: The vaginal bleeding that takes place following childbirth.

passages.text: There are some cases where *wudoo’* is not sufficient to perform an act of worship, but *ghusl* is required. In this lesson, we are going to learn about the meaning of *ghusl*, the reasons for performing it, as well as how to perform it.

passages.heading: The Manner of Performing the Full Ritual Bath (*Ghusl*)
passages.text:
If a Muslim wants to perform *ghusl*, he must do the following:

1. He intends in his heart to perform *ghusl* and washes out his private parts with water.
2. He performs *wudoo’* like the one he performs before the prayer.
3. He washes his entire body with water.

passages.heading: *Tayammum* (Dry Ablution)
passages.text:
If a person who wants to perform *wudoo’* or *ghusl* is unable to do so due to illness, or when water is not readily available, or for any other legitimate reason, he may resort to dry ablution (*tayammum*) instead.

The Manner of Performing *Tayammum*: (1) Intend in his heart to perform *tayammum* and strike both hands slightly on pure earth once, (2) wipe the face with them, (3) wipe the back of the right hand with the palm of the left, and then the back of the left hand with the palm of the right hand.

passages.heading: What shall I do if I find water after having performed *tayammum*?
passages.text: If a Muslim finds water or can use it, his purity becomes invalid, in which case he must perform *wudoo’* or *ghusl*.

passages.heading: How Many Times Do We Wash the Parts of the Body that Are Usually Washed in *Wudoo’*?
passages.text: According to the *Sunnah*, each part of the body is washed three times, except in the case of the head and ears, which are wiped only once. It would suffice, however, to wash these body parts once provided that they are washed thoroughly.

passages.heading: How Do We Pray?
passages.text: If a Muslim wants to pray, he must do the following:

passages.heading: The Meaning of *Wudoo’*
passages.text: *Wudoo’*: The ritual of washing the face, hands, and feet, and wiping over the head in a specific manner.

passages.heading: The Manner of Performing *Wudoo’*
passages.text:
1. He intends in his heart to perform *wudoo’* and says, *bismillaah* “In the name of Allah”.
2. He washes his hands up to the wrists with water.
3. He rinses out his mouth thoroughly by moving water around in the mouth and then spitting it out. This process is called *madmadah*) in Arabic.
4. He cleans his nose by sniffing water into the nostrils and ejecting it out by blowing his nose.
5. He washes his face thoroughly from the hairline at the top of the forehead to the bottom of the chin, along with the beard, if he is bearded, and from ear to ear.
6. He washes his hands from the fingertips up to the elbow, starting with his right hand.
7. With wet hands, and starting with his hands flat on the top of the head near the hairline, he wipes it to the back of the neck and back to the front.
8. With wet fingers, he wipes  
He wipes the inner sides of the ears with his index fingers and behind them with his thumbs.
9. He washes his feet up to the ankles, which are the two prominent bones of the joint connecting the foot to the leg, starting with his right foot.

passages.heading: The Manner of Performing *Wudoo’*
passages.text: If a Muslim wants to perform his ablutions (*wudoo’*), he must do the following:

passages.heading: Wiping over the Socks
passages.text: If a person wants to perform *wudoo’* while he has his socks on, he is allowed to just wipe over the top of them with wet hands, and there is no need to take them off and wash the feet. Three conditions are required for this:

passages.heading: Forbidden Types of Clothing
passages.text:
A man's *'awrah* that must be covered extends from the navel to the knees. A woman must cover herself entirely in the presence of men not related to her; as for men to whom she is related and is forbidden to marry, such as her father, son and brother, she may appear before them as she would normally do in front of other women, showing such parts of her body as the face, hair, the neck and feet.

- Clothing that reveals the *'awrah* and does not conceal it
- Clothing that involves dressing like or imitating the opposite sex, such as when men dress like women and vice versa.
- Clothing that is worn with an air of pride and conceit
- Extravagant clothing
- Men are particularly forbidden to wear silk clothing or adorn themselves with gold or silver jewellery.
- Clothing that involves imitation of the dress traditionally worn by non-Muslims and specific to a certain religion, such as the type of clothing worn by monks and priests

passages.text: A Muslim pays *zakaat* due on his cash once a year. 2.5% of its value must be given out as *zakaat*.

passages.heading: Things That Render *Wudoo’* Invalid
passages.text:
*Wudoo’* becomes invalid as a result of four things:

- Natural discharges from the private parts (both the external genital and excretory organs), such as urine, excrement, wind, semen and the clear, colourless, viscous fluid that is emitted during sexual arousal
- Loss of consciousness due to sleep or intoxication
- Lustfully touching the private parts with bare hands
- Eating camel meat
