passages.heading: The Five Obligatory Prayers
passages.text:
Allah Almighty has enjoined Muslims to perform five prayers throughout the day and night, namely:

| The Prayer | Beginning Time | Ending Time | Number of units (*rak‘ahs*) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| *Fajr* (Dawn) Prayer | at the break of dawn | sunrise | 2 |
| *Dhuhr* (Midday) Prayer | when the sun starts declining westward at midday after reaching its zenith | when the shadow of an object becomes equal in length to the object itself | 4 |
| *‘Asr* (Late Afternoon) Prayer | when the shadow of an object becomes equal in length to the object itself | sunset | 4 |
| *Maghrib* (Sunset) Prayer | sunset | when the red glow (evening twilight) on the western horizon disappears | 3 |
| *‘Ishaa’* (Late Evening) Prayer | when the red glow (evening twilight) on the western horizon disappears | midnight | 4 |

passages.heading: How Do We Pray?
passages.text:
1. He intends in his heart to pray.
2. He stands facing the *qiblah*, raises his hands up to the level of the shoulders or ears, and says, “*Allaahu akbar* Allah is the Greatest.”
3. He places his right hand on his left hand. Then he recites one of the opening supplications, such as, Subhaanak-Allaahumma wa bi hamdika, wa tabaarak-asmuka, wa ta’aalaa jadduka, wa laa ilaaha ghayruka “Glory be to You, O Allah; Yours is the praise, blessed is Your name, exalted is Your majesty, and there is no god besides You.” Then he says, A’oodhu billaahi min-ash-shaytaan-ir-rajeem. Bismillaah-ir-rahmaan-ir-raheem “I seek Allah’s protection from Satan, who has been expelled from His mercy. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.” Then he recites *Soorat Al-Faatihah* and says after it, “*Aameen*”, which means “Answer our supplications, O Allah”. After that, he recites whatever number of verses of the Qur’an as is easy for him, even if it is one verse.
4. He says, “Allaahu akbar Allah is the Greatest” while raising his hands up to the level of his shoulders or ears, and bows down, lowering his head and back and keeping them straight at a right angle, placing the palms of his hands on the knees. He says three times while in this position, “Subhaana rabbiy-al-’adheem Glory be to my Lord, the Almighty.”

5. He resumes the standing position, raising his hands up to the level of the shoulders or the ears, saying: Sami’allaahu li man hamidah “Allah hears those who praise Him.” Then he says while standing: Rabbanaa wa lakal-hamd “Our Lord, to You is due all praise.”

6. He says, Allaahu akbar “Allah is the Greatest” and prostrates himself, with the toes of both feet, the knees, the palms of the hands and the forehead and the nose touching the floor. He says three times while in this position, “Glory be to my Lord, Most High.”

passages.heading: Introduction
passages.text: Since ancient times, people on this earth have led different lives with varying living standards. Some are very well-to-do; others are destitute and can barely find anything to eat. This is one of Allah’s ways in this universe. Islam enjoins the wealthy to pay a certain percentage of their wealth to the poor to relieve them of the burden of poverty and urges Muslims to spend more of what they are required to spend, promising them great rewards for doing so both in this life and after death. It also urges them to give charity to the needy at all times and on every occasion and encourages them to feed the hungry and clothe the naked in order for the Muslim community to become close-knit, just as Allah Almighty wants it to be. In this lesson, we are going to learn about the Islamic ruling on *zakaat*, the manner of paying it and the types of wealth upon which it is due.

passages.heading: Why Do We Pay *Zakaat*?
passages.text: We pay *zakaat* in compliance with the command of Allah who has enjoined us to pay it.

passages.heading: What Is *Zakaat*?
passages.text: *Zakaat*: a religious obligation whereby wealthy Muslims give away a certain portion of their wealth to the poor in their midst. It is the third pillar of Islam.

passages.heading: Second
passages.text: to increase one’s wealth, for *zakaat* does not decrease it, but rather increases it and even blesses it.

passages.heading: First

passages.heading: Third

passages.heading: What Is *Zakaat*?
passages.text: *Zakaat*: a religious obligation whereby wealthy Muslims give away a certain portion of their wealth to the poor in their midst. It is the third pillar of Islam.

passages.heading: Introduction
passages.text: Since ancient times, people on this earth have led different lives with varying living standards. Some are very well-to-do; others are destitute and can barely find anything to eat. This is one of Allah’s ways in this universe. Islam enjoins the wealthy to pay a certain percentage of their wealth to the poor to relieve them of the burden of poverty and urges Muslims to spend more of what they are required to spend, promising them great rewards for doing so both in this life and after death. It also urges them to give charity to the needy at all times and on every occasion and encourages them to feed the hungry and clothe the naked in order for the Muslim community to become close-knit, just as Allah Almighty wants it to be. In this lesson, we are going to learn about the Islamic ruling on *zakaat*, the manner of paying it and the types of wealth upon which it is due.

passages.heading: Discuss
passages.text:
Settling on earth and building a civilization on it is one of man’s roles in this life. To enable him to perform this great and challenging task, Allah has provided him with such physical and mental make-ups to help him perform this role. Explain how, of all other creatures, only man can settle on earth and build a civilization?

Mention some of the practical implications of getting to know the ultimate fate of people after death?

passages.heading: Stories of the Prophets in the Qur’an
passages.text:
The Holy Qur’an is replete with stories of the previous prophets and their people, starting with Adam, and passing through Noah, Hud, Saalih, Shu’ayb, Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, Moses, Jesus, and other prophets and messengers, peace be upon them all. The Holy Qur’an mentions their stories for a number of reasons, including the following:

- to show that the religion of all the prophets is, in essence, the same and that its basis is to worship Allah Almighty alone.
- to give solace to Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and make him stand firm and steadfast, reminding him that prophets before him suffered the same hardships he himself was experiencing.
- to give comfort and solace to the believers, reminding them that even Allah’s honourable servants before them were afflicted with trials and tribulations.
- to afford people the opportunity to learn lessons from such true stories.

passages.heading: My Notes
passages.text: Write down some of the benefits of faith that you have enjoyed after embracing Islam.

passages.text:

Say, Messenger, to those who disbelieve in Allah and His Messenger: You unbelievers.

I do not worship the false gods, such as idols, that you worship.

nor do you worship the True God whom I worship, and who alone is worthy of worship.

I will never worship the false gods that you worship.

nor will you ever worship the True God whom I worship, and who alone is worthy of worship.

“You have your religion, and I have my religion”

You have your religion to which you adhere, and I have my religion to which I adhere.

passages.text: We pay *zakaat* in compliance with the command of Allah who has enjoined us to pay it.

passages.heading: The Blessing of Right Guidance
passages.text: Whoever knows the purpose of his existence and the outcome that awaits people on the Day of Resurrection is bound to realise that the greatest blessing that Allah has ever bestowed upon people is that of guidance to the true religion and righteous deeds. Therefore, Allah Almighty has enjoined His servants to ask Him in their prayer to guide them to the straight path—the religion of Islam which leads to Allah’s good pleasure.

passages.heading: Some Virtues of Good Moral Character
passages.text:
- The Prophet ﷺ informs us that the act that will cause people to enter Paradise the most will be piety and good character.
- He ﷺ states that the heaviest of a person’s good deeds that will be placed on the scales of deeds on the Day of Resurrection will be good moral character.
- He ﷺ further states that the closest believers to him on the Day of Resurrection will be those who possess good moral character.

> **The scales of deeds:** This will be on the Day of Resurrection when a person’s good and bad deeds will be weighed in a balance, whose shape or size none knows but Allah. Those whose good deeds outweigh their bad deeds will be admitted into Paradise, but those whose bad deeds outweigh their bad deeds will be sent to Hell.

passages.heading: Good Moral Character in Islam
passages.text:
- Good moral character occupies a lofty position in Islam, as it is one of the important objectives of *Sharee‘ah* and one of the goals behind the Prophet’s mission.
- Good moral character is closely linked to faith, and the believers with complete faith are those who demonstrate the best moral character.
- A Muslim will be rewarded for his good manners, just as he will be rewarded for the prayer and fasting.

passages.heading: Introduction
passages.text: Islam urges its followers to observe high moral character. The Prophet ﷺ stressed the importance of morals in many of his traditions, combining many acts of worship Muslims perform with good moral character. Islam promises a Muslim who displays such good character great rewards both in this world and the hereafter. In this lesson, we are going to learn about the importance of good moral character in Islam, as well as some of its virtues.

passages.heading: Domains of Good Moral Character in Islam:
passages.text:
Good moral character in Islam is not restricted to one domain; rather, it covers many of them, namely:

- Good moral character vis-à-vis Allah Almighty, such as by devoting oneself sincerely to Him and showing total obedience to Him.
- Good moral character vis-à-vis the Prophet ﷺ, such as by loving him, respecting him, showing politeness when talking about him and invoking Allah’s peace and blessings upon him when his name is mentioned.
- Good moral character vis-à-vis Allah’s laws, such as by honouring and obeying them.
- Good moral character vis-à-vis oneself, such as by gently encouraging oneself to show obedience to Allah and firmly avoiding laziness in this respect.
- Good moral character vis-à-vis others, such as by being honest and trustworthy.
- Good moral character vis-à-vis animals, such as by showing kindness to them and not being cruel to them.
- Good moral character vis-à-vis the environment, such as by preserving it, planting trees and not being extravagant with its natural resources.

passages.heading: Discuss
passages.text: How should a Muslim’s moral character be with others? Do you think that such good character has an impact on their opinion about Islam?

passages.text:

> *Hadath*: This is the state of having our ablutions broken and thus prevents us from performing the prayer before purifying ourselves. It is of two types: one requires us to perform only partial ablutions (*wudoo’*) to remove it, and the other requires us to perform full ablutions (*ghusl*).

passages.heading: The Manner of Performing *Wudoo’*
passages.text:
1. He intends in his heart to perform *wudoo’* and says, *bismillaah* “In the name of Allah”.
2. He washes his hands up to the wrists with water.
3. He rinses out his mouth thoroughly by moving water around in the mouth and then spitting it out. This process is called *madmadah*) in Arabic.
4. He cleans his nose by sniffing water into the nostrils and ejecting it out by blowing his nose.
5. He washes his face thoroughly from the hairline at the top of the forehead to the bottom of the chin, along with the beard, if he is bearded, and from ear to ear.
6. He washes his hands from the fingertips up to the elbow, starting with his right hand.
7. With wet hands, and starting with his hands flat on the top of the head near the hairline, he wipes it to the back of the neck and back to the front.
8. With wet fingers, he wipes  
He wipes the inner sides of the ears with his index fingers and behind them with his thumbs.
9. He washes his feet up to the ankles, which are the two prominent bones of the joint connecting the foot to the leg, starting with his right foot.

passages.text: If a person wants to perform *wudoo’* while he has his socks on, he is allowed to just wipe over the top of them with wet hands, and there is no need to take them off and wash the feet. Three conditions are required for this:

passages.text: If a Muslim performs wudoo’, the general rule is that his wudoo’ is still valid unless one of the previously-mentioned things that break wudoo’ happens, in which case he must perform it again.

passages.heading: Introduction
passages.text: *Wudoo’* is very important in Islam because it is closely connected with the ritual prayer, which is itself the greatest ritual in Islam, hence the importance of learning it and performing it correctly. In this lesson, we are going to learn about the meaning of *wudoo’*, things that require us to perform it, things that make it invalid, and the proper manner of performing it.

passages.heading: How Many Times Do We Wash the Parts of the Body that Are Usually Washed in *Wudoo’*?
passages.text: According to the *Sunnah*, each part of the body is washed three times, except in the case of the head and ears, which are wiped only once. It would suffice, however, to wash these body parts once provided that they are washed thoroughly.

passages.text: *Wudoo’*: The ritual of washing the face, hands, and feet, and wiping over the head in a specific manner.

passages.heading: Things That Render *Wudoo’* Invalid
passages.text:
*Wudoo’* becomes invalid as a result of four things:

- Natural discharges from the private parts (both the external genital and excretory organs), such as urine, excrement, wind, semen and the clear, colourless, viscous fluid that is emitted during sexual arousal
- Loss of consciousness due to sleep or intoxication
- Lustfully touching the private parts with bare hands
- Eating camel meat

passages.heading: Stories of the Prophets in the Qur’an
passages.text:
The Holy Qur’an is replete with stories of the previous prophets and their people, starting with Adam, and passing through Noah, Hud, Saalih, Shu’ayb, Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, Moses, Jesus, and other prophets and messengers, peace be upon them all. The Holy Qur’an mentions their stories for a number of reasons, including the following:

- to show that the religion of all the prophets is, in essence, the same and that its basis is to worship Allah Almighty alone.
- to give solace to Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and make him stand firm and steadfast, reminding him that prophets before him suffered the same hardships he himself was experiencing.
- to give comfort and solace to the believers, reminding them that even Allah’s honourable servants before them were afflicted with trials and tribulations.
- to afford people the opportunity to learn lessons from such true stories.

passages.heading: What Is the Qur’an?
passages.text:
The Holy Qur’an is the Word of Allah Almighty that He revealed to His Messenger, Muhammad ﷺ. It is the last of Allah’s revealed books, and there is no other book after it.

The revealed books are the books that Allah Almighty revealed to His prophets.
A Muslim believes that these books were revealed by Allah Almighty, and that Allah spoke in them in a manner that befits Him. These books include Az-Zaboor (the Psalms), which He revealed to Daawood (David) عليه السلام; At-Tawraat (the Torah), which He revealed to Moosaa (Moses) عليه السلام and Al-Injeel (the Gospel), which He revealed to Jesus, عليه السلام. All these books have undergone alteration and corruption through the ages.

passages.heading: Introduction
passages.text: Islam is the religion with which Allah sent Muhammad ﷺ and is an extension of the same religion with which all the previous messengers came. It is essentially based on the belief that Allah Almighty is the only deity deserving of worship, who has no partners or assistants whatsoever in His kingdom, and who has no intermediaries between Him and His servants. But why should I embrace Islam? Is it a religion for all people or is it only for the Arabs? Who is its prophet, and is there another prophet who will come after him?

passages.heading: Islamic Rulings Pertaining to Meat Served in Restaurants and Shops
passages.text:
1. The meat of animals that are slaughtered by other than a Muslim or a member of the People of the Book (a Christian or a Jew), such as a Buddhist, or a Hindu is strictly forbidden. This includes meat served in restaurants and shops in countries where Muslims or People of the Book constitute a minority.
2. The meat of animals killed by a Muslim or a member of the People of the Book is lawful based on textual evidence to this effect in the Qur’an.
3. The meat of animals that are not killed according to Islamic law, such as by electrocution and drowning, is strictly forbidden.
4. The general rule is that it is permissible to consume the flesh of animals slaughtered by People of the Book as well as meat of animals generally found in their restaurants and shops, making sure, however, to invoke Allah’s name at the time of eating (that is, by saying *Bismillaah*), but it is better for Muslims to eat only meat that has been proven to be lawful (*halaal*).

passages.heading: What is the Islamic Ruling on Seafood Consumption?
passages.text:
It is permissible to eat dead aquatic animals that can live only in water, such as fish and prawns, whether they live in the sea, rivers or lakes.

It is permissible to hunt wild, nonpredatory animals and consume their flesh provided that the name of Allah is mentioned before the hunting weapon is discharged, and the hunted game must be slaughtered if found still alive.

Islam is essentially the religion of all the prophets: to worship Allah alone and reject all false deities that are worshipped besides or instead of Him. Allah Almighty, says, {{Q:21:25}} (Surat al-Anbiyyaa’, 21:25).

Therefore, it is not permissible, under any circumstances, to believe in any deity other than Allah Almighty, nor is it permissible to perform any act of worship to draw nearer to anyone other than Allah Almighty.

passages.heading: Shirk
passages.text:
3. **Belief in the divinely revealed books:** A Muslim believes that Allah sent down divine books to His Messengers to guide people to the truth and teach them their religion. These include the Torah (*At-Tawraah*) which He revealed to Moses (Moosaa) son of ‘Imraan, the Zaboor which He revealed to David (Daawood), the Gospel (*Al-Injeel*) which He revealed to Jesus (‘Eesaa) son of Mary and the Qur’an which He revealed to Muhammad, peace be upon them all. He also believes that the Qur’an is the last of them and that it has final authority over them all.
4. **Belief in the prophets:** A Muslim believes that Allah Almighty sent messengers to their people and supported them with miracles to prove their truthfulness. He sent them to give the believers good news of reward, warn the unbelievers of punishment and teach their people their religion. Those to whom they were sent must obey and follow them. Muhammad ﷺ was the final prophet whom He sent to all mankind.
5. **Belief in the Last Day:** A Muslim believes in Resurrection Day. He believes that Allah will raise the dead from their graves on that day and judge and repay them according to their deeds. Some will enter Paradise while others will enter Hell.
6. **Belief in the divine decree:** A Muslim believes that everything in this universe, whether good or evil, happens according to Allah’s decree, that He foreknows all events which He has already written in the Preserved Tablet, and that everything in this universe happens according to His will.

passages.heading: The Requirements of the Two Testimonies of Faith
passages.text: It is not enough to verbally declare the two testimonies of faith. In addition to this, it is imperative to know what they mean and to meet their requirements. The testimony that there is no god but Allah requires us to reject everything that is worshipped besides or instead of Allah, to firmly believe that Allah alone is our Lord and Cherisher and the One True God worthy of worship and to worship Him sincerely. Allah Almighty says, {{Q:2:256}} (Soorat Al-Baqarah, 2:256) The testimony that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah requires us to believe what he says, do what he commands and avoid what he forbids and worship Allah only according to his instructions.

passages.heading: The Qur’an is a Way of Life
passages.text: A Muslim should be keen on reading/reciting the Holy Qur’an and studying the rules it prescribes.

passages.heading: Its miraculous nature
passages.text: The Arab unbelievers rejected the Qur’an, so Allah challenged them to produce the like of it, or one soorah like it, or even ten verses, but they were unable to do so.

passages.heading: Its language
passages.text: Allah Almighty revealed it in Arabic.

passages.heading: Introduction
passages.text: When Allah sent prophets to their people to call them to the truth, he supported them with some miracles to prove to them that they were true prophets. These miracles, however, ended with the passing of these prophets. As for the Messenger of Islam ﷺ, Allah also furnished him with certain miracles to show his people, and all mankind, for that matter, but the greatest of all of them was His Glorious Book, which He took upon Himself to preserve even after the demise of His prophet ﷺ. In this lesson, we are going to learn about some virtues and etiquette associated with the Qur’an.

passages.heading: The Virtue of Reading/Reciting the Qur’an
passages.text:
- The Prophet ﷺ said, “If anyone reads/recites one single letter in Allah’s Book, he will be credited with a good deed, and a good deed gets a tenfold reward. I do not say that *alif*, *laam*, *meem* are one letter; rather, *alif* is a letter, *laam* is a letter and *meem* is a letter” (Reported by At-Tirmidhee; No. 2910 with an authentic chain of narrators).

- The Prophet ﷺ also said, “Read the Qur’an, for it will come on the Day of Resurrection as an intercessor for those who read it.” (Reported by Muslim; No. 804).

passages.heading: Lesson 1
passages.text: ## Learn about the Holy Qur’an

passages.heading: The Qur’an is Food for the Soul and Mind
passages.text:
The Holy Qur’an addresses both people’s minds and souls. It addresses the mind by:

- encouraging them to use logical reasoning on the various issues. The Almighty says, {{Q:21:22}} (Soorat Al-Anbiyyaa’, 21:22).
- calling them to exercise their intellects and contemplate His signs and the proofs of His power. The Almighty says, {{Q:2:219}} (Soorat Al-Baqarah, 2:219).
- reproving those who do not use their intellects to reflect on His signs. The Almighty says, {{Q:25:44}} (Soorat Al-Furqaan, 25: 44).

It also addresses the soul and emotions by:

- spotlighting and depicting human feelings in many cases. The Almighty says, {{Q:2:165}} (Soorat Al-Baqarah, 2:165).
- calling attention to human emotions and pointing out their good and bad effects. The Almighty says, {{Q:5:82}} (Soorat Al-Maa’idah, 5:82).
- commanding Muslims to exercise kindness and gentleness when inviting others to Islam. The Almighty says, {{Q:16:125}} (Soorat An-Nahl, 16: 125).
- incorporating aspects of faith into verses on legal rules. The Almighty says, {{Q:4:94}} (Soorat An-Nisaa’, 4:94).
- using moving words that evoke genuine emotions. The Almighty says, {{Q:24:22}} (Soorat An-Noor, 24:22).

passages.heading: Why Should I Embrace Islam?
passages.text:
Some people may ask: Why should I embrace Islam?

The answer is: I must do so for a number of reasons, including the following:

1. Islam is the religion that Allah has approved and chosen for His servants and will not accept any other religion. The Almighty says, {{Q:3:85}} (Soorat Aal-’Imraan, 3:85).

2. Islam is the religion of all the prophets and commands its adherents to believe in all of them without exception. Allah says, {{Q:2:136}} (Soorat Al-Baqarah, 2:136).
The difference between prophets lies only in the laws relating to people’s actions, as the Almighty says, {{Q:5:48}} (Soorat Al-Maa’idah, 5:48) That is, for each nation before Islam, Allah appointed a law to which people referred for their disputes and a way of life whereby they drew near to Him. Thus, followers of every prophet had their respective laws and regulations, but the set of beliefs to which prophets called their people was the same. Then Allah sent the last prophet and messenger, Muhammad ﷺ, with the final divine laws, and thus the only religion acceptable to Allah is Islam.

3. Islam is the way to happiness in this life and salvation in the life to come; therefore, those who believe in Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and follow him after his message has reached them will be saved; as for those who deny him, they will be doomed to divine punishment. The Almighty says, {{Q:3:85}} (*Soorat Aal-’Imraan, 3:85*) The Prophet ﷺ also said, “By Him in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, any person of this Community, Jew or Christian, who hears of me and dies without believing in what I have been sent with will be among the dwellers of Hell” (*Saheeh Muslim;* No. 153).

4. Islam gives conclusive answers to the big questions of human existence: Where did we come from? Why are we here? Where do we go after death?

5. Islam is in perfect harmony with the innate human nature (*fitrah*), beginning with the greatest value it embraces, namely the declaration of Allah’s unity, and ending with the rules of etiquette it teaches its adherents to enable them to attain great perfection in moral excellence.

passages.text: How can Islam be considered the religion of all the prophets?

passages.heading: 1. The Meaning of the Testimony that There Is no God but Allah
passages.text:
The meaning of “I bear witness that there is no god but Allah” is: I firmly believe that there is no god worthy of worship except Allah alone.

This testimony consists of two parts:

| The first part | The second part |
| --- | --- |
| negates the existence of any other deity besides Allah Almighty | confirms that Allah is the only True God worthy of worship |

passages.heading: 2. The Meaning of the Testimony that Muhammad is Allah’s Messenger
passages.text: The meaning of the testimony that Muhammad is Allah’s Messenger is: I firmly believe that Muhammad ﷺ is the Messenger of Allah, that he is the Final Prophet without there being any prophet whatsoever after him, and that his message is for all people without exception. Allah Almighty says: {{Q:25:1}} (Surat Al-Furqaan, 25:1).

passages.heading: أن تكون المرأة هي زوجته
passages.text: يجوز لهما ما لا يجوز لغيرهما من النظر والاستماع، وقد سمّى الله الزوج لباساً للزوجة والزوجة لباساً للزوج، كصورة رائعة من الاتصال النفسي والعاطفي والجسدي بينهما

يجب على المرأة المسلمة أن تستر جميع بدنها عن:
- أ) النساء الأخريات.
- ب) الرجال الأجانب.
- ج) والد الزوج.

يجب على الحائض والنفساء إذا طهرت أن تقضي:
- أ) الصلاة.
- ب) الصوم.
- ج) جميع ما سبق.

passages.heading: حجاب المرأة المسلمة:
passages.text: فرض الله الحجاب على المرأة دون الرجل لما أودع فيها من مظاهر الجمال وعوامل الإغراء، مما يجعلها فتنة للرجل أكثر من أن يكون الرجل فتنة لها، وحدود هذا الحجاب أن تغطي جميع بدنها عن الرجال الأجانب عنها، ولها أن تلبس ما شاءت من الأشكال والألوان مع مراعاة ثلاثة شروط:

passages.heading: مكانة المرأة في الإسلام:
passages.text:
من أمثلة الأحكام المتعلقة باحترام المرأة في الإسلام:
- أعطى الإسلام المرأة حقها من الميراث في قسمة عادلة كريمة، تساوي الرجل بالمرأة في مواضع، ويختلف نصيبها عنه في مواضع، بحسب قرابتها وتكاليف النفقة المناطة بها.
- ساوى بين الرجل والمرأة في شؤون كثيرة مختلفة ومن ذلك جميع التعاملات المالية..
- أعطى المرأة حرية اختيار الزوج.
- أبقى لها اسمها وشرف انتسابها لأبيها، فلا تتغير نسبتها بعد الزواج، بل تبقى منتسبة لأبيها وعائلتها.
- أوجب على الرجل رعايتها والإنفاق عليها بدون منّة إن كانت ممن تجب نفقته كالزوجة والأم والبنت.
- أكد على شرف وفضل خدمة المرأة الضعيفة التي ليس لها أحد، ولو لم تكن من الأقارب، ورغب في السعي لخدمتها وجعل ذلك من أفضل الأعمال عند الله.

passages.heading: الأول
passages.text: أن يكون الحجاب ساتراً لما يجب تغطيته.

passages.heading: الثاني
passages.text: أن يكون فضفاضاً واسعاً وليس ضيقاً يحدد أعضاء الجسم.

passages.heading: معنى الغسل:
passages.text:
الغُسل: غسل جميع البدن بالماء بنية رفع الحدث.

الجنابة: وصف للرجل والمرأة إذا حصل منهما جماع، أو نزول المني بشهوة ولو من غير جماع.

passages.heading: الألبسة المحرمة:
passages.text:
حرّم الله عز وجل أنواعًا من الألبسة، منها:

- ما يكشف العورة ولا يسترها، سواء كان اللباس رجلًا أو امرأة، صغيرًا أو كبيرًا.

> حدود عورة الرجل من السرة إلى الركبة، أما المرأة فكلها عورة أمام الرجال الأجانب وأما محارمها كالأب والإبن والأخ فتظهر له ما تظهره أمام النساء.

- وما يكون في تشبّه بالجنس الآخر؛ كلبس الرجال ملابس النساء، أو لبس النساء ملابس الرجال.
- وما يشعر بالكبر والخيلاء.
- وما كان فيه إسراف وتبذير.
- ويحرم على الرجال لبس الحرير، والتحلّي بالذهب والفضة.
- ويحرم لبس ما فيه تشبه بملابس الكفار المخصوصة كلباس القساوسة والرهبان مثلًا.

> شارك زملاءك في معرفة بعض مسببات تحريم أنواع من الألبسة..

نهى الرسول ﷺ عن تشبه الرجال بالنساء والنساء بالرجال ويشمل هذا النهي نوع اللباس وطريقة الكلام وعد هذا التشبه من كبائر الذنوب التي تستوجب عقاب الله وعذابه لمن يفعله ولم يتب منه، والإسلام يريد أن تكون طبيعة الرجل ومظهره متميزًا عن طبيعة المرأة، وكذلك أراد للمرأة؛ فذلك هو دليل الفطرة السليمة والمنطق الصحيح.

passages.heading: علاقة المرأة بالرجل:
passages.text: تنقسم علاقة المرأة بالنسبة للرجل إلى ثلاثة أقسام:

passages.heading: أن تكون من محارمه
passages.text: المقصود بالمحارم كل من يحرم على الرجل الزواج بها تحريماً مؤبداً مثل: الأم والأخت وابنة الأخت، وأخت الأب وأخت الأم وأم الزوجة، وهؤلاء يجوز لهن أن يخرجن أمام محارمهن بزينتهن التي تظهر الذراعين والرقبة والشعر ونحو ذلك بدون إسفاف أو تجاوز.

passages.heading: أن تكون المرأة أجنبية عنه
passages.text: المرأة الأجنبية هي كل امرأة ليست من محارمه، سواء كانت من أقاربه كبنت عمه وبنت عمته، وزوجة أخيه وقريبات العائلة، أو كانت من غير أقاربه ولا تربطه بها علاقة عائلية، وقد وضع الإسلام ضوابط للتعامل بين الجنسين كوجوب الحجاب وعدم الخلوة.

أوجب الإسلام على الرجل رعاية المرأة والإنفاق عليها بدون مِنَّة.
- صح
- خطأ

لا يشترط في الحجاب أن يكون فضفاضًا واسعًا.
- صح
- خطأ

إذا طهرت الحائض فيجب عليها أن تغتسل قبل أن تصلي.
- صح
- خطأ

الحيض هو دم طبيعي يخرج من رحم المرأة بعد الولادة.
- صح
- خطأ

passages.heading: الثالث
passages.text: أن لا يكون شفافاً يظهر أعضاء البدن تحته.

passages.heading: فائدة
passages.text: يحترم الإسلام عادات الشعوب وتقاليدهم ولا يلزمهم بتغييرها إلا إذا خالفت شيئًا من شعائر الإسلام وتعاليمه.

passages.heading: تمهيد
passages.text: من أكثر اللحظات التي لا ينساها المسلم الجديد، هي لحظة إعلان دخوله الإسلام من خلال نطقه للشهادتين، فبهذا الإعلان يُعلن لنفسه قبل أي أحد أنه غدا شيئًا آخر غير ما كان، وأنه منذ هذه اللحظات خطى خطواته الأولى نحو معرفة الحق والتمسك به. وفي هذا الدرس سنتعرف على الشهادتين ومعناهما ولوازمهما على المسلم.

passages.heading: من نحن؟
passages.text:
يعرّف الإسلام الإنسان بأنه مخلوق من مخلوقات الله تعالى الكثيرة، فضّله تعالى على كثيرٍ من المخلوقات، وسخّـر له كثيرًا من المخلوقات ليستعين بها على أداء مهامه المطلوبة منه مدة حياته. قال تعالى: {{Q:17:70}} (الإسراء: ٧٠).

وجعل الله تعالى في الإنسان شبهًا من:
- الملائكة في طهارتها وعبادتها.
- والشياطين في جحودها وعصيانها.
- والحيوانات في إشباعها لنزواتها وشهواتها.

> الملائكة: خلق من خلق الله تعالى، خلقهم الله عز وجل من نور، مربوبون مسخرون، عباد مكرمون، لا يعصون الله ما أمرهم ويفعلون ما يؤمرون، ولا يعلم عددهم إلا الله

وجعل فيه استعدادًا للخير، واستعدادًا للشر، وأعطاه ما يميّز به الخير من الشر؛ كالفطرة والعقل والحواس الخمسة.

وجعله حرًّا مختارًا مسؤولًا عن اختياراته وأعماله.

passages.heading: موجبات الوضوء:
passages.text:
> الحدث: وصف معنوي في الإنسان يمنعه من أداء الصلاة قبل أن يتطهر وليس شيئًا محسوسًا كالنجاسة، وهو نوعين أحدهما يلزم المسلم التوضأ لرفعه والآخر لا يُرفع إلا بالغُسل.

موجبات الوضوء هي الأمور التي يُشترط الوضوءُ لها، ويجب من أجلها، وإذا أحدث الشخصُ حَرُمَت عليه، وهي:

1. الصلاة
2. الطواف حول الكعبة
3. مس المصحف

passages.heading: معنى السورة:

passages.text:
وجوهر دين الإسلام الذي هو دين الأنبياء جميعًا: عبادة الله وحده، والكفر بكل ما يعبد من دونه.

قال الله تعالى: {{Q:21:25}} (الأنبياء: ٢٥).

فلا يجوز بأي حال من الأحوال اعتقاد ألوهية أي شيء سوى الله تعالى، ولا يجوز التقرب إلى غير الله تعالى بأي نوعٍ من العبادات.

passages.heading: ناقش
passages.text: هل يمكن أن تكون الموضة أو العادات والتقاليد أو الأنظمة هي المرجعية التي من خلالها يتحدد اللباس المناسب للرجل أو المرأة؟

passages.heading: من أين جئنا؟
passages.text:
حكى الله لنا في القرآن قصة خلقه وكيف بدأ الشيطان في معاداته، أنظر تفسير سورة البقرة للآيات (٣٠-٣٩).

يبين الإسلام أن أصل خلق الإنسان من طين هذه الأرض، خلق الله منها آدم، وهو أبو البشر جميعًا، قال تعالى: {{Q:23:12}} (المؤمنون: ١٢).

والغاية من خلق هذا الإنسان عبادة الله تعالى، مع غناه سبحانه عن خلقه، قال تعالى: {{Q:51:56}} (الذاريات: ٥٦).

وهناك غاية أخرى فرعية، وهي عمارة هذه الأرض بإصلاحها، وإقامة العدل فيها، ونشر الخير، قال تعالى: {{Q:55:26}} (الرحمن: ٢٦).

passages.heading: ١ الإسلام دين عالمي
passages.text:
دين الإسلام ليس خاصًا بالعرب، بل هو الدين الذي ارتضاه الله تعالى للبشر جميعًا، ولذلك قال الله تعالى لرسوله محمد ﷺ: {{Q:21:107}} (الأنبياء:١٠٧).

فقد جعل الله عز وجل النبي ﷺ رحمةً عامّةً للناس جميعًا، يهديهم لطريق الإيمان، وجعل شريعته أوسع الشرائع رحمةً بالناس.

passages.heading: ٢ الإسلام يكفّر ما سبقه من الذنوب
passages.text:
إذا أسلم العبد، وفعل ما يجب عليه من الواجبات، واجتنب ما حرّم الله عليه، فإن الله تعالى يغفر له ما تقدّم من ذنوبه قبل إسلامه، وقد قال النبي ﷺ: « إذا أسلم العبد فحسن إسلامه، يكفر الله عنه كل سيئة كان زلفها، وكان بعد ذلك القصاص: الحسنة بعشر أمثالها إلى سبع مائة ضعف، والسيئة بمثلها إلا أن يتجاوز الله عنها ». أخرجه البخاري (٤١).

وقد سأل رجل النبي ﷺ: يا رسول الله، أنؤاخذ بما عملنا في الجاهلية؟ فأجابه النبي ﷺ: «من أحسن في الإسلام لم يؤاخذ بما عمل في الجاهلية، ومن أساء في الإسلام أُخذ بالأول والآخر». أخرجه البخاري (٦٩٢١).

passages.heading: ٣ الإسلام الدين الخاتم
passages.text: جعل الله تعالى الإسلام امتدادًا للشرائع السماويّة السابقة، وارتضاه دينًا للخَلق جميعًا إلى قيام الساعة، فلا يوجد على وجه الأرض دينٌ حقٌّ سوى دين الإسلام؛ قال تعالى: {{Q:3:85}} (آل عمران:٨٥).

passages.heading: ناقش
passages.text: كيف ترد على من يزعم أن الإسلام دين خاص بالعرب؟

passages.heading: الشهادتان:
passages.text:
جعل الله عز وجل مفتاح الدخول في الإسلام النطق بالشهادتين، وهما:

- أشهد أن لا إله إلا الله.
- وأشهد أن محمدًا رسول الله.

passages.heading: أولاً: معنى شهادة ألا إله إلا الله
passages.text:
معنى (أشهد ألا إله إلا الله): أي أعتقد اعتقادًا جازمًا ألا معبود يستحق العبادة إلا الله وحده.

وقد تضمنت هذه الشهادة أمرين

| الأول | الثاني |
| :-: | :-: |
| نفي الإلهية عن غير الله تعالى | إثبات الإلهية لله وحده |

passages.heading: تمهيد
passages.text:
تراود البشر أسئلة تتعلق بوجود الإنسان، فيتساءلون عن حقيقة أمرهم، وعن مصدر مجيئهم، وسببه، وعن منتهى أمرهم.

وقد أجاب الإسلام عن هذه التساؤلات بإجابات شافية:

passages.heading: ناقش
passages.text: قارن بين نظرتك لمعنى وجودك قبل دخولك الإسلام وبعده:

passages.heading: إلى أين نذهب؟
passages.text:
بين القرآن الكريم أن كل إنسان سوف يموت في هذه الدنيا، وبموته تنتهي مرحلة العمل، وتبدأ مرحلة الحساب والجزاء، قال تعالى: {{Q:39:30-31}} (الزمر: ٣٠-٣١).

فإذا مات الإنسان انتقل إلى مرحلةٍ يسأل فيها عن دينه، ويجازى فيها على أعماله، قَالَ تَعَالَى: {{Q:3:185}} (آل عمران: ١٨٥).

فإذا جاء يوم القيامة، بعث الله تعالى الموتى من قبورهم للحساب والجزاء، ويجازى أهل الإيمان بالجنات، ويجازى أهل الكفر بالنيران، قال تعالى: {{Q:42:7}} (الشورى: ٧).

passages.heading: ناقش
passages.text: ما الوسائل المعينة على حفظ سورة الفاتحة؟

passages.heading: معنى السورة:
معنى السورة:
ثانيًا: معنى شهادة أن محمدًا رسول الله
passages.text: معنى (أشهد أن محمدًا رسول الله): أي أعتقد اعتقادًا جازمًا أن محمدًا ﷺ هو رسول الله، وأنه خاتم النبيين، فلا نبي بعده، وأن رسالته للناس جميعًا، قال سبحانه وتعالى: {{Q:25:1}} (الفرقان: ١).

passages.heading: لوازم الشهادتين:
passages.text:
لا يكفي النطق بالشهادتين فقط، بل لا بد من العمل بما يلزم منهما. فيلزم من شهادة (لا إله إلا الله) الكفر بجميع ما يعبد من دون الله تعالى، والإيمان بالله وحده ربًّا وإلهًا يستحق العبادة.

قال الله تعالى: {{Q:2:256}} (البقرة: ٢٥٦).

ويلزم من شهادة (محمد رسول الله): تصديقه فيما يخبر به، وطاعته فيما يأمر به أو ينهى عنه.

passages.heading: نعمة الهداية:
passages.text:
من عرف الحكمة من خلقه، والعاقبة التي تنتظر الناس يوم القيامة، أيقن أن أعظم نعمة ينعم الله بها على عباده هي نعمة الهداية إلى الدين الحق والعمل الصالح.

ولذلك أوجب الله عز وجل على عباده في صلاة أن يسألوه الهداية إلى الطريق المستقيم، الذي هو دين الإسلام، الموصل إلى رضوان الله تعالى.

passages.heading: فضل حسن الخلق:
passages.text:
- أخبر النبي ﷺ أن أكثر ما يدخل الناس الجنة: تقوى الله وحسن الخلق.
- وأخبر ﷺ أن أثقل ما يوضع في ميزان الإنسان يوم القيامة من الحسنات: حسن الخلق.
- وأخبر ﷺ أن أقرب المؤمنين منه منزلة يوم القيامة: أحسنهم أخلاقًا.

> يكون ذلك يوم القيامة حين يتم وزن حسنات الإنسان وسيئاته في ميزان مخصص لا يعلم أحدٌ هيئته ولا حجمه، فمن رجحت كفة حسناته دخل الجنة ومن رجحت كفة سيئاته دخل النار.

---

passages.heading: نعمة الهداية:
passages.text:
من عرف الحكمة من خلقه، والعاقبة التي تنتظر الناس يوم القيامة، أيقن أن أعظم نعمة ينعم الله بها على عباده هي نعمة الهداية إلى الدين الحق والعمل الصالح.

ولذلك أوجب الله عز وجل على عباده في صلاة أن يسألوه الهداية إلى الطريق المستقيم، الذي هو دين الإسلام، الموصل إلى رضوان الله تعالى.

passages.heading: إلى أين نذهب؟
passages.text:
بين القرآن الكريم أن كل إنسان سوف يموت في هذه الدنيا، وبموته تنتهي مرحلة العمل، وتبدأ مرحلة الحساب والجزاء، قال تعالى: {{Q:39:30-31}} (الزمر: ٣٠-٣١).

فإذا مات الإنسان انتقل إلى مرحلةٍ يسأل فيها عن دينه، ويجازى فيها على أعماله، قَالَ تَعَالَى: {{Q:3:185}} (آل عمران: ١٨٥).

فإذا جاء يوم القيامة، بعث الله تعالى الموتى من قبورهم للحساب والجزاء، ويجازى أهل الإيمان بالجنات، ويجازى أهل الكفر بالنيران، قال تعالى: {{Q:42:7}} (الشورى: ٧).

passages.heading: ناقش
passages.text: ما الآيات التي طالعتها قبل إسلامك؟ وكيف كان أثرها عليك؟

passages.heading: فضل قراءة القرآن:
passages.text:
- قال النبي ﷺ: «من قرأ حرفًا من كتاب الله فله به حسنة، والحسنة بعشر أمثالها، لا أقول: ﴿الم﴾ حرف، ولكن ألف حرف، ولام حرف، وميم حرف». أخرجه الترمذي في سننه (رقم 2910) بإسناد صحيح
- وقال النبي ﷺ: «اقرءوا القرآن، فإنه يأتي يوم القيامة شفيعًا لأصحابه». أخرجه مسلم في صحيحه (رقم 804)

passages.heading: الشرك بالله
passages.text:
3. **الإيمان بالكتب المنزلة:** فيؤمن العبد بأن الله أنزل إلى عباده من عنده كتبًا على رسله، أنزلها لهداية الناس، وتعليمهم أمور دينهم، ومنها أن الله تعالى قد أنزل التوراة على موسى بن عمران عليه السلام، والزبور على داود عليه السلام، والإنجيل على عيسى ابن مريم عليهما السلام، والقرآن على محمد ﷺ.
4. **الإيمان بالأنبياء عليهم السلام:** فيؤمن بأن الله تعالى أرسل رسلًا إلى أقوامهم وقد أيدهم بالمعجزات الدالة على صدقهم ؛ ليبشروا المؤمنين، وينذروا الكافرين. ويعلموا قومهم أمور دينهم، ويجب على من أرسلوا إليهم طاعتهم واتباعهم..
5. **الإيمان باليوم الآخر:** فيؤمن بيوم القيامة، وأن الله يبعث الموتى من قبورهم في ذلك اليوم، ويحاسبهم على أعمالهم، ويجازيهم عليها، فمنهم من يدخل الجنة، ومنهم من يدخل النار.
6. **الإيمان بالقدر:** فيؤمن العبد بأن كل ما يحدث في هذا الكون من خير أو شر هو بتقدير الله تعالى، وقد علمه الله تعالى، وكتبه في اللوح المحفوظ، وأنه لا يكون في هذا الكون إلا ما شاءه تعالى.

هو الكتاب الذي كتب الله فيه ما هو مقدر على الخلائق إلى قيام الساعة.

passages.heading: ما هو الإيمان؟
passages.text: الإيمان: هو تصديق القلب واللسان بما جاء من عند الله، وانقياد القلب له محبةً ورجاءً وخوفًا، وعمل الجوارح بذلك، قال الله تعالى: {{Q:4:136}} (النساء: ١٣٦).

passages.heading: ناقش
passages.text: كيف يمكن أن تكون أخلاق المسلم مع الآخرين؟ وهل لهذه الأخلاق أثر في حكمهم على الإسلام؟

passages.heading: مجالات الأخلاق في الإسلام:
passages.text:
الأخلاق في الإسلام ليس لها مجالٌ واحد فقط، بل لها مجالات متعددة، وهي:

- الأخلاق مع الله عز وجل؛ كتقوى الله والإخلاص له.
- الأخلاق مع النبي ﷺ؛ كمحبته واحترامه ونصرته بالنفس والمال.
- الأخلاق مع الشريعة، كالتسليم لأحكام الشرع وتوقيرها.
- الأخلاق مع النفس؛ كالصبر والحلم.
- الأخلاق مع الآخرين؛ كالصدق والأمانة.
- الأخلاق مع الحيوانات؛ كالرعاية وعدم ضربها وتعذيبها.
- الأخلاق مع البيئة؛ كالمحافظة عليها من الفساد، وغرس الأشجار، وعدم الإسراف في خيراتها.

passages.heading: ناقش
passages.text:
عمارة الأرض من الأدوار التي يقوم بها الإنسان في حياته، ولتمكينه من تحقيق هذه المهمة العظيمة فقد هيأ الله طبيعته لتكون قادرةً على أداء هذا الدور.. اشرح كيف يمكن للإنسان أن يعمر هذه الأرض دون سائر المخلوقات؟

اذكر بعض الآثار العملية المترتبة على معرفة مصير الخلق بعد الموت؟

passages.heading: ناقش
passages.text: قارن بين نظرتك لمعنى وجودك قبل دخولك الإسلام وبعده:

passages.heading: The Meaning of the Prayer
passages.text:
The prayer: It is a daily act of worship that consists of a set of words and actions with which a Muslim seeks to draw closer to his Lord, and it is performed five times a day and night.

The prayer is the second pillar of Islam.

passages.heading: The Conditions of the Prayer
passages.text:
- Purity: Once’s body and the place where the prayer is to be performed must be cleansed from physical impurities, and any ritual impurity must be removed with *wudoo’* or *ghusl*.
- Covering the intimate parts of the body (*‘awrah*): The word *‘awrah* refers to the parts of the body that must be covered in front of people. A man’s *‘awrah* that must be covered during the prayer extends from the navel to the knees; a woman’s *‘awrah* that must be covered during the prayer is her entire body except for the face and hands.
- Facing the *qiblah*: The *qiblah* is the direction of the Ka‘bah in Makkah. One must, therefore, pray in the direction of the Ka‘bah in Makkah.
- When its appointed time becomes due: The prayer will not be valid if it is performed before its time has started. It is not permissible to delay it beyond its due time, and it is best to perform it at the beginning of its time.

passages.heading: The Position of the Prayer in Islam
passages.text:
The prayer has a number of distinctive characteristics, including the following:

- It is the second pillar of Islam after the two testimonies of faith.
- It is the act of worship that must be performed under all circumstances, in times of war and peace, and whether one is sick or in good health.
- It is the act of worship that distinguishes a Muslim from a non-Muslim.

passages.heading: Good Moral Character in Islam
passages.text:
- Good moral character occupies a lofty position in Islam, as it is one of the important objectives of *Sharee‘ah* and one of the goals behind the Prophet’s mission.
- Good moral character is closely linked to faith, and the believers with complete faith are those who demonstrate the best moral character.
- A Muslim will be rewarded for his good manners, just as he will be rewarded for the prayer and fasting.

passages.heading: The Blessing of Right Guidance
passages.text: Whoever knows the purpose of his existence and the outcome that awaits people on the Day of Resurrection is bound to realise that the greatest blessing that Allah has ever bestowed upon people is that of guidance to the true religion and righteous deeds. Therefore, Allah Almighty has enjoined His servants to ask Him in their prayer to guide them to the straight path—the religion of Islam which leads to Allah’s good pleasure.

passages.heading: Some of the Ultimate Objectives and Benefits of the Prayer:
passages.text:
- It is the direct, special and personal communion a Muslim establishes with his Lord.
- It relieves the mind of worry and all worldly anxieties.
- It strengthens a Muslim’s willpower and determination.
- It refines morals and keeps those who observe it away from evil.

passages.heading: Introduction
passages.text: Islam is the religion with which Allah sent Muhammad ﷺ and is an extension of the same religion with which all the previous messengers came. It is essentially based on the belief that Allah Almighty is the only deity deserving of worship, who has no partners or assistants whatsoever in His kingdom, and who has no intermediaries between Him and His servants. But why should I embrace Islam? Is it a religion for all people or is it only for the Arabs? Who is its prophet, and is there another prophet who will come after him?

passages.heading: Introduction
passages.text: A Muslim often experiences peace and tranquillity when he reads or recites the Qur’an or worships Allah Almighty by engaging in prayer or any other act of worship. This good feeling which elevates some to higher levels of happiness and joy is one of the significant effects of faith that motivates Muslims to dedicate all their lives to Allah, comply with His commands cheerfully and out of love and avoid what He forbids in utter submission and obedience. In this lesson, we are going to learn about the concept of faith and its pillars and benefits.

passages.heading: Introduction
passages.text: The prayer is the greatest religious duty that a Muslim must learn and perform. Allah’s Messenger ﷺ has taught us how to perform it in the manner most pleasing to Allah Almighty. In this lesson, we are going to learn about the obligatory prayers, the position of the prayer in Islam, its conditions, and the correct manner of performing it.

passages.heading: Why Do We Pray?
passages.text: We pray because the prayer is an act of worship that Allah has enjoined on Muslims.

passages.heading: The Conditions of the Prayer

There are several conditions required to perform the prayer, which are:

passages.heading: The Five Obligatory Prayers
passages.text:
Allah Almighty has enjoined Muslims to perform five prayers throughout the day and night, namely:

| The Prayer | Beginning Time | Ending Time | Number of units (*rak‘ahs*) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| *Fajr* (Dawn) Prayer | at the break of dawn | sunrise | 2 |
| *Dhuhr* (Midday) Prayer | when the sun starts declining westward at midday after reaching its zenith | when the shadow of an object becomes equal in length to the object itself | 4 |
| *‘Asr* (Late Afternoon) Prayer | when the shadow of an object becomes equal in length to the object itself | sunset | 4 |

| *‘Ishaa’* (Late Evening) Prayer | when the red glow (evening twilight) on the western horizon disappears | midnight | 4 |

passages.heading: How Do We Pray?
passages.text: If a Muslim wants to pray, he must do the following:

passages.heading: *Tayammum* (Dry Ablution)
passages.text:
If a person who wants to perform *wudoo’* or *ghusl* is unable to do so due to illness, or when water is not readily available, or for any other legitimate reason, he may resort to dry ablution (*tayammum*) instead.

The Manner of Performing *Tayammum*: (1) Intend in his heart to perform *tayammum* and strike both hands slightly on pure earth once, (2) wipe the face with them, (3) wipe the back of the right hand with the palm of the left, and then the back of the left hand with the palm of the right hand.

passages.heading: What shall I do if I find water after having performed *tayammum*?
passages.text: If a Muslim finds water or can use it, his purity becomes invalid, in which case he must perform *wudoo’* or *ghusl*.

passages.heading: Wiping over the Socks
passages.text: If a person wants to perform *wudoo’* while he has his socks on, he is allowed to just wipe over the top of them with wet hands, and there is no need to take them off and wash the feet. Three conditions are required for this:

passages.heading: How Do We Pray?
passages.text:
1. He intends in his heart to pray.
2. He stands facing the *qiblah*, raises his hands up to the level of the shoulders or ears, and says, “*Allaahu akbar* Allah is the Greatest.”
3. He places his right hand on his left hand. Then he recites one of the opening supplications, such as, Subhaanak-Allaahumma wa bi hamdika, wa tabaarak-asmuka, wa ta’aalaa jadduka, wa laa ilaaha ghayruka “Glory be to You, O Allah; Yours is the praise, blessed is Your name, exalted is Your majesty, and there is no god besides You.” Then he says, A’oodhu billaahi min-ash-shaytaan-ir-rajeem. Bismillaah-ir-rahmaan-ir-raheem “I seek Allah’s protection from Satan, who has been expelled from His mercy. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.” Then he recites *Soorat Al-Faatihah* and says after it, “*Aameen*”, which means “Answer our supplications, O Allah”. After that, he recites whatever number of verses of the Qur’an as is easy for him, even if it is one verse.
4. He says, “Allaahu akbar Allah is the Greatest” while raising his hands up to the level of his shoulders or ears, and bows down, lowering his head and back and keeping them straight at a right angle, placing the palms of his hands on the knees. He says three times while in this position, “Subhaana rabbiy-al-’adheem Glory be to my Lord, the Almighty.”

passages.heading: Certain Rulings on Purification
passages.text:
- It is a general Islamic rule that things are naturally clean and pure unless stated otherwise by Islam.
- It would suffice to cleanse the body or clothing of impurities by removing them with water or any cleaning substance that would serve the purpose.
- It would be better for a person who uses the toilet to cleanse the place of urine and faeces with water. It is also permissible for him to cleanse himself with tissues or any other material that serves to remove impurity.

5. He resumes the standing position, raising his hands up to the level of the shoulders or the ears, saying: Sami’allaahu li man hamidah “Allah hears those who praise Him.” Then he says while standing: Rabbanaa wa lakal-hamd “Our Lord, to You is due all praise.”

6. He says, Allaahu akbar “Allah is the Greatest” and prostrates himself, with the toes of both feet, the knees, the palms of the hands and the forehead and the nose touching the floor. He says three times while in this position, “Glory be to my Lord, Most High.”

passages.heading: Things That Render *Wudoo’* Invalid
passages.text:
*Wudoo’* becomes invalid as a result of four things:

- Natural discharges from the private parts (both the external genital and excretory organs), such as urine, excrement, wind, semen and the clear, colourless, viscous fluid that is emitted during sexual arousal
- Loss of consciousness due to sleep or intoxication
- Lustfully touching the private parts with bare hands
- Eating camel meat

passages.heading: The Meaning of Worship
passages.text: By worship is meant everything that Allah has enjoined on us for us to draw closer to Him. It comprises all words and deeds that Allah loves, whether they are outward like the physical acts of worship, such as the prayer and pilgrimage, or inward, like the acts of worship involving the heart, such as love of Allah, fearing His punishment and hoping for His mercy. A person can transform everyday habits into acts of worship simply by having a good intention. If, for instance, he eats, drinks and sleeps with the intention of gaining enough strength to worship Allah better, he will certainly be rewarded for doing so

passages.heading: Things That a Person Who Is in a State of *Jannabah* Must Not Do
passages.text:
The state into which a person gets following intercourse or ejaculation and because of which he must perform *ghusl* is called *janaabah*, and he is described as *junub*. In this case, he is not allowed to do the following:

1. perform the prayer
2. circumambulate the Ka’bah (*tawaaf*)
3. touch or carry the Qur’an
4. stay in the mosque
5. read the Qur’an

passages.heading: Types of Purification
passages.text:
Purification falls into two types:

**Physical Purification**

This means the removal of impurities and the cleansing of the area affected by them

**Moral Purification**

This means the removal of those things that prevent one from performing the prayer, by washing certain parts of the body or the entire body.

Physical purification may be undertaken either by *wudoo’* or *ghusl*

*Wudoo’* (partial ablutions): the ritual washing of certain parts of the body with water

*Ghusl* (full ablutions/bath): the ritual washing of the entire body with water.

Purification must be undertaken with pure water, such as seawater, river water, well water, or any other water that has not been mixed with impurity.

Jejum significa abster-se de comer, beber e manter relações sexuais do nascer até o pôr do sol.

passages.text:
1. Ele evoca em seu coração a intenção da oração.
2. Ele se vira em direção a Qiblah, levanta as palmas das mãos ao lado de seus ombros ou orelhas e diz: “ALLAH é O Maior”.
3. Ele coloca a mão direita sobre a mão esquerda. Em seguida, ele recita uma das súplicas iniciais, como: “Glorificado sejas, ó Allah, o louvor é para Ti. Abençoado seja Teu nome, Altíssimo é sua Glória, e não há divindade real além de Ti”. Em seguida diz: Busco refugio a Allah contra o Satanás o malvado,” “Em nome de Allah, o Misericordioso, o Misericordiador. Em seguida recita Surat Al-Fatihah, então diz: “Amin” quando terminar de ler, e o significado de Amin: Ó Allah, responda nossa súplica. Então, depois de Al-Fatihah, ele recita o que ele memorizou do Sagrado Alcorão, mesmo que seja um versículo.
4. Ele levanta as mãos ao lado dos ombros ou orelhas e diz: “ALLAH é O Maior.” Ele dobra as costas fazendo ruku, coloca as mãos nos joelhos e coloca as costas e a cabeça no mesmo nível. Enquanto se curva, ele diz: “Glória ao meu Senhor, o Grande” três vezes.

passages.heading: Tipos de purificações:
passages.text:
A purificação subdivide-se em dois tipos:

**Pureza física**  
E é remover as impurezas e limpar seu lugar.

**Pureza moral**  
Pretende-se com isso remover os motivos que impedem a oração, e isso é lavando partes do corpo, ou lavando tudo.

A purificação sensorial é feita por ablução ou ghusl

- **Ghusl:** significa lavar todo o corpo com água

passages.heading: Prefácio
passages.text: Um dos momentos mais inesquecíveis para um novo muçulmano é o momento de anunciar sua entrada no Islam, pronunciando os dois testemunhos. Pois nesse momento ele deu seus primeiros passos para conhecer a verdade e aderir a ela. Nesta lição, aprenderemos sobre os dois testemunhos e seu significado e requisitos para um muçulmano.

passages.heading: Significado de “Testemunho que não há divindade além Allah:
passages.text:
Significado do (testemunho que não há deus além de ALLAH): ou seja, acredito firmemente que não há divindade digna de adoração, exceto ALLAH.

E este testemunho contém duas coisas:

| Primeiro | Segundo |
| :--- | :--- |
| Rejeição de existência de outra divindade além de ALLAH | Afirmação de existência de ALLAH exclusivamente |

passages.heading: A Terceira lição
passages.text:
### Como abraço o Islam ?

A essência da religião Islâmica, que é a religião de todos os profetas: a adoração somente a ALLAH e a descrença em tudo o que é adorado além Dele. ALLAH disse: {{Q:21:25}} [Al-Anbiyá: 25]

Não é permitido, sob nenhuma circunstância, acreditar na divindade de qualquer coisa que não seja ALLAH Todo-Poderoso, e não é permitido aproximar-se de ninguém além de ALLAH Todo-Poderoso em qualquer forma de adoração.

passages.heading: O significado de (Testemunho que Muhammad é Mensageiro de Allah):
passages.text: O significado de (testemunho que Muhammad é o Mensageiro de ALLAH): isto é, acredito firmemente que Muhammad, que a paz e bênçãos de ALLAH estejam com ele, é o Mensageiro de ALLAH, e que ele é o selo dos profetas, então não há profeta após ele, e que sua mensagem é para todas as pessoas. O Todo-Poderoso disse: {{Q:25:1}} Al-Furqan: 1

passages.heading: Por que jejuamos?
passages.text: Um muçulmano jejua em obediência a ALLAH Todo-Poderoso e em resposta ao Seu comando.

passages.heading: Das decisões sobre o Jejum e suas vantagens:
passages.text:
- Alcançar a piedade aumentando a adoração e reduzindo os pecados.
- Sentir a dor da fome que aflige os pobres e necessitados.
- Libertar-se de suas luxúrias e treinar para controlá-las e regular.

ALLAH impôs a adoração do jejum aos muçulmanos e a outras nações anteriores, como disse o Todo-Poderoso: {{Q:2:183}} Al-Baqarah:183

passages.heading: As anulações do jejum:
passages.text:
O jejuador deve abster-se de uma série de coisas, se as fizer, invalidará seu jejum, que são:

1. Comer e beber, inclusive tomar injeções intravenosas.
2. Ejacular sêmen deliberadamente, seja durante a relação sexual ou sem relação sexual, e a relação sexual durante o dia no Ramadan é um pecado grave.
3. Vomitar intencionalmente.

Quanto a uma mulher, seu jejum também é invalidado quando:
4. Saída do sangue menstrual ou pós-parto

passages.heading: O que é Alcorão?
passages.text: O Nobre Alcorão é a palavra de ALLAH Todo-Poderoso que Ele revelou ao Seu Mensageiro, Muhammad, que a paz esteja com ele, e é o último dos livros revelados por ALLAH, e não há outro livro depois dele.

passages.heading: O Alcorão é um alimento para a alma e a mente.
passages.text:
O Alcorão Sagrado se dirige às mentes e almas dos seres humanos da mesma forma que Ele se dirige à mente através de:

- Raciocínio mental sobre as questões, o Todo-Poderoso disse: {{Q:21:22}} Al-Anbiya: 22
- O convite para a realização da razão e reflexão sobre as evidências e provas, o Todo-Poderoso disse: {{Q:2:219}} Al-Baqarah: 219
- Ele censura aqueles que não fazem suas mentes funcionarem e não refletem sobre elas.O Todo-Poderoso disse: {{Q:25:44}} [Al-Furqan:44]

Ele aborda suas almas e emoções através de:

- Expressando sentimentos emocionais, destacando-os e retratando-os em muitos casos, o Todo-Poderoso disse: {{Q:2:165}} [Al-Baqarah:165]
- Um lembrete das emoções humanas e uma explicação de seus efeitos bons e ruins. O Todo-Poderoso disse: {{Q:5:82}} Al-Máidah: 82
- A ordem da bondade e gentileza no convite, o Altíssimo disse: {{Q:16:125}} An-Nahl:125
- Inclui nos versículos das decisões os significados da fé, o Todo-Poderoso disse: {{Q:4:94}} An-Nissa: 94
- O uso de palavras que afetam a alma e evocam emoções sinceras. O Todo-Poderoso disse: {{Q:24:22}} An-Noor: 22

passages.heading: O Alcorão é um alimento para a alma e a mente.
passages.text: Ele pode combinar os dois discursos: o mental e o espiritual em um verso, que discute a mente e a convence, e desperta a emoção ao mesmo tempo. O Todo-Poderoso disse: {{Q:35:3}} [Fatir: 3]

passages.text: Se um muçulmano quiser realizar a oração, ele deve fazer o seguinte:

passages.text:
### A oração

5. Ele levanta a cabeça para voltar a ficar de pé com as mãos levantadas junto aos ombros e diz: “ALLAH ouve aqueles que o louvam”. Então ele diz em pé: “Nosso Senhor, para Ti seja o louvor”.

6. Ele cai prostrado, depois coloca a testa e o nariz no chão, com as palmas das mãos, joelhos e pontas dos pés no chão, e diz: “Glória ao meu Senhor, o Altíssimo” três vezes.

7. Ele levanta a cabeça dizendo: “ALLAH é O Maior” e se senta sobre o pé esquerdo, com o pé direito ainda ereto, e coloca as palmas das mãos sobre as coxas, e diz sentado: “Senhor, perdoa-me”.

passages.heading: Sexta lição
passages.text:
11. Ele se vira para a direita e diz: “A paz e a misericórdia de ALLAH esteja convosco.” Então ele se vira para a esquerda e diz o mesmo. Assim termina sua oração.

Esta característica é se sua oração for de duas rak’ahs. como Fajr e sexta-feira, mas se for três rak’ahs; como Maghrib, ou quatro rak’ahs; Como Zuhr, Asr e Isha, depois de completar o primeiro tashahhud, ele completa as rak’ahs restantes como na primeira rak’ah, exceto que ele não recita nada depois de al-Fatihah, então se senta como sentou após a segunda rak’ah, e diz o primeiro tashahhud, então a oração abraâmica, e então dá as saudações.

passages.heading: Oração de Sexta-Feira (al-jumah)
passages.text:
- ALLAH Todo-Poderoso ordenou aos muçulmanos que fizessem uma oração especial na sexta-feira chamada (oração de sexta-feira), e tem um caráter especial e condições especiais, e é uma alternativa à oração do meio-dia para esse dia.
- Os muçulmanos se reúnem para isso na mesquita, então o pregador da mesquita faz dois sermões para eles, então reza com eles duas unidades de oração, nas quais ele recita o Alcorão em voz alta.
- Prescreve-se tomar banho para assistir à oração de sexta-feira e comparecer cedo. Não é permitido ausentar-se dela exceto por uma desculpa, e quem não o fizer deve fazer a oração do meio-dia quatro unidades de oração, durante as quais a recitação do Alcorão não é em voz alta.
- A oração de sexta-feira não é obrigatório para a mulher ou o viajante.

passages.heading: ¿Qué tengo que hacer al encontrar agua después de haber realizado la ablución seca (tayamum)?
passages.text: Cuando el musulmán encuentra agua o es capaz de usarla sin causarle daño, en este caso se anula su ablución seca y debe realizar la ablución menor o mayor con agua.

passages.heading: La manera de realizar la ablución mayor completa:
passages.text:
Si el musulmán quiere realizar la ablución mayor debe hacer los pasos siguientes:

1. Realizar la intención con su corazón (sin pronunciarla) y lavarse la parte íntima con agua.
2. Realizar la ablución menor conocida.
3. Lavar todo su cuerpo con agua.

passages.heading: Los tipos de purificación
passages.text:
La purificación se divide en dos tipos:

* **Purificación corporal**
  Es quitar la impureza y limpiar su sitio.

* **la purificación del lugar**
  Se quiere decir por esto, la eliminación de todo lo que impide la oración, y esto se realiza con el lavado de algunas partes del cuerpo o con el lavado de todo el cuerpo.

La purificación corporal se realiza mediante la ablución menor o mayor.

* Se quiere decir por ablución menor (wudu): lavarse algunas partes del cuerpo con agua.

* Se quiere decir por ablución mayor (ghusl): lavarse todo el cuerpo con agua.

para la purificación se usa agua pura tal como el agua del mar, de los ríos, de los pozos, entre otros tipos de aguas que no sean impuras.

passages.heading: ¿Cómo realizar la ablución menor (wudu)?
passages.text:
1. Debe tener la intención de la ablución menor en su corazón y decir: ““En el nombre de Al-láh””.
2. Lavarse las manos con agua empezando por la derecha.
3. Limpiar la boca enjuagándola con agua y echándola, a lo que se le llama el enjuague.
4. . Limpiar la nariz poniendo agua con la inhalación, y luego sacarla de la nariz.
5. Lavarse toda la cara, su límite verticalmente es desde el inicio del cabello encima de la frente hasta el fin de la barba incluido el pelo de la barba si existe, y horizontalmente entre las dos orejas.
6. Lavarse las manos desde las puntas de sus dedos hasta los codos, empezando con la mano derecha.
7. Con las manos mojadas, pasarlas sobre la cabeza empezando por el inicio de la cabeza hasta la nuca, luego regresar con sus manos al inicio de la cabeza.
8. Pasar los dedos mojados sobre sus orejas limpiando cada una con el índice por dentro, y con el pulgar por detrás.
9. Lavarse los pies hasta los tobillos empezando por el pie derecho.

passages.heading: El significado del wudu (la ablución menor):
passages.text: La ablución menor (wudu’): lavarse la cara, las manos, los pies y pasar las manos mojadas sobre la cabeza con un modo específico.

passages.heading: Normas relacionadas con la purificación:
passages.text:
- Los objetos en su origen son puros, y se considera impuro solo lo clasificado por las normas religiosas como tal.
- Es suficiente purificar el cuerpo o la vestimenta quitando las impurezas con agua o con algo que purifica.
- Al entrar al cuarto de baño para orinar o defecar, es preferible limpiar el sitio de la orina o de los heces con agua, y es permitido también quitar la suciedad y purificar el sitio con un papel higiénico u otro objeto que quite las impurezas.

passages.heading: ¿Cómo realizar la ablución mayor (Ghusl)?
passages.text:
Al realizar la ablución mayor (ghusl) debe lavarse todo el cuerpo con agua, además de realizar el enjuague y la inhalación, y de este modo el musulmán habrá realizado la purificación mayor.

Al Hadaz Al Akbar: es lo que exige una purificación mayor y no se quita con solo realizar la ablución menor (wudu), y es de tres tipos:

1. Al Yanaba (estado de impureza mayor): es un estado que acompaña el coito o la eyaculación con deseo aunque no se haya dado el coito.
2. La menstruación: es la sangre que sale mensualmente de la mujer.
3. El postparto: es la sangre que sale de la mujer después del parto.

passages.heading: Preámbulo
passages.text: La ablución menor (wudu’) tiene una gran importancia en islam ya que está relacionada con un pilar fundamental que es la oración, desde entonces el musulmán debe aprender a realizarla correctamente, y en esta lección vamos a estudiar el significado de la ablución menor, lo que exige y lo que anula la ablución menor y cómo se realiza de la manera correcta.

passages.heading: Taiámmum (ablución seca):
passages.text: Cuando la persona que debe realizar la ablución menor o mayor es incapaz de realizarlas por la falta de agua, o por una enfermedad u otra causa, en este caso es permitido para él realizar la ablución seca (tayamum). La forma de realizarla es tener la intención en el corazón (sin pronunciarla), tocar con sus dos manos el suelo una sola vez, luego pasar sus manos sobre su cara, luego sus manos.

passages.heading: ¿Cuándo es obligatoria la ablución mayor (ghusl)?
passages.text:
El musulmán debe realizar la ablución mayor (ghusl) en tres casos:

- **El primero:** la eyaculación con deseo, sea si eyacula estando despierto o dormido.
- **El segundo:** el coito, si hay eyaculación o no.
- **Tercero:** la sangre de la menstruación o el postparto de la mujer, y cuando se termina debe realizar la ablución mayor.

passages.heading: A discutir
passages.text: ¿Qué indica la purificación mayor para salir del Hadaz Al Akbar (estado de impureza mayor)?

passages.heading: Lo prohibido en el estado de impureza mayor:
passages.text:
El estado de la persona que necesita realizar la ablución mayor por el coito o por la eyaculación se llama (Yanaba) y a la persona se le llama (Yunub) y en este estado lo está prohibido lo siguiente:

1. La oración.
2. La circunvalación alrededor del Kaaba.
3. Tocar o llevar el Libro del Corán.
4. Quedarse en la mezquita.
5. La recitación del Noble Corán.

passages.heading: A discutir
passages.text: ¿Qué significa insistir sobre la necesidad de la purificación del musulmán y su higiene personal?

passages.heading: ¿Cómo realizar la ablución menor (wudu)?
passages.text: Si el musulmán quiere realizar la ablución menor debe realizar los pasos siguientes:

passages.heading: La cantidad de veces del lavado de los miembros de la ablución menor:
passages.text: La sunna en la ablución menor (wudu) es lavarse cada órgano o parte tres veces salvo la cabeza y las orejas una sola vez, pero también es suficiente lavarlas una sola vez con la condición de lavarse el órgano por completo.

passages.heading: Lo que invalida el wudú:
passages.text:
La ablución menor se invalida por cuatro acciones:

■ La salida de uno de los siguientes: los gases, la orina, los heces, el semen, o la humedad que acompaña la excitación sexual.

■ La pérdida de la razón con un sueño o con las sustancias embriagantes.

■ Tocar directamente la parte íntima con deseo sexual.

■ Comer carne de camello.

passages.heading: Los actos que exigen la ablución menor:
passages.text:
Lo que exige la ablución menor son los actos que al realizarlos se debe estar puros y no se puede realizarlos sino al purificarse, y son:

Al Hadaz: es un estado moral del hombre que impide la realización de la oración antes de purificarse y no es algo tangible como las inmundicias, y es de dos tipos: uno exige la ablución menor (wudu) y el otro exige la ablución mayor (ghusl).

1. La oración.
2. La circunvalación alrededor de la Kaaba.
3. Al tocar el Libro del Corán.

passages.heading: Important Notes Related to Fasting
passages.text:
- Whoever breaks his fast in Ramadaan for a legitimate reason must make up for every day he has missed after than Ramadaan.
- If a sick person breaks the fast because of an incurable disease, he is exempt from fasting the month of Ramadaan, but he must feed one poor person for each day he does not fast.
- If a Muslim cannot possibly fast due to old age, he is exempt from fasting the month of Ramadaan but he must feed one poor person for each day he does not fast.

**Muslims break their fast as soon as the call to *Maghrib* (sunset) prayer is announced, and many Muslims are very keen to share their Ramadaan breakfast, or *iftar*, with fellow Muslims.**

passages.heading: Things that render the Fast Invalid
passages.text:
The fasting person must abstain from several things which, if he does them, his fast will be invalid. They are:

1. Eating and drinking, including intravenous injections which have some nutritional value.
2. Deliberate seminal emission as a result of intercourse or any other means. Intercourse during the day in Ramadaan is a grave sin.
3. Deliberate vomiting.

A woman’s fast is broken as a result of:

4. Menstrual or postnatal bleeding.

passages.heading: The Manner of Performing *Wudoo’*
passages.text:
1. He intends in his heart to perform *wudoo’* and says, *bismillaah* “In the name of Allah”.
2. He washes his hands up to the wrists with water.
3. He rinses out his mouth thoroughly by moving water around in the mouth and then spitting it out. This process is called *madmadah*) in Arabic.
4. He cleans his nose by sniffing water into the nostrils and ejecting it out by blowing his nose.
5. He washes his face thoroughly from the hairline at the top of the forehead to the bottom of the chin, along with the beard, if he is bearded, and from ear to ear.
6. He washes his hands from the fingertips up to the elbow, starting with his right hand.
7. With wet hands, and starting with his hands flat on the top of the head near the hairline, he wipes it to the back of the neck and back to the front.
8. With wet fingers, he wipes  
He wipes the inner sides of the ears with his index fingers and behind them with his thumbs.
9. He washes his feet up to the ankles, which are the two prominent bones of the joint connecting the foot to the leg, starting with his right foot.

A Muslim woman must cover her entire body from:
- A- other women
- B- men who are not related to her
- C- her father-in-law

If a menstruating woman or a woman experiencing post-natal bleeding becomes clean and the bleeding stops, she must make up for
- A- the prayer
- B- the fasting days she has missed
- C- all the above

passages.heading: How to Perform *Ghusl*?
passages.text:
To perform *ghusl*, one must wash the entire body with water, rinse out one’s mouth and clean one’s nose by sniffing water into the nostrils and ejecting it out by blowing one’s nose. A Muslim removes the major ritual impurity by simply doing so.

> The major ritual impurity: what must be removed by ghusl, and ablution is not sufficient, and these are types:
> 
> 1- *Janaabah*: The state of ritual impurity following intercourse or ejaculation as a result of an orgasm even if no intercourse takes place.
> 2- Menstruation: the normal vaginal bleeding that occurs as part of a woman’s monthly cycle.
> 3- Postnatal bleeding: The vaginal bleeding that takes place following childbirth.

passages.heading: 2 Islam Wipes out the Sins Committed before It
passages.text: If a person sincerely embraces Islam, the Most Gracious and the Most Merciful God will forgive him all his past sins, and this is one of the outstanding merits of Islam. The Almighty says to His Prophet ﷺ, {{Q:8:38}} (Soorat Al-Anfaal, 8:38). A man once showed interest in Islam, and so he went to the Prophet ﷺ but he stipulated that Allah should forgive him his past sins. The Prophet ﷺ gave him the good news, saying, “Don’t you know that Islam wipes out all the sins committed before it?” (Reported by Muslim; No. 121).

passages.heading: The Types of People Who Are Exempt from Fasting
passages.text:
Allah Almighty has permitted several types of people to break their fast during the day in Ramadaan. They are:

1. Sick people whose medical condition is bound to be further worsened by fasting.
2. The elderly who are unable to fast.
3. Travellers, while moving from one place to another.
4. Menstruating women and women experiencing postnatal bleeding.
5. Pregnant and nursing mothers if they fear it would be dangerous for them or for their babies if they fast.

passages.heading: Some of the Ultimate Objectives and Benefits of Fasting
passages.text:
- To attain true piety by increasing acts of worship and avoiding sins as much as possible.
- To experience the pangs of hunger from which the poor and needy often suffer.
- To train oneself to bring one’s whims and desires under control.

Allah has enjoined fasting on Muslims, just as He prescribed it on the other nations before them:
{{Q:2:183}} (Soorat Al-Baqarah, 2:183).

passages.heading: The Blessed Month of Ramadaan
passages.text:
Ramadaan is the ninth month of the Islamic lunar calendar. It is a blessed month, in which Allah revealed the Qur’an to His Messenger, Muhammad ﷺ. Allah has promised to forgive all the past sins of those who fast during the daylight hours and stands in prayer at night throughout this month. The Almighty has also distinguished it with a night that is better than a thousand months. It is called *Laylat-ul-Qadr* (The Night of Decree; also called the Night of Power), and whoever spends it remembering Allah and standing in prayer will have all his past sins forgiven.

Muslims perform the *Taraaweeh* prayer in the month of Ramadaan. It is one of the Prophet’s practices (*Sunnah*) that is particularly associated with it, and it is performed after *'Ishaa’* (late evening) prayer.

passages.heading: The Manner of Performing *Wudoo’*
passages.text: If a Muslim wants to perform his ablutions (*wudoo’*), he must do the following:

passages.heading: How Many Times Do We Wash the Parts of the Body that Are Usually Washed in *Wudoo’*?
passages.text: According to the *Sunnah*, each part of the body is washed three times, except in the case of the head and ears, which are wiped only once. It would suffice, however, to wash these body parts once provided that they are washed thoroughly.

passages.heading: Things That Render *Wudoo’* Invalid
passages.text:
*Wudoo’* becomes invalid as a result of four things:

- Natural discharges from the private parts (both the external genital and excretory organs), such as urine, excrement, wind, semen and the clear, colourless, viscous fluid that is emitted during sexual arousal
- Loss of consciousness due to sleep or intoxication
- Lustfully touching the private parts with bare hands
- Eating camel meat

passages.heading: The Meaning of *Ghusl*
passages.text: *Ghusl*: Washing the entire body with water to remove the major ritual impurity.

passages.heading: Lesson 4
passages.text: ## Ghusl (Full Ablutions/Bath)

passages.heading: The Manner of Performing the Full Ritual Bath (*Ghusl*)
passages.text:
If a Muslim wants to perform *ghusl*, he must do the following:

1. He intends in his heart to perform *ghusl* and washes out his private parts with water.
2. He performs *wudoo’* like the one he performs before the prayer.
3. He washes his entire body with water.

passages.heading: Conditions for Acts of Worship to Be Accepted
passages.text:
For an act of worship to be accepted, two conditions must be fulfilled:

The first condition: It has to be done sincerely for the sake of Allah to draw closer to alone, without showing off.

The second condition: It has to be done in the manner Allah has enjoined it and exactly as it was performed by the Prophet ﷺ.

> *Aririyyaa’* (showing off) is the act of doing an act of worship only to be seen and praised by people for doing it.

passages.heading: Forbidden financial transactions
passages.text: *Riba* (usury, interest) is one of the financial transactions that Islam strictly forbids because of the harm it involves. It is also one of the major sins, and Allah warns those who engage in it of a severe punishment.

passages.heading: The Criterion of Superiority in Islam
passages.text:
Piety is the criterion whereby Allah grants superiority to some over others. Superiority among Muslims can only be attained through strong faith, not one’s appearance, lineage, colour, or wealth. Allah Almighty says, {{Q:49:13}} (Soorat Al-Hjuraat, 49:13).

The Prophet ﷺ said: “O people! Your Lord is one and your father [Adam] is one. An Arab has no superiority over a non-Arab, nor does a non-Arab have any superiority over an Arab; a white person has no superiority over a black person, nor does a black person have any superiority over a white person except in piety.” (Reported by Al-Bayhaqee in Shu’ab al-Eemaan; No. 4774).

passages.text:

passages.heading: Conditions for Acts of Worship to Be Accepted
passages.text:
For an act of worship to be accepted, two conditions must be fulfilled:

The first condition: It has to be done sincerely for the sake of Allah to draw closer to alone, without showing off.

The second condition: It has to be done in the manner Allah has enjoined it and exactly as it was performed by the Prophet ﷺ.

> *Aririyyaa’* (showing off) is the act of doing an act of worship only to be seen and praised by people for doing it.

passages.heading: The Pillars of Faith
passages.text:
The Muslim faith rests on six pillars, namely:

1. **Belief in Allah:** A Muslim believes that Allah Almighty exists and believes in His names and attributes. He equally believes that He is the Lord and sole Creator of this vast universe, to whom belongs everything in it, who manages all its affairs and provides sustenance to all His creation, that there is no god is worthy of worship besides or instead of Him and that He has perfect attributes.
2. **Belief in the angels:** A Muslim believes that the honourable angels exist, that it is Allah Almighty who created them and that they worship Him, execute His commands and never disobey Him. He also believes in their attributes and duties which are mentioned in the Book and the *Sunnah*.

passages.heading: Shirk
passages.text:
3. **Belief in the divinely revealed books:** A Muslim believes that Allah sent down divine books to His Messengers to guide people to the truth and teach them their religion. These include the Torah (*At-Tawraah*) which He revealed to Moses (Moosaa) son of ‘Imraan, the Zaboor which He revealed to David (Daawood), the Gospel (*Al-Injeel*) which He revealed to Jesus (‘Eesaa) son of Mary and the Qur’an which He revealed to Muhammad, peace be upon them all. He also believes that the Qur’an is the last of them and that it has final authority over them all.
4. **Belief in the prophets:** A Muslim believes that Allah Almighty sent messengers to their people and supported them with miracles to prove their truthfulness. He sent them to give the believers good news of reward, warn the unbelievers of punishment and teach their people their religion. Those to whom they were sent must obey and follow them. Muhammad ﷺ was the final prophet whom He sent to all mankind.
5. **Belief in the Last Day:** A Muslim believes in Resurrection Day. He believes that Allah will raise the dead from their graves on that day and judge and repay them according to their deeds. Some will enter Paradise while others will enter Hell.
6. **Belief in the divine decree:** A Muslim believes that everything in this universe, whether good or evil, happens according to Allah’s decree, that He foreknows all events which He has already written in the Preserved Tablet, and that everything in this universe happens according to His will.
