passages.heading: The Position of the Prayer in Islam
passages.text:
The prayer has a number of distinctive characteristics, including the following:

- It is the second pillar of Islam after the two testimonies of faith.
- It is the act of worship that must be performed under all circumstances, in times of war and peace, and whether one is sick or in good health.

passages.heading: Some of the Ultimate Objectives and Benefits of the Prayer:
passages.text:
- It is the direct, special and personal communion a Muslim establishes with his Lord.
- It relieves the mind of worry and all worldly anxieties.
- It strengthens a Muslim’s willpower and determination.
- It refines morals and keeps those who observe it away from evil.

To perform the prayer, several conditions must be met:
There are several conditions required to perform the prayer, which are:

passages.heading: The Conditions of the Prayer
passages.text:
- Purity: Once’s body and the place where the prayer is to be performed must be cleansed from physical impurities, and any ritual impurity must be removed with *wudoo’* or *ghusl*.
- Covering the intimate parts of the body (*‘awrah*): The word *‘awrah* refers to the parts of the body that must be covered in front of people. A man’s *‘awrah* that must be covered during the prayer extends from the navel to the knees; a woman’s *‘awrah* that must be covered during the prayer is her entire body except for the face and hands.
- Facing the *qiblah*: The *qiblah* is the direction of the Ka‘bah in Makkah. One must, therefore, pray in the direction of the Ka‘bah in Makkah.
- When its appointed time becomes due: The prayer will not be valid if it is performed before its time has started. It is not permissible to delay it beyond its due time, and it is best to perform it at the beginning of its time.

Thus, followers of every prophet had their respective laws and regulations, but the set of beliefs to which prophets called their people was the same. Then Allah sent the last prophet and messenger, Muhammad ﷺ, with the final divine laws, and thus the only religion acceptable to Allah is Islam.

5. Islam is in perfect harmony with the innate human nature (*fitrah*), beginning with the greatest value it embraces, namely the declaration of Allah’s unity, and ending with the rules of etiquette it teaches its adherents to enable them to attain great perfection in moral excellence.

passages.heading: Types of Purification
passages.text:
Purification falls into two types:

**Physical Purification**

This means the removal of impurities and the cleansing of the area affected by them

**Moral Purification**

This means the removal of those things that prevent one from performing the prayer, by washing certain parts of the body or the entire body.

Physical purification may be undertaken either by *wudoo’* or *ghusl*

*Wudoo’* (partial ablutions): the ritual washing of certain parts of the body with water

*Ghusl* (full ablutions/bath): the ritual washing of the entire body with water.

Purification must be undertaken with pure water, such as seawater, river water, well water, or any other water that has not been mixed with impurity.

1. He intends in his heart to pray.

3. He places his right hand on his left hand. Bismillaah-ir-rahmaan-ir-raheem “I seek Allah’s protection from Satan, who has been expelled from His mercy. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.” Then he recites *Soorat Al-Faatihah* and says after it, “*Aameen*”, which means “Answer our supplications, O Allah”. After that, he recites whatever number of verses of the Qur’an as is easy for him, even if it is one verse.

He says, “Allaahu akbar Allah is the Greatest” while raising his hands up to the level of his shoulders or ears, and bows down, lowering his head and back and keeping them straight at a right angle, placing the palms of his hands on the knees. passages.text:
It is permissible to eat dead aquatic animals that can live only in water, such as fish and prawns, whether they live in the sea, rivers or lakes.

It is permissible to hunt wild, nonpredatory animals and consume their flesh provided that the name of Allah is mentioned before the hunting weapon is discharged, and the hunted game must be slaughtered if found still alive.

passages.heading: The Five Obligatory Prayers
passages.text:
Allah Almighty has enjoined Muslims to perform five prayers throughout the day and night, namely:

| The Prayer | Beginning Time | Ending Time | Number of units (*rak‘ahs*) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |

passages.heading: The Position of the Prayer in Islam
passages.text:
The prayer has a number of distinctive characteristics, including the following:

- It is the second pillar of Islam after the two testimonies of faith.
- It is the act of worship that must be performed under all circumstances, in times of war and peace, and whether one is sick or in good health.
- It is the act of worship that distinguishes a Muslim from a non-Muslim.

passages.heading: Some of the Ultimate Objectives and Benefits of the Prayer:
passages.text:
- It is the direct, special and personal communion a Muslim establishes with his Lord.
- It relieves the mind of worry and all worldly anxieties.
- It strengthens a Muslim’s willpower and determination.
- It refines morals and keeps those who observe it away from evil.

passages.heading: Pendahuluan
passages.text: Seorang Muslim memandang makanan dan minuman sebagai bagian dari nikmat Allah yang menuntut sikap syukur. Di antara bentuk mensyukuri keduanya ialah menggunakannya untuk memperkuat diri dalam menunaikan ibadah. Pada pelajaran ini kita akan mengenal lebih jauh tentang sejumlah hukum dan adab yang berkaitan dengan makanan dan minuman. Selain itu, kita juga akan mempelajari makanan-makanan haram yang wajib dihindari oleh seorang Muslim.

passages.heading: Bagaimana Cara Kita Menunaikan Zakat Uang?
passages.text: Seorang Muslim menunaikan zakat pada hartanya yang berupa uang dan wajib zakat yaitu sekali setahun hitungan tahun hijriah. Kadar zakatnya 2,5% dan zakat tersebut diberikan kepada orang-orang fakir dan yang membutuhkan.

passages.heading: Pendahuluan
passages.text: Sejak dahulu, semenjak manusia ada di atas bumi ini, mereka hidup dengan tingkat kehidupan yang berbeda-beda. Ada orang kaya yang memiliki banyak harta dan ada orang miskin yang tidak mendapatkan makanan pokoknya. Ini adalah satu di antara sunatullah pada alam ini. Tetapi, Islam telah mewajibkan pada harta orang-orang kaya sebuah kewajiban yang harus mereka tunaikan kepada orang-orang miskin untuk membantu mereka serta meringankan tekanan kemiskinan dari mereka. Islam menganjurkan agar seorang Muslim memberikan sebagian hartanya lebih dari kewajibannya, dan menyediakan pahala besar untuk itu yang akan diperoleh oleh seorang Muslim di masa hidupnya dan setelah kematian. Di samping itu, Islam juga menganjurkan berbuat baik kepada orang-orang miskin di semua waktu dan semua keadaan. Juga menganjurkan memberi makan kepada orang-orang yang kelaparan dan memberi pakaian kepada orang-orang yang tidak mendapatkan pakaian. Semua ini bertujuan agar masyarakat Islam saling bahu-membahu dan bersaudara sebagaimana yang Allah inginkan. Pada pelajaran ini kita akan

passages.heading: Definisi Ibadah
passages.text: Ibadah ialah amal perbuatan yang disyariatkan oleh Allah agar dengannya seorang Muslim mendekatkan diri kepada-Nya. Ibadah ini mencakup semua perbuatan dan perkataan yang dicintai oleh Allah, baik yang tampak seperti ibadah-ibadah badan semisal salat dan haji, maupun yang tidak tampak seperti ibadah-ibadah hati semisal cinta, takut, harap kepada Allah, dan ibadah-ibadah hati lainnya. Seorang hamba bisa mengubah kebiasaannya menjadi bernilai ibadah dengan menyertakan niat yang baik; yaitu apabila ia meniatkan makan, minum, dan tidurnya dalam rangka memperkuat diri untuk melakukan ketaatan kepada Allah, niscaya ia akan diberikan pahala atas hal itu.

passages.heading: Mengapa Kita Berzakat?
passages.text: Kita menunaikan zakat dalam rangka melaksanakan perintah Allah yang telah mewajibkannya kepada kita.

passages.heading: Pendahuluan
passages.text: Salat tercatat sebagai syiar agama paling besar yang wajib dipelajari dan dikerjakan. Rasulullah ﷺ telah mengajari kita tata cara menunaikannya menurut cara yang diridai Allah ‘*Azza wa Jalla*. Pada pelajaran ini kita akan mengenal lebih jauh tentang salat-salat wajib, kedudukannya, syarat-syaratnya, dan tata cara menunaikannya menurut cara yang benar.

passages.heading: Hukum Asal Makanan dan Minuman
passages.text: Hukum asal makanan dan minuman ialah dibolehkan. Sebab itu, ia tidak boleh diharamkan kecuali kalau ada pengharamannya dalam Al-Qur`ān al-Karīm ataupun Sunnah Nabi ﷺ. Allah *Ta'ālā* berfirman, *"Wahai manusia! Makanlah dari (makanan) yang halal dan baik yang terdapat di bumi."* (QS. Al-Baqarah: 168)

passages.heading: Bagaimana Cara Kita Mandi?
passages.text:
Ketika mandi, kita harus mengalirkan air ke seluruh tubuh disertai berkumur-kumur dan menarik air ke dalam hidung. Bila itu telah dilakukan oleh seorang Muslim, maka dia telah suci dari hadas besar.

Hadas besar ialah hadas yang mewajibkan mandi demi menghilangkannya dan tidak cukup dengan wudu. Hadas besar memiliki beberapa macam:
1. Junub; yaitu sebuah keadaan pada laki-laki dan perempuan bila terjadi hubungan suami istri antara keduanya atau keluar mani dengan syahwat walaupun tanpa hubungan suami istri.
2. Haid; yaitu darah bulanan yang keluar dari perempuan.
3. Nifas; yaitu darah yang keluar dari perempuan setelah janin keluar dari rahimnya.

passages.heading: Makanan dan Minuman yang Diharamkan
passages.text:
Allah *'Azza wa Jalla* mengharamkan beberapa jenis makanan dan minuman, di antaranya:

- Khamar; karena khamar menghilangkan akal, sedangkan melindungi akal adalah satu di antara *Maqāṣid syarī'ah* (tujuan besar syariat) Islam.
- Narkoba; karena merusak akal dan fisik.
- Hewan yang mati tanpa disembelih atau tidak dibacakan nama Allah ketika penyembelihannya.
- Daging babi; karena merupakan daging najis yang tidak boleh dimakan.
- Binatang buas; seperti singa, harimau, dan elang.
- Binatang yang disembelih dalam rangka mendekatkan diri kepada tuhan-tuhan yang batil, seperti berhala.

> *Maqāṣid syarī'ah* ialah salah satu ilmu Islam untuk mengetahui hikmah dan rahasia syariat. Misalnya: mengapa Allah mensyariatkan hukum-hukum ini? Untuk tujuan apa hukum ini ada?

passages.heading: Apa Syarat-syarat Penyembelihan yang Disyariatkan?
passages.text:
Penyembelihan yang disyariatkan ialah penyembelihan yang memenuhi syarat-syarat berikut:

1. Orang yang menyembelih adalah seorang Muslim, Yahudi, atau Nasrani yang mampu membedakan (baik dan buruk), serta meniatkan penyembelihan.
2. Alat yang digunakan bisa menyembelih, mengalirkan darah, dan memotong dengan ketajamannya, seperti pisau. Haram hukumnya menggunakan alat yang membunuh dengan berat bebannya dan benturannya pada kepala hewan, atau dengan sengatannya seperti setrum listrik.
3. Menyebut nama Allah dengan membaca, “Bismillāh” ketika menggerakkan tangan untuk menyembelih.
4. Memotong bagian yang wajib dipotong dalam penyembelihan, yaitu *marī`* (saluran makanan), *ḥulqūm* (saluran napas), *wadajān* (dua urat besar pada leher), atau memotong 3 di antara 4 saluran ini.

passages.text: The Arab unbelievers rejected the Qur’an, so Allah challenged them to produce the like of it, or one soorah like it, or even ten verses, but they were unable to do so.

passages.heading: What Is the Qur’an?
passages.text:
The Holy Qur’an is the Word of Allah Almighty that He revealed to His Messenger, Muhammad ﷺ. It is the last of Allah’s revealed books, and there is no other book after it.

The revealed books are the books that Allah Almighty revealed to His prophets.
A Muslim believes that these books were revealed by Allah Almighty, and that Allah spoke in them in a manner that befits Him. These books include Az-Zaboor (the Psalms), which He revealed to Daawood (David) عليه السلام; At-Tawraat (the Torah), which He revealed to Moosaa (Moses) عليه السلام and Al-Injeel (the Gospel), which He revealed to Jesus, عليه السلام. All these books have undergone alteration and corruption through the ages.

passages.heading: Introduction
passages.text: When Allah sent prophets to their people to call them to the truth, he supported them with some miracles to prove to them that they were true prophets. These miracles, however, ended with the passing of these prophets. As for the Messenger of Islam ﷺ, Allah also furnished him with certain miracles to show his people, and all mankind, for that matter, but the greatest of all of them was His Glorious Book, which He took upon Himself to preserve even after the demise of His prophet ﷺ. In this lesson, we are going to learn about some virtues and etiquette associated with the Qur’an.

passages.heading: Stories of the Prophets in the Qur’an
passages.text:
The Holy Qur’an is replete with stories of the previous prophets and their people, starting with Adam, and passing through Noah, Hud, Saalih, Shu’ayb, Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, Moses, Jesus, and other prophets and messengers, peace be upon them all. The Holy Qur’an mentions their stories for a number of reasons, including the following:

- to show that the religion of all the prophets is, in essence, the same and that its basis is to worship Allah Almighty alone.
- to give solace to Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and make him stand firm and steadfast, reminding him that prophets before him suffered the same hardships he himself was experiencing.
- to give comfort and solace to the believers, reminding them that even Allah’s honourable servants before them were afflicted with trials and tribulations.
- to afford people the opportunity to learn lessons from such true stories.

passages.heading: Lesson 2
passages.text:
“The path of those whom You have blessed, not of those who have incurred Your wrath, nor of those who have gone astray”
It is the path of those whom You have blessed with guidance from among the prophets and their supporters, and those who follow in their footsteps—These are the ones who have been rightly guided.

Keep us away from the path of those with whom you are angry because they know the truth but choose not to follow it. Also, keep us away from the path of those who have not been guided to the straight path due to their ignorance.

passages.heading: The Virtue of Reading/Reciting the Qur’an
passages.text:
- The Prophet ﷺ said, “If anyone reads/recites one single letter in Allah’s Book, he will be credited with a good deed, and a good deed gets a tenfold reward. I do not say that *alif*, *laam*, *meem* are one letter; rather, *alif* is a letter, *laam* is a letter and *meem* is a letter” (Reported by At-Tirmidhee; No. 2910 with an authentic chain of narrators).

- The Prophet ﷺ also said, “Read the Qur’an, for it will come on the Day of Resurrection as an intercessor for those who read it.” (Reported by Muslim; No. 804).

passages.heading: Lesson 1
passages.text: ## Learn about the Holy Qur’an

passages.heading: The Qur’an is Food for the Soul and Mind
passages.text:
The Holy Qur’an addresses both people’s minds and souls. It addresses the mind by:

- encouraging them to use logical reasoning on the various issues. The Almighty says, {{Q:21:22}} (Soorat Al-Anbiyyaa’, 21:22).
- calling them to exercise their intellects and contemplate His signs and the proofs of His power. The Almighty says, {{Q:2:219}} (Soorat Al-Baqarah, 2:219).
- reproving those who do not use their intellects to reflect on His signs. The Almighty says, {{Q:25:44}} (Soorat Al-Furqaan, 25: 44).

It also addresses the soul and emotions by:

- spotlighting and depicting human feelings in many cases. The Almighty says, {{Q:2:165}} (Soorat Al-Baqarah, 2:165).
- calling attention to human emotions and pointing out their good and bad effects. The Almighty says, {{Q:5:82}} (Soorat Al-Maa’idah, 5:82).
- commanding Muslims to exercise kindness and gentleness when inviting others to Islam. The Almighty says, {{Q:16:125}} (Soorat An-Nahl, 16: 125).
- incorporating aspects of faith into verses on legal rules. The Almighty says, {{Q:4:94}} (Soorat An-Nisaa’, 4:94).
- using moving words that evoke genuine emotions. The Almighty says, {{Q:24:22}} (Soorat An-Noor, 24:22).

passages.heading: Who Are We?
passages.text:
Islam defines ‘man’ as one of Allah’s many creatures. The Almighty has honoured man and favoured him greatly above many other creatures, and subjected many of them to him so that he may benefit from them to perform the duties required of him during his life. The Almighty says, {{Q:17:70}} (Surat Al-Israa’, 17:70).

Allah Almighty has made in man some kind of likeness to:

> The angels are among Allah’s creatures. The Almighty created them from light and with a natural predisposition to worship and obey Him. They are His honoured servants who never disobey His orders but always do as they are commanded. There are a great many of them, but only Allah knows their number.

- the angels in their purity and worship.
- the devils in their ingratitude and disobedience, and
- the animals in their satisfying their whims and desires.

passages.heading: Who Are We?
passages.text:
He has provided him with an innate readiness to do good or evil but has at the same time furnished him with such cognitive tools as the innate human nature (*fitrah*) and the intellect to discern good from evil.

He has also given him free will to be responsible for his own choices and actions.

passages.heading: Muslim Women’s Modest Style of Dress (*Hijaab*)
passages.text:
Allah enjoins women to wear the *hijaab* because women enjoy natural beauty and attraction that could easily tempt men into sinful acts, more than the other way round. Women are to cover their entire bodies when in the presence of men who are not related to them, and they may choose any design or colour they like for their *hijaab* as long as the following four conditions are met:

| First Condition | Second Condition | Third condition | Fourth Condition |

passages.heading: Why Should I Embrace Islam?
passages.text:
Some people may ask: Why should I embrace Islam?

The answer is: I must do so for a number of reasons, including the following:

1. Islam is the religion that Allah has approved and chosen for His servants and will not accept any other religion. The Almighty says, {{Q:3:85}} (Soorat Aal-’Imraan, 3:85).

2. Islam is the religion of all the prophets and commands its adherents to believe in all of them without exception. Allah says, {{Q:2:136}} (Soorat Al-Baqarah, 2:136).
The difference between prophets lies only in the laws relating to people’s actions, as the Almighty says, {{Q:5:48}} (Soorat Al-Maa’idah, 5:48) That is, for each nation before Islam, Allah appointed a law to which people referred for their disputes and a way of life whereby they drew near to Him. Thus, followers of every prophet had their respective laws and regulations, but the set of beliefs to which prophets called their people was the same. Then Allah sent the last prophet and messenger, Muhammad ﷺ, with the final divine laws, and thus the only religion acceptable to Allah is Islam.

- Islam has granted women the right to inheritance, allocating them equitable shares with men, which sometimes differ under certain circumstances depending on their relationship with others and the financial obligations they have to discharge. While men support the family as a matter of religious obligation, women are not obliged to spend anything at all.
- It has established total equality between men and women in numerous matters including financial transactions.
- It has granted them the right to choose their own husbands.
- It has granted them the right to retain their maiden names. In Islam, a woman does not change her surname to that of her husband upon marriage; rather, she retains her maiden name, and thus her independent personality.

passages.heading: Forbidden Types of Clothing
passages.text:
With your partners, discuss the reasons why some types of clothing are forbidden in Islam.

The Prophet ﷺ forbade men from imitating women and women from imitating men. This prohibition includes the type of clothing and the manner of speech. Islam strictly forbids imitation of the opposite sex, considering it a major sin that invites Allah’s punishment unless one repents and desists from committing it. Islam enjoins men to ensure that their true nature and appearance are distinct from that of women, and vice versa, which clearly testifies to common sense and sound logic.

passages.heading: Islamic Rulings Pertaining to Menstrual and Postnatal Bleeding
passages.text:
Allah Almighty has prescribed several rulings relating to menstruating women and women experiencing their postnatal bleeding, including the following:

- They are exempt from performing the prayers during this period and do not have to make up for the prayers they have missed while in this state after the end of menstrual and postnatal bleeding.
- They are exempt from fasting and are not allowed to fast while in this state, but they must make up for the fasting days they have missed in Ramadaan.
- During this period, a husband must not have intercourse with his wife during her menstrual or postnatal period. He is allowed, however, to satisfy his sexual desire but without having intercourse.
- At the end of the menstrual and postnatal period, when bleeding stops completely, women must take a ritual bath (*ghusl*).

Islam is the way to happiness in this life and salvation in the life to come; therefore, those who believe in Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and follow him after his message has reached them will be saved; as for those who deny him, they will be doomed to divine punishment. The Almighty says, {{Q:3:85}} (*Soorat Aal-’Imraan, 3:85*) The Prophet ﷺ also said, “By Him in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, any person of this Community, Jew or Christian, who hears of me and dies without believing in what I have been sent with will be among the dwellers of Hell” (*Saheeh Muslim;* No. 153).

4. Islam gives conclusive answers to the big questions of human existence: Where did we come from? Why are we here? Where do we go after death?

5. Islam is in perfect harmony with the innate human nature (*fitrah*), beginning with the greatest value it embraces, namely the declaration of Allah’s unity, and ending with the rules of etiquette it teaches its adherents to enable them to attain great perfection in moral excellence.

A man's *'awrah* that must be covered extends from the navel to the knees. A woman must cover herself entirely in the presence of men not related to her; as for men to whom she is related and is forbidden to marry, such as her father, son and brother, she may appear before them as she would normally do in front of other women, showing such parts of her body as the face, hair, the neck and feet.

الذكاة الشرعية هي الذبح أو النحر المستوفي للشروط التالية:

1. أن يكون الذابح مسلماً أو يهودياً أو نصرانياً يميز ويقصد الذكاة.
2. أن تكون الآلة صالحة للذبح وتُجري الدم وتقطع بحدها كالسكين، ويحرم استخدام ما يقتلها بثقله واصطدامه برأس الحيوان، أو بحرقه كالصعق الكهربائي.
3. أن يذكر اسم الله فيقول: (بسم الله) عند تحريك يده للذبح.
4. قطع ما يجب قطعه في الذكاة، وهو: المريء، والحلقوم، والودجان وهما العرقان الكبيران في الرقبة، أو قطع ثلاثة من هذه الأربعة.

passages.heading: What is the Islamic Ruling on Seafood Consumption?
passages.text:
It is permissible to eat dead aquatic animals that can live only in water, such as fish and prawns, whether they live in the sea, rivers or lakes.

It is permissible to hunt wild, nonpredatory animals and consume their flesh provided that the name of Allah is mentioned before the hunting weapon is discharged, and the hunted game must be slaughtered if found still alive.

{{Q:109:1-6}}

“Say: Unbelievers!”

passages.heading: 2 Islam Wipes out the Sins Committed before It
passages.text: If a person sincerely embraces Islam, the Most Gracious and the Most Merciful God will forgive him all his past sins, and this is one of the outstanding merits of Islam. The Almighty says to His Prophet ﷺ, {{Q:8:38}} (Soorat Al-Anfaal, 8:38). A man once showed interest in Islam, and so he went to the Prophet ﷺ but he stipulated that Allah should forgive him his past sins. The Prophet ﷺ gave him the good news, saying, “Don’t you know that Islam wipes out all the sins committed before it?” (Reported by Muslim; No. 121).

passages.heading: The Pillars of Islam
passages.text:
Islam is built on five pillars:

Every Muslim must strictly adhere to these pillars to ensure he is practising Islam in full; negligence in one of these pillars is bound to render the way you practise Islam deficient.

1. The two testimonies of faith: To bear witness that none is worthy of worship except Allah and that Muhammad is His His Messenger
2. Establish the prayer: A Muslim must pray five times a day. These prayers will be explained in due course.
3. Paying zakaat
4. Fasting in the month of Ramadaan
5. Making the pilgrimage to Allah’s House

passages.heading: How Do We Pray?
passages.text:
1. He intends in his heart to pray.
2. He stands facing the *qiblah*, raises his hands up to the level of the shoulders or ears, and says, “*Allaahu akbar* Allah is the Greatest.”
3. He places his right hand on his left hand. Then he recites one of the opening supplications, such as, Subhaanak-Allaahumma wa bi hamdika, wa tabaarak-asmuka, wa ta’aalaa jadduka, wa laa ilaaha ghayruka “Glory be to You, O Allah; Yours is the praise, blessed is Your name, exalted is Your majesty, and there is no god besides You.” Then he says, A’oodhu billaahi min-ash-shaytaan-ir-rajeem. Bismillaah-ir-rahmaan-ir-raheem “I seek Allah’s protection from Satan, who has been expelled from His mercy. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.” Then he recites *Soorat Al-Faatihah* and says after it, “*Aameen*”, which means “Answer our supplications, O Allah”. After that, he recites whatever number of verses of the Qur’an as is easy for him, even if it is one verse.
4. He says, “Allaahu akbar Allah is the Greatest” while raising his hands up to the level of his shoulders or ears, and bows down, lowering his head and back and keeping them straight at a right angle, placing the palms of his hands on the knees. He says three times while in this position, “Subhaana rabbiy-al-’adheem Glory be to my Lord, the Almighty.”

passages.heading: The Manner of Performing the Full Ritual Bath (*Ghusl*)
passages.text:
If a Muslim wants to perform *ghusl*, he must do the following:

1. He intends in his heart to perform *ghusl* and washes out his private parts with water.
2. He performs *wudoo’* like the one he performs before the prayer.
3. He washes his entire body with water.

passages.heading: What Are the Conditions for Islamic Slaughter?
passages.text:
Islamic slaughter is one that satisfies the following conditions:

1. The person undertaking the slaughtering process must be Muslim, Jew or Christian who has reached the age of discretion and carries out this act for the intended purpose.
2. The tool used for slaughter must be suitable for the intended purpose, causes blood to flow and sharp, such as a knife. It is forbidden to use anything that may kill the animal due to its heavy weight, hit its head to death or render it unconscious by resorting to electric stunning, for instance.
3. The name of Allah must be pronounced by saying *Bismillaah* (in the name of Allah) at the time of slaughtering the animal.
4. Cutting what must be cut in the Islamic slaughter, namely, the oesophagus, the throat, and the two jugular veins, or just three of these four.

passages.heading: Islamic Rulings Pertaining to Meat Served in Restaurants and Shops
passages.text:
1. The meat of animals that are slaughtered by other than a Muslim or a member of the People of the Book (a Christian or a Jew), such as a Buddhist, or a Hindu is strictly forbidden. This includes meat served in restaurants and shops in countries where Muslims or People of the Book constitute a minority.
2. The meat of animals killed by a Muslim or a member of the People of the Book is lawful based on textual evidence to this effect in the Qur’an.
3. The meat of animals that are not killed according to Islamic law, such as by electrocution and drowning, is strictly forbidden.
4. The general rule is that it is permissible to consume the flesh of animals slaughtered by People of the Book as well as meat of animals generally found in their restaurants and shops, making sure, however, to invoke Allah’s name at the time of eating (that is, by saying *Bismillaah*), but it is better for Muslims to eat only meat that has been proven to be lawful (*halaal*).

passages.heading: Benefits of Faith
passages.text:
* **Getting to know Allah Almighty:** A believer gets to know his Lord and His names, attributes and actions, so much so that he becomes more attached to Him.
* **Glorying Allah:** the more a believer gets to know his Lord, the more he extols and loves Him, the more he hopes for His mercy and the more God-fearing he becomes.
* **Getting to know Allah’s graciousness to His servants:** for sending messengers to them and divine books to them to guide them to the true religion.
* **Loving the angels:** for worshipping Allah and showing obedience to Him.
* **Loving Allah’s Messengers:** Allah Almighty chose them to convey His message to people.
* **Diligent worship:** the stronger the faith, the more worship one performs.
* **A truly happy life:** A believer is content with what Allah has apportioned to him and knows that whatever calamities befall him in this world elevate his rank and efface his sins. He also hopes for the bliss He has prepared for the believers in the life to come.
* **Not to be deluded by this world:** The life of this world is temporary and only serves as a means to eternal life in the hereafter.
* **Exposing myths:** Faith exposes and nullifies many myths.
* **Entering Paradise:** This is the abode of eternal bliss which Allah Almighty has prepared for His believing servants.

from the devils among the jinn and mankind.

*Soorat Al-Kawthar* **Explained**

{{Q:108:1-3}}

“We have bestowed on you abundant good”

We have given you, Messenger, immeasurable, abundant good in this life and the life to come, part of which is River Al-Kawthar in Paradise.

“So pray to your Lord and sacrifice to Him”

Therefore, sincerely pray to your Lord and worship Him alone, and sacrifice to Him, pronouncing Allah’s name alone when slaughtering animals, in gratitude to Him for the honour and good He has bestowed on you.

“He who hates you is the one who is truly cut off”

The one who hates you and hates the true religion you have brought is the most disgraced and contemptible, whose mention is short-lived and who is cut off from all good.

passages.heading: The Criterion of Superiority in Islam
passages.text:
Piety is the criterion whereby Allah grants superiority to some over others. Superiority among Muslims can only be attained through strong faith, not one’s appearance, lineage, colour, or wealth. Allah Almighty says, {{Q:49:13}} (Soorat Al-Hjuraat, 49:13).

The Prophet ﷺ said: “O people! Your Lord is one and your father [Adam] is one. An Arab has no superiority over a non-Arab, nor does a non-Arab have any superiority over an Arab; a white person has no superiority over a black person, nor does a black person have any superiority over a white person except in piety.” (Reported by Al-Bayhaqee in Shu’ab al-Eemaan; No. 4774).

passages.heading: The Requirements of the Two Testimonies of Faith
passages.text: It is not enough to verbally declare the two testimonies of faith. In addition to this, it is imperative to know what they mean and to meet their requirements. The testimony that there is no god but Allah requires us to reject everything that is worshipped besides or instead of Allah, to firmly believe that Allah alone is our Lord and Cherisher and the One True God worthy of worship and to worship Him sincerely. Allah Almighty says, {{Q:2:256}} (Soorat Al-Baqarah, 2:256) The testimony that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah requires us to believe what he says, do what he commands and avoid what he forbids and worship Allah only according to his instructions.

passages.heading: Conditions for Acts of Worship to Be Accepted
passages.text:
For an act of worship to be accepted, two conditions must be fulfilled:

The first condition: It has to be done sincerely for the sake of Allah to draw closer to alone, without showing off.

The second condition: It has to be done in the manner Allah has enjoined it and exactly as it was performed by the Prophet ﷺ.

> *Aririyyaa’* (showing off) is the act of doing an act of worship only to be seen and praised by people for doing it.

passages.heading: The Criterion of Superiority in Islam
passages.text:
Piety is the criterion whereby Allah grants superiority to some over others. Superiority among Muslims can only be attained through strong faith, not one’s appearance, lineage, colour, or wealth. Allah Almighty says, {{Q:49:13}} (Soorat Al-Hjuraat, 49:13).

The Prophet ﷺ said: “O people! Your Lord is one and your father [Adam] is one. An Arab has no superiority over a non-Arab, nor does a non-Arab have any superiority over an Arab; a white person has no superiority over a black person, nor does a black person have any superiority over a white person except in piety.” (Reported by Al-Bayhaqee in Shu’ab al-Eemaan; No. 4774).

passages.heading: Certain Rulings on Purification
passages.text:
- It is a general Islamic rule that things are naturally clean and pure unless stated otherwise by Islam.
- It would suffice to cleanse the body or clothing of impurities by removing them with water or any cleaning substance that would serve the purpose.
- It would be better for a person who uses the toilet to cleanse the place of urine and faeces with water. It is also permissible for him to cleanse himself with tissues or any other material that serves to remove impurity.

passages.heading: Things That a Person Who Is in a State of *Jannabah* Must Not Do
passages.text:
The state into which a person gets following intercourse or ejaculation and because of which he must perform *ghusl* is called *janaabah*, and he is described as *junub*. In this case, he is not allowed to do the following:

1. perform the prayer
2. circumambulate the Ka’bah (*tawaaf*)
3. touch or carry the Qur’an
4. stay in the mosque

passages.heading: *Tayammum* (Dry Ablution)
passages.text:
If a person who wants to perform *wudoo’* or *ghusl* is unable to do so due to illness, or when water is not readily available, or for any other legitimate reason, he may resort to dry ablution (*tayammum*) instead.

The Manner of Performing *Tayammum*: (1) Intend in his heart to perform *tayammum* and strike both hands slightly on pure earth once, (2) wipe the face with them, (3) wipe the back of the right hand with the palm of the left, and then the back of the left hand with the palm of the right hand.

passages.heading: What shall I do if I find water after having performed *tayammum*?
passages.text: If a Muslim finds water or can use it, his purity becomes invalid, in which case he must perform *wudoo’* or *ghusl*.

passages.heading: Types of Acts of Worship
passages.text:
Acts of worship fall into different categories:

| Acts of worship involving the heart | A Muslim performs these with his heart. Examples include love, fear, hope and *khushoo’*. |
| --- | --- |
| Physical acts of worship | A Muslim performs these physically. Examples include the prayer, *zakaat* and pilgrimage. |
| Acts that are abandoned in obedience to Allah | A Muslim draws closer to his Lord by abandoning the acts He has forbidden him, such as drinking alcohol and committing adultery, or by refraining from certain permissible acts at specific times, such as abstaining from food and drink while fasting. |

> *Ar-Rajaa’*(Hope): This refers to rejoicing in Allah’s grace and hoping for His benevolence, while at the same time ensuring proper reliance on Allah by doing good deeds to the best of one’s ability.
> 
> *Al-khushoo’* is a state of utter humility and calmness and deep concentration into which one gets while performing an act of worship, such as the prayer, bringing about outward composure and tranquillity.

passages.heading: Introduction
passages.text: When Allah sent prophets to their people to call them to the truth, he supported them with some miracles to prove to them that they were true prophets. These miracles, however, ended with the passing of these prophets. As for the Messenger of Islam ﷺ, Allah also furnished him with certain miracles to show his people, and all mankind, for that matter, but the greatest of all of them was His Glorious Book, which He took upon Himself to preserve even after the demise of His prophet ﷺ. In this lesson, we are going to learn about some virtues and etiquette associated with the Qur’an.

passages.heading: Important Notes Related to Fasting
passages.text:
- Whoever breaks his fast in Ramadaan for a legitimate reason must make up for every day he has missed after than Ramadaan.
- If a sick person breaks the fast because of an incurable disease, he is exempt from fasting the month of Ramadaan, but he must feed one poor person for each day he does not fast.
- If a Muslim cannot possibly fast due to old age, he is exempt from fasting the month of Ramadaan but he must feed one poor person for each day he does not fast.

**Muslims break their fast as soon as the call to *Maghrib* (sunset) prayer is announced, and many Muslims are very keen to share their Ramadaan breakfast, or *iftar*, with fellow Muslims.**

passages.text:
1. He intends in his heart to pray.

6. He washes his hands from the fingertips up to the elbow, starting with his right hand.

passages.heading: Islamic Rulings Pertaining to Menstrual and Postnatal Bleeding
passages.text:
Allah Almighty has prescribed several rulings relating to menstruating women and women experiencing their postnatal bleeding, including the following:

- They are exempt from performing the prayers during this period and do not have to make up for the prayers they have missed while in this state after the end of menstrual and postnatal bleeding.
- They are exempt from fasting and are not allowed to fast while in this state, but they must make up for the fasting days they have missed in Ramadaan.
- During this period, a husband must not have intercourse with his wife during her menstrual or postnatal period. He is allowed, however, to satisfy his sexual desire but without having intercourse.
- At the end of the menstrual and postnatal period, when bleeding stops completely, women must take a ritual bath (*ghusl*).

passages.text:

It is forbidden to use anything that may kill the animal due to its heavy weight, hit its head to death or render it unconscious by resorting to electric stunning, for instance.
3. The name of Allah must be pronounced by saying *Bismillaah* (in the name of Allah) at the time of slaughtering the animal.
4. Cutting what must be cut in the Islamic slaughter, namely, the oesophagus, the throat, and the two jugular veins, or just three of these four.

passages.text: ## Learn about the Holy Qur’an

passages.heading: What Is the Qur’an?
passages.text:
The Holy Qur’an is the Word of Allah Almighty that He revealed to His Messenger, Muhammad ﷺ. It is the last of Allah’s revealed books, and there is no other book after it.

The revealed books are the books that Allah Almighty revealed to His prophets.
A Muslim believes that these books were revealed by Allah Almighty, and that Allah spoke in them in a manner that befits Him. These books include Az-Zaboor (the Psalms), which He revealed to Daawood (David) عليه السلام; At-Tawraat (the Torah), which He revealed to Moosaa (Moses) عليه السلام and Al-Injeel (the Gospel), which He revealed to Jesus, عليه السلام. All these books have undergone alteration and corruption through the ages.

passages.heading: The Virtue of Reading/Reciting the Qur’an
passages.text:
- The Prophet ﷺ said, “If anyone reads/recites one single letter in Allah’s Book, he will be credited with a good deed, and a good deed gets a tenfold reward. I do not say that *alif*, *laam*, *meem* are one letter; rather, *alif* is a letter, *laam* is a letter and *meem* is a letter” (Reported by At-Tirmidhee; No. 2910 with an authentic chain of narrators).

- The Prophet ﷺ also said, “Read the Qur’an, for it will come on the Day of Resurrection as an intercessor for those who read it.” (Reported by Muslim; No. 804).

passages.heading: Forbidden Types of Clothing
passages.text:
A man's *'awrah* that must be covered extends from the navel to the knees. A woman must cover herself entirely in the presence of men not related to her; as for men to whom she is related and is forbidden to marry, such as her father, son and brother, she may appear before them as she would normally do in front of other women, showing such parts of her body as the face, hair, the neck and feet.

- Clothing that reveals the *'awrah* and does not conceal it
- Clothing that involves dressing like or imitating the opposite sex, such as when men dress like women and vice versa.
- Clothing that is worn with an air of pride and conceit
- Extravagant clothing
- Men are particularly forbidden to wear silk clothing or adorn themselves with gold or silver jewellery.
- Clothing that involves imitation of the dress traditionally worn by non-Muslims and specific to a certain religion, such as the type of clothing worn by monks and priests

passages.heading: Introduction
passages.text: The clothes we wear are some of the countless blessings Allah has bestowed on us. The Qur’an states, {{Q:7:26}} (Soorat Al-A’raaf, 7:26).

passages.heading: Discuss
passages.text: Can we turn to fashion trends, customs, traditions or official regulations to determine for us what the appropriate clothing for men and women is?

passages.heading: The General Islamic Rule Regarding Clothing
passages.text:
The general Islamic rule is that all types of clothing are allowed, unless stated otherwise in the Qur’an or the Prophet’s Sunnah.

the general Islamic rule regarding dealings in general, including clothing, is that everything is permissible unless there is evidence to the contrary. All types of clothing mentioned here are forbidden due to textual evidence either in the Qur’an or the Prophet’s Sunnah.

passages.heading: Forbidden Types of Clothing
passages.text:
With your partners, discuss the reasons why some types of clothing are forbidden in Islam.

The Prophet ﷺ forbade men from imitating women and women from imitating men. This prohibition includes the type of clothing and the manner of speech. Islam strictly forbids imitation of the opposite sex, considering it a major sin that invites Allah’s punishment unless one repents and desists from committing it. Islam enjoins men to ensure that their true nature and appearance are distinct from that of women, and vice versa, which clearly testifies to common sense and sound logic.

passages.heading: Discuss
passages.text: What purposes does clothing serve?

passages.heading: Сколько раз следует омывать каждый орган, подлежащий омовению?
passages.text: Сунной малого омовения является троекратное омывание каждого органа, кроме головы и ушей, которые протираются один раз. Допустимо ограничиться однократным омыванием органа при условии, что он будет омыт полностью.

passages.heading: Столпы имана
passages.text:
1. Вера в Аллаха. Мусульманин верует в существование Всевышнего Аллаха, в Его имена и качества. Он верует, что Аллах — Господь всей этой огромной вселенной, ее Творец, Владыка всего, что в ней есть, Управляющий ее делами и Наделяющий уделом Своих рабов. Он верует, что нет другого божества, достойного поклонения. Он верует, что Аллах обладает качествами совершенства.
2. Вера в ангелов. Мусульманин верует в существование благородных ангелов. Он верует, что их создал Аллах и что они поклоняются Аллаху и не ослушиваются его в том, что Он повелел им. Он верует в их описания и функции, о которых говорится в Коране и Сунне.
3. Вера в Писания. Мусульманин верует, что Аллах через Своих посланников ниспослал Своим рабам Писания, чтобы наставить людей на прямой путь и обучить их положениям религии. К этой вере относится также вера в то, что Мусе (Моисею), мир ему, Аллах ниспослал Таурат (Тору); Дауду (Давиду) — Забур (Псалмы); ‘Исе (Иисусу), мир ему, — Инджиль (Евангелие); а Мухаммаду ﷺ — Коран; и что Коран является последним из Писаний и свидетельствует о них.
4. Вера в пророков, мир им всем. Мусульманин верует, что Всевышний Аллах отправил к народам посланников и поддержал их чудесами, свидетельствующими об их правдивости, чтобы они обрадовали верующих, предостерегли неверующих, и обучили свои народы положениям их религии. Люди, к которым были отправлены посланники, обязаны повиноваться им и следовать за ними. Мусульманин также верует, что Мухаммад ﷺ — последний пророк.
5. Вера в Судный день. Мусульманин верует в Судный день и в то, что в этот День Аллах воскресит мертвых, подняв их из могил, спросит с них за их деяния и воздаст им за них, после чего одни люди войдут в Рай, а другие — в Ад.
6. Вера в предопределение. Мусульманин верует, что, всё происходящее в этой вселенной, будь то добро или зло, происходит по предопределению Всевышнего Аллаха. Аллах знал, что это произойдет, и записал это в Хранимой скрижали (Ляуху-ль-махфуз). Мусульманин также верует, что в этой вселенной происходит только то, что пожелал Аллах.

passages.heading: Что такое полное омовение?
passages.text: Полное омовение — это омывание водой всего тела с целью устранения большого ритуального осквернения.

passages.heading: Виды очищения
passages.text:
Очищение бывает двух видов:

**Физическое очищение**
Это удаление нечистот и очищение мест, откуда они выходят.

**Ритуальное очищение**
Речь идет об устранении причин, препятствующих совершению молитвы. Достигается это посредством омывания некоторых частей тела или всего тела.

Ритуальное очищение достигается либо посредством малого омовения (вуду’), либо посредством полного омовения (гусль).

- Малое омовение (вуду’) — это омывание водой некоторых частей тела.
- Полное омовение (гусль) — омывание водой всего тела целиком.

Для очищения используется чистая вода: морская, речная, колодезная или любая другая, не смешанная с нечистотами.

passages.heading: Достоинство благонравия
passages.text:
- Пророк ﷺ сообщил, что больше всего людей введет в Рай богобоязненность и благонравие.
- Пророк ﷺ сообщил, что в Судный день благонравие станет самым тяжелым из благих дел на весах человека.
- Пророк ﷺ сообщил, что в Судный день ближе всех к нему окажутся самые благонравные люди.

> Весы человека. В Судный день будут установлены особые Весы, на которых будут взвешены благие и греховные деяния человека. Тот, чьи благие деяния перевесят его грехи, войдет в Рай; а тот, чьи грехи перевесят благие деяния, войдет в Огонь.

passages.heading: Введение
passages.text: Одним из самых незабываемых моментов для новообращенного мусульманина является момент объявления о принятии Ислама путем произнесения двух свидетельств. Этим объявлением он говорит прежде всего себе, что он стал иным, чем был до этого, и что в этот момент он делает свои первые шаги к познанию истины и следованию ей. На этом уроке мы ознакомимся с двумя свидетельствами, их смыслом и требованиями.

passages.heading: Кто мы?
passages.text:
Ислам определяет человека как одно из многочисленных творений Всевышнего Аллаха, которое Аллах возвысил над множеством других творений и которому Он подчинил некоторых из них, чтобы он использовал их для выполнения повседневных задач. Всевышний сказал: {{Q:17:70}} (сура «аль-Исра’», аят 70).

Всевышний Аллах уподобил человека:

- ангелам — в их чистоте и поклонении;
- шайтанам — в их неблагодарности и ослушании;
- животным — в их удовлетворении своих прихотей и страстей.

Аллах заложил в человека склонность к добру и склонность ко злу и дал ему то, что помогает отличить добро от зла: естество (фитра) и разум. И Он сделал его свободным, обладающим выбором и ответственным за свой выбор и свои действия.

Ангелы — одно из творений Всевышнего Аллаха. Всевышний Аллах создал их из света. Это благородные рабы Аллаха, которые не ослушиваются Его и совершают то, что им велено. Их количество известно только Аллаху.

passages.heading: Условия молитвы
passages.text:
Для совершения молитвы необходимо соблюдение нескольких условий:

- Очищение. К нему относится очищение от нечистот тела и места молитвы, а также очищение от ритуального осквернения посредством малого или полного омовения.
- Покрытие аурата. Аурат — это те, части тела, которые необходимо скрывать от людей. Аурат мужчины, который должен быть закрыт во время молитвы, — от пупка до колен, а аурат женщины, который должен быть закрыт во время молитвы, — все ее тело, кроме лица и кистей рук.
- Обращение в сторону киблы. Кибла — это направление в сторону священной Каабы, которая находится в достопочтенной Мекке. Во время молитвы мусульманин должен обращаться в ее сторону.
- Наступление времени молитвы. Молитва, совершённая до наступления ее времени, недействительна. Кроме того, не дозволено откладывать молитву до истечения ее времени. Лучше всего совершать каждую обязательную молитву в начале времени ее наступления.

passages.heading: Как совершить малое омовение?
passages.text:
Чтобы совершить малое омовение, мусульманин должен сделать следующие действия:

1. Вознамериться в сердце совершить малое омовение и сказать: «Би-сми-Ллях / С Именем Аллаха»
2. Омыть кисти рук, начиная с правой
3. Прополоскать рот
4. Прополоскать нос
5. Омыть все лицо; область его омывания по вертикали — от корней волос надо лбом до нижней точки подбородка, включая бороду, если таковая имеется; по горизонтали — от уха до уха
6. Омыть руки от кончиков пальцев до локтевого сустава, начиная с правой руки
7. Смочить руки водой, затем протереть ими голову от передней части головы к затылку, а затем обратно
8. Протереть уши внутри указательными пальцами, а за ушами — большими
9. Омыть ноги до лодыжек, которые отмечены двумя выступающими косточками над ступнями, начиная с правой стопы

passages.heading: Что нарушает малое омовение?
Обсуждение
passages.text: Перечислите некоторые средства , помогающие обучаться омовению и совершать его правильным образом.

passages.heading: Столпы имана
passages.text: Иман основывается на шести столпах:

passages.heading: Придание Аллаху сотоварищей
passages.text:
Это вера в божественность кого-либо или чего-либо помимо Всевышнего Аллаха или желание приблизиться к Нему посредством какого-либо поклонения. Это великий грех и страшное преступлением, которое Аллах не прощает. Всевышний Аллах сказал: {{Q:4:48}} (сура «ан-Ниса’», аят 48).

Благородны Коран и Сунна - хадисы посланника Аллаха ﷺ - считаются двумя основными иисточниками закона в Исламе.

Хранимая скрижаль (Ляуху-ль-махфуз) — это книга, в которой Аллах записал всё, что будет происходить до Судного дня.

passages.heading: Плоды имана
passages.text:
У имана много плодов, и мы приведем здесь лишь некоторые из них:

* Умиротворение души. Иман умиротворяет душу человека, вселяет в нее довольство Аллахом и Его предопределением и избавляет ее от страха перед кем-либо или чем-либо, помимо Аллаха.

> Аль-Кадар (судьба) — это изначальное предопределение Всевышним Аллахом всех вещей и Его знание, что они произойдут в известное Ему время определенным образом.

passages.heading: Плоды имана
passages.text:
* Познание Всевышнего Аллаха. Верующий познаёт своего Господа и это увеличивает его привязанность к Нему, и он узнаёт Его имена, качества и деяния.
* Возвеличивание Аллаха. Чем больше верующий познаёт своего Господа, тем больше он возвеличивает, почитает и любит Его, тем сильнее он надеется на Него, боится Его и проявляет смиренность перед Ним.
* Осознание того, насколько милостив Аллах к Своим рабам, ведь Он отправил к ним посланников и ниспослал им писания, чтобы люди пришли к истинной религии.
* Любовь к ангелам, ведь они поклоняются и повинуются Аллаху.
* Любовь к посланникам, ведь Всевышний Аллах избрал их для донесения Своего послания людям.
* Усердие в поклонении. Чем сильнее становится иман, тем больше и лучше человек поклоняется Аллаху.
* Благая жизнь. Верующий доволен тем уделом, которым Аллах наделил его, он знает, что бедствия, которые постигают его в этом мире, возвышают его степень и стирают его грехи, и он надеется обрести те милости, которые Аллах уготовил для верующих в жизни вечной.
* Стойкость перед обольщениями этого мира. Жизнь в этом мире временна, она является лишь путем, ведущим к вечной жизни в следующем мире.
* Разоблачение суеверий. Иман разоблачает суеверия, выявляя их несостоятельность.
* Вхождение в Рай. Рай — это обитель вечного, непрерывного наслаждения. Всевышний Аллах создал его для Своих верующих рабов.

passages.heading: Введение
passages.text: В некоторых случаях для совершения поклонения недостаточно малого омовения, а требуется полное омовение. На этом уроке мы узнаем, что такое гусль и когда и как его необходимо совершать.

passages.heading: Как совершать полное омовение?
Описание полного омовения
Когда полное омовение становится обязательным?
passages.text:
Полное омовение обязательно для мусульманина в трех случаях:

- **Первое:** Выделение семенной жидкости с вожделением, независимо от того, произошло ли это во время бодрствования или во сне.
- **Второе:** Половой акт, независимо от того, произошло семяизвержение или нет.
- **Третье:** Менструальное или послеродовое кровотечение у женщины. Когда кровотечение прекращается, она должна совершить полное омовение.

passages.heading: Введение
passages.text: **Людей всегда интересовали вопросы,** связанные с их существованием: откуда и зачем они пришли и где окажутся в итоге? Ислам дает исчерпывающие ответы на эти вопросы.

passages.heading: Откуда мы пришли и зачем?
passages.text:
Ислам разъясняет, что человек сотворен из глины. Аллах сотворил из нее Адама, праотца всех людей. Всевышний сказал: {{Q:23:12}} (сура «аль-Му’минун», аят 12).

Цель сотворения человека — поклонение Всевышнему Аллаху, хотя Аллах не нуждается не в одном из своих творений, Всевышний сказал: {{Q:51:56}} (сура «аз-Зарият» аяь 56).

Адам
Аллах поведал нам в Коране историю сотворения Адама и начала его вражды с шайтаном. См. толкование 30–39 аятов суры «аль-Бакара».

Есть и другая, второстепенная цель, а именно: обустройство этого мира посредством его улучшения, установления справедливости и распространения блага. Всевышний сказал: {{Q:11:61}} (сура «Худ», аят 61).

passages.heading: Обсуждение
passages.text: Сравните свои представления о смысле человеческого существования до и после принятия Ислама.

passages.heading: Куда мы идем?
passages.text:
Священный Коран разъяснил, что каждый человек умрет в этом мире и с его смертью закончится этап совершения деяний и начнется этап спроса и воздаяния. Всевышний сказал: {{Q:39:30-31}} (сура «аз-Зумар», аяты 30–31).

После того как человек умирает, он переходит к следующему этапу своего существования, на котором он будет спрошен о своей религии и ему воздастся за его деяния. Всевышний сказал: {{Q:3:185}} (сура «Али ‘Имран», аят 185).

Когда наступит День суда, Аллах воскресит мертвых и выведет их из могил для спроса и воздаяния, и тогда верующим будет дарован Рай, а неверующим — Огонь. Всевышний сказал: {{Q:42:7}} (сура «аш-Шура», аят 7).

passages.heading: *Soorat Al-Kaafiroon* Explained
passages.text:
{{Q:109:1-6}}

“Say: Unbelievers!”

Say, Messenger, to those who disbelieve in Allah and His Messenger: You unbelievers.

“I do not worship what you worship”

I do not worship the false gods, such as idols, that you worship.

“nor do you worship what I worship”

nor do you worship the True God whom I worship, and who alone is worthy of worship.

“I will never worship what you worship”

I will never worship the false gods that you worship.

“nor will you ever worship what I worship”

nor will you ever worship the True God whom I worship, and who alone is worthy of worship.

Al-kaafir: The person who does not proclaim pure monotheism and does not follow the divine message Prophet Muhammad ﷺ has brought.

“You have your religion, and I have my religion”

You have your religion to which you adhere, and I have my religion to which I adhere.

passages.heading: My Notes
passages.text: Write down some of the benefits of faith that you have enjoyed after embracing Islam.

passages.heading: Discuss
passages.text: How should a Muslim’s moral character be with others? Do you think that such good character has an impact on their opinion about Islam?

passages.heading: Note
passages.text: Islam respects the customs and traditions of all peoples and does not require them to change them unless they contravene any of the teachings of Islam.

passages.heading: The Position of Women in Islam
passages.text:
- Islam has granted women the right to inheritance, allocating them equitable shares with men, which sometimes differ under certain circumstances depending on their relationship with others and the financial obligations they have to discharge. While men support the family as a matter of religious obligation, women are not obliged to spend anything at all.
- It has established total equality between men and women in numerous matters including financial transactions.
- It has granted them the right to choose their own husbands.
- It has granted them the right to retain their maiden names. In Islam, a woman does not change her surname to that of her husband upon marriage; rather, she retains her maiden name, and thus her independent personality.
- It has made it the husband’s duty to spend on those women entitled to his support, such as his wife, mother and daughters, without attempting in the least to remind them of his favours.
- It stresses the importance of helping weak and vulnerable women who are in need of support, even if they are not one’s relatives, and urges its adherents to engage in such a noble act, which it considers one of the meritorious deeds in the sight of Allah.

passages.heading: Introduction
passages.text: The prayer is the greatest religious duty that a Muslim must learn and perform. Allah’s Messenger ﷺ has taught us how to perform it in the manner most pleasing to Allah Almighty. In this lesson, we are going to learn about the obligatory prayers, the position of the prayer in Islam, its conditions, and the correct manner of performing it.

passages.heading: Discuss
passages.text: Islam stresses the necessity of maintaining personal hygiene. What does this indicate?

passages.heading: Purification
passages.text:
* **Engaging in the worship of Almighty Allah**  
  This is expressed by the intention to act in obedience to Allah Almighty and to draw closer to Him

* **by removing ritual impurity**  
  Ritual impurity (*hadath*) refers to anything that takes place in the body, thus rendering purity invalid

* **and physical impurities**  
  Physical impurity (*najaasah*) refers to all physical substances which Islam considers impure, such as urine and faeces, and commands us to remove.

passages.heading: *Soorat An-Naas* Explained
passages.text:
“Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of mankind”

Say, Messenger, “I seek refuge and protection in Allah, the Lord of all mankind, who alone has power over all things.

“the King of mankind”

The King of all people, who manages all their affairs.

“the God of mankind”

The True God of all people, who alone deserves to be worshipped by them.

“from the evil of the slinking whisperer”

from the harm of Satan who whispers evil suggestions to people when they are heedless of Allah and refrains from doing so when they remember Him.

“who whispers into the hearts of mankind”

who whispers evil suggestions and thoughts into people’s chests and controls their feelings and thoughts.

“from among the jinn and mankind”

from the devils among the jinn and mankind.

passages.heading: Discuss

*Soorat Al-Kawthar* **Explained**

{{Q:108:1-3}}

“We have bestowed on you abundant good”

We have given you, Messenger, immeasurable, abundant good in this life and the life to come, part of which is River Al-Kawthar in Paradise.

“So pray to your Lord and sacrifice to Him”

Therefore, sincerely pray to your Lord and worship Him alone, and sacrifice to Him, pronouncing Allah’s name alone when slaughtering animals, in gratitude to Him for the honour and good He has bestowed on you.

“He who hates you is the one who is truly cut off”

*Shaani’aka*: The one who hates you and hates the true religion you have brought.

The one who hates you and hates the true religion you have brought is the most disgraced and contemptible, whose mention is short-lived and who is cut off from all good.

passages.heading: Benefits of Faith
passages.text:
* **Getting to know Allah Almighty:** A believer gets to know his Lord and His names, attributes and actions, so much so that he becomes more attached to Him.
* **Glorying Allah:** the more a believer gets to know his Lord, the more he extols and loves Him, the more he hopes for His mercy and the more God-fearing he becomes.
* **Getting to know Allah’s graciousness to His servants:** for sending messengers to them and divine books to them to guide them to the true religion.
* **Loving the angels:** for worshipping Allah and showing obedience to Him.
* **Loving Allah’s Messengers:** Allah Almighty chose them to convey His message to people.
* **Diligent worship:** the stronger the faith, the more worship one performs.
* **A truly happy life:** A believer is content with what Allah has apportioned to him and knows that whatever calamities befall him in this world elevate his rank and efface his sins. He also hopes for the bliss He has prepared for the believers in the life to come.
* **Not to be deluded by this world:** The life of this world is temporary and only serves as a means to eternal life in the hereafter.
* **Exposing myths:** Faith exposes and nullifies many myths.
* **Entering Paradise:** This is the abode of eternal bliss which Allah Almighty has prepared for His believing servants.

passages.heading: 1 Islam is a Universal Religion
passages.text: Islam is not only for the Arabs; rather, it is the religion that Allah Almighty has approved for all mankind. Addressing His Messenger Muhammad ﷺ, the Almighty says, {{Q:21:107}} (*Soorat Al-Anbiyaa’, 21:107*). Thus, Prophet Muhammad ﷺ is a mercy to all people without exception, guiding them to the path of faith; and, of all laws, his law reflects all aspects of mercy for people.

passages.heading: 2 Islam Wipes out the Sins Committed before It
passages.text: If a person sincerely embraces Islam, the Most Gracious and the Most Merciful God will forgive him all his past sins, and this is one of the outstanding merits of Islam. The Almighty says to His Prophet ﷺ, {{Q:8:38}} (Soorat Al-Anfaal, 8:38). A man once showed interest in Islam, and so he went to the Prophet ﷺ but he stipulated that Allah should forgive him his past sins. The Prophet ﷺ gave him the good news, saying, “Don’t you know that Islam wipes out all the sins committed before it?” (Reported by Muslim; No. 121).

passages.heading: 3 Islam is the Final Religion
passages.text: Allah Almighty has made Islam an extension of the previous divinely revealed religions and has approved and chosen it for all mankind until the end of the world. Thus, it is the only true religion on the face of the earth. The Almighty says, {{Q:3:85}} (Soorat Aal-’Imraan, 3:85).

passages.heading: Why Should I Embrace Islam?
passages.text:
Some people may ask: Why should I embrace Islam?

The answer is: I must do so for a number of reasons, including the following:

1. Islam is the religion that Allah has approved and chosen for His servants and will not accept any other religion. The Almighty says, {{Q:3:85}} (Soorat Aal-’Imraan, 3:85).

2. Islam is the religion of all the prophets and commands its adherents to believe in all of them without exception. Allah says, {{Q:2:136}} (Soorat Al-Baqarah, 2:136).
The difference between prophets lies only in the laws relating to people’s actions, as the Almighty says, {{Q:5:48}} (Soorat Al-Maa’idah, 5:48) That is, for each nation before Islam, Allah appointed a law to which people referred for their disputes and a way of life whereby they drew near to Him. Thus, followers of every prophet had their respective laws and regulations, but the set of beliefs to which prophets called their people was the same. Then Allah sent the last prophet and messenger, Muhammad ﷺ, with the final divine laws, and thus the only religion acceptable to Allah is Islam.

passages.heading: Introduction
passages.text: Since ancient times, people on this earth have led different lives with varying living standards. Some are very well-to-do; others are destitute and can barely find anything to eat. This is one of Allah’s ways in this universe. Islam enjoins the wealthy to pay a certain percentage of their wealth to the poor to relieve them of the burden of poverty and urges Muslims to spend more of what they are required to spend, promising them great rewards for doing so both in this life and after death. It also urges them to give charity to the needy at all times and on every occasion and encourages them to feed the hungry and clothe the naked in order for the Muslim community to become close-knit, just as Allah Almighty wants it to be. In this lesson, we are going to learn about the Islamic ruling on *zakaat*, the manner of paying it and the types of wealth upon which it is due.

passages.heading: Introduction
passages.text: Islam enjoins purity and cleanliness on its adherents and stresses that they must take good care of their personal hygiene and considers this matter one of the apparent rituals of religion and a requisite for the validity of many acts of worship. Indeed, observing purity and cleanliness is one of the characteristics of believers, which distinguishes them from others. In this lesson, we are going to learn the meaning of purity, its types, and some rulings on it.

passages.heading: The Requirements of the Two Testimonies of Faith
passages.text: It is not enough to verbally declare the two testimonies of faith. In addition to this, it is imperative to know what they mean and to meet their requirements. The testimony that there is no god but Allah requires us to reject everything that is worshipped besides or instead of Allah, to firmly believe that Allah alone is our Lord and Cherisher and the One True God worthy of worship and to worship Him sincerely. Allah Almighty says, {{Q:2:256}} (Soorat Al-Baqarah, 2:256) The testimony that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah requires us to believe what he says, do what he commands and avoid what he forbids and worship Allah only according to his instructions.

passages.heading: Introduction
passages.text: Islam is the religion with which Allah sent Muhammad ﷺ and is an extension of the same religion with which all the previous messengers came. It is essentially based on the belief that Allah Almighty is the only deity deserving of worship, who has no partners or assistants whatsoever in His kingdom, and who has no intermediaries between Him and His servants. The Almighty says, {{Q:3:85}} (*Soorat Aal-’Imraan, 3:85*) The Prophet ﷺ also said, “By Him in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, any person of this Community, Jew or Christian, who hears of me and dies without believing in what I have been sent with will be among the dwellers of Hell” (*Saheeh Muslim;* No. 153).

passages.heading: What Are the Conditions for Islamic Slaughter?
passages.text:
Islamic slaughter is one that satisfies the following conditions:

1. The person undertaking the slaughtering process must be Muslim, Jew or Christian who has reached the age of discretion and carries out this act for the intended purpose.
2. The tool used for slaughter must be suitable for the intended purpose, causes blood to flow and sharp, such as a knife. It is forbidden to use anything that may kill the animal due to its heavy weight, hit its head to death or render it unconscious by resorting to electric stunning, for instance.
3. The name of Allah must be pronounced by saying *Bismillaah* (in the name of Allah) at the time of slaughtering the animal.
4. Cutting what must be cut in the Islamic slaughter, namely, the oesophagus, the throat, and the two jugular veins, or just three of these four.

passages.heading: Islamic Rulings Pertaining to Meat Served in Restaurants and Shops
passages.text:
1. The meat of animals that are slaughtered by other than a Muslim or a member of the People of the Book (a Christian or a Jew), such as a Buddhist, or a Hindu is strictly forbidden. This includes meat served in restaurants and shops in countries where Muslims or People of the Book constitute a minority.
2. The meat of animals killed by a Muslim or a member of the People of the Book is lawful based on textual evidence to this effect in the Qur’an.
3. The meat of animals that are not killed according to Islamic law, such as by electrocution and drowning, is strictly forbidden.
4. The general rule is that it is permissible to consume the flesh of animals slaughtered by People of the Book as well as meat of animals generally found in their restaurants and shops, making sure, however, to invoke Allah’s name at the time of eating (that is, by saying *Bismillaah*), but it is better for Muslims to eat only meat that has been proven to be lawful (*halaal*).

passages.text:
* **Engaging in the worship of Almighty Allah**  
  This is expressed by the intention to act in obedience to Allah Almighty and to draw closer to Him

* **by removing ritual impurity**  
  Ritual impurity (*hadath*) refers to anything that takes place in the body, thus rendering purity invalid

* **and physical impurities**  
  Physical impurity (*najaasah*) refers to all physical substances which Islam considers impure, such as urine and faeces, and commands us to remove.

passages.heading: Types of Purification
passages.text:
Purification falls into two types:

**Physical Purification**

This means the removal of impurities and the cleansing of the area affected by them

**Moral Purification**

This means the removal of those things that prevent one from performing the prayer, by washing certain parts of the body or the entire body.

Physical purification may be undertaken either by *wudoo’* or *ghusl*

*Wudoo’* (partial ablutions): the ritual washing of certain parts of the body with water

*Ghusl* (full ablutions/bath): the ritual washing of the entire body with water.

Purification must be undertaken with pure water, such as seawater, river water, well water, or any other water that has not been mixed with impurity.

passages.heading: Domains of Good Moral Character in Islam:
passages.text:
Good moral character in Islam is not restricted to one domain; rather, it covers many of them, namely:

- Good moral character vis-à-vis Allah Almighty, such as by devoting oneself sincerely to Him and showing total obedience to Him.
- Good moral character vis-à-vis the Prophet ﷺ, such as by loving him, respecting him, showing politeness when talking about him and invoking Allah’s peace and blessings upon him when his name is mentioned.
- Good moral character vis-à-vis Allah’s laws, such as by honouring and obeying them.
- Good moral character vis-à-vis oneself, such as by gently encouraging oneself to show obedience to Allah and firmly avoiding laziness in this respect.
- Good moral character vis-à-vis others, such as by being honest and trustworthy.
- Good moral character vis-à-vis animals, such as by showing kindness to them and not being cruel to them.
- Good moral character vis-à-vis the environment, such as by preserving it, planting trees and not being extravagant with its natural resources.

passages.heading: The Virtue of Reading/Reciting the Qur’an
passages.text:
- The Prophet ﷺ said, “If anyone reads/recites one single letter in Allah’s Book, he will be credited with a good deed, and a good deed gets a tenfold reward. I do not say that *alif*, *laam*, *meem* are one letter; rather, *alif* is a letter, *laam* is a letter and *meem* is a letter” (Reported by At-Tirmidhee; No. 2910 with an authentic chain of narrators).

- The Prophet ﷺ also said, “Read the Qur’an, for it will come on the Day of Resurrection as an intercessor for those who read it.” (Reported by Muslim; No. 804).

passages.heading: The Criterion of Superiority in Islam
passages.text:
Piety is the criterion whereby Allah grants superiority to some over others. Superiority among Muslims can only be attained through strong faith, not one’s appearance, lineage, colour, or wealth. Allah Almighty says, {{Q:49:13}} (Soorat Al-Hjuraat, 49:13).

The Prophet ﷺ said: “O people! Your Lord is one and your father [Adam] is one. An Arab has no superiority over a non-Arab, nor does a non-Arab have any superiority over an Arab; a white person has no superiority over a black person, nor does a black person have any superiority over a white person except in piety.” (Reported by Al-Bayhaqee in Shu’ab al-Eemaan; No. 4774).

passages.heading: Good Moral Character in Islam
passages.text:
- Good moral character occupies a lofty position in Islam, as it is one of the important objectives of *Sharee‘ah* and one of the goals behind the Prophet’s mission.
- Good moral character is closely linked to faith, and the believers with complete faith are those who demonstrate the best moral character.
- A Muslim will be rewarded for his good manners, just as he will be rewarded for the prayer and fasting.

passages.heading: Soorat Al-Kawthar (Abundant Good)
passages.text:
*Soorat Al-Kawthar* **Explained**

{{Q:108:1-3}}

“We have bestowed on you abundant good”

We have given you, Messenger, immeasurable, abundant good in this life and the life to come, part of which is River Al-Kawthar in Paradise.

“So pray to your Lord and sacrifice to Him”

Therefore, sincerely pray to your Lord and worship Him alone, and sacrifice to Him, pronouncing Allah’s name alone when slaughtering animals, in gratitude to Him for the honour and good He has bestowed on you.

“He who hates you is the one who is truly cut off”

*Shaani’aka*: The one who hates you and hates the true religion you have brought.

The one who hates you and hates the true religion you have brought is the most disgraced and contemptible, whose mention is short-lived and who is cut off from all good.

passages.heading: The Blessing of Right Guidance
passages.text: Whoever knows the purpose of his existence and the outcome that awaits people on the Day of Resurrection is bound to realise that the greatest blessing that Allah has ever bestowed upon people is that of guidance to the true religion and righteous deeds. Therefore, Allah Almighty has enjoined His servants to ask Him in their prayer to guide them to the straight path—the religion of Islam which leads to Allah’s good pleasure.

passages.heading: Learning Your religion
passages.text:
- A Muslim is required to learn his religion based on sound knowledge in order to worship his Lord properly.
- The Prophet ﷺ urges us to study and understand our religion. He once said, “When Allah wishes to bestow His favour on someone, He makes him understand the religion.” (Reported by Al-Bukhaaree; No. 71).
- The Prophet ﷺ states that acquiring religious knowledge leads to Paradise. He once said, “Whoever treads a path in search of knowledge, Allah will ease the way to Paradise for him.” (Saheeh Ibn Hibbaan; No. 84).

passages.heading: What Is the Qur’an?
passages.text:
The Holy Qur’an is the Word of Allah Almighty that He revealed to His Messenger, Muhammad ﷺ. It is the last of Allah’s revealed books, and there is no other book after it.

The revealed books are the books that Allah Almighty revealed to His prophets.
A Muslim believes that these books were revealed by Allah Almighty, and that Allah spoke in them in a manner that befits Him. These books include Az-Zaboor (the Psalms), which He revealed to Daawood (David) عليه السلام; At-Tawraat (the Torah), which He revealed to Moosaa (Moses) عليه السلام and Al-Injeel (the Gospel), which He revealed to Jesus, عليه السلام. All these books have undergone alteration and corruption through the ages.

passages.heading: Lesson 1
passages.text: ## Learn about the Holy Qur’an

passages.heading: The Qur’an is Food for the Soul and Mind
passages.text:
The Holy Qur’an addresses both people’s minds and souls. It addresses the mind by:

- encouraging them to use logical reasoning on the various issues. The Almighty says, {{Q:21:22}} (Soorat Al-Anbiyyaa’, 21:22).
- calling them to exercise their intellects and contemplate His signs and the proofs of His power. The Almighty says, {{Q:2:219}} (Soorat Al-Baqarah, 2:219).
- reproving those who do not use their intellects to reflect on His signs. The Almighty says, {{Q:25:44}} (Soorat Al-Furqaan, 25: 44).

It also addresses the soul and emotions by:

- spotlighting and depicting human feelings in many cases. The Almighty says, {{Q:2:165}} (Soorat Al-Baqarah, 2:165).
- calling attention to human emotions and pointing out their good and bad effects. The Almighty says, {{Q:5:82}} (Soorat Al-Maa’idah, 5:82).
- commanding Muslims to exercise kindness and gentleness when inviting others to Islam. The Almighty says, {{Q:16:125}} (Soorat An-Nahl, 16: 125).
- incorporating aspects of faith into verses on legal rules. The Almighty says, {{Q:4:94}} (Soorat An-Nisaa’, 4:94).
- using moving words that evoke genuine emotions. The Almighty says, {{Q:24:22}} (Soorat An-Noor, 24:22).

passages.heading: The Qur’an is Food for the Soul and Mind
passages.text: It may at times address the mind and the soul at the same time in one single verse which not only convinces the mind through logical reasoning but also arouses human passions. The Almighty says, {{Q:35:3}} (Soorat Faaṭir, 35:3).

passages.heading: *Soorat Al-Kaafiroon* Explained
passages.text:
{{Q:109:1-6}}

“Say: Unbelievers!”

Say, Messenger, to those who disbelieve in Allah and His Messenger: You unbelievers.

“I do not worship what you worship”

I do not worship the false gods, such as idols, that you worship.

“nor do you worship what I worship”

nor do you worship the True God whom I worship, and who alone is worthy of worship.

“I will never worship what you worship”

I will never worship the false gods that you worship.

“nor will you ever worship what I worship”

nor will you ever worship the True God whom I worship, and who alone is worthy of worship.

Al-kaafir: The person who does not proclaim pure monotheism and does not follow the divine message Prophet Muhammad ﷺ has brought.

“You have your religion, and I have my religion”

You have your religion to which you adhere, and I have my religion to which I adhere.

passages.text: Islam respects the customs and traditions of all peoples and does not require them to change them unless they contravene any of the teachings of Islam.
