passages.text:
A man's *'awrah* that must be covered extends from the navel to the knees. A woman must cover herself entirely in the presence of men not related to her; as for men to whom she is related and is forbidden to marry, such as her father, son and brother, she may appear before them as she would normally do in front of other women, showing such parts of her body as the face, hair, the neck and feet.

- Clothing that reveals the *'awrah* and does not conceal it
- Clothing that involves dressing like or imitating the opposite sex, such as when men dress like women and vice versa.
- Clothing that is worn with an air of pride and conceit
- Extravagant clothing
- Men are particularly forbidden to wear silk clothing or adorn themselves with gold or silver jewellery.
- Clothing that involves imitation of the dress traditionally worn by non-Muslims and specific to a certain religion, such as the type of clothing worn by monks and priests

3. Deliberate vomiting.

A woman’s fast is broken as a result of:

4. Menstrual or postnatal bleeding.

passages.heading: *Soorat An-Naas* Explained
passages.text:
“Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of mankind”

Say, Messenger, “I seek refuge and protection in Allah, the Lord of all mankind, who alone has power over all things.

The King of all people, who manages all their affairs.

passages.heading: Benefits of Faith
passages.text:
* **Getting to know Allah Almighty:** A believer gets to know his Lord and His names, attributes and actions, so much so that he becomes more attached to Him.
* **Glorying Allah:** the more a believer gets to know his Lord, the more he extols and loves Him, the more he hopes for His mercy and the more God-fearing he becomes.
* **Getting to know Allah’s graciousness to His servants:** for sending messengers to them and divine books to them to guide them to the true religion.
* **Loving the angels:** for worshipping Allah and showing obedience to Him.
* **Loving Allah’s Messengers:** Allah Almighty chose them to convey His message to people.
* **Diligent worship:** the stronger the faith, the more worship one performs.
* **A truly happy life:** A believer is content with what Allah has apportioned to him and knows that whatever calamities befall him in this world elevate his rank and efface his sins. He also hopes for the bliss He has prepared for the believers in the life to come.
* **Not to be deluded by this world:** The life of this world is temporary and only serves as a means to eternal life in the hereafter.
* **Exposing myths:** Faith exposes and nullifies many myths.
* **Entering Paradise:** This is the abode of eternal bliss which Allah Almighty has prepared for His believing servants.

passages.heading: 1 Islam is a Universal Religion
passages.text: Islam is not only for the Arabs; rather, it is the religion that Allah Almighty has approved for all mankind. Addressing His Messenger Muhammad ﷺ, the Almighty says, {{Q:21:107}} (*Soorat Al-Anbiyaa’, 21:107*). Thus, Prophet Muhammad ﷺ is a mercy to all people without exception, guiding them to the path of faith; and, of all laws, his law reflects all aspects of mercy for people.

passages.heading: 2 Islam Wipes out the Sins Committed before It
passages.text: If a person sincerely embraces Islam, the Most Gracious and the Most Merciful God will forgive him all his past sins, and this is one of the outstanding merits of Islam. The Almighty says to His Prophet ﷺ, {{Q:8:38}} (Soorat Al-Anfaal, 8:38). A man once showed interest in Islam, and so he went to the Prophet ﷺ but he stipulated that Allah should forgive him his past sins. The Prophet ﷺ gave him the good news, saying, “Don’t you know that Islam wipes out all the sins committed before it?” (Reported by Muslim; No. 121).

passages.heading: 3 Islam is the Final Religion
passages.text: Allah Almighty has made Islam an extension of the previous divinely revealed religions and has approved and chosen it for all mankind until the end of the world. Thus, it is the only true religion on the face of the earth. The Almighty says, {{Q:3:85}} (Soorat Aal-’Imraan, 3:85).

passages.heading: Forbidden Types of Clothing
passages.text:
With your partners, discuss the reasons why some types of clothing are forbidden in Islam.

The Prophet ﷺ forbade men from imitating women and women from imitating men. This prohibition includes the type of clothing and the manner of speech. Islam strictly forbids imitation of the opposite sex, considering it a major sin that invites Allah’s punishment unless one repents and desists from committing it. Islam enjoins men to ensure that their true nature and appearance are distinct from that of women, and vice versa, which clearly testifies to common sense and sound logic.

passages.heading: Some of the Ultimate Objectives and Benefits of Fasting
passages.text:
- To attain true piety by increasing acts of worship and avoiding sins as much as possible.
- To experience the pangs of hunger from which the poor and needy often suffer.
- To train oneself to bring one’s whims and desires under control.

Allah has enjoined fasting on Muslims, just as He prescribed it on the other nations before them:
{{Q:2:183}} (Soorat Al-Baqarah, 2:183).

passages.heading: The Blessed Month of Ramadaan
passages.text:
Ramadaan is the ninth month of the Islamic lunar calendar. It is a blessed month, in which Allah revealed the Qur’an to His Messenger, Muhammad ﷺ. Allah has promised to forgive all the past sins of those who fast during the daylight hours and stands in prayer at night throughout this month. The Almighty has also distinguished it with a night that is better than a thousand months. It is called *Laylat-ul-Qadr* (The Night of Decree; also called the Night of Power), and whoever spends it remembering Allah and standing in prayer will have all his past sins forgiven.

Muslims perform the *Taraaweeh* prayer in the month of Ramadaan. It is one of the Prophet’s practices (*Sunnah*) that is particularly associated with it, and it is performed after *'Ishaa’* (late evening) prayer.

passages.heading: The Types of People Who Are Exempt from Fasting
passages.text:
Allah Almighty has permitted several types of people to break their fast during the day in Ramadaan. They are:

1. Sick people whose medical condition is bound to be further worsened by fasting.
2. The elderly who are unable to fast.
3. Travellers, while moving from one place to another.
4. Menstruating women and women experiencing postnatal bleeding.
5. Pregnant and nursing mothers if they fear it would be dangerous for them or for their babies if they fast.

passages.heading: Important Notes Related to Fasting
passages.text:
- Whoever breaks his fast in Ramadaan for a legitimate reason must make up for every day he has missed after than Ramadaan.
- If a sick person breaks the fast because of an incurable disease, he is exempt from fasting the month of Ramadaan, but he must feed one poor person for each day he does not fast.
- If a Muslim cannot possibly fast due to old age, he is exempt from fasting the month of Ramadaan but he must feed one poor person for each day he does not fast.

**Muslims break their fast as soon as the call to *Maghrib* (sunset) prayer is announced, and many Muslims are very keen to share their Ramadaan breakfast, or *iftar*, with fellow Muslims.**

passages.heading: The Manner of Performing the Full Ritual Bath (*Ghusl*)
passages.text:
If a Muslim wants to perform *ghusl*, he must do the following:

1. He intends in his heart to perform *ghusl* and washes out his private parts with water.
2. He performs *wudoo’* like the one he performs before the prayer.
3. He washes his entire body with water.

passages.heading: What are the types of wealth upon which *zakaat* is due?
passages.text:
- **Gold and silver**
- **All types of currency (banknotes and coins)**
- **Farm produce (crops and fruit)**
- **Grazing livestock**

Grazing livestock: This refers to camels, cattle, sheep and goats.

- **Commercial commodities**

Commercial commodities: all properties owned with the aim of investing them in trade. They generally include assets, such as a house, a shop, a car and an animal.

passages.heading: How Do We Pay *Zakaat* Due on Cash?
passages.text: A Muslim pays *zakaat* due on his cash once a year. 2.5% of its value must be given out as *zakaat*.

passages.heading: How Do We Pray?
passages.text:
1. He intends in his heart to pray.
2. He stands facing the *qiblah*, raises his hands up to the level of the shoulders or ears, and says, “*Allaahu akbar* Allah is the Greatest.”
3. He places his right hand on his left hand. Then he recites one of the opening supplications, such as, Subhaanak-Allaahumma wa bi hamdika, wa tabaarak-asmuka, wa ta’aalaa jadduka, wa laa ilaaha ghayruka “Glory be to You, O Allah; Yours is the praise, blessed is Your name, exalted is Your majesty, and there is no god besides You.” Then he says, A’oodhu billaahi min-ash-shaytaan-ir-rajeem. Bismillaah-ir-rahmaan-ir-raheem “I seek Allah’s protection from Satan, who has been expelled from His mercy. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.” Then he recites *Soorat Al-Faatihah* and says after it, “*Aameen*”, which means “Answer our supplications, O Allah”. After that, he recites whatever number of verses of the Qur’an as is easy for him, even if it is one verse.
4. He says, “Allaahu akbar Allah is the Greatest” while raising his hands up to the level of his shoulders or ears, and bows down, lowering his head and back and keeping them straight at a right angle, placing the palms of his hands on the knees. He says three times while in this position, “Subhaana rabbiy-al-’adheem Glory be to my Lord, the Almighty.”

7. He says, Allaahu akbar “Allah is the Greatest” and sits down on the left leg while keeping the right foot upright with the toes pointing towards the *qiblah*, resting his hands on his thighs close to the knees. He says while in this position, “My Lord, forgive me.”

8. He says, Allaahu akbar “Allah is the Greatest” and prostrates himself again just as he has done the first time, saying the same thing.

9. Then he rises to the standing position again, saying, Allaahu akbar “Allah is the Greatest” as he does so, and performs the second unit (*rak’ah*) in exactly the same way as the first one.

passages.heading: مجالات الأخلاق في الإسلام:
passages.text:
الأخلاق في الإسلام ليس لها مجالٌ واحد فقط، بل لها مجالات متعددة، وهي:

- الأخلاق مع الله عز وجل؛ كتقوى الله والإخلاص له.
- الأخلاق مع النبي ﷺ؛ كمحبته واحترامه ونصرته بالنفس والمال.
- الأخلاق مع الشريعة، كالتسليم لأحكام الشرع وتوقيرها.
- الأخلاق مع النفس؛ كالصبر والحلم.
- الأخلاق مع الآخرين؛ كالصدق والأمانة.
- الأخلاق مع الحيوانات؛ كالرعاية وعدم ضربها وتعذيبها.
- الأخلاق مع البيئة؛ كالمحافظة عليها من الفساد، وغرس الأشجار، وعدم الإسراف في خيراتها.

passages.heading: صلاة الجمعة:
passages.text:
- فرض الله عز وجل على المسلمين أداء صلاة خاصة يوم الجمعة تسمى (صلاة الجمعة)، ولها صفة خاصة وشروط خاصة، وهي بدل عن صلاة الظهر لذلك اليوم.
- يجتمع المسلمون من أجلها في المسجد، يخطب فيهم إمام المسجد خطبتين، ثم يصلي بهم ركعتين، يجهر فيها بقراءة القرآن.
- يشرع الاغتسال لحضور صلاة الجمعة، والتبكير لحضورها. ولا يجوز التخلف عنها إلا لعذر، ومن تخلّف عنها فإنه يصلي صلاة الظهر أربع ركعات، لا يجهر فيها بقراءة القرآن.
- لا تجب صلاة الجمعة على المرأة أو المسافر.

passages.heading: تمهيد
passages.text: كثيرًا ما يشعر المسلم بسكينة واطمئنان حين يتلو القرآن أو يتعبد الله تعالى بالصلاة أو بغيرها من العبادات، هذا الشعور الذي يعلو بالبعض فيصل بهم إلى مراحل متقدمة من الانشراح والسعادة هو لُب الإيمان الذي يدفع المسلم إلى أن يجعل حياته كلها لله يمتثل فيها أوامره برغبة وحُب ويجتنب نواهيه بانقيادٍ وطاعة مُطلقة. وفي هذا الدرس سنتعرف على مفهوم الإيمان وأركانه وثمراته.

passages.heading: الأخلاق في الإسلام:
passages.text:
- الأخلاق الحسنة لها مكانة عظيمة في الإسلام، فهي مقصد مهم من مقاصد الشرعية الإسلامية، وهدف من أهداف بعثة النبي ﷺ.
- الأخلاق لها ارتباط وثيق بالإيمان، فأكمل المؤمنين إيمانًا أحسنهم أخلاقًا.
- يؤجر العبد على حسن خلقه، كما يؤجر على الصلاة والصوم.

الجهة التي يجب على المصلي التوجه لها هي:
أ) جهة الشمال.
ب) جهة الغرب.
ج) جهة الكعبة.

يقول المصلي في سجوده:
أ) سبحان ربي العظيم.
ب) سبحان ربي الأعلى.

passages.heading: The Meaning of Worship
passages.text: By worship is meant everything that Allah has enjoined on us for us to draw closer to Him. It comprises all words and deeds that Allah loves, whether they are outward like the physical acts of worship, such as the prayer and pilgrimage, or inward, like the acts of worship involving the heart, such as love of Allah, fearing His punishment and hoping for His mercy. A person can transform everyday habits into acts of worship simply by having a good intention. If, for instance, he eats, drinks and sleeps with the intention of gaining enough strength to worship Allah better, he will certainly be rewarded for doing so

passages.heading: Good Moral Character in Islam
passages.text:
- Good moral character occupies a lofty position in Islam, as it is one of the important objectives of *Sharee‘ah* and one of the goals behind the Prophet’s mission.
- Good moral character is closely linked to faith, and the believers with complete faith are those who demonstrate the best moral character.
- A Muslim will be rewarded for his good manners, just as he will be rewarded for the prayer and fasting.

passages.heading: Introduction
passages.text: *Wudoo’* is very important in Islam because it is closely connected with the ritual prayer, which is itself the greatest ritual in Islam, hence the importance of learning it and performing it correctly. In this lesson, we are going to learn about the meaning of *wudoo’*, things that require us to perform it, things that make it invalid, and the proper manner of performing it.

passages.heading: Introduction
passages.text: Fasting is one of the acts of worship that Allah Almighty has enjoined on all nations. In Islam, a Muslim performs this religious duty in obedience to Allah Almighty. In this lesson, we are going to learn about what fasting means, the things that render it invalid and some of the most important rulings regarding it.

passages.heading: The Qur’an is a Way of Life
passages.text: A Muslim should be keen on reading/reciting the Holy Qur’an and studying the rules it prescribes.

passages.heading: Certain Rulings on Purification
passages.text:
- It is a general Islamic rule that things are naturally clean and pure unless stated otherwise by Islam.
- It would suffice to cleanse the body or clothing of impurities by removing them with water or any cleaning substance that would serve the purpose.
- It would be better for a person who uses the toilet to cleanse the place of urine and faeces with water. It is also permissible for him to cleanse himself with tissues or any other material that serves to remove impurity.

passages.heading: Introduction
passages.text: *Soorat Al-Faatihah* is the greatest *soorah* in the Qur’an. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ emphasized its virtues and greatness in many of his sayings. It is the *soorah* that every Muslim must learn by heart because it is the only *soorah* that he must recite in every single prayer. In this lesson, we are going to study this *soorah*, memorize its verses and understand its meanings, in addition to studying several other short *suwar* (sing, *soorah*) that have great significance.

passages.heading: What Is Fasting?
passages.text:
Fasting: an act of worship whereby a Muslim abstains from food, drink and sexual intercourse from dawn to sunset.

Fasting in the month of Ramadaan is the fourth pillar of Islam.

passages.heading: Introduction
passages.text: In his life, a Muslim performs a number of acts of worship whereby he draws closer to his Creator, Glory is to Him. We do such acts to glorify Allah Almighty and submit to Him alone. The more a Muslim’s heart glorifies Allah, Exalted be He, the greater the effect of doing so is on his worship. A true Muslim dedicates all life, including the time he spends at work, sleeping and having fun, to Allah Almighty, bearing in mind the verse: {{Q:6:162-163}} (Soorat Al-An’aam, 6:162-163) In this lesson, we are going to learn about the meaning of worship, its types, the conditions that must be met for it to be accepted, and its levels.

passages.heading: Types of Acts of Worship
passages.text:
Acts of worship fall into different categories:

| Acts of worship involving the heart | A Muslim performs these with his heart. Examples include love, fear, hope and *khushoo’*. |
| --- | --- |
| Physical acts of worship | A Muslim performs these physically. Examples include the prayer, *zakaat* and pilgrimage. |
| Acts that are abandoned in obedience to Allah | A Muslim draws closer to his Lord by abandoning the acts He has forbidden him, such as drinking alcohol and committing adultery, or by refraining from certain permissible acts at specific times, such as abstaining from food and drink while fasting. |

> *Ar-Rajaa’*(Hope): This refers to rejoicing in Allah’s grace and hoping for His benevolence, while at the same time ensuring proper reliance on Allah by doing good deeds to the best of one’s ability.
> 
> *Al-khushoo’* is a state of utter humility and calmness and deep concentration into which one gets while performing an act of worship, such as the prayer, bringing about outward composure and tranquillity.

passages.heading: Conditions for Acts of Worship to Be Accepted
passages.text:
For an act of worship to be accepted, two conditions must be fulfilled:

The first condition: It has to be done sincerely for the sake of Allah to draw closer to alone, without showing off.

The second condition: It has to be done in the manner Allah has enjoined it and exactly as it was performed by the Prophet ﷺ.

> *Aririyyaa’* (showing off) is the act of doing an act of worship only to be seen and praised by people for doing it.

passages.heading: Discuss
passages.text: What will a person who shows off his acts of worship lose by not intending to do them for the sake of Allah?

passages.heading: Introduction
passages.text: Islam urges its followers to observe high moral character. The Prophet ﷺ stressed the importance of morals in many of his traditions, combining many acts of worship Muslims perform with good moral character. Islam promises a Muslim who displays such good character great rewards both in this world and the hereafter. In this lesson, we are going to learn about the importance of good moral character in Islam, as well as some of its virtues.

passages.heading: Discuss
passages.text: How should a Muslim’s moral character be with others? Do you think that such good character has an impact on their opinion about Islam?

passages.heading: Some Virtues of Good Moral Character
passages.text:
- The Prophet ﷺ informs us that the act that will cause people to enter Paradise the most will be piety and good character.
- He ﷺ states that the heaviest of a person’s good deeds that will be placed on the scales of deeds on the Day of Resurrection will be good moral character.
- He ﷺ further states that the closest believers to him on the Day of Resurrection will be those who possess good moral character.

> **The scales of deeds:** This will be on the Day of Resurrection when a person’s good and bad deeds will be weighed in a balance, whose shape or size none knows but Allah. Those whose good deeds outweigh their bad deeds will be admitted into Paradise, but those whose bad deeds outweigh their bad deeds will be sent to Hell.

passages.heading: The Meaning of *Wudoo’*
passages.text: *Wudoo’*: The ritual of washing the face, hands, and feet, and wiping over the head in a specific manner.

passages.heading: Things Which Require Us to Perform *Wudoo’*:
passages.text:
These are those things for which *wudoo’* is necessary and must be performed before engaging in them and which we are forbidden to do once *wudoo’* is broken. They are:

> *Hadath*: This is the state of having our ablutions broken and thus prevents us from performing the prayer before purifying ourselves. It is of two types: one requires us to perform only partial ablutions (*wudoo’*) to remove it, and the other requires us to perform full ablutions (*ghusl*).

1. the prayer
2. circumambulation around the Ka’bah (*tawaaf*)
3. touching the Qur’an

passages.heading: Lesson 3
passages.text: ### *Wudoo’* (Partial Ablutions)

passages.heading: Why Do We Fast?
passages.text: Muslims fast in obedience to Allah Almighty and in response to His command.

passages.heading: Some of the Ultimate Objectives and Benefits of Fasting
passages.text:
- To attain true piety by increasing acts of worship and avoiding sins as much as possible.
- To experience the pangs of hunger from which the poor and needy often suffer.
- To train oneself to bring one’s whims and desires under control.

Allah has enjoined fasting on Muslims, just as He prescribed it on the other nations before them:
{{Q:2:183}} (Soorat Al-Baqarah, 2:183).

passages.heading: The Qur’an is a Way of Life
passages.text:
The Holy Qur’an is the Word of the Lord of all the worlds, who has created all mankind, knows them better than they know themselves and knows what benefits them and what harms them, hence the reason why Allah Almighty has made the Qur’an, which was the last of His revealed books, a didactic book which maps out a way of life for people, as evidenced by the following points:

- It deals with human life extensively, taking into account its three intrinsic spheres: personal life, family life and community life.
- Its deals with a wide array of matters, including, among other things, beliefs, acts of worship, customs, social and financial relations, man’s mental, emotional and physical states, international relations and peace and war.
- It promotes justice under all circumstances, even when dealing with enemies, and forbids injustice in all its forms.

> The Holy Qur’an maps out the way of life for people and defines and explains to them their rights and obligations with great flexibility, making its laws valid for all times and places.

passages.heading: Stories of the Prophets in the Qur’an
passages.text:
The Holy Qur’an is replete with stories of the previous prophets and their people, starting with Adam, and passing through Noah, Hud, Saalih, Shu’ayb, Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, Moses, Jesus, and other prophets and messengers, peace be upon them all. The Holy Qur’an mentions their stories for a number of reasons, including the following:

- to show that the religion of all the prophets is, in essence, the same and that its basis is to worship Allah Almighty alone.
- to give solace to Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and make him stand firm and steadfast, reminding him that prophets before him suffered the same hardships he himself was experiencing.
- to give comfort and solace to the believers, reminding them that even Allah’s honourable servants before them were afflicted with trials and tribulations.
- to afford people the opportunity to learn lessons from such true stories.

passages.heading: Things that render the Fast Invalid
passages.text:
The fasting person must abstain from several things which, if he does them, his fast will be invalid. They are:

1. Eating and drinking, including intravenous injections which have some nutritional value.
2. Deliberate seminal emission as a result of intercourse or any other means. Intercourse during the day in Ramadaan is a grave sin.
3. Deliberate vomiting.

A woman’s fast is broken as a result of:

4. Menstrual or postnatal bleeding.

8. He says, Allaahu akbar “Allah is the Greatest” and prostrates himself again just as he has done the first time, saying the same thing.

9. Then he rises to the standing position again, saying, Allaahu akbar “Allah is the Greatest” as he does so, and performs the second unit (*rak’ah*) in exactly the same way as the first one.

passages.heading: Soorat Al-Kawthar (Abundant Good)
passages.text:
*Soorat Al-Kawthar* **Explained**

{{Q:108:1-3}}

“We have bestowed on you abundant good”

We have given you, Messenger, immeasurable, abundant good in this life and the life to come, part of which is River Al-Kawthar in Paradise.

“So pray to your Lord and sacrifice to Him”

Therefore, sincerely pray to your Lord and worship Him alone, and sacrifice to Him, pronouncing Allah’s name alone when slaughtering animals, in gratitude to Him for the honour and good He has bestowed on you.

“He who hates you is the one who is truly cut off”

*Shaani’aka*: The one who hates you and hates the true religion you have brought.

The one who hates you and hates the true religion you have brought is the most disgraced and contemptible, whose mention is short-lived and who is cut off from all good.

passages.heading: What is Faith?
passages.text: Faith (*Eemaan* in Arabic) is to confess with one’s mouth and believe in one’s heart everything that has come from Allah, totally submit to His will, out of love, hope and fear, and translate that into reality. Allah Almighty says, {{Q:4:136}} (Soorat An-Nisaa’, 4:136)

passages.text:

These may, therefore, appear before him without covering those body parts that are not, according to the prevailing custom, generally covered in front of relatives but without excess and without exceeding the limits of decency. These body parts include the forearms, the neck and the hair. | Such a woman does not belong to the category of women known as *mahaarim* (sing. *mahram*) whether she is one of his relatives, such as his maternal or paternal uncle’s daughter, or she is not one of his relatives at all. Islam has laid down some criteria that govern a Muslim man’s relationship with such women. For instance, she must wear the modest Muslim style of dress (*hijaab*), and they must not be alone with each other in a place where no one can see them (*khalwah*). |

passages.heading: The Friday Prayer (Salaat-ul-Jumu’ah)
passages.text:
- Allah Almighty has enjoined Muslims to perform a special prayer on Friday, called *Salaat-ul-Jumu’ah* (the Friday prayer). It is performed in a special manner, has special conditions and takes the place of the daily *Dhuhr* (midday) prayer on this day.
- Muslims gather together to perform it in the mosque. The *imaam* delivers a two-section *khutbah* (sermon), then he leads them in a two-*rak’ahs* prayer in which he recites the Qur’an aloud.
- It is recommended to take a ritual bath (*ghusl*) to attend the Friday prayer and proceed early to the mosque. It is not permissible to miss it without a legitimate excuse, and if for any reason a person misses it he must perform the four-unit *Dhuhr* (midday) prayer instead but without reciting the Qur’an aloud.
- Women and people on a journey are exempt from performing the Friday prayer.

3. Islam is the way to happiness in this life and salvation in the life to come; therefore, those who believe in Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and follow him after his message has reached them will be saved; as for those who deny him, they will be doomed to divine punishment. The Almighty says, {{Q:3:85}} (*Soorat Aal-’Imraan, 3:85*) The Prophet ﷺ also said, “By Him in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, any person of this Community, Jew or Christian, who hears of me and dies without believing in what I have been sent with will be among the dwellers of Hell” (*Saheeh Muslim;* No. 153).

4. Islam gives conclusive answers to the big questions of human existence: Where did we come from? Why are we here? Where do we go after death?

5. Islam is in perfect harmony with the innate human nature (*fitrah*), beginning with the greatest value it embraces, namely the declaration of Allah’s unity, and ending with the rules of etiquette it teaches its adherents to enable them to attain great perfection in moral excellence.

passages.heading: Learning Your religion
passages.text:
- A Muslim is required to learn his religion based on sound knowledge in order to worship his Lord properly.
- The Prophet ﷺ urges us to study and understand our religion. He once said, “When Allah wishes to bestow His favour on someone, He makes him understand the religion.” (Reported by Al-Bukhaaree; No. 71).
- The Prophet ﷺ states that acquiring religious knowledge leads to Paradise. He once said, “Whoever treads a path in search of knowledge, Allah will ease the way to Paradise for him.” (Saheeh Ibn Hibbaan; No. 84).

passages.text:
Discuss with your classmates some of the challenges facing Muslims that prevent them from performing the prayers on time, and how to overcome these challenges.

passages.text:
*Soorat Al-’A<u>s</u>r* **Explained**

{{Q:103:1-3}}

“By the time”

Allah swears by the time in which people’s good and evil deeds take place.

“Truly man is in loss”

Mankind is indeed in sheer loss and ruin,

“except for those who believe and do good works; who exhort each other to justice and to fortitude”

except for those who believe in Allah, do righteous deeds, and urge one another to adhere to the truth and to be patient and steadfast in doing so.

passages.heading: Introduction
passages.text: A Muslim often experiences peace and tranquillity when he reads or recites the Qur’an or worships Allah Almighty by engaging in prayer or any other act of worship. This good feeling which elevates some to higher levels of happiness and joy is one of the significant effects of faith that motivates Muslims to dedicate all their lives to Allah, comply with His commands cheerfully and out of love and avoid what He forbids in utter submission and obedience. In this lesson, we are going to learn about the concept of faith and its pillars and benefits.

passages.heading: Discuss
passages.text: What is the difference between hope and fear?

passages.heading: The Pillars of Faith
passages.text:
The Muslim faith rests on six pillars, namely:

1. **Belief in Allah:** A Muslim believes that Allah Almighty exists and believes in His names and attributes. He equally believes that He is the Lord and sole Creator of this vast universe, to whom belongs everything in it, who manages all its affairs and provides sustenance to all His creation, that there is no god is worthy of worship besides or instead of Him and that He has perfect attributes.
2. **Belief in the angels:** A Muslim believes that the honourable angels exist, that it is Allah Almighty who created them and that they worship Him, execute His commands and never disobey Him. He also believes in their attributes and duties which are mentioned in the Book and the *Sunnah*.

passages.heading: Shirk
passages.text:
This means the act of holding someone or something as equal to Allah and directing acts of worship to them. It is a grave and an unforgivable sin. The Qur’an says, {{Q:4:48}} (Soorat An-Nisaa’, 4:48).

By the phrase “the Book and Sunnah” is meant the Noble Qur’an and the sayings of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, as they are the two main sources of legislation in Islam.

passages.heading: Women in Relation to a Man
passages.text: Women in relation to a man fall into three categories:

passages.heading: Muslim Women’s Modest Style of Dress (*Hijaab*)
passages.text:
Allah enjoins women to wear the *hijaab* because women enjoy natural beauty and attraction that could easily tempt men into sinful acts, more than the other way round. Women are to cover their entire bodies when in the presence of men who are not related to them, and they may choose any design or colour they like for their *hijaab* as long as the following four conditions are met:

| First Condition | Second Condition | Third condition | Fourth Condition |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| It must appropriately cover the parts of the body that must be covered in public. | It must hang loose and must not fit very closely to the body so that the shape of the body is not revealed. | It must not allow the wearer’s body to be seen through its fabric. | It must not be a type of clothing that is generally considered attractive. |

passages.heading: The Types of Blood that Are Naturally Discharged by Women
passages.text:
The blood that is naturally discharged by women is of two types:

| Menstrual blood | Postnatal blood |
| --- | --- |
| This is a natural type of blood that flows from a woman’s uterus every month during her menstrual cycle and usually lasts for a few days. | This bleeding takes place after giving birth and lasts for several days, up to 40 days. |

passages.heading: Islamic Rulings Pertaining to Menstrual and Postnatal Bleeding
passages.text:
Allah Almighty has prescribed several rulings relating to menstruating women and women experiencing their postnatal bleeding, including the following:

- They are exempt from performing the prayers during this period and do not have to make up for the prayers they have missed while in this state after the end of menstrual and postnatal bleeding.
- They are exempt from fasting and are not allowed to fast while in this state, but they must make up for the fasting days they have missed in Ramadaan.
- During this period, a husband must not have intercourse with his wife during her menstrual or postnatal period. He is allowed, however, to satisfy his sexual desire but without having intercourse.
- At the end of the menstrual and postnatal period, when bleeding stops completely, women must take a ritual bath (*ghusl*).

passages.heading: Who is the prophet of Islam?
passages.text: Muslims believe that Muhammad ﷺ is the Last Prophet whom Allah has sent to all mankind to call them to worship Allah alone and to declare that Muhammad is His Last Prophet. Allah Almighty says, {{Q:33:40}} (Soorat Al-Ahzaab, 33:40)

passages.heading: The Criterion of Superiority in Islam
passages.text:
Piety is the criterion whereby Allah grants superiority to some over others. Superiority among Muslims can only be attained through strong faith, not one’s appearance, lineage, colour, or wealth. Allah Almighty says, {{Q:49:13}} (Soorat Al-Hjuraat, 49:13).

The Prophet ﷺ said: “O people! Your Lord is one and your father [Adam] is one. An Arab has no superiority over a non-Arab, nor does a non-Arab have any superiority over an Arab; a white person has no superiority over a black person, nor does a black person have any superiority over a white person except in piety.” (Reported by Al-Bayhaqee in Shu’ab al-Eemaan; No. 4774).

passages.heading: The Pillars of Islam
passages.text:
Islam is built on five pillars:

Every Muslim must strictly adhere to these pillars to ensure he is practising Islam in full; negligence in one of these pillars is bound to render the way you practise Islam deficient.

1. The two testimonies of faith: To bear witness that none is worthy of worship except Allah and that Muhammad is His His Messenger
2. Establish the prayer: A Muslim must pray five times a day. These prayers will be explained in due course.
3. Paying zakaat
4. Fasting in the month of Ramadaan
5. Making the pilgrimage to Allah’s House

passages.heading: لماذا نحج؟
passages.text:
يحجّ المسلم إلى مكة المكرمة:

- استجابة لنداء الله تعالى بالحج إلى البيت الحرام.
- اهتداء بالأنبياء الكرام الذين حجّوا إلى البيت الحرام، وعلى رأسهم إبراهيم عليه السلام.
- الانشغال بالعبادة، فالحاج يمكث أيامًا متفرغًا للعبادة، ينتقل من عبادة إلى أخرى.
- الالتقاء بالمسلمين المجتمعين في المشاعر المقدسة، والتعرف عليهم، وبناء جسور التواصل معهم.

passages.heading: تمهيد
passages.text: حث الإسلام أتباعه على التحلي بالأخلاق الحسنة، وقد أرشد الرسول ﷺ إلى أهمية الأخلاق في كثير من الأحاديث النبوية، وقرن بين كثير من العبادات التي يؤديها المسلم وبين حسن الخلق، والمسلم ذو الأخلاق الحميدة موعود بأجور عظيمة في الدنيا والآخرة، وفي هذا الدرس سنتعرف على أهمية الأخلاق في الإسلام، مع بيان بعض فضائلها.

passages.heading: تمهيد
passages.text: منذ القدم والبشر على هذه الأرض يعيشون بمستويات مختلفة فمنهم الغني الذي يملك الكثير من الأموال، ومنهم الفقير الذي لا يجد قوته، وهي سُنة من سنن الله في هذا الكون، وقد أوجب الإسلام في أموال الأغنياء فرضًا يؤدونه إلى الفقراء ليعينوهم ويخففوا عن من وطأة الفقر، وحث على أن يبذل المسلم من أمواله أكثر مما يجب عليه وجعل جزاءً لذلك أجور عظيمة ينالها المسلم في حياته وبعد مماته. كما حثّ على الإحسان إلى الفقراء في كل وقت وفي كل مناسبة، ورغَّب في إطعام الجائعين، وكسوة العارين، كل هذا لأجل أن يتماسك المجتمع المسلم ويكونوا كما أراد الله عز وجل، وفي هذا الدرس سنتعرف على حكم الزكاة. وكيفيتها، والأموال التي تجب فيها.

passages.heading: تمهيد
passages.text: دعى الإسلام إلى الطهارة والنظافة، وأكد على المسلم أن يعتني بنظافته الشخصية، وجعل هذا الأمر من شعائر الدين، وربط صحة كثير من العبادات بتحقيق المسلم للطهارة، وهي من خصال المؤمن، ومن السمات التي يتميز بها المسلم عن غيره، وفي هذا الدرس سنتعرف على معنى الطهارة، وأنواعها، وبعض الأحكام المتعلقة بها.

passages.heading: تمهيد
passages.text: من عظمة الدين الإسلام أنه شامل لجميع نواحي حياة البشر، ومن ذلك اعتناؤه بضبط تعاملات الناس فيما بينهم، وحفظ حقوقهم، ومنع وقوع الظلم على أي منهم، ومن لوازم هذه العناية: سن القوانين والضوابط التي تحكم المعاملات المالية بينهم، وفي هذا الدرس سنتعرف على مجموعة من الأحكام المالية، وأسباب تحريم بعضها.

passages.heading: تمهيد
passages.text: يعتبر الصوم من العبادات التي فرضها الله عز وجل على جميع الأمم، وفي الإسلام فإن المسلم يؤدي هذه الفريضة طاعةً لله تعالى، وفي هذا الدرس سنتعرف على المراد من الصوم، وكيفيته، ومفسداته، وبعض أهم أحكامه.

passages.heading: مكانة المرأة في الإسلام:
passages.text:
من أمثلة الأحكام المتعلقة باحترام المرأة في الإسلام:
- أعطى الإسلام المرأة حقها من الميراث في قسمة عادلة كريمة، تساوي الرجل بالمرأة في مواضع، ويختلف نصيبها عنه في مواضع، بحسب قرابتها وتكاليف النفقة المناطة بها.
- ساوى بين الرجل والمرأة في شؤون كثيرة مختلفة ومن ذلك جميع التعاملات المالية..
- أعطى المرأة حرية اختيار الزوج.
- أبقى لها اسمها وشرف انتسابها لأبيها، فلا تتغير نسبتها بعد الزواج، بل تبقى منتسبة لأبيها وعائلتها.
- أوجب على الرجل رعايتها والإنفاق عليها بدون منّة إن كانت ممن تجب نفقته كالزوجة والأم والبنت.
- أكد على شرف وفضل خدمة المرأة الضعيفة التي ليس لها أحد، ولو لم تكن من الأقارب، ورغب في السعي لخدمتها وجعل ذلك من أفضل الأعمال عند الله.

passages.heading: الأخلاق في الإسلام:
passages.text:
- الأخلاق الحسنة لها مكانة عظيمة في الإسلام، فهي مقصد مهم من مقاصد الشرعية الإسلامية، وهدف من أهداف بعثة النبي ﷺ.
- الأخلاق لها ارتباط وثيق بالإيمان، فأكمل المؤمنين إيمانًا أحسنهم أخلاقًا.
- يؤجر العبد على حسن خلقه، كما يؤجر على الصلاة والصوم.

passages.heading: ما هو الحج؟
passages.text:
الحج: عبادة يذهب لأجلها المسلم المستطيع إلى مكة المكرمة للقيام بعبادات معينة في شهر ذي الحجة، وهو الشهر الأخير من السنة الهجرية.

والحج هو الركن الخامس من أركان الإسلام.

السنة الهجرية: هي إشارةٌ إلى الهجرة النبوية المباركة من مكة المكرمة إلى المدينة النبوية، وقد اختار الخليفة عمر بن الخطاب ؓ يوم هجرة الرسول ﷺ ليكون بداية لحساب التاريخ الإسلامي الهجري. وللسنة الهجرية إثنا عشر شهر تبدء بشهر (محرم) وتنتهي بشهر (ذي الحجة)، وقد اعتمد المسلمون التأريخ للحوادث والوقائع بالسنة الهجرية منذ السنة الأولى للهجرة والتي تقابلها سنة ٦٢٢ ميلادية.

passages.heading: ناقش
passages.text: يحتاج وضع موضوع مناسب للنقاش:

passages.heading: على من يجب الحج؟
passages.text: يجب الحج مرة واحدة في العمر على من يقدر عليه من المسلمين والمسلمات، فكل من قدر على الحج جسديًا وماليًا فإن الحج واجب عليه.

passages.heading: تنبيهات متعلقة بالحج:
passages.text:
- لا يمكن للمسلم أداء الحج إلا في مكان مخصوص هو (مكة)، وفي وقت مخصوص من السنة.
- يشتمل الحج على عدد من العبادات التي ينبغي على المسلم تعلمها قبل ذهابه لأداء الحج.

يؤدي الحج في كل عام مجموعة من المسلمين من دول مختلفة، ويتوحدون في لباسهم فلا يكون هناك تمييز بين الغني والفقير منهم.

passages.heading: ناقش
passages.text: كيف يمكن أن تكون أخلاق المسلم مع الآخرين؟ وهل لهذه الأخلاق أثر في حكمهم على الإسلام؟

passages.heading: فضل حسن الخلق:
passages.text:
- أخبر النبي ﷺ أن أكثر ما يدخل الناس الجنة: تقوى الله وحسن الخلق.
- وأخبر ﷺ أن أثقل ما يوضع في ميزان الإنسان يوم القيامة من الحسنات: حسن الخلق.
- وأخبر ﷺ أن أقرب المؤمنين منه منزلة يوم القيامة: أحسنهم أخلاقًا.

> يكون ذلك يوم القيامة حين يتم وزن حسنات الإنسان وسيئاته في ميزان مخصص لا يعلم أحدٌ هيئته ولا حجمه، فمن رجحت كفة حسناته دخل الجنة ومن رجحت كفة سيئاته دخل النار.

---

passages.heading: ما هي الزكاة؟
passages.text:
الزكاة: إخراج نصيب مقدر من أموال أغنياء المسلمين يعطى لفقرائهم.

وهي الركن الثالث من أركان الإسلام.

passages.heading: لماذا نزكي؟
passages.text: يزكي المسلم من ماله؛ لأن في الزكاة ثلاثة أمور:

passages.heading: تمهيد
passages.text: خص الله عز وجل المرأة ببعض الصفات والخصائص التي تميزها عن الرجل، كما أوجب عليها بعض العبادات دون الرجل، وفي هذا الدرس سنتعرف على بعض الأحكام التي تخص المرأة المسلمة.

passages.heading: الدرس الخامس
passages.text: ## أحكام تخص المرأة المسلمة

passages.heading: علاقة المرأة بالرجل:
passages.text: تنقسم علاقة المرأة بالنسبة للرجل إلى ثلاثة أقسام:

passages.heading: A discutir
passages.text: ¿Qué significa insistir sobre la necesidad de la purificación del musulmán y su higiene personal?

passages.heading: As-Salat (el rezo ritual).
passages.text: 10. Después de la segunda prosternación en la segunda unidad se queda sentado igual que su posición entre las dos prosternaciones y dice: At tahiiátu lillahi uas salauátu uat taiibátu as salámu ‘alaika aiiuhan nabíiu ua rahmatullahi ua barakátuhu as salámu ‘alaina ua ‘ala ‘ibádillahi salihín ash-hadu an la iláha il lallahu ua ash hadu anna muhammadan ‘abduhu ua rasúluh “Las salutaciones, los actos de devoción y las buenas obras son para Al-láh. La paz, misericordia y bendiciones de Al-láh sean para ti ¡Oh Profeta! La paz sea sobre nosotros y sobre los siervos virtuosos de Al-láh. Atestiguo que no hay otra divinidad salvo Al-láh y atestiguo que Muhammad es Su Siervo y Mensajero.»» Y esto se llama el primer Tashahud. Luego dice: {Al-láhuma Sali ala Muhammadin wa ala ali Muahammad, kama salayta ala ibrahim wa ala ali ibrahim inaka Hamidun Mayid. Wa barik ala Muahmmadin wa ala ali Muhammad, kama barakta ala ibrahim wa ala ali ibrahim inaka Hamidun Mayid} (¡Oh, Al-láh! Exalta a Muhammad y a la familia de Muhammad como exaltaste a Abraham y a la famila de Abraham, ciertamente eres loable y glorioso. ¡Oh, Al-láh! Bendice a Muhammad y a la familia de Muhammad como bendijiste a Abraham y a la familia de Abraham, ciertamente eres loable y glorioso.) Y ésta se llama la oración abrahámica.

passages.heading: ¿Por qué ayunamos?
passages.text: El musulmán ayuna por obediencia a Al-láh y aplicando Sus órdenes.

passages.heading: ¿Qué significan los dos testimonios de fe?
passages.text:
Primero: el significado de “Atestiguo que no hay divinidad digna de ser adorada fuera de Al-láh”.

El significado de (atestiguo que no hay divinidad digna de ser adorada salvo Al-láh): es decir creo sin duda alguna que Al-láh es el Único Dios que merece ser adorado.

Este testimonio incluye dos asuntos

| El primero | El Segundo |
| --- | --- |
| Negar la divinidad a otro fuera de Al-láh -Enaltecido sea- | Afirmar la divinidad para Al-láh unicamente |

passages.heading: ¿En qué consiste la fe?
passages.text: La fe: es creer con el corazón y con la lengua en lo que reveló Al-láh, someter el corazón con amor, esperanza y temor, y obrar con los actos, Al-láh-Enaltecido sea- dice: {{Q:4:136}} Corán (4: 136)

passages.heading: ¿Por qué realizamos la oración?
passages.text:
Rezamos porque la oración es una adoración prescrita por Al-láh para todos los musulmanes.

Entre las sabidurías y los beneficios de la oración citamos:

- Es el lazo entre el musulmán y su Señor.
- Fortalece la voluntad y la perseverancia del musulmán.
- Libera el alma de las preocupaciones de la vida mundana.
- Mejora la conducta, y aleja a la persona de los vicios.

passages.heading: ¿En qué consiste la oración?
passages.text:
La oración es un rito diario que incluye un conjunto de dichos y actos con los cuales el musulmán adora a su Señor, y se realiza cinco veces al día.

La oración es el segundo pilar del Islam.

passages.heading: ¿En qué consiste el ayuno?
passages.text:
El ayuno consiste en abstenerse de comer, beber y mantener relaciones maritales desde la aparición del alba hasta el ocaso, durante todos los días del mes de Ramadán.

El ayuno en el mes de Ramadán es el cuarto pilar del Islam.

passages.heading: Normas relacionadas con la purificación:
passages.text:
- Los objetos en su origen son puros, y se considera impuro solo lo clasificado por las normas religiosas como tal.
- Es suficiente purificar el cuerpo o la vestimenta quitando las impurezas con agua o con algo que purifica.
- Al entrar al cuarto de baño para orinar o defecar, es preferible limpiar el sitio de la orina o de los heces con agua, y es permitido también quitar la suciedad y purificar el sitio con un papel higiénico u otro objeto que quite las impurezas.

7. Eleva su cabeza diciendo «»Al-láhu Akbar»» luego se siente sobre su pie izquierda, poniendo su pie derecha elevada, sus manos sobre sus muslos luego dice sentado: «»Rabi ighfir li= Oh Señor mío perdóname»».

8. Se prosterna otra vez como en la primera prosternación, y dice al inclinarse para la prosternación «»Al-láhu Akbar»» y hace en su segunda prosternación igual que hizo en la primera.

9. Levanta su cabeza, luego se levanta para la segunda unidad (rak›a) diciendo «»Al-láhu Akbar»» y realiza la segunda unidad igual como la primera.

passages.heading: As-Salat (el rezo ritual).
passages.text:
11. Se dirige con su cabeza hacia la parte derecha diciendo “”As-salamu alaykum wa rahmatulláh = que la paz y la misericordia de Al-láh sean con ustedes”” luego a la izquierda diciendo lo mismo. Y de este modo termina su oración.

Se realiza de esta manera cuando se trata de una oración de dos unidades como la del alba y del viernes. Pero si consta de tres unidades como la del Maghreb o de cuatro como la del Dhuhr, Asr e Isha en este caso cuando termina el primer tashahud, luego sigue con las unidades que faltan igual que la primera unidad pero solo recita la sura de Al Fatiha, luego se sienta como la sentada después de la segunda unidad y recita el segundo tashahud y la oración abrahámica, luego saluda y así se termina la oración.

passages.heading: Salat al-Yumu’a [La Oración del Viernes].
passages.text:
- Al-láh -Enaltecido y Exaltado sea- prescribió la realización de la oración del viernes con condiciones y modos precisos, y que sustituye la oración del Dhuhr para este día.
- Los musulmanes se reúnen en la mezquita para realizarla, escuchan los dos sermones del imam, luego rezan con él dos unidades donde el imam recita el Corán en voz alta.
- Está permitida la ablución mayor (ghusl) para asistir a la oración del viernes y asisitir pronto. Y no está permitido ausentarse sin excusa, quien no asiste a la oración del viernes debe realizar la oración del Dhuhr cuatro unidades y no recitar el Corán en voz alta.
- La oración del viernes no es obligatoria para la mujer ni para el viajero.

passages.heading: A discutir
passages.text:
Menciona con tus compañeros las dificultades que enfrenta el musulmán y le impiden realizar la oración en su tiempo prescrito y cómo se puede superar estas dificultades.

{{Q:62:9}} (Corán 62: 9)

passages.heading: Entre las sabidurías y los beneficios del ayuno citamos:
passages.text:
- Llegar a la piedad (takwa) al abundar las adoraciones y disminuir los pecados.
- Que sienta el dolor del hambre que sienten los pobres y necesitados.
- Que se libera de los caprichos y mejora su auto control.

Al-láh ha prescrito la adoración del ayuno para los musulmanes igual que a las comunidades anteriores. Al-láh -Enaltecido sea- dice: {{Q:2:183}} (Corán 2: 183)

passages.heading: Lo que anula el ayuno:
passages.text:
**El ayunante debe abstenerse de un conjunto de actos que anulan su ayuno como:**

1. Comer, beber, y las jeringas de alimentación intravenosas.
2. La eyaculación intencionalmente, sea con o sin coito, el coito durante el día de ayuno de Ramadán es un pecado muy grave.
3. El vómito intencional.

**En cuanto a la mujer, se anula su ayuno con:**

4. La salida de sangre de menstruación o de postparto.

passages.heading: El bendito mes de Ramadán:
passages.text:
Es el noveno mes del año lunar, es un mes bendito en lo cual Al-láh reveló el Corán a Su mensajero Muhammad -que la paz y las bendiciones de Al-láh sean con él-. Al-láh -Enaltecido sea- hizo del ayuno durante el día y la oración durante la noche una causa de expiación de los pecados. Se destaca una noche mejor que mil meses llamada (Laylatul Qadr= la noche del decreto). Quien dedica esta noche a recordar y orar Al-láh le perdona todos sus pecados anteriores.

**Los musulmanes realizan la oración de Tarawih en el mes de Ramadán, y es una sunna relacionada con Ramadán y que se realiza después de la oración del Isha.**

passages.heading: Los dos testimonios de fe:
passages.text:
Al-láh -Enaltecido y Exaltado sea- hizo de la confesión de los dos testimonios de fe la llave de la conversión al Islam, estos dos testimonios son:

- atestiguo que no hay divinidad digna de ser adorada salvo Al-láh,
- y atestiguo que Muhammad es el mensajero de Al-láh.

La esencia del Islam que es la religión de todos los profetas: es decir adorar a Al-láh solo y negar todo lo que se adora fuera de Él. Al-láh -Enaltecido sea- dice: {{Q:21:25}} Corán (21: 25)

No está permitido de ninguna manera creer en la divinidad de otro fuera de Al-láh -Enaltecido sea- y no está permitido dedicar cualquier tipo de adoración a otro fuera de Al-láh.

passages.heading: Segundo: el significado del testimonio de que Muhammad es el Mensajero de Al-láh.
passages.text: El significado de (atestiguo que Muhammad es mensajero de Al-láh) es: creo sin lugar a duda que Muhammad -que la paz y las bendiciones de Al-láh sean con él- es mensajero de Al-láh, el último de los mensajeros no habrá ningún profeta después de él y que su mensaje es universal. Al-láh- Glorificado sea- dice: {{Q:25:1}} Corán (25: 1)

passages.heading: Preámbulo
passages.text: El musulmán siente siempre la tranquilidad y la paz interna al recitar Corán o al realizar una obra de adoración como la oración u otras, este sentimiento eleva a algunos hasta llegar a niveles muy avanzados de bienestar y felicidad, y esto es gracias a la fe que hace el musulmán realizar las órdenes divinas con amor y satisfacción y se aleja de las prohibiciones con total sumisión y obediencia. Y en esta lección vamos a estudiar el significado de la fe, sus pilares y sus frutos.

passages.heading: A discutir
passages.text: ¿Cuál es la diferencia entre el temor y la esperanza?

passages.heading: Los pilares de la fe:
passages.text: La fe se basa en seis pilares que son:

passages.heading: Los pilares de la fe:
passages.text:
1. **La creencia en Al-láh:** el musulmán cree en la existencia de Al-láh -Enaltecido sea- y en Sus atributos, como Señor de este universo, es el Creador, el Soberano, y Quien maneja todos los asuntos según Su Voluntad, es Él Quien sostiene a sus siervos. Y cree también que Al-láh es el Único que merece ser adorado y el Único que posee los atributos de perfección.
2. **La creencia en los ángeles:** el musulmán cree en la existencia de los nobles ángeles, y que fueron creados por Al-láh, que adoran a Al-láh y nunca Le desobedecen. Cree también en sus características y en sus roles como fueron mencionados en el Corán y en la sunnah profética.
3. **La creencia en los Libros revelados:** el musulmán cree que Al-láh ha revelado libros a Sus siervos a través de los mensajeros, estos libros fueron revelados para guiar a la gente y enseñarla los asuntos religiosos. Entre estos libros se encuentra la Torá revelada al profeta Moisés ibn Imrán -la paz sea con él-, los Salmos revelados a David -la paz sea con él-, el Evangelio a Jesús hijo de María -la paz sea con ambos- y el Corán a Muhammad -que la paz y las bendiciones de Al-láh sean con él- y fue el último y el dominante.
4. **La creencia en los profetas -la paz sea con ellos-:** el musulmán cree que Al-láh ha enviado mensajeros para sus pueblos y les apoyaba con milagros que indican su veracidad, para transmitir la buena noticia a los creyentes y para advertir a los incrédulos, para enseñar a sus pueblos los asuntos religiosos. Sin embargo cada pueblo debe creer en el mensajero enviado a él obedeciéndole y siguiéndole y que Muhammad -que la paz y las bendiciones de Al-láh sean con él- es el último de los mensajeros enviados.
5. **La creencia en el Día de Juicio:** el musulmán cree en el día de Resurrección, y cree que Al-láh resucita a los muertos de sus tumbas y serán juzgados y recompensados por sus actos, unos entrarán al paraíso y otros al fuego de infierno.
6. **La creencia en la Predestinación:** el musulmán cree que todo lo que ocurre de bien o de mal en este universo es predestinado y conocido previamente por Al-láh -Enaltecido sea- redactado en la Tabla Protegida, y cree que nada puede ocurrir sino es con la Voluntad de Al-láh -Enaltecido sea.

passages.heading: La importancia de la oración:
passages.text:
La oración tiene varias características, entre ellas:

- Es el segundo pilar del Islam después de los dos testimonios.
- La adoración que se debe realizar en todas las circunstancias, sea al estar bien o al estar enfermo, al sentir seguridad o miedo.
- La oración es la adoración que distingue el musulmán del incrédulo.

passages.heading: Las condiciones de la oración:
passages.text:
Para realizar la oración, se debe cumplir ciertas condiciones que son:

- **La purificación:** incluye la purificación del cuerpo y del lugar de todas las impurezas e incluye también la ablución menor (wudu) y mayor (ghusl).
- **Cubrir la parte íntima (A’ura) que es todo lo que se cubre en presencia de la gente.** En cuanto a la parte íntima del hombre que tiene que cubrir al rezar es entre el ombligo y las rodillas, mientras que la mujer debe tapar todo su cuerpo salvo el rostro y las dos manos.
- **Dirigirse hacia la Quibla que es la dirección hacia la Kaaba honrada que se encuentra en la Meca,** el orante debe dirigirse hacia ella al rezar.
- **La llegada del tiempo del rezo:** no se debe rezar antes del tiempo de la oración, ni se debe retrasarla hasta que pase su tiempo, y lo mejor es realizarla al inicio de su tiempo prescrito.

passages.heading: Las cinco oraciones:
passages.text:
Al-láh -Enaltecido y Exaltado sea- prescribe a sus siervos rezar cinco oraciones al día que son:

| | El inicio de su tiempo | El fin de su tiempo | Sus unidades (Rak’as) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Salat al Fayer (el rezo del alba) | el alba. | el amanecer. | 2 |
| Salat ad-Duhur (el rezo del mediodía): | la puesta del sol (es decir cuando el sol empieza a dirigirse hacia el oeste a mediodía). | cuando se iguala la sombra de una cosa a su longitud. | 4 |
| Salat al- Asr (el rezo de la tarde): | cuando se iguala la sombra de una cosa a su longitud. | el atardecer. | 4 |
| Salat al Magrib (el rezo del ocaso): | el atardecer. | el crepúsculo. | 3 |
| Salat al ‘Isha (el rezo de la noche): | el crepúsculo. | la medianoche. | 4 |

passages.heading: ¿Cómo rezamos?
passages.text: Si el musulmán quiere realizar la oración debe hacer los pasos siguientes:

passages.heading: Preámbulo
passages.text:
La oración se considera el fundamento trascendental de la religión, por ello que el musulmán debe aprender a realizarla, por lo tanto el mensajero -que la paz y las bendiciones de Al-láh sean con él- nos ha enseñado cómo realizarla de un modo que complace a Al-láh -Enaltecido y Exaltado sea.

En este curso vamos a estudiar las oraciones prescritas, su posición, sus condiciones, y cómo realizarlas correctamente.

passages.heading: Preámbulo
passages.text: El ayuno es una de las adoraciones prescritas por Al-láh -Enaltecido y Exaltado sea- a todas las naciones, y en Islam el musulmán realiza esta adoración como forma de obedecer a su Señor, entonces en esta lección vamos a saber la sabiduría del ayuno, lo que anula el ayuno y algunas de las normas del ayuno.

passages.heading: What Is *Zakaat*?
passages.text: *Zakaat*: a religious obligation whereby wealthy Muslims give away a certain portion of their wealth to the poor in their midst. It is the third pillar of Islam.

passages.heading: Introduction
passages.text: There are some cases where *wudoo’* is not sufficient to perform an act of worship, but *ghusl* is required. In this lesson, we are going to learn about the meaning of *ghusl*, the reasons for performing it, as well as how to perform it.

passages.heading: 1. The Meaning of the Testimony that There Is no God but Allah
passages.text:
The meaning of “I bear witness that there is no god but Allah” is: I firmly believe that there is no god worthy of worship except Allah alone.

This testimony consists of two parts:

| The first part | The second part |
| --- | --- |
| negates the existence of any other deity besides Allah Almighty | confirms that Allah is the only True God worthy of worship |

passages.heading: The Requirements of the Two Testimonies of Faith
passages.text: It is not enough to verbally declare the two testimonies of faith. In addition to this, it is imperative to know what they mean and to meet their requirements. The testimony that there is no god but Allah requires us to reject everything that is worshipped besides or instead of Allah, to firmly believe that Allah alone is our Lord and Cherisher and the One True God worthy of worship and to worship Him sincerely. Allah Almighty says, {{Q:2:256}} (Soorat Al-Baqarah, 2:256) The testimony that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah requires us to believe what he says, do what he commands and avoid what he forbids and worship Allah only according to his instructions.

passages.heading: Who is Required to Perform _Hajj_?
passages.text: Hajj is a religious obligation that must be carried out once in a lifetime by every able Muslim man and woman. Thus, anyone who is physically and financially able must perform the pilgrimage.

passages.heading: What is *Hajj*?
passages.text:
*Hajj* is an act of worship for which physically and financially able Muslims travel to Makkah to perform certain acts of worship during the month of Dhul-Hijjah, which is the last month of the lunar calendar.

*Hajj* is the fifth pillar of Islam

The Islamic *Hijri* Calendar is a lunar calendar is associated with the Prophet’s migration, or *hijrah*, from Makkah to Madeenah. Third Rightly-Guided Caliph ‘Umar ibn Al-Khattaab, may Allah be pleased with him, decided that the most appropriate reference point for the Islamic calendar would be the Prophet’s *hijrah*. The Islamic Calendar has twelve months, beginning with the month of Muharram and ending with the month of Dhul-Hijjah. Muslims have adopted the Islamic *Hijri* calendar to date incidents and events.

passages.heading: Introduction
passages.text: Islam is the religion with which Allah sent Muhammad ﷺ and is an extension of the same religion with which all the previous messengers came. It is essentially based on the belief that Allah Almighty is the only deity deserving of worship, who has no partners or assistants whatsoever in His kingdom, and who has no intermediaries between Him and His servants. But why should I embrace Islam? Is it a religion for all people or is it only for the Arabs? Who is its prophet, and is there another prophet who will come after him?

passages.heading: Second
passages.text: to increase one’s wealth, for *zakaat* does not decrease it, but rather increases it and even blesses it.

passages.heading: Introduction
passages.text: Since ancient times, people on this earth have led different lives with varying living standards. Some are very well-to-do; others are destitute and can barely find anything to eat. This is one of Allah’s ways in this universe. Islam enjoins the wealthy to pay a certain percentage of their wealth to the poor to relieve them of the burden of poverty and urges Muslims to spend more of what they are required to spend, promising them great rewards for doing so both in this life and after death. It also urges them to give charity to the needy at all times and on every occasion and encourages them to feed the hungry and clothe the naked in order for the Muslim community to become close-knit, just as Allah Almighty wants it to be. In this lesson, we are going to learn about the Islamic ruling on *zakaat*, the manner of paying it and the types of wealth upon which it is due.

passages.heading: Why Do We Pay *Zakaat*?
passages.text: We pay *zakaat* in compliance with the command of Allah who has enjoined us to pay it.

passages.text: ## Ghusl (Full Ablutions/Bath)

passages.heading: The Meaning of *Ghusl*
passages.text: *Ghusl*: Washing the entire body with water to remove the major ritual impurity.

passages.heading: How to Perform *Ghusl*?
passages.text:
To perform *ghusl*, one must wash the entire body with water, rinse out one’s mouth and clean one’s nose by sniffing water into the nostrils and ejecting it out by blowing one’s nose. A Muslim removes the major ritual impurity by simply doing so.

> The major ritual impurity: what must be removed by ghusl, and ablution is not sufficient, and these are types:
> 
> 1- *Janaabah*: The state of ritual impurity following intercourse or ejaculation as a result of an orgasm even if no intercourse takes place.
> 2- Menstruation: the normal vaginal bleeding that occurs as part of a woman’s monthly cycle.
> 3- Postnatal bleeding: The vaginal bleeding that takes place following childbirth.

passages.heading: The Two Testimonies of Faith
passages.text:
Allah Almighty has made the declaration of the two testimonies of faith the key to joining the fold of Islam. They are:

- I bear witness that there is no god worthy of worship but Allah,
- and I bear witness that Muhammad is Allah’s Messenger.

Islam is essentially the religion of all the prophets: to worship Allah alone and reject all false deities that are worshipped besides or instead of Him. Allah Almighty, says, {{Q:21:25}} (Surat al-Anbiyyaa’, 21:25).

Therefore, it is not permissible, under any circumstances, to believe in any deity other than Allah Almighty, nor is it permissible to perform any act of worship to draw nearer to anyone other than Allah Almighty.

passages.heading: 2. The Meaning of the Testimony that Muhammad is Allah’s Messenger
passages.text: The meaning of the testimony that Muhammad is Allah’s Messenger is: I firmly believe that Muhammad ﷺ is the Messenger of Allah, that he is the Final Prophet without there being any prophet whatsoever after him, and that his message is for all people without exception. Allah Almighty says: {{Q:25:1}} (Surat Al-Furqaan, 25:1).

passages.heading: Important Notes Related to _Hajj_
passages.text:
- A Muslim cannot perform hajj except in a specific place, namely Makkah, and only at a specific time of the year.
- Hajj includes several acts of worship that a Muslim must learn before going to perform the pilgrimage.

Every year, Muslims from different countries perform hajj in large groups. Donning uniform simple clothing, both rich and poor appear to be the same with all social barriers and distinctions broken down.

passages.heading: Introduction
passages.text: *Hajj*, the annual Muslim pilgrimage to Makkah, is one of the pillars of Islam and one of the best deeds whereby Muslims seek to draw closer to Allah Almighty. Its virtues are mentioned in numerous traditions of the Prophet ﷺ. In this lesson, we are going to learn a little information about this great act of worship.

passages.heading: Why Do We Perform *Hajj*?
passages.text: Muslims perform *Hajj* to the Sacred House in Makkah in response to Allah’s command to do so.

passages.heading: Some of the Ultimate Objectives and Benefits of *Hajj*
passages.text:
- To follow the example of the honourable prophets who made the pilgrimage to the Sacred House.
- To occupy oneself with worship: Pilgrims devote themselves to the worship of Allah, moving from one act of worship to another.
- To meet Muslims who come from the four corners of the world and gather in the holy sites, get to know them and build bridges of communication with them.

passages.heading: Why Should I Embrace Islam?
passages.text:
Some people may ask: Why should I embrace Islam?

The answer is: I must do so for a number of reasons, including the following:

1. Islam is the religion that Allah has approved and chosen for His servants and will not accept any other religion. The Almighty says, {{Q:3:85}} (Soorat Aal-’Imraan, 3:85).

2. Islam is the religion of all the prophets and commands its adherents to believe in all of them without exception. Allah says, {{Q:2:136}} (Soorat Al-Baqarah, 2:136).
The difference between prophets lies only in the laws relating to people’s actions, as the Almighty says, {{Q:5:48}} (Soorat Al-Maa’idah, 5:48) That is, for each nation before Islam, Allah appointed a law to which people referred for their disputes and a way of life whereby they drew near to Him. Thus, followers of every prophet had their respective laws and regulations, but the set of beliefs to which prophets called their people was the same. Then Allah sent the last prophet and messenger, Muhammad ﷺ, with the final divine laws, and thus the only religion acceptable to Allah is Islam.

3. Islam is the way to happiness in this life and salvation in the life to come; therefore, those who believe in Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and follow him after his message has reached them will be saved; as for those who deny him, they will be doomed to divine punishment. The Almighty says, {{Q:3:85}} (*Soorat Aal-’Imraan, 3:85*) The Prophet ﷺ also said, “By Him in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, any person of this Community, Jew or Christian, who hears of me and dies without believing in what I have been sent with will be among the dwellers of Hell” (*Saheeh Muslim;* No. 153).

4. Islam gives conclusive answers to the big questions of human existence: Where did we come from? Why are we here? Where do we go after death?

5. Islam is in perfect harmony with the innate human nature (*fitrah*), beginning with the greatest value it embraces, namely the declaration of Allah’s unity, and ending with the rules of etiquette it teaches its adherents to enable them to attain great perfection in moral excellence.

passages.heading: What are the types of wealth upon which *zakaat* is due?
passages.text:
- **Gold and silver**
- **All types of currency (banknotes and coins)**
- **Farm produce (crops and fruit)**
- **Grazing livestock**

Grazing livestock: This refers to camels, cattle, sheep and goats.

- **Commercial commodities**

Commercial commodities: all properties owned with the aim of investing them in trade. They generally include assets, such as a house, a shop, a car and an animal.

passages.heading: How Do We Pay *Zakaat* Due on Cash?
passages.text: A Muslim pays *zakaat* due on his cash once a year. 2.5% of its value must be given out as *zakaat*.

passages.heading: When do I have to perform wudoo’ again?
passages.text: If a Muslim performs wudoo’, the general rule is that his wudoo’ is still valid unless one of the previously-mentioned things that break wudoo’ happens, in which case he must perform it again.

passages.heading: Forbidden financial transactions
passages.text: *Riba* (usury, interest) is one of the financial transactions that Islam strictly forbids because of the harm it involves. It is also one of the major sins, and Allah warns those who engage in it of a severe punishment.

passages.heading: What is the Islamic Ruling on Seafood Consumption?
passages.text:
It is permissible to eat dead aquatic animals that can live only in water, such as fish and prawns, whether they live in the sea, rivers or lakes.

It is permissible to hunt wild, nonpredatory animals and consume their flesh provided that the name of Allah is mentioned before the hunting weapon is discharged, and the hunted game must be slaughtered if found still alive.

passages.heading: How Do We Pray?
passages.text:
1. He intends in his heart to pray.
2. He stands facing the *qiblah*, raises his hands up to the level of the shoulders or ears, and says, “*Allaahu akbar* Allah is the Greatest.”
3. He places his right hand on his left hand. Then he recites one of the opening supplications, such as, Subhaanak-Allaahumma wa bi hamdika, wa tabaarak-asmuka, wa ta’aalaa jadduka, wa laa ilaaha ghayruka “Glory be to You, O Allah; Yours is the praise, blessed is Your name, exalted is Your majesty, and there is no god besides You.” Then he says, A’oodhu billaahi min-ash-shaytaan-ir-rajeem. Bismillaah-ir-rahmaan-ir-raheem “I seek Allah’s protection from Satan, who has been expelled from His mercy. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.” Then he recites *Soorat Al-Faatihah* and says after it, “*Aameen*”, which means “Answer our supplications, O Allah”. After that, he recites whatever number of verses of the Qur’an as is easy for him, even if it is one verse.
4. He says, “Allaahu akbar Allah is the Greatest” while raising his hands up to the level of his shoulders or ears, and bows down, lowering his head and back and keeping them straight at a right angle, placing the palms of his hands on the knees. He says three times while in this position, “Subhaana rabbiy-al-’adheem Glory be to my Lord, the Almighty.”

5. He resumes the standing position, raising his hands up to the level of the shoulders or the ears, saying: Sami’allaahu li man hamidah “Allah hears those who praise Him.” Then he says while standing: Rabbanaa wa lakal-hamd “Our Lord, to You is due all praise.”

6. He says, Allaahu akbar “Allah is the Greatest” and prostrates himself, with the toes of both feet, the knees, the palms of the hands and the forehead and the nose touching the floor. He says three times while in this position, “Glory be to my Lord, Most High.”

passages.heading: The Manner of Performing *Wudoo’*
passages.text:
1. He intends in his heart to perform *wudoo’* and says, *bismillaah* “In the name of Allah”.
2. He washes his hands up to the wrists with water.
3. He rinses out his mouth thoroughly by moving water around in the mouth and then spitting it out. This process is called *madmadah*) in Arabic.
4. He cleans his nose by sniffing water into the nostrils and ejecting it out by blowing his nose.
5. He washes his face thoroughly from the hairline at the top of the forehead to the bottom of the chin, along with the beard, if he is bearded, and from ear to ear.
6. He washes his hands from the fingertips up to the elbow, starting with his right hand.
7. With wet hands, and starting with his hands flat on the top of the head near the hairline, he wipes it to the back of the neck and back to the front.
8. With wet fingers, he wipes  
He wipes the inner sides of the ears with his index fingers and behind them with his thumbs.
9. He washes his feet up to the ankles, which are the two prominent bones of the joint connecting the foot to the leg, starting with his right foot.

passages.heading: *Tayammum* (Dry Ablution)
passages.text:
If a person who wants to perform *wudoo’* or *ghusl* is unable to do so due to illness, or when water is not readily available, or for any other legitimate reason, he may resort to dry ablution (*tayammum*) instead.

The Manner of Performing *Tayammum*: (1) Intend in his heart to perform *tayammum* and strike both hands slightly on pure earth once, (2) wipe the face with them, (3) wipe the back of the right hand with the palm of the left, and then the back of the left hand with the palm of the right hand.

passages.heading: Benefits of Faith
passages.text:
* **Getting to know Allah Almighty:** A believer gets to know his Lord and His names, attributes and actions, so much so that he becomes more attached to Him.
* **Glorying Allah:** the more a believer gets to know his Lord, the more he extols and loves Him, the more he hopes for His mercy and the more God-fearing he becomes.
* **Getting to know Allah’s graciousness to His servants:** for sending messengers to them and divine books to them to guide them to the true religion.
* **Loving the angels:** for worshipping Allah and showing obedience to Him.
* **Loving Allah’s Messengers:** Allah Almighty chose them to convey His message to people.
* **Diligent worship:** the stronger the faith, the more worship one performs.
* **A truly happy life:** A believer is content with what Allah has apportioned to him and knows that whatever calamities befall him in this world elevate his rank and efface his sins. He also hopes for the bliss He has prepared for the believers in the life to come.
* **Not to be deluded by this world:** The life of this world is temporary and only serves as a means to eternal life in the hereafter.
* **Exposing myths:** Faith exposes and nullifies many myths.
* **Entering Paradise:** This is the abode of eternal bliss which Allah Almighty has prepared for His believing servants.

passages.heading: How Many Times Do We Wash the Parts of the Body that Are Usually Washed in *Wudoo’*?
passages.text: According to the *Sunnah*, each part of the body is washed three times, except in the case of the head and ears, which are wiped only once. It would suffice, however, to wash these body parts once provided that they are washed thoroughly.

passages.heading: Things That Render *Wudoo’* Invalid
passages.text:
*Wudoo’* becomes invalid as a result of four things:

- Natural discharges from the private parts (both the external genital and excretory organs), such as urine, excrement, wind, semen and the clear, colourless, viscous fluid that is emitted during sexual arousal
- Loss of consciousness due to sleep or intoxication
- Lustfully touching the private parts with bare hands
- Eating camel meat

passages.heading: Introduction
passages.text: *Soorat Al-Faatihah* is the greatest *soorah* in the Qur’an. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ emphasized its virtues and greatness in many of his sayings. It is the *soorah* that every Muslim must learn by heart because it is the only *soorah* that he must recite in every single prayer. In this lesson, we are going to study this *soorah*, memorize its verses and understand its meanings, in addition to studying several other short *suwar* (sing, *soorah*) that have great significance.

passages.heading: The Requirements of the Two Testimonies of Faith
passages.text: It is not enough to verbally declare the two testimonies of faith. In addition to this, it is imperative to know what they mean and to meet their requirements. The testimony that there is no god but Allah requires us to reject everything that is worshipped besides or instead of Allah, to firmly believe that Allah alone is our Lord and Cherisher and the One True God worthy of worship and to worship Him sincerely. Allah Almighty says, {{Q:2:256}} (Soorat Al-Baqarah, 2:256) The testimony that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah requires us to believe what he says, do what he commands and avoid what he forbids and worship Allah only according to his instructions.

passages.heading: Islamic Rulings Pertaining to Menstrual and Postnatal Bleeding
passages.text:
Allah Almighty has prescribed several rulings relating to menstruating women and women experiencing their postnatal bleeding, including the following:

- They are exempt from performing the prayers during this period and do not have to make up for the prayers they have missed while in this state after the end of menstrual and postnatal bleeding.
- They are exempt from fasting and are not allowed to fast while in this state, but they must make up for the fasting days they have missed in Ramadaan.
- During this period, a husband must not have intercourse with his wife during her menstrual or postnatal period. He is allowed, however, to satisfy his sexual desire but without having intercourse.
- At the end of the menstrual and postnatal period, when bleeding stops completely, women must take a ritual bath (*ghusl*).

passages.heading: When do I have to perform wudoo’ again?
passages.text: If a Muslim performs wudoo’, the general rule is that his wudoo’ is still valid unless one of the previously-mentioned things that break wudoo’ happens, in which case he must perform it again.

passages.heading: How Do We Pray?
passages.text:
1. He intends in his heart to pray.
2. He stands facing the *qiblah*, raises his hands up to the level of the shoulders or ears, and says, “*Allaahu akbar* Allah is the Greatest.”
3. He places his right hand on his left hand. Then he recites one of the opening supplications, such as, Subhaanak-Allaahumma wa bi hamdika, wa tabaarak-asmuka, wa ta’aalaa jadduka, wa laa ilaaha ghayruka “Glory be to You, O Allah; Yours is the praise, blessed is Your name, exalted is Your majesty, and there is no god besides You.” Then he says, A’oodhu billaahi min-ash-shaytaan-ir-rajeem. Bismillaah-ir-rahmaan-ir-raheem “I seek Allah’s protection from Satan, who has been expelled from His mercy. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.” Then he recites *Soorat Al-Faatihah* and says after it, “*Aameen*”, which means “Answer our supplications, O Allah”. After that, he recites whatever number of verses of the Qur’an as is easy for him, even if it is one verse.
4. He says, “Allaahu akbar Allah is the Greatest” while raising his hands up to the level of his shoulders or ears, and bows down, lowering his head and back and keeping them straight at a right angle, placing the palms of his hands on the knees. He says three times while in this position, “Subhaana rabbiy-al-’adheem Glory be to my Lord, the Almighty.”

passages.heading: Soorat Al-Kawthar (Abundant Good)
passages.text:
*Soorat Al-Kawthar* **Explained**

{{Q:108:1-3}}

“We have bestowed on you abundant good”

We have given you, Messenger, immeasurable, abundant good in this life and the life to come, part of which is River Al-Kawthar in Paradise.

“So pray to your Lord and sacrifice to Him”

Therefore, sincerely pray to your Lord and worship Him alone, and sacrifice to Him, pronouncing Allah’s name alone when slaughtering animals, in gratitude to Him for the honour and good He has bestowed on you.

“He who hates you is the one who is truly cut off”

*Shaani’aka*: The one who hates you and hates the true religion you have brought.

The one who hates you and hates the true religion you have brought is the most disgraced and contemptible, whose mention is short-lived and who is cut off from all good.

passages.heading: What shall I do if I find water after having performed *tayammum*?
passages.text: If a Muslim finds water or can use it, his purity becomes invalid, in which case he must perform *wudoo’* or *ghusl*.

passages.heading: *Soorat Al-Kaafiroon* Explained
passages.text:
{{Q:109:1-6}}

“Say: Unbelievers!”

Say, Messenger, to those who disbelieve in Allah and His Messenger: You unbelievers.

“I do not worship what you worship”

I do not worship the false gods, such as idols, that you worship.

“nor do you worship what I worship”

nor do you worship the True God whom I worship, and who alone is worthy of worship.

“I will never worship what you worship”

I will never worship the false gods that you worship.

“nor will you ever worship what I worship”

nor will you ever worship the True God whom I worship, and who alone is worthy of worship.

Al-kaafir: The person who does not proclaim pure monotheism and does not follow the divine message Prophet Muhammad ﷺ has brought.

“You have your religion, and I have my religion”

You have your religion to which you adhere, and I have my religion to which I adhere.

passages.heading: Soorat Al-Faatiẖah (The Opening)
passages.text:
*Soorat Al-Faatiẖah* Explained

“In the name of Allah, the All-Compassionate, the All-Merciful”

I begin reading the Qur’an in the name of Allah, seeking the help of Allah, the True Deity, the All-Compassionate, whose mercy encompasses all creation in general, the All-Merciful, who bestows His special mercy to the believers.

“Praise be to Allah, Lord of all the worlds”

All praise is due to Allah for His perfect attributes and for His grace towards all His creation. He alone is worthy of all forms of praise and is the Lord of all creation, who has created all that exists out of absolutely nothing, who manages all their affairs and improves their condition.
