passages.text:

“The All-Compassionate, the All-Merciful”
*Ar-Rahmaan*: The All-Gracious whose mercy encompasses all His creation; *Ar-Raheem*: The All-Merciful who bestows His special mercy to the believers.

The All-Gracious towards all His creation

The All-Merciful towards the believers in particular

“Master of the Day of Judgement” Owner of the Day of Judgement, the day He will judge everyone and repay them according to their deeds.

“You alone do we worship and You alone do we ask for help” We worship You alone, our Lord, and we seek help from You alone in all our affairs, for indeed all matters are in Your hands.

“Guide us to the straight path” Show us the straight path and make us firm on it until we meet You. The straight path here is Islam, the clear path that leads to Allah’s good pleasure and to His Gardens in Paradise.

passages.heading: Lesson 2
passages.text:
“The path of those whom You have blessed, not of those who have incurred Your wrath, nor of those who have gone astray”
It is the path of those whom You have blessed with guidance from among the prophets and their supporters, and those who follow in their footsteps—These are the ones who have been rightly guided.

Keep us away from the path of those with whom you are angry because they know the truth but choose not to follow it. Also, keep us away from the path of those who have not been guided to the straight path due to their ignorance.

passages.heading: Soorat Al-’A<u>s</u>r (The Time)
passages.text:
*Soorat Al-’A<u>s</u>r* **Explained**

{{Q:103:1-3}}

“By the time”

Allah swears by the time in which people’s good and evil deeds take place.

Mankind is indeed in sheer loss and ruin,

“except for those who believe and do good works; who exhort each other to justice and to fortitude”

except for those who believe in Allah, do righteous deeds, and urge one another to adhere to the truth and to be patient and steadfast in doing so.

passages.text:

Say, Messenger, “I seek refuge and protection in Allah, the Lord of all mankind, who alone has power over all things.

The King of all people, who manages all their affairs.

The True God of all people, who alone deserves to be worshipped by them.

from the harm of Satan who whispers evil suggestions to people when they are heedless of Allah and refrains from doing so when they remember Him.

passages.heading: Types of Acts of Worship
passages.text:
Acts of worship fall into different categories:

| Acts of worship involving the heart | A Muslim performs these with his heart. Examples include love, fear, hope and *khushoo’*. |
| --- | --- |
| Physical acts of worship | A Muslim performs these physically. Examples include the prayer, *zakaat* and pilgrimage. |
| Acts that are abandoned in obedience to Allah | A Muslim draws closer to his Lord by abandoning the acts He has forbidden him, such as drinking alcohol and committing adultery, or by refraining from certain permissible acts at specific times, such as abstaining from food and drink while fasting. |

> *Ar-Rajaa’*(Hope): This refers to rejoicing in Allah’s grace and hoping for His benevolence, while at the same time ensuring proper reliance on Allah by doing good deeds to the best of one’s ability.
> 
> *Al-khushoo’* is a state of utter humility and calmness and deep concentration into which one gets while performing an act of worship, such as the prayer, bringing about outward composure and tranquillity.

passages.heading: 2. The Meaning of the Testimony that Muhammad is Allah’s Messenger
passages.text: The meaning of the testimony that Muhammad is Allah’s Messenger is: I firmly believe that Muhammad ﷺ is the Messenger of Allah, that he is the Final Prophet without there being any prophet whatsoever after him, and that his message is for all people without exception. Allah Almighty says: {{Q:25:1}} (Surat Al-Furqaan, 25:1).

passages.heading: Conditions for Acts of Worship to Be Accepted
passages.text:
For an act of worship to be accepted, two conditions must be fulfilled:

The first condition: It has to be done sincerely for the sake of Allah to draw closer to alone, without showing off.

The second condition: It has to be done in the manner Allah has enjoined it and exactly as it was performed by the Prophet ﷺ.

> *Aririyyaa’* (showing off) is the act of doing an act of worship only to be seen and praised by people for doing it.

passages.heading: Introduction
passages.text: Since ancient times, people on this earth have led different lives with varying living standards. Some are very well-to-do; others are destitute and can barely find anything to eat. This is one of Allah’s ways in this universe. Islam enjoins the wealthy to pay a certain percentage of their wealth to the poor to relieve them of the burden of poverty and urges Muslims to spend more of what they are required to spend, promising them great rewards for doing so both in this life and after death. It also urges them to give charity to the needy at all times and on every occasion and encourages them to feed the hungry and clothe the naked in order for the Muslim community to become close-knit, just as Allah Almighty wants it to be. In this lesson, we are going to learn about the Islamic ruling on *zakaat*, the manner of paying it and the types of wealth upon which it is due.

passages.heading: Introduction
passages.text: People have always pondered the big questions of human existence: Where did we come from? Why are we here? Where do we go after death? Islam provides definitive and conclusive answers to these questions which arise in the heart of every reflective human being.

passages.heading: The Meaning of Worship
passages.text: By worship is meant everything that Allah has enjoined on us for us to draw closer to Him. It comprises all words and deeds that Allah loves, whether they are outward like the physical acts of worship, such as the prayer and pilgrimage, or inward, like the acts of worship involving the heart, such as love of Allah, fearing His punishment and hoping for His mercy. A person can transform everyday habits into acts of worship simply by having a good intention. If, for instance, he eats, drinks and sleeps with the intention of gaining enough strength to worship Allah better, he will certainly be rewarded for doing so

passages.heading: What is Faith?
passages.text: Faith (*Eemaan* in Arabic) is to confess with one’s mouth and believe in one’s heart everything that has come from Allah, totally submit to His will, out of love, hope and fear, and translate that into reality. Allah Almighty says, {{Q:4:136}} (Soorat An-Nisaa’, 4:136)

passages.heading: 1 Islam is a Universal Religion
passages.text: Islam is not only for the Arabs; rather, it is the religion that Allah Almighty has approved for all mankind. Addressing His Messenger Muhammad ﷺ, the Almighty says, {{Q:21:107}} (*Soorat Al-Anbiyaa’, 21:107*). Thus, Prophet Muhammad ﷺ is a mercy to all people without exception, guiding them to the path of faith; and, of all laws, his law reflects all aspects of mercy for people.

passages.heading: Levels of Worship

passages.text:
Islam is essentially the religion of all the prophets: to worship Allah alone and reject all false deities that are worshipped besides or instead of Him. Allah Almighty, says, {{Q:21:25}} (Surat al-Anbiyyaa’, 21:25).

Therefore, it is not permissible, under any circumstances, to believe in any deity other than Allah Almighty, nor is it permissible to perform any act of worship to draw nearer to anyone other than Allah Almighty.

passages.text: It is not enough to verbally declare the two testimonies of faith. In addition to this, it is imperative to know what they mean and to meet their requirements. The testimony that there is no god but Allah requires us to reject everything that is worshipped besides or instead of Allah, to firmly believe that Allah alone is our Lord and Cherisher and the One True God worthy of worship and to worship Him sincerely. Allah Almighty says, {{Q:2:256}} (Soorat Al-Baqarah, 2:256) The testimony that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah requires us to believe what he says, do what he commands and avoid what he forbids and worship Allah only according to his instructions.

passages.heading: Introduction
passages.text: In his life, a Muslim performs a number of acts of worship whereby he draws closer to his Creator, Glory is to Him. We do such acts to glorify Allah Almighty and submit to Him alone. The more a Muslim’s heart glorifies Allah, Exalted be He, the greater the effect of doing so is on his worship. A true Muslim dedicates all life, including the time he spends at work, sleeping and having fun, to Allah Almighty, bearing in mind the verse: {{Q:6:162-163}} (Soorat Al-An’aam, 6:162-163) In this lesson, we are going to learn about the meaning of worship, its types, the conditions that must be met for it to be accepted, and its levels.

passages.heading: Introduction
passages.text: A Muslim often experiences peace and tranquillity when he reads or recites the Qur’an or worships Allah Almighty by engaging in prayer or any other act of worship. This good feeling which elevates some to higher levels of happiness and joy is one of the significant effects of faith that motivates Muslims to dedicate all their lives to Allah, comply with His commands cheerfully and out of love and avoid what He forbids in utter submission and obedience. In this lesson, we are going to learn about the concept of faith and its pillars and benefits.

passages.heading: Discuss
passages.text: What is the difference between hope and fear?

passages.heading: The Pillars of Faith
passages.text:
The Muslim faith rests on six pillars, namely:

1. **Belief in Allah:** A Muslim believes that Allah Almighty exists and believes in His names and attributes. He equally believes that He is the Lord and sole Creator of this vast universe, to whom belongs everything in it, who manages all its affairs and provides sustenance to all His creation, that there is no god is worthy of worship besides or instead of Him and that He has perfect attributes.
2. **Belief in the angels:** A Muslim believes that the honourable angels exist, that it is Allah Almighty who created them and that they worship Him, execute His commands and never disobey Him. He also believes in their attributes and duties which are mentioned in the Book and the *Sunnah*.

passages.heading: Shirk
passages.text:
This means the act of holding someone or something as equal to Allah and directing acts of worship to them. It is a grave and an unforgivable sin. The Qur’an says, {{Q:4:48}} (Soorat An-Nisaa’, 4:48).

By the phrase “the Book and Sunnah” is meant the Noble Qur’an and the sayings of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, as they are the two main sources of legislation in Islam.

*Ar-Rahmaan*: The All-Gracious whose mercy encompasses all His creation; *Ar-Raheem*: The All-Merciful who bestows His special mercy to the believers.

passages.heading: The Blessing of Right Guidance
passages.text: Whoever knows the purpose of his existence and the outcome that awaits people on the Day of Resurrection is bound to realise that the greatest blessing that Allah has ever bestowed upon people is that of guidance to the true religion and righteous deeds. Therefore, Allah Almighty has enjoined His servants to ask Him in their prayer to guide them to the straight path—the religion of Islam which leads to Allah’s good pleasure.

passages.text:

It is the path of those whom You have blessed with guidance from among the prophets and their supporters, and those who follow in their footsteps—These are the ones who have been rightly guided.

passages.heading: Soorat Al-Falaq Explained
passages.text:
“Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of the daybreak” Say, Messenger: I seek refuge and protection in Allah, the Lord of the daybreak.

“from the evil of what He has created”

from the evil of everything He has created, visible and invisible.

“and from the evil of the night when it spreads its darkness”

and from the evil of the night when it comes and grows dark, and of whatever evil and harm that may happen in it.

Al-ghasaq: the intense darkness of the night

Al-falaq: the daybreak

passages.heading: The Meaning of the Prayer
passages.text:
The prayer: It is a daily act of worship that consists of a set of words and actions with which a Muslim seeks to draw closer to his Lord, and it is performed five times a day and night.

The prayer is the second pillar of Islam.

passages.heading: Learning Your religion
passages.text:
- A Muslim is required to learn his religion based on sound knowledge in order to worship his Lord properly.
- The Prophet ﷺ urges us to study and understand our religion. He once said, “When Allah wishes to bestow His favour on someone, He makes him understand the religion.” (Reported by Al-Bukhaaree; No. 71).
- The Prophet ﷺ states that acquiring religious knowledge leads to Paradise. He once said, “Whoever treads a path in search of knowledge, Allah will ease the way to Paradise for him.” (Saheeh Ibn Hibbaan; No. 84).

passages.heading: The Virtue of Reading/Reciting the Qur’an
passages.text:
- The Prophet ﷺ said, “If anyone reads/recites one single letter in Allah’s Book, he will be credited with a good deed, and a good deed gets a tenfold reward. I do not say that *alif*, *laam*, *meem* are one letter; rather, *alif* is a letter, *laam* is a letter and *meem* is a letter” (Reported by At-Tirmidhee; No. 2910 with an authentic chain of narrators).

- The Prophet ﷺ also said, “Read the Qur’an, for it will come on the Day of Resurrection as an intercessor for those who read it.” (Reported by Muslim; No. 804).

passages.heading: Soorat Al-Faatiẖah (The Opening)
passages.text:
*Soorat Al-Faatiẖah* Explained

“In the name of Allah, the All-Compassionate, the All-Merciful”

I begin reading the Qur’an in the name of Allah, seeking the help of Allah, the True Deity, the All-Compassionate, whose mercy encompasses all creation in general, the All-Merciful, who bestows His special mercy to the believers.

“Praise be to Allah, Lord of all the worlds”

All praise is due to Allah for His perfect attributes and for His grace towards all His creation. He alone is worthy of all forms of praise and is the Lord of all creation, who has created all that exists out of absolutely nothing, who manages all their affairs and improves their condition.

passages.heading: Discuss
passages.text: What are the means of memorizing *Soorat Al-Faatihah*?

passages.heading: Soorat Al-Ikhlaas Explained
passages.text:
“Say: He is Allah, the One and Only”

Say, Messenger, to those who ask you about your Lord: He is Allah, the One and Only Lord and God, besides whom there is no deity deserving of worship.

“Allah, the Everlasting Sustainer of all”

He is Allah, the Eternal and Absolute God with perfect attributes, to whom all creation turns to fulfil their needs, while He stands in need of none.

“He has not begotten anyone, nor was He Himself begotten by anyone”

He is Allah, who has no offspring whatsoever, neither son nor daughter, and He has no parents, neither father nor mother.

“And none is equal to Him”

And there is no one and nothing among His creation that resembles Him in any way whatsoever with regard to His being, names attributes or actions.

passages.heading: The Third Question
passages.text:
#### Where Do We Go?

The Qur’an teaches that every human being will die and, following his death, the stage of doing deeds will end and the stage of judgement and recompense will begin. The Almighty says, {{Q:39:30-31}} (Soorat Az-Zumar, 39:30-31).

Thus when a person dies, he moves on to a stage in which he will be asked about his religion and will be repaid according to his deeds. The Almighty says, {{Q:3:185}} (Soorat Aal-’Imraan, 3:185).

When the Day of Resurrection comes, Allah will raise the dead from their graves for judgement and recompense. The believers will be rewarded with Paradise, while the unbelievers will be punished in Hell. The Almighty says, {{Q:42:7}} (Soorat Ash-Shooraa, 42:7).

passages.heading: Discuss
passages.text:
Settling on earth and building a civilization on it is one of man’s roles in this life. To enable him to perform this great and challenging task, Allah has provided him with such physical and mental make-ups to help him perform this role. Explain how, of all other creatures, only man can settle on earth and build a civilization?

Mention some of the practical implications of getting to know the ultimate fate of people after death?

passages.heading: Belajar agama:
passages.text:
- Seorang Muslim wajib mempelajari ilmu yang dia butuhkan dalam perkara agamanya agar dia beribadah kepada Tuhannya berdasarkan ilmu.
- Nabi ﷺ menganjurkan untuk belajar agama seraya bersabda, *"Siapa yang Allah kehendaki baginya kebaikan, niscaya Allah akan menjadikannya paham tentang urusan agamanya."* (HR. Bukhari: 71)
- Nabi ﷺ mengabarkan bahwa belajar ilmu agama adalah jalan untuk masuk surga. Beliau bersabda, *"Siapa yang menempuh sebuah jalan dalam rangka mencari ilmu, maka Allah akan memudahkan baginya jalan menuju surga."* (HR. Muslim: 2699)

Tersedia banyak buku yang bisa dimanfaatkan oleh seorang Muslim untuk mempelajari hukum-hukum dalam agamanya sehingga dia dapat beribadah kepada Tuhannya di atas dasar ilmu. Hendaklah dia berkonsultasi kepada para ahli untuk mengarahkannya kepada buku yang paling bagus.

passages.heading: Pendahuluan
passages.text: Islam adalah agama yang dengannya Allah mengutus Muhammad ﷺ dan merupakan kelanjutan dari agama yang dibawa oleh rasul-rasul terdahulu. Pilar Islam tegak di atas konsep bahwa sembahan yang berhak disembah ialah tunggal, tidak memiliki sekutu, yaitu Allah Jalla wa 'Alā; tidak ada yang membantu-Nya dalam kerajaan-Nya dan tidak pula ada perantara antara Dia dan hamba-hamba-Nya. Hanya saja, mengapa saya harus memeluk Islam? Apakah Islam agama bagi seluruh umat manusia ataukah khusus bagi bangsa Arab? Siapakah nabi Islam? Apakah akan ada nabi lain yang datang setelahnya?

passages.heading: Syarat Diterimanya Ibadah
passages.text:
Ada dua syarat untuk diterimanya ibadah: Pertama: ikhlas kepada Allah. Oleh karena itu, seorang muslim harus mengerjakan ibadah hanya untuk mendekatkan diri kepada Allah saja, tanpa ada kesyirikan maupun ria. Kedua: sesuai syariat Allah. Jadi, seorang muslim harus menunaikan ibadah sebagaimana yang disyariatkan oleh Allah Ta’ālā dan seperti yang dipraktikkan oleh Nabi ﷺ.

Ria ialah seorang Muslim mengerjakan ibadah dengan tujuan supaya dilihat orang ketika mengerjakannya lalu mereka memujinya atas perbuatannya itu.

passages.heading: Mengapa Saya Masuk Islam?
passages.text:
**Mungkin sebagian orang bertanya-tanya: mengapa saya harus masuk Islam?**

Jawabannya: Saya harus masuk Islam karena beberapa faktor, di antaranya:

Pertama: agama Islam adalah agama yang diridai oleh Allah bagi hamba-hamba-Nya, dan Allah tidak menerima agama lainnya dari siapa pun. Dia berfirman, {{Q:3:85}} (QS. Āli 'Imrān: 85)

Kedua: agama Islam adalah agama para nabi semuanya. Islam memerintahkan beriman kepada para nabi seluruhnya, dan tidak membeda-bedakan di antara mereka. Allah Ta'ālā berfirman, {{Q:2:136}} (QS. Al-Baqarah: 136)

passages.heading: Konsekuensi Dua Kalimat Syahadat
passages.text:
Tidak cukup hanya melafalkan dua kalimat syahadat. Akan tetapi, harus mengerti maknanya serta mengamalkan apa yang menjadi konsekuensinya. Syahadat *lā ilāha illallāh* memiliki konsekuensi berupa ingkar terhadap semua yang disembah selain Allah *Ta’ālā* serta mengimani bahwa Allah saja sebagai tuhan dan sembahan yang berhak terhadap ibadah disertai keikhlasan dalam beribadah kepada-Nya. Allah *Ta’ālā* berfirman, *"Barang siapa ingkar kepada tagut dan beriman kepada Allah, maka sungguh dia telah berpegang (teguh) pada tali yang sangat kuat yang tidak akan putus."* (QS. Al-Baqarah: 256)

Sedangkan konsekuensi syahadat *"muḥammad rasūlullāh"* ialah membenarkan berita yang beliau sampaikan, menaati perintah yang beliau perintahkan atau larangan yang beliau larang, serta Allah tidak diibadahi kecuali dengan syariat yang beliau bawa.

passages.heading: Jumlah pengulangan membasuh anggota wudu
passages.text: Disunahkan dalam wudu untuk membasuh setiap anggota sebanyak tiga kali, kecuali mengusap kepala dan telinga, maka cukup sekali saja. Dibolehkan mencukupkan dengan satu kali basuhan pada anggota yang dibasuh dengan syarat dibasuh seluruhnya.

passages.heading: Bagaimana Cara Kita Mandi?
passages.text:
Ketika mandi, kita harus mengalirkan air ke seluruh tubuh disertai berkumur-kumur dan menarik air ke dalam hidung. Bila itu telah dilakukan oleh seorang Muslim, maka dia telah suci dari hadas besar.

Hadas besar ialah hadas yang mewajibkan mandi demi menghilangkannya dan tidak cukup dengan wudu. Hadas besar memiliki beberapa macam:
1. Junub; yaitu sebuah keadaan pada laki-laki dan perempuan bila terjadi hubungan suami istri antara keduanya atau keluar mani dengan syahwat walaupun tanpa hubungan suami istri.
2. Haid; yaitu darah bulanan yang keluar dari perempuan.
3. Nifas; yaitu darah yang keluar dari perempuan setelah janin keluar dari rahimnya.

passages.heading: Hukum-hukum yang berkaitan dengan bersuci:
passages.text:
- Hukum asal segala sesuatu adalah suci, dan tidak boleh menghukumi sesuatu sebagai najis kecuali yang dihukumi najis oleh agama.
- Cukup dalam menyucikan badan atau pakaian dari najis dengan cara menghilangkannya menggunakan air atau pembersih lainnya.
- Bila seseorang masuk WC untuk buang hajat, maka yang paling afdal ialah dia membersihkan tempat keluarnya kencing dan tinja menggunakan air, dan diperbolehkan untuk dibersihkan dengan tisu atau media lainnya yang dapat menghilangkan najis.

passages.heading: Standar perbedaan tingkat keutamaan dalam Islam
passages.text:
Allah 'Azza wa Jalla telah menjadikan standar perbedaan tingkat keutamaan di antara hamba-hamba-Nya berdasarkan keimanan dan ketakwaan. Perbedaan keutamaan di antara kaum muslimin berdasarkan tingkat kekuatan iman mereka, bukan berdasarkan rupa, nasab, warna kulit, maupun harta mereka. Allah Ta’ālā berfirman, *"Wahai manusia! Sungguh, Kami telah menciptakan kamu dari seorang laki-laki dan seorang perempuan, kemudian Kami jadikan kamu berbangsa-bangsa dan bersuku-suku agar kamu saling mengenal. Sungguh, yang paling mulia di antara kamu di sisi Allah ialah orang yang paling bertakwa. Sungguh, Allah Maha Mengetahui lagi Mahateliti."* (QS. Al-Ḥujurāt: 13)

Nabi ﷺ juga bersabda, *"Wahai sekalian manusia! Ketahuilah, sesungguhnya sembahan kalian satu, dan bapak kalian satu. Tidak ada keutamaan bagi seorang Arab atas non-Arab, tidak juga non-Arab atas Arab, tidak bagi yang berkulit merah atas kulit hitam, tidak juga kulit hitam atas kulit merah, kecuali dengan ketakwaan."* (HR. Al-Baihaqiy dalam Syu’ab al-Īmān: 4774)

passages.heading: Rukun Islam
passages.text:
Agama Islam dibangun di atas lima rukun (pilar):

Setiap Muslim harus berkomitmen dengan rukun-rukun ini supaya keislamannya utuh, sebab cacat pada salah satu rukun ini akan berdampak buruk terhadap keislamannya.

passages.heading: Rukun Islam
passages.text:
1. **Dua kalimat syahadat**  
   *Syahadat Lā ilāha illallāh Muhammad rasūlullāh* (Tidak ada sembahan yang benar kecuali Allah, Muhammad adalah utusan Allah)
2. **Menegakkan salat**  
   Seorang Muslim wajib mengerjakan lima salat setiap hari. Hal ini akan dijelaskan pada buku ini.
3. **Menunaikan zakat**
4. **Berpuasa Ramadan**
5. **Berhaji ke Baitullah**

passages.heading: Mengapa Saya Masuk Islam?
passages.text: Perbedaan di antara para nabi terletak pada hukum-hukum syariat yang berkaitan dengan perbuatan hamba, sebagaimana Allah Subḥānahu wa Ta'ālā berfirman, {{Q:5:48}} (QS. Al-Mā'idah: 48) Maksudnya ialah Allah menetapkan bagi masing-masing umat satu syariat yang mereka jadikan sebagai acuan hukum serta jalan yang mereka lalui dalam mendekatkan diri kepada Allah. Sebab itu, masing-masing umat memiliki hukum yang khusus bagi mereka serta syariat-syariat yang sesuai dengan kondisi mereka. Adapun dalam persoalan akidah, maka akidah semua nabi sama. Kemudian Allah mengutus penutup para nabi dan rasul-Nya, Muhammad ﷺ. Dengannya, Allah menutup semua rasul, dengan syariatnya pula Allah menutup semua syariat. Sebab itulah, Allah tidak akan menerima agama selain Islam dari siapa pun.

passages.heading: Pelajaran 2
passages.text:
### Apakah Islam Itu?

Ketiga: masuk Islam adalah jalan kebahagiaan di dunia dan keselamatan di akhirat. Orang yang sampai kepadanya dakwah Nabi Muhammad ﷺ tidak akan selamat di akhirat kelak kecuali bila ia beriman kepadanya serta mengikutinya. Allah Ta’ālā berfirman, “Barang siapa mencari agama selain Islam, ia tidak akan diterima dan di akhirat dia termasuk orang yang rugi.” (QS. Āli ‘Imrān: 85)

Nabi ﷺ bersabda, “Demi (Tuhan) yang jiwa Muhammad berada di tangan-Nya! Tidak ada seorang pun dari umat ini, baik Yahudi maupun Nasrani, yang mendengar tentang diriku lalu ia meninggal dalam keadaan tidak beriman kepada apa yang aku bawa, melainkan ia adalah penghuni neraka.” (HR. Muslim: 153)

Keempat: Islam memberikan jawaban sempurna terhadap pertanyaan-pertanyaan besarku: untuk apa aku hadir ke dunia? Dari mana aku berasal? Dan kemana aku akan pergi setelah kematian?

Kelima: Islam adalah agama yang sejalan dengan fitrah, mulai dari nilai Islam yang paling besar, yaitu menauhidkan Allah, hingga pada adab-adabnya yang mengajak kepada akhlak baik nan lurus.

passages.heading: Ibadah tarkiyah (berupa meninggalkan sesuatu)
passages.text: Seorang muslim mendekatkan diri kepada Tuhannya dengan meninggalkan perkara yang diharamkan baginya, seperti meninggalkan Muslim khamar dan zina, atau meninggalkan sebagian perkara mubah di waktu-waktu tertentu, seperti meninggalkan makan dan minum ketika berpuasa.

passages.heading: Diskusikan!
passages.text: Kerugian apa yang akan didapat oleh pelaku ria ketika ia meninggalkan ikhlas kepada Allah?

passages.heading: Tingkatan Ibadah
passages.text:
Ibadah terbagi ke dalam berbagai tingkatan berbeda.

- Di antaranya ada yang wajib atas semua Muslim, seperti salat.
- Ada juga yang wajib atas sebagian Muslim, seperti zakat, yaitu wajib atas orang-orang kaya, tidak kepada orang fakir.
- Di antaranya juga ada yang disunahkan mengerjakannya dan tidak wajib, seperti doa dan zikir yang dibaca setelah salat.

passages.text:

passages.text: أن لا يكون شفافاً يظهر أعضاء البدن تحته.

passages.heading: Introduction
passages.text: When Allah sent prophets to their people to call them to the truth, he supported them with some miracles to prove to them that they were true prophets. These miracles, however, ended with the passing of these prophets. As for the Messenger of Islam ﷺ, Allah also furnished him with certain miracles to show his people, and all mankind, for that matter, but the greatest of all of them was His Glorious Book, which He took upon Himself to preserve even after the demise of His prophet ﷺ. In this lesson, we are going to learn about some virtues and etiquette associated with the Qur’an.

passages.heading: Stories of the Prophets in the Qur’an
passages.text:
The Holy Qur’an is replete with stories of the previous prophets and their people, starting with Adam, and passing through Noah, Hud, Saalih, Shu’ayb, Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, Moses, Jesus, and other prophets and messengers, peace be upon them all. The Holy Qur’an mentions their stories for a number of reasons, including the following:

- to show that the religion of all the prophets is, in essence, the same and that its basis is to worship Allah Almighty alone.
- to give solace to Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and make him stand firm and steadfast, reminding him that prophets before him suffered the same hardships he himself was experiencing.
- to give comfort and solace to the believers, reminding them that even Allah’s honourable servants before them were afflicted with trials and tribulations.
- to afford people the opportunity to learn lessons from such true stories.

passages.heading: Why Should I Embrace Islam?
passages.text:
Some people may ask: Why should I embrace Islam?

The answer is: I must do so for a number of reasons, including the following:

1. Islam is the religion that Allah has approved and chosen for His servants and will not accept any other religion. The Almighty says, {{Q:3:85}} (Soorat Aal-’Imraan, 3:85).

2. Islam is the religion of all the prophets and commands its adherents to believe in all of them without exception. Allah says, {{Q:2:136}} (Soorat Al-Baqarah, 2:136).
The difference between prophets lies only in the laws relating to people’s actions, as the Almighty says, {{Q:5:48}} (Soorat Al-Maa’idah, 5:48) That is, for each nation before Islam, Allah appointed a law to which people referred for their disputes and a way of life whereby they drew near to Him. Thus, followers of every prophet had their respective laws and regulations, but the set of beliefs to which prophets called their people was the same. Then Allah sent the last prophet and messenger, Muhammad ﷺ, with the final divine laws, and thus the only religion acceptable to Allah is Islam.

Islam is essentially the religion of all the prophets: to worship Allah alone and reject all false deities that are worshipped besides or instead of Him. Allah Almighty, says, {{Q:21:25}} (Surat al-Anbiyyaa’, 21:25).

Therefore, it is not permissible, under any circumstances, to believe in any deity other than Allah Almighty, nor is it permissible to perform any act of worship to draw nearer to anyone other than Allah Almighty.

passages.heading: What Is the Qur’an?
passages.text:
The Holy Qur’an is the Word of Allah Almighty that He revealed to His Messenger, Muhammad ﷺ. It is the last of Allah’s revealed books, and there is no other book after it.

The revealed books are the books that Allah Almighty revealed to His prophets.
A Muslim believes that these books were revealed by Allah Almighty, and that Allah spoke in them in a manner that befits Him. These books include Az-Zaboor (the Psalms), which He revealed to Daawood (David) عليه السلام; At-Tawraat (the Torah), which He revealed to Moosaa (Moses) عليه السلام and Al-Injeel (the Gospel), which He revealed to Jesus, عليه السلام. All these books have undergone alteration and corruption through the ages.

passages.heading: Discuss
passages.text: What Qur’anic verses did you read before your conversion to Islam? How did they affect you?

passages.heading: Shirk
passages.text:
3. **Belief in the divinely revealed books:** A Muslim believes that Allah sent down divine books to His Messengers to guide people to the truth and teach them their religion. These include the Torah (*At-Tawraah*) which He revealed to Moses (Moosaa) son of ‘Imraan, the Zaboor which He revealed to David (Daawood), the Gospel (*Al-Injeel*) which He revealed to Jesus (‘Eesaa) son of Mary and the Qur’an which He revealed to Muhammad, peace be upon them all. He also believes that the Qur’an is the last of them and that it has final authority over them all.
4. **Belief in the prophets:** A Muslim believes that Allah Almighty sent messengers to their people and supported them with miracles to prove their truthfulness. He sent them to give the believers good news of reward, warn the unbelievers of punishment and teach their people their religion. Those to whom they were sent must obey and follow them. Muhammad ﷺ was the final prophet whom He sent to all mankind.
5. **Belief in the Last Day:** A Muslim believes in Resurrection Day. He believes that Allah will raise the dead from their graves on that day and judge and repay them according to their deeds. Some will enter Paradise while others will enter Hell.
6. **Belief in the divine decree:** A Muslim believes that everything in this universe, whether good or evil, happens according to Allah’s decree, that He foreknows all events which He has already written in the Preserved Tablet, and that everything in this universe happens according to His will.

passages.heading: Introduction
passages.text: People have always pondered the big questions of human existence: Where did we come from? Why are we here? Where do we go after death? Islam provides definitive and conclusive answers to these questions which arise in the heart of every reflective human being.

passages.heading: Lesson 1
passages.text: ## Learn about the Holy Qur’an

passages.heading: The Virtue of Reading/Reciting the Qur’an
passages.text:
- The Prophet ﷺ said, “If anyone reads/recites one single letter in Allah’s Book, he will be credited with a good deed, and a good deed gets a tenfold reward. I do not say that *alif*, *laam*, *meem* are one letter; rather, *alif* is a letter, *laam* is a letter and *meem* is a letter” (Reported by At-Tirmidhee; No. 2910 with an authentic chain of narrators).

- The Prophet ﷺ also said, “Read the Qur’an, for it will come on the Day of Resurrection as an intercessor for those who read it.” (Reported by Muslim; No. 804).

passages.heading: Lesson 1
passages.text: ## Learn about the Holy Qur’an

passages.heading: The Qur’an is a Way of Life
passages.text: A Muslim should be keen on reading/reciting the Holy Qur’an and studying the rules it prescribes.

passages.heading: Its miraculous nature
passages.text: The Arab unbelievers rejected the Qur’an, so Allah challenged them to produce the like of it, or one soorah like it, or even ten verses, but they were unable to do so.

passages.heading: Its language
passages.text: Allah Almighty revealed it in Arabic.

passages.heading: Introduction
passages.text: Islam is the religion with which Allah sent Muhammad ﷺ and is an extension of the same religion with which all the previous messengers came. It is essentially based on the belief that Allah Almighty is the only deity deserving of worship, who has no partners or assistants whatsoever in His kingdom, and who has no intermediaries between Him and His servants. But why should I embrace Islam? Is it a religion for all people or is it only for the Arabs? Who is its prophet, and is there another prophet who will come after him?

3. Islam is the way to happiness in this life and salvation in the life to come; therefore, those who believe in Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and follow him after his message has reached them will be saved; as for those who deny him, they will be doomed to divine punishment. The Almighty says, {{Q:3:85}} (*Soorat Aal-’Imraan, 3:85*) The Prophet ﷺ also said, “By Him in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, any person of this Community, Jew or Christian, who hears of me and dies without believing in what I have been sent with will be among the dwellers of Hell” (*Saheeh Muslim;* No. 153).

4. Islam gives conclusive answers to the big questions of human existence: Where did we come from? Why are we here? Where do we go after death?

5. Islam is in perfect harmony with the innate human nature (*fitrah*), beginning with the greatest value it embraces, namely the declaration of Allah’s unity, and ending with the rules of etiquette it teaches its adherents to enable them to attain great perfection in moral excellence.

passages.heading: Discuss
passages.text: How can Islam be considered the religion of all the prophets?

passages.heading: Some Distinguishing Characteristics of Islam
passages.text: Islam is distinguished from other religions by many characteristics, the most prominent of which are:

passages.heading: 1. The Meaning of the Testimony that There Is no God but Allah
passages.text:
The meaning of “I bear witness that there is no god but Allah” is: I firmly believe that there is no god worthy of worship except Allah alone.

This testimony consists of two parts:

| The first part | The second part |
| --- | --- |
| negates the existence of any other deity besides Allah Almighty | confirms that Allah is the only True God worthy of worship |

passages.heading: 2. The Meaning of the Testimony that Muhammad is Allah’s Messenger
passages.text: The meaning of the testimony that Muhammad is Allah’s Messenger is: I firmly believe that Muhammad ﷺ is the Messenger of Allah, that he is the Final Prophet without there being any prophet whatsoever after him, and that his message is for all people without exception. Allah Almighty says: {{Q:25:1}} (Surat Al-Furqaan, 25:1).

passages.heading: The Requirements of the Two Testimonies of Faith
passages.text: It is not enough to verbally declare the two testimonies of faith. In addition to this, it is imperative to know what they mean and to meet their requirements. The testimony that there is no god but Allah requires us to reject everything that is worshipped besides or instead of Allah, to firmly believe that Allah alone is our Lord and Cherisher and the One True God worthy of worship and to worship Him sincerely. Allah Almighty says, {{Q:2:256}} (Soorat Al-Baqarah, 2:256) The testimony that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah requires us to believe what he says, do what he commands and avoid what he forbids and worship Allah only according to his instructions.

passages.heading: The Qur’an is Food for the Soul and Mind
passages.text:
The Holy Qur’an addresses both people’s minds and souls. It addresses the mind by:

- encouraging them to use logical reasoning on the various issues. The Almighty says, {{Q:21:22}} (Soorat Al-Anbiyyaa’, 21:22).
- calling them to exercise their intellects and contemplate His signs and the proofs of His power. The Almighty says, {{Q:2:219}} (Soorat Al-Baqarah, 2:219).
- reproving those who do not use their intellects to reflect on His signs. The Almighty says, {{Q:25:44}} (Soorat Al-Furqaan, 25: 44).

It also addresses the soul and emotions by:

- spotlighting and depicting human feelings in many cases. The Almighty says, {{Q:2:165}} (Soorat Al-Baqarah, 2:165).
- calling attention to human emotions and pointing out their good and bad effects. The Almighty says, {{Q:5:82}} (Soorat Al-Maa’idah, 5:82).
- commanding Muslims to exercise kindness and gentleness when inviting others to Islam. The Almighty says, {{Q:16:125}} (Soorat An-Nahl, 16: 125).
- incorporating aspects of faith into verses on legal rules. The Almighty says, {{Q:4:94}} (Soorat An-Nisaa’, 4:94).
- using moving words that evoke genuine emotions. The Almighty says, {{Q:24:22}} (Soorat An-Noor, 24:22).

passages.heading: Definisi Ibadah
passages.text: Ibadah ialah amal perbuatan yang disyariatkan oleh Allah agar dengannya seorang Muslim mendekatkan diri kepada-Nya. Ibadah ini mencakup semua perbuatan dan perkataan yang dicintai oleh Allah, baik yang tampak seperti ibadah-ibadah badan semisal salat dan haji, maupun yang tidak tampak seperti ibadah-ibadah hati semisal cinta, takut, harap kepada Allah, dan ibadah-ibadah hati lainnya. Seorang hamba bisa mengubah kebiasaannya menjadi bernilai ibadah dengan menyertakan niat yang baik; yaitu apabila ia meniatkan makan, minum, dan tidurnya dalam rangka memperkuat diri untuk melakukan ketaatan kepada Allah, niscaya ia akan diberikan pahala atas hal itu.

passages.heading: Siapakah kita?
passages.text:
Allah berikan padanya kemungkinan untuk baik dan kemungkinan untuk buruk. Allah juga membekalinya sesuatu untuk membedakan kebaikan dan keburukan, seperti fitrah dan akal.

Allah menjadikannya merdeka, berhak memilih, dan bertanggung jawab terhadap pilihan dan amal perbuatannya.

passages.heading: Mengapa Saya Masuk Islam?
passages.text: Perbedaan di antara para nabi terletak pada hukum-hukum syariat yang berkaitan dengan perbuatan hamba, sebagaimana Allah Subḥānahu wa Ta'ālā berfirman, {{Q:5:48}} (QS. Al-Mā'idah: 48) Maksudnya ialah Allah menetapkan bagi masing-masing umat satu syariat yang mereka jadikan sebagai acuan hukum serta jalan yang mereka lalui dalam mendekatkan diri kepada Allah. Sebab itu, masing-masing umat memiliki hukum yang khusus bagi mereka serta syariat-syariat yang sesuai dengan kondisi mereka. Adapun dalam persoalan akidah, maka akidah semua nabi sama. Kemudian Allah mengutus penutup para nabi dan rasul-Nya, Muhammad ﷺ. Dengannya, Allah menutup semua rasul, dengan syariatnya pula Allah menutup semua syariat. Sebab itulah, Allah tidak akan menerima agama selain Islam dari siapa pun.

passages.heading: Apa Syarat-syarat Penyembelihan yang Disyariatkan?
passages.text:
Penyembelihan yang disyariatkan ialah penyembelihan yang memenuhi syarat-syarat berikut:

1. Orang yang menyembelih adalah seorang Muslim, Yahudi, atau Nasrani yang mampu membedakan (baik dan buruk), serta meniatkan penyembelihan.
2. Alat yang digunakan bisa menyembelih, mengalirkan darah, dan memotong dengan ketajamannya, seperti pisau. Haram hukumnya menggunakan alat yang membunuh dengan berat bebannya dan benturannya pada kepala hewan, atau dengan sengatannya seperti setrum listrik.
3. Menyebut nama Allah dengan membaca, “Bismillāh” ketika menggerakkan tangan untuk menyembelih.
4. Memotong bagian yang wajib dipotong dalam penyembelihan, yaitu *marī`* (saluran makanan), *ḥulqūm* (saluran napas), *wadajān* (dua urat besar pada leher), atau memotong 3 di antara 4 saluran ini.

passages.heading: Rukun Islam
passages.text:
Agama Islam dibangun di atas lima rukun (pilar):

Setiap Muslim harus berkomitmen dengan rukun-rukun ini supaya keislamannya utuh, sebab cacat pada salah satu rukun ini akan berdampak buruk terhadap keislamannya.

passages.heading: Pendahuluan
passages.text: Salah satu keagungan agama Islam ialah ajarannya mencakup semua lini kehidupan manusia. Di antaranya, perhatian agama untuk mengatur hubungan muamalah manusia di antara mereka, menjaga hak-hak mereka, dan mencegah terjadinya kezaliman terhadap siapa pun di antara mereka. Di antara bentuk perhatian Islam terhadap hal ini adalah menetapkan aturan dan batasan yang mengatur persoalan muamalah di antara mereka. Pada pelajaran ini, kita akan mengenal lebih jauh tentang beberapa hukum muamalah harta dan faktor pengharaman terhadap sebagiannya.

passages.heading: Harta Apa Sajakah yang Wajib Zakat?
passages.text:
- Emas dan perak
- Uang
- Hasil pertanian dan buah-buahan
- Hewan ternak
  Hewan ternak yaitu unta, sapi, dan kambing.
- Barang dagangan
  Barang dagangan maksudnya semua barang yang disiapkan dengan tujuan dagang, berupa rumah, toko, mobil, binatang, dan lain sebagainya.

passages.heading: Buah Keimanan
passages.text:
- Ketenangan jiwa; karena iman menjadikan jiwa seorang mukmin merasa tenang serta rida kepada Allah dan kepada takdir-Nya, ia tidak takut kecuali kepada Allah.
- Mengenal Allah *Ta’ālā*; yaitu orang yang beriman akan mengenal Tuhannya pada tingkat menambah keterikatannya dengan-Nya, sehingga ia bisa mengenal nama, sifat, dan perbuatan-perbuatan-Nya.
- Mengagungkan Allah; karena orang beriman itu, semakin ia mengenal Tuhannya maka akan semakin bertambah mengagungkan dan memuliakan-Nya, bertambah cinta dan harap kepada-Nya, dan bertambah takut kepada-Nya.
- Merasakan karunia Allah kepada hamba-hamba-Nya; yaitu Allah telah mengutus para rasul kepada mereka serta menurunkan kitab-kitab supaya mereka mendapat petunjuk kepada agama yang benar.
- Mencintai malaikat; karena ibadah dan ketaatan mereka kepada Allah.
- Mencintai para rasul; karena Allah *Ta’ālā* telah memilih mereka untuk menyampaikan agama-Nya kepada manusia.
- Bersungguh-sungguh dalam ibadah; karena semakin kuat tingkat keimanan, maka akan bertambah ibadah seseorang.
- Kehidupan yang baik; yaitu orang yang beriman akan rida dengan pembagian Allah untuknya. Dia mengetahui bahwa musibah yang menimpanya di dunia sebagai pengangkat derajatnya dan penghapus kesalahannya, sebagaimana ia mengharapkan kenikmatan surga yang Allah siapkan bagi orang beriman di akhirat.
- Tidak teperdaya dengan dunia; karena kehidupan dunia bersifat sementara dan merupakan sarana menuju kehidupan abadi di akhirat.
- Membongkar khurafat; karena keimanan membongkar banyak khurafat serta membatalkannya.
- Masuk surga yang merupakan negeri kenikmatan abadi yang tidak berhenti. Allah *Ta’ālā* telah mengkhususkannya bagi orang-orang yang beriman di antara hamba-Nya.

passages.heading: Pendahuluan
passages.text:
Dalam kehidupannya, seorang Muslim rutin mengerjakan sejumlah ibadah demi mendekatkan diri kepada Sang Pencipta *Subḥānahu wa Ta’ālā*. Tujuan semua ibadah ini ialah untuk mengagungkan Allah *'Azza wa Jalla* serta merendahkan diri kepada-Nya semata. Semakin jiwa seorang muslim mengagungkan Allah, maka dampaknya pada ibadahnya semakin terlihat. Muslim sejati adalah yang menjadikan seluruh hidupnya termasuk pekerjaannya, tidurnya, dan waktu santainya hanya untuk Allah *Subḥānahu wa Ta’ālā*, sebagai implementasi firman Allah *Ta’ālā*: {{Q:6:162-163}} (QS. Al-An’ām: 162-163)

Pada pelajaran ini kita akan mengenal lebih jauh tentang makna ibadah, macam-macamnya, syarat diterimanya, dan tingkatannya.

passages.heading: Macam-macam ibadah:
passages.text: Ibadah terbagi menjadi beberapa macam:

passages.heading: Ibadah hati
passages.text:
Yaitu ibadah yang dikerjakan oleh seorang Muslim dengan hatinya, seperti cinta, takut, harap, dan khusyuk.

Harap ialah menanti kabar gembira berupa karunia Allah dan mengharapkan kebaikan dan anugerah-Nya disertai mengerahkan usaha keras dan bertawakal dengan baik kepada Allah.

Khusyuk ialah kondisi yang di dalamnya jiwa merasa tenang dan pikiran tidak bercabang saat menunaikan ibadah seperti salat dan imbasnya akan terlihat pada ketenangan anggota badan.

passages.heading: Ibadah badan
passages.text: Yaitu ibadah yang dikerjakan oleh seorang Muslim dengan anggota badannya, seperti salat, zakat, dan haji.

passages.heading: Dari mana asal muasal kita dan untuk apa kita hidup?
passages.text:
> **Adam**  
> Allah telah menceritakan kepada kita dalam Al-Qur`ān tentang kisah penciptaan Adam dan bagaimana setan mulai memusuhinya. Silakan lihat tafsir surah Al-Baqarah ayat: 30-39.

Islam telah menjelaskan bahwa asal penciptaan manusia dari tanah. Darinya Allah menciptakan Adam yang merupakan bapak seluruh manusia. Allah Ta’ālā berfirman, “Sungguh, Kami telah menciptakan manusia dari saripati (berasal) dari tanah.” (QS. Al-Mu`minūn: 12)

Tujuan penciptaan manusia ialah beribadah kepada Allah Ta’ālā, meskipun Dia tidak membutuhkan makhluk-makhluk-Nya. Allah Ta’ālā berfirman, “Aku tidak menciptakan jin dan manusia melainkan agar mereka beribadah kepada-Ku.” (QS. Aż-Żāriyāt: 56)

passages.heading: Diskusikan
passages.text: Bandingkan pandangan Anda tentang konsep keberadaan Anda sebelum masuk Islam dan setelahnya.

passages.heading: Mengapa Saya Masuk Islam?
passages.text:
**Mungkin sebagian orang bertanya-tanya: mengapa saya harus masuk Islam?**

Jawabannya: Saya harus masuk Islam karena beberapa faktor, di antaranya:

Pertama: agama Islam adalah agama yang diridai oleh Allah bagi hamba-hamba-Nya, dan Allah tidak menerima agama lainnya dari siapa pun. Dia berfirman, {{Q:3:85}} (QS. Āli 'Imrān: 85)

Kedua: agama Islam adalah agama para nabi semuanya. Islam memerintahkan beriman kepada para nabi seluruhnya, dan tidak membeda-bedakan di antara mereka. Allah Ta'ālā berfirman, {{Q:2:136}} (QS. Al-Baqarah: 136)

passages.heading: Pelajaran 2
passages.text:
### Apakah Islam Itu?

Ketiga: masuk Islam adalah jalan kebahagiaan di dunia dan keselamatan di akhirat. Orang yang sampai kepadanya dakwah Nabi Muhammad ﷺ tidak akan selamat di akhirat kelak kecuali bila ia beriman kepadanya serta mengikutinya. Allah Ta’ālā berfirman, “Barang siapa mencari agama selain Islam, ia tidak akan diterima dan di akhirat dia termasuk orang yang rugi.” (QS. Āli ‘Imrān: 85)

Nabi ﷺ bersabda, “Demi (Tuhan) yang jiwa Muhammad berada di tangan-Nya! Tidak ada seorang pun dari umat ini, baik Yahudi maupun Nasrani, yang mendengar tentang diriku lalu ia meninggal dalam keadaan tidak beriman kepada apa yang aku bawa, melainkan ia adalah penghuni neraka.” (HR. Muslim: 153)

Keempat: Islam memberikan jawaban sempurna terhadap pertanyaan-pertanyaan besarku: untuk apa aku hadir ke dunia? Dari mana aku berasal? Dan kemana aku akan pergi setelah kematian?

Kelima: Islam adalah agama yang sejalan dengan fitrah, mulai dari nilai Islam yang paling besar, yaitu menauhidkan Allah, hingga pada adab-adabnya yang mengajak kepada akhlak baik nan lurus.

passages.heading: Diskusikan
passages.text: Bagaimana Islam menjadi agama semua nabi?

passages.heading: Keistimewaan Islam
passages.text: Islam berbeda dari semua agama lainnya dengan sejumlah keistimewaan. Di antara keistimewaan tersebut yang paling tampak:

passages.heading: Apa Muamalah Harta Itu?
passages.text: Muamalah harta ialah transaksi-transaksi yang di dalamnya dilakukan pertukaran harta, baik dengan imbalan harta yang lain, seperti jual beli, atau imbalan manfaat seperti sewa menyewa, atau tanpa imbalan seperti hadiah.

passages.heading: Hukum Asal Muamalah Harta
passages.text:
Hukum asal muamalah harta ialah dibolehkan. Sebab itu, ia tidak boleh diharamkan kecuali kalau ada pengharamannya dalam Al-Qur`ān al-Karīm atau Sunnah Nabi ﷺ.

> Hukum asal muamalah, di antaranya muamalah harta, ialah dibolehkan. Sebab itu, tidak boleh ada pengharamannya kecuali dengan dalil. Ia kebalikan dari ibadah yang hukum asalnya ialah tauqīfiyah (baku), sehingga tidak boleh ada ibadah kecuali berdasarkan dalil.

passages.heading: Muamalah Harta yang Diharamkan
passages.text:
Allah 'Azza wa Jalla mengharamkan sebagian muamalah harta, di antaranya:

- Mengambil harta orang lain dengan cara yang tidak benar, seperti mengambilnya lewat penipuan atau perampasan.
- Memaksa salah satu pihak yang bertransaksi untuk melakukan muamalah yang tidak ingin dia lakukan.
- Berbisnis komoditi yang membahayakan kesehatan manusia seperti khamar, narkoba, tembakau, dan lain sebagainya.
- Riba; yaitu meminjamkan harta dengan syarat dikembalikan bersama tambahan atas harta yang dipinjam, seperti tambahan 5%, misalnya.
- Menjual sesuatu yang majhul; yaitu yang tidak diketahui barangnya, seperti menjual kotak yang tidak diketahui apa isinya.
- Perjudian dan taruhan yang di dalamnya orang yang menang mengambil harta orang yang kalah tanpa alasan yang benar.

passages.text: **Keimanan memiliki banyak buah positif, di antaranya:**

passages.heading: The Conditions of the Prayer
passages.text:
- Purity: Once’s body and the place where the prayer is to be performed must be cleansed from physical impurities, and any ritual impurity must be removed with *wudoo’* or *ghusl*.
- Covering the intimate parts of the body (*‘awrah*): The word *‘awrah* refers to the parts of the body that must be covered in front of people. A man’s *‘awrah* that must be covered during the prayer extends from the navel to the knees; a woman’s *‘awrah* that must be covered during the prayer is her entire body except for the face and hands.
- Facing the *qiblah*: The *qiblah* is the direction of the Ka‘bah in Makkah. One must, therefore, pray in the direction of the Ka‘bah in Makkah.
- When its appointed time becomes due: The prayer will not be valid if it is performed before its time has started. It is not permissible to delay it beyond its due time, and it is best to perform it at the beginning of its time.

passages.heading: The Friday Prayer (Salaat-ul-Jumu’ah)
passages.text:
- Allah Almighty has enjoined Muslims to perform a special prayer on Friday, called *Salaat-ul-Jumu’ah* (the Friday prayer). It is performed in a special manner, has special conditions and takes the place of the daily *Dhuhr* (midday) prayer on this day.
- Muslims gather together to perform it in the mosque. The *imaam* delivers a two-section *khutbah* (sermon), then he leads them in a two-*rak’ahs* prayer in which he recites the Qur’an aloud.
- It is recommended to take a ritual bath (*ghusl*) to attend the Friday prayer and proceed early to the mosque. It is not permissible to miss it without a legitimate excuse, and if for any reason a person misses it he must perform the four-unit *Dhuhr* (midday) prayer instead but without reciting the Qur’an aloud.
- Women and people on a journey are exempt from performing the Friday prayer.

passages.heading: Introduction
passages.text: The prayer is the greatest religious duty that a Muslim must learn and perform. Allah’s Messenger ﷺ has taught us how to perform it in the manner most pleasing to Allah Almighty. In this lesson, we are going to learn about the obligatory prayers, the position of the prayer in Islam, its conditions, and the correct manner of performing it.

passages.heading: Introduction
passages.text: People have always pondered the big questions of human existence: Where did we come from? Why are we here? Where do we go after death? Islam provides definitive and conclusive answers to these questions which arise in the heart of every reflective human being.

passages.heading: The Meaning of the Prayer
passages.text:
The prayer: It is a daily act of worship that consists of a set of words and actions with which a Muslim seeks to draw closer to his Lord, and it is performed five times a day and night.

The prayer is the second pillar of Islam.

passages.heading: The Position of the Prayer in Islam
passages.text:
The prayer has a number of distinctive characteristics, including the following:

- It is the second pillar of Islam after the two testimonies of faith.
- It is the act of worship that must be performed under all circumstances, in times of war and peace, and whether one is sick or in good health.
- It is the act of worship that distinguishes a Muslim from a non-Muslim.

This manner only applies to a prayer that consists of two units (*rak’ahs*), such as *Fajr* and *Jumu’ah* prayers. If, however, the prayer consists of three units (*rak’ahs*), namely *Maghrib*, or four units (*rak’ahs*), namely *Dhuhr*, *‘Asr* and *‘Ishaa’*, he completes the remaining units after concluding the first *tashahhud*, in the same way he has performed the first *rak’ah* but without reciting anything else after *Soorat Al-Faatihah*, then sits as he has done after the second *rak’ah*, recites the first *tashahhud* and *As-Salaatu Al-Ibraaheemiyyah*, and then concludes the prayer by saying, Assalaamu ‘alaykum wa rahmatullaah May Allah’s peace and mercy be upon you.” first to the right and then to the left.

passages.heading: The Virtue of Reading/Reciting the Qur’an
passages.text:
- The Prophet ﷺ said, “If anyone reads/recites one single letter in Allah’s Book, he will be credited with a good deed, and a good deed gets a tenfold reward. I do not say that *alif*, *laam*, *meem* are one letter; rather, *alif* is a letter, *laam* is a letter and *meem* is a letter” (Reported by At-Tirmidhee; No. 2910 with an authentic chain of narrators).

- The Prophet ﷺ also said, “Read the Qur’an, for it will come on the Day of Resurrection as an intercessor for those who read it.” (Reported by Muslim; No. 804).

passages.heading: What is the Islamic Ruling on Seafood Consumption?
passages.text:
It is permissible to eat dead aquatic animals that can live only in water, such as fish and prawns, whether they live in the sea, rivers or lakes.

It is permissible to hunt wild, nonpredatory animals and consume their flesh provided that the name of Allah is mentioned before the hunting weapon is discharged, and the hunted game must be slaughtered if found still alive.

passages.heading: How Do We Pray?
passages.text: If a Muslim wants to pray, he must do the following:

passages.heading: Why Do We Pray?
passages.text: We pray because the prayer is an act of worship that Allah has enjoined on Muslims.

passages.heading: How Do We Pray?
passages.text:
1. He intends in his heart to pray.
2. He stands facing the *qiblah*, raises his hands up to the level of the shoulders or ears, and says, “*Allaahu akbar* Allah is the Greatest.”
3. He places his right hand on his left hand. Then he recites one of the opening supplications, such as, Subhaanak-Allaahumma wa bi hamdika, wa tabaarak-asmuka, wa ta’aalaa jadduka, wa laa ilaaha ghayruka “Glory be to You, O Allah; Yours is the praise, blessed is Your name, exalted is Your majesty, and there is no god besides You.” Then he says, A’oodhu billaahi min-ash-shaytaan-ir-rajeem. Bismillaah-ir-rahmaan-ir-raheem “I seek Allah’s protection from Satan, who has been expelled from His mercy. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.” Then he recites *Soorat Al-Faatihah* and says after it, “*Aameen*”, which means “Answer our supplications, O Allah”. After that, he recites whatever number of verses of the Qur’an as is easy for him, even if it is one verse.
4. He says, “Allaahu akbar Allah is the Greatest” while raising his hands up to the level of his shoulders or ears, and bows down, lowering his head and back and keeping them straight at a right angle, placing the palms of his hands on the knees. He says three times while in this position, “Subhaana rabbiy-al-’adheem Glory be to my Lord, the Almighty.”

passages.heading: Soorat Al-Kawthar (Abundant Good)
passages.text:
*Soorat Al-Kawthar* **Explained**

{{Q:108:1-3}}

“We have bestowed on you abundant good”

We have given you, Messenger, immeasurable, abundant good in this life and the life to come, part of which is River Al-Kawthar in Paradise.

“So pray to your Lord and sacrifice to Him”

Therefore, sincerely pray to your Lord and worship Him alone, and sacrifice to Him, pronouncing Allah’s name alone when slaughtering animals, in gratitude to Him for the honour and good He has bestowed on you.

“He who hates you is the one who is truly cut off”

*Shaani’aka*: The one who hates you and hates the true religion you have brought.

The one who hates you and hates the true religion you have brought is the most disgraced and contemptible, whose mention is short-lived and who is cut off from all good.

passages.heading: The Pillars of Islam
passages.text:
Islam is built on five pillars:

Every Muslim must strictly adhere to these pillars to ensure he is practising Islam in full; negligence in one of these pillars is bound to render the way you practise Islam deficient.

1. The two testimonies of faith: To bear witness that none is worthy of worship except Allah and that Muhammad is His His Messenger
2. Establish the prayer: A Muslim must pray five times a day. These prayers will be explained in due course.
3. Paying zakaat
4. Fasting in the month of Ramadaan
5. Making the pilgrimage to Allah’s House

passages.heading: What Are the Conditions for Islamic Slaughter?
passages.text:
Islamic slaughter is one that satisfies the following conditions:

1. The person undertaking the slaughtering process must be Muslim, Jew or Christian who has reached the age of discretion and carries out this act for the intended purpose.
2. The tool used for slaughter must be suitable for the intended purpose, causes blood to flow and sharp, such as a knife. It is forbidden to use anything that may kill the animal due to its heavy weight, hit its head to death or render it unconscious by resorting to electric stunning, for instance.
3. The name of Allah must be pronounced by saying *Bismillaah* (in the name of Allah) at the time of slaughtering the animal.
4. Cutting what must be cut in the Islamic slaughter, namely, the oesophagus, the throat, and the two jugular veins, or just three of these four.

passages.heading: Islamic Rulings Pertaining to Meat Served in Restaurants and Shops
passages.text:
1. The meat of animals that are slaughtered by other than a Muslim or a member of the People of the Book (a Christian or a Jew), such as a Buddhist, or a Hindu is strictly forbidden. This includes meat served in restaurants and shops in countries where Muslims or People of the Book constitute a minority.
2. The meat of animals killed by a Muslim or a member of the People of the Book is lawful based on textual evidence to this effect in the Qur’an.
3. The meat of animals that are not killed according to Islamic law, such as by electrocution and drowning, is strictly forbidden.
4. The general rule is that it is permissible to consume the flesh of animals slaughtered by People of the Book as well as meat of animals generally found in their restaurants and shops, making sure, however, to invoke Allah’s name at the time of eating (that is, by saying *Bismillaah*), but it is better for Muslims to eat only meat that has been proven to be lawful (*halaal*).

passages.text:

The Islamic rulings on the meat of animals that are sold in shops and restaurants vary according to the religion of the person who slaughtered such animals.

To perform the prayer, several conditions must be met:
There are several conditions required to perform the prayer, which are:

passages.heading: The Position of the Prayer in Islam
passages.text:
The prayer has a number of distinctive characteristics, including the following:

- It is the second pillar of Islam after the two testimonies of faith.
- It is the act of worship that must be performed under all circumstances, in times of war and peace, and whether one is sick or in good health.
- It is the act of worship that distinguishes a Muslim from a non-Muslim.

passages.heading: Why Do We Pray?
passages.text: We pray because the prayer is an act of worship that Allah has enjoined on Muslims.

passages.heading: The Conditions of the Prayer
passages.text:
To perform the prayer, several conditions must be met:
There are several conditions required to perform the prayer, which are:

passages.heading: Some of the Ultimate Objectives and Benefits of the Prayer:
passages.text:
- It is the direct, special and personal communion a Muslim establishes with his Lord.
- It relieves the mind of worry and all worldly anxieties.
- It strengthens a Muslim’s willpower and determination.
- It refines morals and keeps those who observe it away from evil.

passages.heading: Introduction
passages.text: The prayer is the greatest religious duty that a Muslim must learn and perform. Allah’s Messenger ﷺ has taught us how to perform it in the manner most pleasing to Allah Almighty. In this lesson, we are going to learn about the obligatory prayers, the position of the prayer in Islam, its conditions, and the correct manner of performing it.

passages.heading: The Conditions of the Prayer
passages.text:
- Purity: Once’s body and the place where the prayer is to be performed must be cleansed from physical impurities, and any ritual impurity must be removed with *wudoo’* or *ghusl*.
- Covering the intimate parts of the body (*‘awrah*): The word *‘awrah* refers to the parts of the body that must be covered in front of people. A man’s *‘awrah* that must be covered during the prayer extends from the navel to the knees; a woman’s *‘awrah* that must be covered during the prayer is her entire body except for the face and hands.
- Facing the *qiblah*: The *qiblah* is the direction of the Ka‘bah in Makkah. One must, therefore, pray in the direction of the Ka‘bah in Makkah.
- When its appointed time becomes due: The prayer will not be valid if it is performed before its time has started. It is not permissible to delay it beyond its due time, and it is best to perform it at the beginning of its time.

passages.heading: The Meaning of the Prayer
passages.text:
The prayer: It is a daily act of worship that consists of a set of words and actions with which a Muslim seeks to draw closer to his Lord, and it is performed five times a day and night.

The prayer is the second pillar of Islam.

passages.heading: The Friday Prayer (Salaat-ul-Jumu’ah)
passages.text:
- Allah Almighty has enjoined Muslims to perform a special prayer on Friday, called *Salaat-ul-Jumu’ah* (the Friday prayer). It is performed in a special manner, has special conditions and takes the place of the daily *Dhuhr* (midday) prayer on this day.
- Muslims gather together to perform it in the mosque. The *imaam* delivers a two-section *khutbah* (sermon), then he leads them in a two-*rak’ahs* prayer in which he recites the Qur’an aloud.
- It is recommended to take a ritual bath (*ghusl*) to attend the Friday prayer and proceed early to the mosque. It is not permissible to miss it without a legitimate excuse, and if for any reason a person misses it he must perform the four-unit *Dhuhr* (midday) prayer instead but without reciting the Qur’an aloud.
- Women and people on a journey are exempt from performing the Friday prayer.

passages.heading: The Five Obligatory Prayers
passages.text:
Allah Almighty has enjoined Muslims to perform five prayers throughout the day and night, namely:

| The Prayer | Beginning Time | Ending Time | Number of units (*rak‘ahs*) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| *Fajr* (Dawn) Prayer | at the break of dawn | sunrise | 2 |
| *Dhuhr* (Midday) Prayer | when the sun starts declining westward at midday after reaching its zenith | when the shadow of an object becomes equal in length to the object itself | 4 |
| *‘Asr* (Late Afternoon) Prayer | when the shadow of an object becomes equal in length to the object itself | sunset | 4 |
| *Maghrib* (Sunset) Prayer | sunset | when the red glow (evening twilight) on the western horizon disappears | 3 |
| *‘Ishaa’* (Late Evening) Prayer | when the red glow (evening twilight) on the western horizon disappears | midnight | 4 |

passages.heading: How Do We Pray?
passages.text: If a Muslim wants to pray, he must do the following:

passages.heading: The Prayer
passages.text:
11. He turns his face to his right and says: Assalaamu ‘alaykum wa rahmatullaah “May Allah’s peace and mercy be upon you.” Then he turns his face to his left and says the same this. With this, he concludes his prayer.

This manner only applies to a prayer that consists of two units (*rak’ahs*), such as *Fajr* and *Jumu’ah* prayers. If, however, the prayer consists of three units (*rak’ahs*), namely *Maghrib*, or four units (*rak’ahs*), namely *Dhuhr*, *‘Asr* and *‘Ishaa’*, he completes the remaining units after concluding the first *tashahhud*, in the same way he has performed the first *rak’ah* but without reciting anything else after *Soorat Al-Faatihah*, then sits as he has done after the second *rak’ah*, recites the first *tashahhud* and *As-Salaatu Al-Ibraaheemiyyah*, and then concludes the prayer by saying, Assalaamu ‘alaykum wa rahmatullaah May Allah’s peace and mercy be upon you.” first to the right and then to the left.

passages.heading: Discuss
passages.text:
Discuss with your classmates some of the challenges facing Muslims that prevent them from performing the prayers on time, and how to overcome these challenges.

{{Q:62:9}} (Soorat Al-Jumu’ah, 62:9)

7. Поднять голову, произнося при этом: «Аллаху Акбар!»; сесть на левую ногу, оставив правую стопу в вертикальном положении, положить кисти рук на бедра и во время этого сидения сказать: «Рабби-гфир ли / Господь мой, прости меня!»

8. Совершить еще один земной поклон, такой же, как и первый, говоря при опускании в него: «Аллаху Акбар!» — и делая то же, что делал в первом суджуде.

9. Поднять голову и встать для совершения второго ракаата, произнося при этом: «Аллаху Акбар!»; совершить второй ракаат точно таким же образом, как и первый.

passages.heading: (Неверующие)
passages.text:
{{Q:?}}

Смысл суры:

*«Скажи: “О неверующие!”»* Скажи, о Посланник, тем, которые не веруют в Аллаха и Его Посланника: «О неверующие в Аллаха!»

*«Я не поклоняюсь тому, чему поклоняетесь вы»* Я не поклоняюсь идолам и ложным божествам, которым вы поклоняетесь.

*«И вы не поклоняетесь Тому, Кому поклоняюсь я»* А вы не поклоняетесь Единому Богу — Аллаху, Господу миров, Единственному достойному поклонения.

*«Я не буду поклоняться тому, чему поклоняетесь вы».* Я не буду поклоняться идолам и ложным божествам, которым вы поклоняетесь.

*«И вы не будете поклоняться Тому, Кому поклоняюсь я».* И вы не станете поклоняться Единому Богу — Аллаху, Господу миров, Единственному достойному поклонения.

*«У вас — ваша религия, а у меня — моя».* Вам — ваша религия, в приверженности которой вы упорствуете, а мне — моя религия, и я не желаю иной.

> Неверующий (кяфир) — тот, кто не засвидетельствовал Единственность Аллаха и не последовал посланию Его Посланника Мухаммада ﷺ.

passages.heading: Описание полного омовения
Что мне следует делать, если после совершения таяммума я нашел воду?
passages.text: Если после таяммума мусульманин нашел воду или возможность воспользоваться ею, то его очищение признаётся недействительным и он должен совершить малое или полное омовение в зависимости от того, в каком осквернении он находится.

passages.heading: Смысл суры:
passages.text:
«Скажи: “Я ищу защиты у Господа рассвета”» Скажи, о Посланник: «Я прошу защиты у Аллаха — Господа рассвета, то есть начала утра».

«От зла того, что Он сотворил» От зла всех творений и вреда, причиняемого ими, видимого нам и невидимого.

«И от зла мрака, когда он наступает» От зла наступающей ночи с ее мраком и от дурных и вредных вещей, таящихся под ее покровом.

Аль-фаляк — начало утра.

Аль-гасак — непроглядный мрак ночи.

passages.heading: Смысл суры:
passages.text:
«Скажи: “Он — Аллах — Един”» Скажи, о Посланник, тем, кто попросил тебя описать своего Господа: «Он — Аллах, Единственный обладающий Божественностью и Господством, нет божества, кроме Него».

«Аллах самодостаточен» Он — Аллах, который совершенен в качествах славы и величия, к Которому творения обращаются за удовлетворением своих нужд и желаний.

«Он не родил и не был рожден» У него нет ни детей, ни родителей, ни супруги.

«…и нет никого, равного Ему» Среди Его творений нет никого, такого же, как Он, или хотя бы подобного Ему, — ни в Его именах, ни в Его качествах, ни в Его действиях.

passages.heading: Введение
passages.text: Одним из самых незабываемых моментов для новообращенного мусульманина является момент объявления о принятии Ислама путем произнесения двух свидетельств. Этим объявлением он говорит прежде всего себе, что он стал иным, чем был до этого, и что в этот момент он делает свои первые шаги к познанию истины и следованию ей. На этом уроке мы ознакомимся с двумя свидетельствами, их смыслом и требованиями.

passages.heading: Сура «аль-Фатиха»
passages.text:
### (Открывающая)

**Смысл суры:**

«С именем Аллаха Милостивого, Милующего». Я начинаю чтение Корана с произнесения имени Аллаха, испрашивая у Него помощи. Аллах — это имя Всевышнего Господа, Единственного достойного поклонения. Милостивый — Обладатель милости, распространяющейся на все Его творения. Милующий — по отношению к Своим верующим рабам.

«Хвала Аллаху, Господу миров». Восхваление Аллаха посредством Его совершенных качеств и Его милостей ко всем творениям. Лишь Он Один достоин всех видов восхваления и благодарности. Он — Господь всех творений, Который создал их из ничего, управляет их делами и исправляет их положение.

5. Поднять голову, чтобы снова принять стоячее положение, поднимая руки до уровня плеч и говоря при этом: «Сами‘а-Ллаху ли-ман хамида-х / Да услышит Аллах тех, кто воздал Ему хвалу!» — а затем, уже в стоячем положении, сказать: «Рабба-на уа-ля-ка-ль-хамд / Господь наш, хвала тебе!»

6. Опуститься на землю для земного поклона (суджуд), прижать к земле лоб и нос, а также кисти рук, колени и пальцы ног и трижды сказать: «Субхана Раббийа-ль-А‘ля / Пречист мой Высочайший Господь!»

passages.heading: Урок шестой
passages.text:
## Молитва

10. После второго земного поклона во втором ракаате сесть так же, как садятся между двумя земными поклонами, и сказать: «Ат-тахиййату лиЛляхи уа-с-саляуату уат-таййибату. Ас-саляму ‘аляйка аййуха-н-набиййу уа рахматуЛлахи уа баракатух! Ас-саляму ‘аляйна уа ‘аля ‘ибади-Лляхи-с-салихин! Ашхаду ал-ля иляха илляЛлаху уа ашхаду анна Мухаммадан ‘абдуху уа расулюх / Приветствия, мольбы и благие [слова] Аллаху! Мир тебе, о Пророк, милость Аллаха и Его благословения! Мир нам и всем праведным рабам Аллаха! Свидетельствую, что нет бога, кроме Аллаха, и свидетельствую, что Мухаммад — Его раб и Его посланник». Это называется первый ташаххуд. После этого сказать: «Аллахумма салли ‘аля Мухаммадин, уа ‘аля али Мухаммадин кяма салляйта ‘аля Ибрахима уа ‘аля али Ибрахима иннака Хамидун Маджид. Аллахумма барик ‘аля Мухаммадин уа ‘аля али Мухаммадин кяма баракта ‘аля Ибрахима ва ‘аля али Ибрахима иннака Хамидун Маджид / О Аллах! Благослови Мухаммада и семейство Мухаммада, как благословил Ты Ибрахима и семейство Ибрахима, поистине, Ты — Достойный похвалы, Славный. О Аллах! Благословляй Мухаммада и семейство Мухаммада, как благословлял Ты Ибрахима и семейство Ибрахима, поистине, Ты — Достойный похвалы, Славный». Это называется «Салауат Ибрахимия».

passages.heading: Урок шестой
passages.text:
11. Повернуть голову направо, говоря при этом: «Ас-саляму ‘аляйкум уа рахматуЛлах!»; затем повернуть голову налево, говоря то же самое. На этом молитва подходит к концу.

Это описание молитвы, состоящей из двух ракаатов, как утренняя или пятничная молитвы. Если же молитва состоит из трех ракаатов, как вечерняя, или из четырех, как обеденная, послеобеденная и ночная, то после первого ташаххуда нужно совершить оставшиеся ракааты так же, как и первые два, за исключением того, что в третьем и четвертом ракаатах после «аль-Фатихи» не читаются аяты Корана. Затем следует сесть, как на первый ташаххуд, прочесть ташаххуд и салауат Ибрахимия, а затем дать таслим.

passages.heading: Сура «ан-Нас» (Люди)
passages.text:
{{Q:114:1-6}}

**Смысл суры:**

_«Скажи: “Я ищу защиты у Господа людей”»._ Скажи, о Посланник: «Я прошу защиты у Господа людей, ибо только Он мощен над всякой вещью».

_«Царя людей»_ Властелина всех людей, распоряжающегося всеми их делами и не нуждающегося ни в ком из них.

_«Бога людей»_ Бога всех людей, кроме Которого никто не достоин поклонения.

_«…от зла искусителя, отбегающего [при поминании Аллаха]»_ От зла, причиняемого шайтаном, который наущает людей, когда они беспечны, и скрывается при поминании Аллаха.

_«…который нашептывает в сердца людей»_ Который внушает зло и сомнения людским сердцам.

_«…от джиннов и людей»._ От шайтанов из числа джиннов и людей.

passages.heading: Обсуждение
passages.text: Какова основная тема сур «аль-Ихляс» и «аль-Кяфирун»?

passages.heading: Урок второй
passages.text: ## Толкование коротких сур

passages.heading: Сура «аль-Кяусар»
passages.text:
**Смысл суры:**

«Поистине, Мы даровали тебе Кяусар» Поистине, Мы даровали тебе, о Пророк, множество благ в этом мире и мире вечном, в том числе и реку Кяусар в Раю.

«Потому молись своему Господу и закалывай [жертву]» Посвяти свою молитву целиком своему Господу, и совершай заклание жертвенного животного только ради Него и с Его Именем.

«Поистине, твой ненавистник сам лишен всякого блага» Поистине, тот, кто ненавидит тебя и принесенное тобой верное руководство и свет, сам является ничтожным и презренным, и он будет лишен всякого блага.

Твой ненавистник — тот, кто ненавидит тебя и истинную религию, которую ты принес.

passages.heading: Как совершать полное омовение?
Когда полное омовение становится обязательным?
passages.text:
Полное омовение обязательно для мусульманина в трех случаях:

- **Первое:** Выделение семенной жидкости с вожделением, независимо от того, произошло ли это во время бодрствования или во сне.
- **Второе:** Половой акт, независимо от того, произошло семяизвержение или нет.
- **Третье:** Менструальное или послеродовое кровотечение у женщины. Когда кровотечение прекращается, она должна совершить полное омовение.

passages.heading: Обсуждение
passages.text: На что указывает требование совершить полное омовение для устранения большого осквернения?

passages.heading: Что запрещено делать человеку, находящемуся в состоянии полового осквернения?
passages.text:
Состояние человека, который должен совершить полное омовение по причине полового акта или извержения семенной жидкости, называется джана́ба, а человек, находящийся в этом состоянии, — джунуб. Ему запрещено:

1. совершать молитву
2. совершать обход вокруг Каабы
3. прикасаться к мусхафу
4. пребывать в мечети
5. читать Священный Коран

passages.heading: Описание таяммума
passages.text: Сначала нужно вознамериться в сердце совершить таяммум, затем однократно ударить руками по поверхности земли и протереть руками с оставшейся на них пылью лицо и кисти рук.

passages.heading: Урок второй
passages.text:
### Толкование коротких сур

_«От зла [колдуний], поплевывающих на узлы»_ От зла колдуний, дующих на узлы, завязанные для колдовских деяний.

_«От зла завистника, когда он завидует»_ От зла завистника, желающего, чтобы объект его зависти лишился своих благ и его постигла беда.

passages.heading: Обсуждение
passages.text: Что помогает запомнить суру «аль-Фатиха»?

passages.heading: Два свидетельства
passages.text:
Всевышний Аллах сделал ключом для вхождения в Ислам произнесение двух свидетельств. Это свидетельство состоит из двух частей.

*Я свидетельствую, что нет божества, кроме Аллаха, и я свидетельствую, что Мухаммад — Посланник Аллаха.*

passages.heading: Каков смысл этих свидетельств?
passages.text:
*Первое. Смысл свидетельства «Нет божества, кроме Аллаха»*

Слова «Нет божества, кроме Аллаха» означают: «Я твердо верую, что нет бога, достойного поклонения, кроме Одного лишь Аллаха».

Это свидетельство состоит из двух

| Первая | Вторая |
| :--- | :--- |
| Отрицание божественности кого-либо или чего-либо, кроме Аллаха. | Подтверждение Божественности Одного лишь Аллаха. |

passages.heading: Урок третий
passages.text:
## Как принять Ислам?

Суть Ислама, являющегося религией всех пророков, — это поклонение Одному лишь Аллаху и неверие во все, чему поклоняются помимо Него. Всевышний Аллах сказал: {{Q:21:25}} (сура «аль-Анбия», аят 25).

Поэтому ни при каких обстоятельствах не дозволено верить в божественность чего-либо или кого-либо, кроме Всевышнего Аллаха, и искать приближения к кому-либо, кроме Всевышнего Аллаха, посредством какого бы то ни было вида поклонения.

passages.heading: Введение
passages.text: Сура «аль-Фатиха» является величайшей сурой Корана, и Посланник Аллаха ﷺ во многих хадисах подчеркивал ее достоинство и величие. Каждый мусульманин обязан выучить «аль-Фатиху» наизусть, поскольку она является единственной сурой, которую обязательно читать в каждой молитве. На этом уроке мы познакомимся с «аль-Фатихой», выучим наизусть ее аяты, узнаем их значения, а также познакомимся с некоторыми другими короткими сурами Корана, в которых заключен великий смысл.

passages.heading: Урок второй
passages.text:
### Толкование коротких сур

«Милостивому, Милующему». Милостивый — Обладатель милости, распространяющейся на все Его творения. Милующий — по отношению к верующим.

Милостивый: ко всем творениям.

Милующий: по отношению к верующим.

passages.heading: Préface
passages.text: La sourate Al Fâtihah est considérée comme la plus immense et majestueuse des sourates du Coran. Le Messager d’Allah ﷺ a insisté sur son mérite et sa grandeur dans de nombreux hadiths. C’est la sourate que tout musulman doit mémoriser parce que c’est la seule sourate qu’il doit réciter dans chaque prière. Et dans cette leçon, nous allons en apprendre davantage sur cette sourate, mémoriser ses versets, apprendre leurs significations, et aussi apprendre un certain nombre de courtes sourates du Coran qui renferment d’immenses significations.

passages.heading: Signification de la sourate :
passages.text:
Au nom d’Allah, le Tout-Miséricordieux, le Très-Miséricordieux.

Je commence la lecture du Coran par le nom d’Allah en cherchant assistance auprès de Lui. Allah est la divinité adorée, Celui qui est décrit par la miséricorde générale qui a embrassé l’ensemble de la création. Et Il est le Très Miséricordieux envers Ses serviteurs d’une miséricorde spécifique.

{Louange à Allah Seigneur des mondes.}

L’éloge à Allah pour Ses attributs parfaits et Ses bienfaits sur l’ensemble de Sa création. Il est donc le Seul à mériter l’ensemble des formes de louange. Il est le Seigneur de toutes les créatures, Celui qui les a créées après le néant, Celui qui se charge de leurs affaires et Celui qui s’occupe de leurs situations.
